items.doc: Computing `f` alongside `g` on `S` is at least as hard as computing `f` on `S`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityOn_le_ecomplexityOn_append_left (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    ecomplexityOn I S f ≤ ecomplexityOn I S (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityOn_le_ecomplexityOn_append_right
items.doc: Computing `g` alongside `f` on `S` is at least as hard as computing `g` on `S`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityOn_le_ecomplexityOn_append_right (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    ecomplexityOn I S g ≤ ecomplexityOn I S (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_le_of_computes
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_le_of_computes (c : Circuit σ n m) (hc : c.Computes I f) :
    ecomplexity I f ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_ne_top_iff
items.statement: theorem ecomplexity_ne_top_iff : ecomplexity I f ≠ ⊤ ↔ ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.exists_computes_size_eq_ecomplexity
items.doc:
When some circuit computes `f`, the least size is attained by some (potentially different)
circuit.
items.statement:
theorem exists_computes_size_eq_ecomplexity (h : ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f) :
    ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f ∧ (c.size : ℕ∞) = ecomplexity I f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_le_iff
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_le_iff :
    ecomplexity I f ≤ k ↔ ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f ∧ c.size ≤ k

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.le_ecomplexity_iff
items.doc:
Lower bounds on complexity are exactly lower bounds on the size of every circuit computing
the function, including when no such circuit exists.
items.statement:
theorem le_ecomplexity_iff {k : ℕ∞} :
    k ≤ ecomplexity I f ↔ ∀ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f → k ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_wiring
items.doc: Selecting, permuting, or duplicating inputs costs nothing.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_wiring (select : Fin m → Fin n) :
ecomplexity I (fun x => x ∘ select) = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_comp_le
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_comp_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin m → U) → Fin p → U) :
    ecomplexity I (g ∘ f) ≤ ecomplexity I f + ecomplexity I g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_append_le
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_append_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    ecomplexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x)) ≤ ecomplexity I f + ecomplexity I g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_le_ecomplexity_append_left
items.doc: Computing `f` alongside `g` is at least as hard as computing `f`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_le_ecomplexity_append_left (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    ecomplexity I f ≤ ecomplexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_le_ecomplexity_append_right
items.doc: Computing `g` alongside `f` is at least as hard as computing `g`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_le_ecomplexity_append_right (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    ecomplexity I g ≤ ecomplexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.ecomplexity_le
items.doc: A synthesis bound on the input projections bounds the extended complexity.
items.statement:
theorem Synthesis.ecomplexity_le {f : (Fin n → U) → U} {cost : ℕ}
    (h : Synthesis I (inputs n) {f} cost) : ecomplexity I (single f) ≤ cost

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityOn_ne_top
items.statement: theorem ecomplexityOn_ne_top [I.IsComplete] : ecomplexityOn I S f ≠ ⊤

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_ne_top
items.statement: theorem ecomplexity_ne_top [I.IsComplete] : ecomplexity I f ≠ ⊤

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn
items.doc:
The complexity `C^S(f)` of `f` on the support `S` over a complete basis, as a natural
number.
items.statement:
noncomputable def complexityOn (I : Interpretation σ U) [I.IsComplete] (S : Set (Fin n → U))
    (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity
items.doc: The complexity `C(f)` of `f` over a complete basis, as a natural number.
items.statement:
noncomputable def complexity (I : Interpretation σ U) [I.IsComplete]
    (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.natCast_complexityOn
items.statement: theorem natCast_complexityOn : (complexityOn I S f : ℕ∞) = ecomplexityOn I S f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.natCast_complexity
items.statement: theorem natCast_complexity : (complexity I f : ℕ∞) = ecomplexity I f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_le_of_computesOn
items.doc: A circuit computing `f` on `S` bounds its support complexity.
items.statement:
theorem complexityOn_le_of_computesOn (c : Circuit σ n m) (hc : c.ComputesOn I S f) :
    complexityOn I S f ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.exists_computesOn_size_eq_complexityOn
items.doc: Over a complete basis the least size on a support is attained.
items.statement:
theorem exists_computesOn_size_eq_complexityOn :
    ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesOn I S f ∧ c.size = complexityOn I S f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_le_iff
items.doc:
Support complexity is at most `k` exactly when some circuit of size at most `k` computes
the function on the support.
items.statement:
theorem complexityOn_le_iff :
    complexityOn I S f ≤ k ↔ ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesOn I S f ∧ c.size ≤ k

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.le_complexityOn_iff
items.doc:
Over a complete basis, lower bounds on support complexity are exactly lower bounds on the
size of every circuit computing the function on the support.
items.statement:
theorem le_complexityOn_iff :
    k ≤ complexityOn I S f ↔ ∀ c : Circuit σ n m, c.ComputesOn I S f → k ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_le_of_computes
items.statement:
theorem complexity_le_of_computes (c : Circuit σ n m) (hc : c.Computes I f) :
    complexity I f ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.le_size_of_le_complexity
items.doc: A lower bound on the complexity is a lower bound on the size of every circuit.
items.statement:
theorem le_size_of_le_complexity (h : k ≤ complexity I f) {c : Circuit σ n m}
    (hc : c.Computes I f) : k ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.exists_computes_size_eq_complexity
items.doc: Over a complete basis the least size is attained.
items.statement:
theorem exists_computes_size_eq_complexity :
    ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f ∧ c.size = complexity I f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_le_iff
items.statement:
theorem complexity_le_iff :
    complexity I f ≤ k ↔ ∃ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f ∧ c.size ≤ k

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.le_complexity_iff
items.doc:
Over a complete basis, lower bounds on complexity are exactly lower bounds on the size
of every circuit.
items.statement:
theorem le_complexity_iff :
    k ≤ complexity I f ↔ ∀ c : Circuit σ n m, c.Computes I f → k ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_mono
items.statement: theorem complexityOn_mono (h : S ⊆ T) : complexityOn I S f ≤ complexityOn I T f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_congr
items.doc: Complexity on a support depends only on the values of the function on the support.
items.statement: theorem complexityOn_congr (h : Set.EqOn f f' S) : complexityOn I S f = complexityOn I S f'

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_le_complexity
items.doc: Restricting the inputs to a support cannot increase complexity.
items.statement: theorem complexityOn_le_complexity : complexityOn I S f ≤ complexity I f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_wiring
items.doc: Selecting, permuting, or duplicating inputs costs nothing.
items.statement:
theorem complexityOn_wiring (select : Fin m → Fin n) :
complexityOn I S (fun x => x ∘ select) = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_comp_le
items.statement:
theorem complexityOn_comp_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin m → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexityOn I S (g ∘ f) ≤ complexityOn I S f + complexityOn I (f '' S) g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_append_le
items.statement:
theorem complexityOn_append_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexityOn I S (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x)) ≤
      complexityOn I S f + complexityOn I S g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_le_complexityOn_append_left
items.doc: Computing `f` alongside `g` on `S` is at least as hard as computing `f` on `S`.
items.statement:
theorem complexityOn_le_complexityOn_append_left (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexityOn I S f ≤ complexityOn I S (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityOn_le_complexityOn_append_right
items.doc: Computing `g` alongside `f` on `S` is at least as hard as computing `g` on `S`.
items.statement:
theorem complexityOn_le_complexityOn_append_right (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexityOn I S g ≤ complexityOn I S (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_wiring
items.doc: Selecting, permuting, or duplicating inputs costs nothing.
items.statement:
theorem complexity_wiring (select : Fin m → Fin n) :
complexity I (fun x => x ∘ select) = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_comp_le
items.doc: Computing a composite costs at most the sum of the complexities of its two functions.
items.statement:
theorem complexity_comp_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin m → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexity I (g ∘ f) ≤ complexity I f + complexity I g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_append_le
items.doc: Computing two functions side by side costs at most the sum of their complexities.
items.statement:
theorem complexity_append_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x)) ≤ complexity I f + complexity I g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_le_complexity_append_left
items.doc: Computing `f` alongside `g` is at least as hard as computing `f`.
items.statement:
theorem complexity_le_complexity_append_left (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexity I f ≤ complexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_le_complexity_append_right
items.doc: Computing `g` alongside `f` is at least as hard as computing `g`.
items.statement:
theorem complexity_le_complexity_append_right (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin p → U) :
    complexity I g ≤ complexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.complexity_le
items.doc: A synthesis bound on the input projections bounds the complexity.
items.statement:
theorem Synthesis.complexity_le {f : (Fin n → U) → U} {cost : ℕ}
    (h : Synthesis I (inputs n) {f} cost) : complexity I (single f) ≤ cost

modules.title: Composing circuits
modules.doc:
A program can be continued by a second program whose inputs are read from wires of the first.
Reading them from the outputs of a circuit gives sequential composition, `Circuit.comp`, which
evaluates to the composite of the two functions. Reading them from the original inputs gives
parallel composition on shared inputs, `Circuit.append`, whose outputs are those of the first
circuit followed by those of the second. In both cases the gate counts add.

items.name: Fin.append_comp_castAdd
items.statement:
theorem append_comp_castAdd (u : Fin m → α) (v : Fin n → α) :
append u v ∘ castAdd n = u

items.name: Fin.append_comp_natAdd
items.statement:
theorem append_comp_natAdd (u : Fin m → α) (v : Fin n → α) :
append u v ∘ natAdd m = v

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.appendedWire
items.doc:
For programs `p : Program σ n g₁` and `q : Program σ k g₂`, with
`feed : Fin k → Wire n g₁`, map a wire of `q` to its wire in the combined program.
Inputs follow `feed`, and gate indices are shifted past the gates of `p`.
This is the wire map used by `Program.append` below.
items.statement: def appendedWire (feed : Fin k → Wire n g₁) : Wire k g₂ → Wire n (g₁ + g₂)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.appendedWire_input
items.statement:
theorem appendedWire_input (feed : Fin k → Wire n g₁) (i : Fin k) :
appendedWire (g₂ := g₂) feed (Wire.input i) = (feed i).castAdd g₂

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.appendedWire_gate
items.statement:
theorem appendedWire_gate (feed : Fin k → Wire n g₁) (j : Fin g₂) :
appendedWire feed (Wire.gate j) = Wire.gate (Fin.natAdd g₁ j)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.append
items.doc: Continue `p` by `q`, reading the inputs of `q` from the wires `feed` of `p`.
items.statement:
def append (p : Program σ n g₁) (feed : Fin k → Wire n g₁)
    {g₂ : ℕ} (q : Program σ k g₂) : Program σ n (g₁ + g₂)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.trace_append_castAdd
items.doc: The wires of `p` keep their values after `p` is continued.
items.statement:
theorem trace_append_castAdd (q : Program σ k g₂) (w : Wire n g₁) :
    (p.append feed q).trace I x (w.castAdd g₂) = p.trace I x w

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.trace_append_appendedWire
items.doc:
A wire of `q` carries, in the continued program, the value it has when `q` runs on the
values of the wires feeding it.
items.statement:
theorem trace_append_appendedWire (q : Program σ k g₂) (w : Wire k g₂) :
    (p.append feed q).trace I x (appendedWire feed w) =
      q.trace I (fun i => p.trace I x (feed i)) w

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.comp
items.doc: Feed the outputs of `c` to the inputs of `d`.
items.statement: protected def comp (d : Circuit σ m p) (c : Circuit σ n m) : Circuit σ n p

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.size_comp
items.statement:
theorem size_comp (d : Circuit σ m p) (c : Circuit σ n m) :
(d.comp c).size = c.size + d.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.program_comp
items.statement:
theorem program_comp (d : Circuit σ m p) (c : Circuit σ n m) :
    (d.comp c).program = c.program.append c.outputs d.program

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.outputs_comp
items.statement:
theorem outputs_comp (d : Circuit σ m p) (c : Circuit σ n m) :
    (d.comp c).outputs = Program.appendedWire c.outputs ∘ d.outputs

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.eval_comp
items.statement:
theorem eval_comp (d : Circuit σ m p) (c : Circuit σ n m) (x : Fin n → U) :
(d.comp c).eval I x = d.eval I (c.eval I x)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.append
items.doc: Run `c` and `d` on the same inputs, listing the outputs of `c` before those of `d`.
items.statement: def append (c : Circuit σ n m) (d : Circuit σ n p) : Circuit σ n (m + p)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.size_append
items.statement:
theorem size_append (c : Circuit σ n m) (d : Circuit σ n p) :
(c.append d).size = c.size + d.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.eval_append
items.statement:
theorem eval_append (c : Circuit σ n m) (d : Circuit σ n p) (x : Fin n → U) :
(c.append d).eval I x = Fin.append (c.eval I x) (d.eval I x)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.Computes.comp
items.doc: Feeding a circuit computing `f` into one computing `g` computes `g ∘ f`.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.Computes.append
items.doc: Circuits computing `f` and `g`, run side by side, compute their outputs together.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.ComputesOn.comp
items.doc:
Feeding a circuit computing `f` on `S` into one computing `g` on the image of `S` computes
`g ∘ f` on `S`.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.ComputesOn.append
items.doc: Circuits computing `f` and `g` on `S`, run side by side, compute their outputs together.

modules.title: Counting functions computed by finite circuits
modules.doc:
For a finite signature, only finitely many functions can be computed with a fixed gate budget,
even when the carrier is infinite. We enumerate the programs of each size together with an
output wire and collect the scalar functions they compute, so that `computableFunctions I n s`
is the finite set of functions whose `ecomplexity` is at most `s`. Semantic equality and
normalization use classical reasoning, as does choosing an enumeration of the finite syntax.

After merging gates that compute the same function, a circuit with `g` gates has `g!` distinct
labeled presentations. This factorial correction sharpens the count used in Shannon's lower bound.
The main bound accepts any uniform bound on the number of lines;
`card_computableFunctions_mul_factorial_le_of_arity_le` specializes it to operation arities.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.computableFunctions
items.doc:
Scalar functions computable with at most `s` gates. Enumerating the programs of each size
with an output wire makes this set finite without requiring a finite carrier.
items.statement:
noncomputable def computableFunctions (I : Interpretation σ U) (n s : ℕ) :
    Finset ((Fin n → U) → U)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.mem_computableFunctions
items.statement:
theorem mem_computableFunctions {f : (Fin n → U) → U} :
f ∈ computableFunctions I n s ↔
∃ c : Circuit σ n 1, c.Computes I (single f) ∧ c.size ≤ s

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.mem_computableFunctions_iff_ecomplexity_le
items.doc: The functions computable with at most `s` gates are those of complexity at most `s`.
items.statement:
theorem mem_computableFunctions_iff_ecomplexity_le {f : (Fin n → U) → U} :
    f ∈ computableFunctions I n s ↔ ecomplexity I (single f) ≤ s

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.irredundantFunctions
items.doc:
Functions computed at an output wire of a program whose `g` gates compute pairwise distinct
functions. Permuting the gates of such a program, ignoring their order, gives `g!` distinct gate
lists; this is the factorial saving in the counting bound.
items.statement:
noncomputable def irredundantFunctions (I : Interpretation σ U) (n g : ℕ) :
    Finset ((Fin n → U) → U)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.mem_irredundantFunctions
items.statement:
theorem mem_irredundantFunctions {f : (Fin n → U) → U} :
f ∈ irredundantFunctions I n g ↔
∃ c : Circuit σ n 1, c.Computes I (single f) ∧ c.Irredundant I ∧ c.size = g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.card_irredundantFunctions_mul_factorial_le
items.doc: Distinct functions and permutations of their irredundant gates give distinct presentations.
items.statement:
theorem card_irredundantFunctions_mul_factorial_le (I : Interpretation σ U) (n g : ℕ) :
    (irredundantFunctions I n g).card * g.factorial ≤
      Nat.card (Line σ n g) ^ g * (n + g)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.card_computableFunctions_le_sum
items.doc:
Normalizing a circuit with at most `s` gates leaves an irredundant program with at most `s`
gates computing the same function.
items.statement:
theorem card_computableFunctions_le_sum (I : Interpretation σ U) (n s : ℕ) :
    (computableFunctions I n s).card ≤
      ∑ g ∈ Finset.range (s + 1), (irredundantFunctions I n g).card

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.card_computableFunctions_mul_factorial_le
items.doc:
Bound the number of computable functions using a uniform line count `B`. The condition
`s ≤ B` absorbs the extra factorial factors from circuits with fewer than `s` gates.
items.statement:
theorem card_computableFunctions_mul_factorial_le (I : Interpretation σ U) (n s B : ℕ)
    (hB : s ≤ B) (hlines : ∀ g ≤ s, Nat.card (Line σ n g) ≤ B) :
    (computableFunctions I n s).card * s.factorial ≤
      (s + 1) * B ^ s * (n + s)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.card_computableFunctions_mul_factorial_le_of_arity_le
items.doc:
A cardinality bound for any finite signature with bounded arities. The maximum also
covers empty signatures and signatures containing only nullary operations.
items.statement:
theorem card_computableFunctions_mul_factorial_le_of_arity_le
    (I : Interpretation σ U) (n s r : ℕ) (arity_le : ∀ op, σ.Arity op ≤ r) :
    (computableFunctions I n s).card * s.factorial ≤
      (s + 1) * (max s (Nat.card σ.Op * (n + s + 1) ^ r)) ^ s * (n + s)

modules.title: Circuit depth bounds
modules.doc:
This file proves bounds for `Program.depth`, defined in `Cslib.Computability.Circuit.Program`,
and `Circuit.depth`, defined in `Cslib.Computability.Circuit.Basic`. Program depth is the maximum
depth of its gates; circuit depth is the maximum depth of its designated outputs.
`Program.depth_le_iff` and `Circuit.depth_le_iff` express bounds in terms of the individual
gates and outputs. These characterizations give
`Circuit.depth_le_program_depth` and `Circuit.depth_le_size` without assumptions on the
signature's fan-in or its interpretation.

Constructor simplification lemmas preserve the depth of earlier wires when a gate is added.
Every gate, including a constant gate, contributes one level; selecting outputs contributes
none. A circuit with no outputs has depth zero, even when its program contains gates.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.depth_le_add_one_iff
items.doc: Bounding every argument by `d` bounds the gate's depth by `d + 1`.
items.statement:
theorem Line.depth_le_add_one_iff (line : Line σ n g) (depths : Wire n g → Nat) {d : Nat} :
    line.depth depths ≤ d + 1 ↔ ∀ j, depths (line.wires j) ≤ d

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.depth_pos
items.doc: Every gate, including a constant gate, has positive depth.
items.statement:
theorem Line.depth_pos (line : Line σ n g) (depths : Wire n g → Nat) :
    0 < line.depth depths

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.depths_gate_last
items.statement:
theorem Program.depths_gate_last (p : Program σ n g) (line : Line σ n g) :
(p.gate line).depths (Fin.last g) = line.depth p.wireDepths

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.depths_gate_castSucc
items.statement:
theorem Program.depths_gate_castSucc (p : Program σ n g) (line : Line σ n g)
(j : Fin g) : (p.gate line).depths j.castSucc = p.depths j

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.wireDepths_input
items.statement:
theorem Program.wireDepths_input (p : Program σ n g) (i : Fin n) :
p.wireDepths (.input i) = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.wireDepths_gateWire
items.statement:
theorem Program.wireDepths_gateWire (p : Program σ n g) (j : Fin g) :
p.wireDepths (.gate j) = p.depths j

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.wireDepths_gate_castSucc
items.statement:
theorem Program.wireDepths_gate_castSucc (p : Program σ n g) (line : Line σ n g)
(w : Wire n g) : (p.gate line).wireDepths w.castSucc = p.wireDepths w

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.depth_empty
items.statement: theorem Program.depth_empty : (Program.empty : Program σ n 0).depth = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.depth_gate
items.statement:
theorem Program.depth_gate (p : Program σ n g) (line : Line σ n g) :
(p.gate line).depth = max p.depth (line.depth p.wireDepths)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.depth_le_iff
items.doc: Program depth is bounded by `d` exactly when every gate depth is bounded by `d`.
items.statement:
theorem Program.depth_le_iff (p : Program σ n g) {d : Nat} :
    p.depth ≤ d ↔ ∀ j, p.depths j ≤ d

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.depths_le_depth
items.doc: Every gate depth is at most the depth of the program.
items.statement: theorem Program.depths_le_depth (p : Program σ n g) (j : Fin g) : p.depths j ≤ p.depth

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.wireDepths_le_depth
items.doc: Every input or gate wire has depth at most the depth of the program.
items.statement:
theorem Program.wireDepths_le_depth (p : Program σ n g) (w : Wire n g) :
    p.wireDepths w ≤ p.depth

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.depth_le_gateCount
items.doc: A program's depth is at most its number of gates.
items.statement: theorem Program.depth_le_gateCount (p : Program σ n g) : p.depth ≤ g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.depth_le_iff
items.doc: Circuit depth is bounded by `d` exactly when every designated output depth is bounded by `d`.
items.statement:
theorem Circuit.depth_le_iff (c : Circuit σ n m) {d : Nat} :
    c.depth ≤ d ↔ ∀ j, c.outputDepths j ≤ d

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.outputDepths_le_depth
items.doc: Every designated output has depth at most the circuit depth.
items.statement:
theorem Circuit.outputDepths_le_depth (c : Circuit σ n m) (j : Fin m) :
    c.outputDepths j ≤ c.depth

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.depth_le_program_depth
items.doc: Selecting outputs cannot increase the maximum depth over all program gates.
items.statement: theorem Circuit.depth_le_program_depth (c : Circuit σ n m) : c.depth ≤ c.program.depth

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.depth_le_size
items.doc: Circuit depth is at most the number of gates.
items.statement: theorem Circuit.depth_le_size (c : Circuit σ n m) : c.depth ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.depth_zero_outputs
items.statement: theorem Circuit.depth_zero_outputs (c : Circuit σ n 0) : c.depth = 0

modules.title: Finite circuit syntax
modules.doc:
A finite signature gives finitely many lines and programs of each fixed size.
Their cardinalities count syntax and are independent of any interpretation or carrier.
`Line.card_le` bounds the number of lines when all operation arities are bounded.
For the full basis on a carrier of size `q`, there are `q ^ (q ^ k)` operation tables
and `q` constants. `Line.card_full` counts their possible arguments separately.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.instFinite
items.statement: instance Line.instFinite (n g : ℕ) : Finite (Line σ n g)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.instFinite
items.statement: instance Program.instFinite (n : ℕ) : (g : ℕ) → Finite (Program σ n g)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.card
items.doc: For each operation, choose one wire for each of its arguments.
items.statement:
theorem Line.card (n g : ℕ) :
    Nat.card (Line σ n g) = ∑ᶠ op : σ.Op, (n + g) ^ σ.Arity op

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.card_le
items.doc:
A uniform arity bound gives a uniform bound on the number of lines, including when
there are no available wires.
items.statement:
theorem Line.card_le (n g r : ℕ) (arity_le : ∀ op, σ.Arity op ≤ r) :
    Nat.card (Line σ n g) ≤ Nat.card σ.Op * (n + g + 1) ^ r

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.card_zero
items.doc: There is one empty program, regardless of the signature or number of inputs.
items.statement: theorem Program.card_zero (n : ℕ) : Nat.card (Program σ n 0) = 1

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.card_succ
items.doc: Choose a prefix program and then its last line.
items.statement:
theorem Program.card_succ (n g : ℕ) :
    Nat.card (Program σ n (g + 1)) =
      Nat.card (Program σ n g) * Nat.card (Line σ n g)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.card
items.doc: The line at each position may refer to the inputs and all preceding gates.
items.statement:
theorem Program.card (n g : ℕ) :
    Nat.card (Program σ n g) =
      ∏ j ∈ Finset.range g, ∑ᶠ op : σ.Op, (n + j) ^ σ.Arity op

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.FullOp.equiv
items.doc: A full-basis operation is either a `k`-ary function or a constant.
items.statement: def equiv (k : ℕ) (U : Type*) : FullOp k U ≃ (((Fin k → U) → U) ⊕ U)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.FullOp.card
items.doc: Full-basis operations consist of all function tables and all constants.
items.statement:
theorem card (k : ℕ) (U : Type*) [Finite U] :
Nat.card (FullOp k U) = Nat.card U ^ (Nat.card U ^ k) + Nat.card U

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.card_full
items.doc: A function table takes `k` wire arguments; a constant takes none.
items.statement:
theorem Line.card_full (k n g : ℕ) (U : Type*) [Finite U] :
    Nat.card (Line (fullSignature k U) n g) =
      Nat.card U ^ (Nat.card U ^ k) * (n + g) ^ k + Nat.card U

modules.title: Circuits over the full basis
modules.doc:
The full basis of arity `k` contains every constant and every operation with `k` arguments.
Each takes one gate, and so does every operation with at most `k` arguments: a nullary
operation is a constant, and other operations repeat their arguments to fill all `k`
positions. Applying such an operation to `r` functions synthesized with budgets `cost i`
therefore takes at most `∑ i, cost i + 1` gates. `Synthesis.full_binary` states the binary
case with two separate budgets. All constructions preserve previously available functions.

Consequently, the full basis of arity `k` simulates any interpretation whose operations have
arity at most `k`, replacing each operation by one gate. This includes nullary operations and
the case `k = 0`, and needs no assumption on the carrier.

On a finite carrier, every full basis of arity at least two is functionally complete. The idea
is disjunctive normal form: a function on a finite carrier is a finite table, so a circuit can
find the row that matches its input and return that row's value. For each row, binary gates
compare the input with the row one coordinate at a time, giving the row's value on a match and a
fixed default otherwise. Further binary gates merge these answers by keeping the one that differs
from the default. Over `Bool` with default `false`, this is exactly disjunctive normal form.
Larger arities follow by simulation.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_const
items.doc: A constant can be synthesized with one gate of the full basis.
items.statement:
theorem full_const (value : U) :
    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := k)) s {fun _ => value} 1

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_gate
items.doc:
Apply any operation with at most `k` arguments to available functions using one gate.
Nullary operations use a constant gate; other operations pad their arguments by repetition.
items.statement:
theorem full_gate {r : ℕ} (hr : r ≤ k) (op : (Fin r → U) → U)
    (args : Fin r → (Fin n → U) → U) (hargs : ∀ i, args i ∈ s) :
    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := k)) s {fun x => op (fun i => args i x)} 1

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_gate_of_syntheses
items.doc:
Construct the arguments of an operation of arity at most `k`, then apply it with one
further gate. All functions computed while constructing the arguments remain available.
items.statement:
theorem full_gate_of_syntheses {r : ℕ} (hr : r ≤ k) (op : (Fin r → U) → U)
    (args : Fin r → (Fin n → U) → U) (cost : Fin r → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := k)) s {args i} (cost i)) :
    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := k)) s {fun x => op (fun i => args i x)}
      ((∑ i, cost i) + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.full_binary
items.doc: Apply any binary operation to synthesized functions in the binary full basis.
items.statement:
theorem full_binary {f g : (Fin n → U) → U}
    (hf : Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s {f} a)
    (hg : Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s {g} b) (op : U → U → U) :
    Synthesis (fullInterpretation (k := 2)) s {fun x => op (f x) (g x)} (a + b + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.fullInterpretation_simulatesWithCost
items.doc: The full basis simulates operations of arity at most `k` with a budget of one gate each.
items.statement:
theorem fullInterpretation_simulatesWithCost {σ : Signature.{v}} (I : Interpretation σ U)
    (h : ∀ op, σ.Arity op ≤ k) :
    (fullInterpretation (k := k)).SimulatesWithCost I (fun _ => 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.fullInterpretation_simulates
items.doc: The full basis simulates any interpretation whose operations have arity at most `k`.
items.statement:
theorem fullInterpretation_simulates {σ : Signature.{v}} (I : Interpretation σ U)
    (h : ∀ op, σ.Arity op ≤ k) : (fullInterpretation (k := k)).Simulates I

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.fullInterpretation_isComplete
items.doc: Every full basis of arity at least two is complete on a finite carrier.
items.statement:
theorem fullInterpretation_isComplete [Finite U] (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    (fullInterpretation (k := k) (Carrier := U)).IsComplete

modules.title: Homomorphisms of interpretations
modules.doc:
A homomorphism between two interpretations of the same signature is a map of
carriers that commutes with every operation. This file defines identity and
composition and proves their laws.

The main use of homomorphisms in this library is that evaluation of lines,
programs, and circuits commutes with them (`Line.map_eval`, `Program.map_eval`,
`Program.map_trace`, and `Circuit.map_eval`).

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism
items.doc: A map that preserves every operation in a pair of interpretations.
items.statement:
structure Homomorphism (i₁ : Interpretation σ U₁) (i₂ : Interpretation σ U₂) where
  /-- The underlying map. -/
  map : U₁ → U₂
  /-- The map commutes with every operation in the signature. -/
  homomorphic :
    ∀ (op : σ.Op) (input : Fin (σ.Arity op) → U₁),
      map (i₁ op input) = i₂ op (map ∘ input)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.ext
Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.id
items.doc: The identity map is a homomorphism.
items.statement:
def id (interpretation : Interpretation σ U) :
    Homomorphism interpretation interpretation

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.comp
items.doc: Compose homomorphisms in the direction of their underlying maps.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.id_map
items.statement:
theorem id_map
(interpretation : Interpretation σ U) :
(Homomorphism.id interpretation).map = _root_.id

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.comp_map
Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.id_comp
Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.comp_id
Cslib.Circuits.Homomorphism.comp_assoc

modules.title: Semantic circuit normalization
modules.doc:
Merging gates that compute the same function preserves wire values and does not
increase circuit size.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.Irredundant
items.doc:
Distinct gates compute distinct scalar functions. Gates may still duplicate input
functions or be unused by the outputs.
items.statement: def Program.Irredundant (p : Program σ n g) (i : Interpretation σ U) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.Irredundant
items.doc: A circuit is irredundant when its internal gates compute pairwise distinct functions.
items.statement: def Circuit.Irredundant (c : Circuit σ n m) (i : Interpretation σ U) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.exists_irredundant
items.doc: A program can be rebuilt with distinct gate functions, preserving every wire's value.
items.statement:
theorem Program.exists_irredundant (p : Program σ n g) (i : Interpretation σ U) :
    ∃ k ≤ g, ∃ q : Program σ n k, ∃ ρ : Wire.Renaming n g k,
      (∀ x w, q.trace i x (ρ w) = p.trace i x w) ∧
        q.Irredundant i

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.exists_irredundant
items.doc: Every circuit has an equivalent circuit with distinct gate functions and no more gates.
items.statement:
theorem Circuit.exists_irredundant (c : Circuit σ n m) (i : Interpretation σ U) :
    ∃ d : Circuit σ n m, d.eval i = c.eval i ∧ d.Irredundant i ∧ d.size ≤ c.size

modules.title: Straight-line programs
modules.doc:
A program is a topologically ordered sequence of gates. Each `Line` records an
operation and its argument wires. The gate-count index ensures that wires refer
only to original inputs or earlier gates.

This file defines

* lines, their evaluation and depth, and `Line.mapWires` together with the
  transport lemmas `Line.eval_mapWires` and `Line.eval_mapRenaming`;
* programs, their evaluation `Program.eval`, the input-and-gate valuation
  `Program.trace`, gate depths, and the bounded-fan-in predicate
  `Program.FanInAtMost`;
* folds over program lines in execution order (`Program.foldl`) and reverse
  execution order (`Program.foldr`), with `Program.foldl_rel` and `Program.foldr_rel`
  for proving that the steps preserve a relation between accumulators;
* the scalar views `Program.gateFunction` and `Program.wireFunction`, and the
  widened line collection `Program.lines` with `Program.lines_eval`.

Evaluation of lines and programs commutes with homomorphisms
(`Line.map_eval`, `Program.map_eval`, `Program.map_trace`).

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line
items.doc: One gate together with the wires supplying its arguments.
items.statement:
structure Line (σ : Signature) (inputCount gateCount : Nat) where
  /-- The operation performed by the gate. -/
  op : σ.Op
  /-- The wire supplying each argument of the operation. -/
  wires : Fin (σ.Arity op) → Wire inputCount gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.equiv
items.doc: A line is an operation symbol together with a tuple of argument wires.
items.statement:
def Line.equiv (σ : Signature) (inputCount gateCount : Nat) :
    Line σ inputCount gateCount ≃ Σ op : σ.Op, Fin (σ.Arity op) → Wire inputCount gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.ext
items.statement:
protected theorem Line.ext {l₁ l₂ : Line σ inputCount gateCount} (hop : l₁.op = l₂.op)
    (hw : l₁.wires = hop ▸ l₂.wires) : l₁ = l₂

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.mapInputs
items.doc: Map the inputs of a line through a function, if it is connected to any.
items.statement:
def Line.mapInputs {inputCount' : ℕ} (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount')
    (l : Line σ inputCount gateCount) : Line σ inputCount' gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.mapInputs_id
items.statement:
theorem Line.mapInputs_id :
(Line.mapInputs id : Line σ inputCount gateCount → Line σ inputCount gateCount) = id

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.mapInputs_mapInputs
Cslib.Circuits.Line.mapWires
items.doc: Apply a function to every wire read by a line.
items.statement:
def Line.mapWires
    (line : Line σ sourceInputCount sourceGateCount)
    (wireMap : Wire sourceInputCount sourceGateCount → Wire targetInputCount targetGateCount) :
    Line σ targetInputCount targetGateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.mapWires_op
items.statement:
theorem Line.mapWires_op
(line : Line σ sourceInputCount sourceGateCount)
(wireMap : Wire sourceInputCount sourceGateCount → Wire targetInputCount targetGateCount) :
(line.mapWires wireMap).op = line.op

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.mapWires_wires
items.statement:
theorem Line.mapWires_wires
(line : Line σ sourceInputCount sourceGateCount)
(wireMap : Wire sourceInputCount sourceGateCount → Wire targetInputCount targetGateCount)
(argument : Fin (σ.Arity line.op)) :
(line.mapWires wireMap).wires argument = wireMap (line.wires argument)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program
items.doc: A topologically ordered straight-line program, indexed by its gate count.
items.statement:
inductive Program (σ : Signature.{v}) (inputCount : Nat) : Nat → Type v where
  | empty : Program σ inputCount 0
  | gate {gateCount : Nat} :
      Program σ inputCount gateCount → Line σ inputCount gateCount →
        Program σ inputCount (gateCount + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.emptyEquiv
items.doc: The empty program is the only program with no gates.
items.statement: def Program.emptyEquiv (σ : Signature) (inputCount : Nat) : Program σ inputCount 0 ≃ PUnit.{1}

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.gateEquiv
items.doc: A nonempty program is a prefix followed by its last gate.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.foldl
items.doc:
Fold the lines from the first gate to the last. The step accepts a line at any gate count,
retaining its original bound on references to previous gates.
items.statement:
def Program.foldl {gateCount : Nat} (p : Program σ inputCount gateCount)
    (f : ∀ {k : Nat}, α → Line σ inputCount k → α) (init : α) : α

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.foldl_empty
items.statement:
theorem Program.foldl_empty
(f : ∀ {k : Nat}, α → Line σ inputCount k → α) (init : α) :
(Program.empty : Program σ inputCount 0).foldl f init = init

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.foldl_gate
items.statement:
theorem Program.foldl_gate (p : Program σ inputCount gateCount)
(line : Line σ inputCount gateCount)
(f : ∀ {k : Nat}, α → Line σ inputCount k → α) (init : α) :
(p.gate line).foldl f init = f (p.foldl f init) line

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.foldl_rel
items.doc:
Two left folds preserve a relation if their initial accumulators are related and each
pair of steps preserves it. For example, use equality or an order relation.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.foldr
items.doc:
Fold the lines from the last gate to the first. Each line retains its original bound on
references to previous gates, and the step receives the line before the accumulator.
items.statement:
def Program.foldr {gateCount : Nat} (p : Program σ inputCount gateCount)
    (f : ∀ {k : Nat}, Line σ inputCount k → α → α) (init : α) : α

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.foldr_empty
items.statement:

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.eval_mapWires
items.doc:
Mapping a line's wires preserves evaluation when the new valuation agrees
with the old valuation along the map. The source and target input namespaces
may differ.
items.statement:
theorem Line.eval_mapWires
    (line : Line σ sourceInputCount sourceGateCount)
    (wireMap : Wire sourceInputCount sourceGateCount → Wire targetInputCount targetGateCount)
    (interpretation : Interpretation σ U)
    (oldInputs : Fin sourceInputCount → U)
    (newInputs : Fin targetInputCount → U)
    (oldGates : Fin sourceGateCount → U)
    (newGates : Fin targetGateCount → U)
    (preserves : ∀ wire,
      Wire.elim newInputs newGates (wireMap wire) = Wire.elim oldInputs oldGates wire) :
    (line.mapWires wireMap).eval interpretation newInputs newGates =
      line.eval interpretation oldInputs oldGates

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.eval_mapInputs
items.doc: Evaluating a line with relabeled inputs precomposes its input valuation.
items.statement:
theorem Line.eval_mapInputs {inputCount' : ℕ}
(line : Line σ inputCount gateCount) (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount')
(i : Interpretation σ U) (inputs : Fin inputCount' → U) (gates : Fin gateCount → U) :
(line.mapInputs f).eval i inputs gates = line.eval i (inputs ∘ f) gates

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Line.eval_mapRenaming
items.doc: Specialization of `Line.eval_mapWires` to an input-fixing wire renaming.
items.statement:
theorem Line.eval_mapRenaming
    (line : Line σ inputCount sourceGateCount)
    (ρ : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount)
    (interpretation : Interpretation σ U)
    (inputs : Fin inputCount → U)
    (oldGates : Fin sourceGateCount → U)
    (newGates : Fin targetGateCount → U)
    (preservesGates : ∀ gate, Wire.elim inputs newGates (ρ.gates gate) = oldGates gate) :
    (line.mapWires ρ).eval interpretation inputs newGates =
      line.eval interpretation inputs oldGates

modules.title: Relative circuit complexity
modules.doc:
The complexity `C(f | g)` of `f` relative to `g` is the least number of gates needed to compute
`f` when the values of `g` come for free: the circuit reads an input `x` followed by the values
`g x`. Such a circuit only ever sees inputs of this form, which make up the graph of `g`, so
computing `f` given `g` is computing `f` of the first part of the input, on the graph of `g`.
Relative complexity is defined as this complexity on a support, `C(f | g) = C^Γ(f ∘ π)` where
`Γ` is the graph of `g` and `π` forgets the values of `g`. The reading in terms of circuits on
`x` and `g x` is recovered by `ecomplexityGiven_le_iff`.

The rules of relative complexity follow from the calculus of support complexity. Knowing `g`
never makes `f` harder, and knowing more never makes it harder either.
Computing `g` and then `f` from it gives the chain rule `C(f) ≤ C(g) + C(f | g)`, and its
variant for computing `f` and `g` together. Relative complexity satisfies the triangle
inequality `C(f | h) ≤ C(g | h) + C(f | g)`, and every function is free given itself.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.graph
items.doc: The graph of `g`: every input followed by the values of `g` on it.
items.statement: def graph (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) : Set (Fin (n + k) → U)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.onFirstInputs
items.doc: Apply `f` to the first `n` inputs, ignoring the last `k` inputs.
items.statement: def onFirstInputs (k : ℕ) (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) : (Fin (n + k) → U) → Fin m → U

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven
items.doc:
The complexity `C(f | g)` of `f` relative to `g`: the least size of a single circuit satisfying
`c.eval I (Fin.append x (g x)) = f x` for every `x`, or `⊤` if there is none.
Each evaluation supplies only `x` and `g x`; values of `g` at other inputs are not provided.
`graph g` specifies the inputs on which the circuit must be correct, and `onFirstInputs k f`
specifies its required output on those inputs.
items.statement:
noncomputable def ecomplexityGiven (I : Interpretation σ U) (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) : ℕ∞

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.computesOn_graph_iff
items.doc:
A circuit computes `f` of the first `n` inputs on the graph of `g` exactly when, reading an
input followed by the values of `g` on it, it outputs the values of `f` on that input.
items.statement:
theorem Circuit.computesOn_graph_iff {f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U} {g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U}
    (c : Circuit σ (n + k) m) :
    c.ComputesOn I (graph g) (onFirstInputs k f) ↔
      ∀ x, c.eval I (Fin.append x (g x)) = f x

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven_le_of_eval
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityGiven_le_of_eval (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U)
    (c : Circuit σ (n + k) m) (hc : ∀ x, c.eval I (Fin.append x (g x)) = f x) :
    ecomplexityGiven I f g ≤ c.size

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven_le_iff
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityGiven_le_iff (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) :
    ecomplexityGiven I f g ≤ s ↔
      ∃ c : Circuit σ (n + k) m, (∀ x, c.eval I (Fin.append x (g x)) = f x) ∧ c.size ≤ s

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_append_self_le
items.doc: Computing the graph map `x ↦ (x, g x)` costs no more than computing `g`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_append_self_le (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) :
    ecomplexity I (fun x => Fin.append x (g x)) ≤ ecomplexity I g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven_self
items.doc: Every function is free given itself: `C(f | f) = 0`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityGiven_self (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) :
ecomplexityGiven I f f = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven_le_ecomplexity
items.doc: Knowing `g` never makes `f` harder: `C(f | g) ≤ C(f)`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityGiven_le_ecomplexity (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) : ecomplexityGiven I f g ≤ ecomplexity I f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_le_add_ecomplexityGiven
items.doc: The chain rule: computing `g` and then `f` from it gives `C(f) ≤ C(g) + C(f | g)`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_le_add_ecomplexityGiven (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) :
    ecomplexity I f ≤ ecomplexity I g + ecomplexityGiven I f g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexity_append_le_add_ecomplexityGiven
items.doc: Computing `f` and `g` together costs at most computing `f` and then `g` given `f`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexity_append_le_add_ecomplexityGiven (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) :
    ecomplexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x)) ≤ ecomplexity I f + ecomplexityGiven I g f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven_le_add
items.doc:
The triangle inequality: `C(f | h) ≤ C(g | h) + C(f | g)`. Given `h`, compute `g`, and then
`f` from `g`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityGiven_le_add (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U)
    (h : (Fin n → U) → Fin l → U) :
    ecomplexityGiven I f h ≤ ecomplexityGiven I g h + ecomplexityGiven I f g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven_append_le
items.doc: Knowing more never makes `f` harder: `C(f | g, g') ≤ C(f | g)`.
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityGiven_append_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U)
    (g' : (Fin n → U) → Fin l → U) :
    ecomplexityGiven I f (fun x => Fin.append (g x) (g' x)) ≤ ecomplexityGiven I f g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.ecomplexityGiven_ne_top
items.statement:
theorem ecomplexityGiven_ne_top [I.IsComplete] (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) : ecomplexityGiven I f g ≠ ⊤

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityGiven
items.doc:
The complexity `C(f | g)` of `f` relative to `g` over a complete basis, as a natural
number.
items.statement:
noncomputable def complexityGiven (I : Interpretation σ U) [I.IsComplete]
    (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.natCast_complexityGiven
items.statement:
theorem natCast_complexityGiven (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
(g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) : (complexityGiven I f g : ℕ∞) = ecomplexityGiven I f g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityGiven_self
items.statement:
theorem complexityGiven_self (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) :
complexityGiven I f f = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityGiven_le_complexity
items.statement:
theorem complexityGiven_le_complexity (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) : complexityGiven I f g ≤ complexity I f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_le_add_complexityGiven
items.statement:
theorem complexity_le_add_complexityGiven (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) :
    complexity I f ≤ complexity I g + complexityGiven I f g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexity_append_le_add_complexityGiven
items.statement:
theorem complexity_append_le_add_complexityGiven (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) :
    complexity I (fun x => Fin.append (f x) (g x)) ≤ complexity I f + complexityGiven I g f

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityGiven_le_add
items.statement:
theorem complexityGiven_le_add (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U) (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U)
    (h : (Fin n → U) → Fin l → U) :
    complexityGiven I f h ≤ complexityGiven I g h + complexityGiven I f g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.complexityGiven_append_le
items.statement:
theorem complexityGiven_append_le (f : (Fin n → U) → Fin m → U)
    (g : (Fin n → U) → Fin k → U) (g' : (Fin n → U) → Fin l → U) :
    complexityGiven I f (fun x => Fin.append (g x) (g' x)) ≤ complexityGiven I f g

modules.title: Shannon's lower bound for finite carriers and binary bases
modules.doc:
For any fixed finite signature with operation arities at most two, interpreted on a finite
carrier `U` with `q ≥ 2` elements, some function on `n` inputs requires more than `qⁿ/n` gates
for all sufficiently large `n`. The threshold may depend on the signature and carrier.
For the De Morgan basis on `Bool`, this matches Lupanov's upper bound asymptotically.

The logarithm of the counting bound is at most `s log s + O(s)` for `n + 1 ≤ s`.
At `s = ⌊qⁿ/n⌋`, this is smaller than the logarithm of the `q^(qⁿ)` functions.
This extends the Boolean counting argument in the references to finite carriers.

## References

* [Claude E. Shannon, *The Synthesis of Two-Terminal Switching Circuits*][Shannon1949]:
  Theorem 7, Section 3(e), pp. 77-79, the original counting argument for switching circuits.
* [Stasys Jukna, *Boolean Function Complexity: Advances and Frontiers*][Jukna2012]:
  Lemma 1.12 and Theorem 1.14, a modern treatment of Boolean circuit counting.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Shannon.exists_hard_function
items.doc:
For all sufficiently large `n`, some function on `n` inputs over `U` requires more than
`|U|ⁿ/n` gates over the fixed finite signature, whose operations have arity at most two.
items.statement:
theorem exists_hard_function [Finite σ.Op] [Finite U] [Nontrivial U]
    (I : Interpretation σ U) (arity_le : ∀ op, σ.Arity op ≤ 2) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ f : (Fin n → U) → U,
      ∀ c : Circuit σ n 1,
        c.Computes I (single f) → (Nat.card U : ℝ) ^ n / n < (c.size : ℝ)

modules.title: Signatures and interpretations
modules.doc:
A `Signature` specifies operation symbols with finite arities. The set of symbols
may be infinite, and their arities need not have a uniform bound.
An `Interpretation` assigns each symbol an operation on a carrier type.
Programs and circuits keep the signature separate from its interpretation.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Signature
items.doc: A collection of operation symbols, each with a fixed finite arity.
items.statement:
structure Signature where
  /-- The operation symbols of the signature. -/
  Op : Type v
  /-- The number of arguments taken by each operation symbol. -/
  Arity : Op → Nat

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation
items.doc: An interpretation assigns an operation on `Carrier` to every symbol in `σ`.
items.statement: abbrev Interpretation (σ : Signature) (Carrier : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.FullOp
items.doc: An operation with labels for all constants and operations of arity k.
items.statement:
inductive FullOp (k : Nat) Carrier where
  | fn : ((Fin k -> Carrier) -> Carrier) -> FullOp k Carrier
  | con : Carrier → FullOp k Carrier

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.fullSignature
items.doc: The signature for FullOp.
items.statement: def fullSignature (k : Nat) (Carrier : Type v) : Signature

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.fullInterpretation
items.doc:
The natural interpretation for FullOp, where we evaluate each constant
and function to itself.
items.statement: def fullInterpretation : Interpretation (fullSignature k Carrier) Carrier

modules.title: Simulation between circuit bases with gate budgets
modules.doc:
`J.Simulates I` means that every operation of `I` can be computed by a circuit over `J`.
`J.SimulatesWithCost I cost` also bounds the number of gates used for each operation.
Replacing each gate of a program preserves all input and intermediate wire values, with
total gate count at most `Program.cost`. The interpretations share a carrier, but their
signatures and gate arities may differ. A budget may be zero when wiring suffices.

`Program.simulate` constructs the replacement program and wire map from supplied circuits.
`Program.simulateProgram` and `Program.simulateRenaming` name these two components.
`Program.trace_simulate` proves that this construction preserves every wire value.

Gate replacement yields equivalent circuits and preserves computation on any support.
Simulations compose, multiplying uniform gate budgets, and transfer functional completeness
from the simulated basis to the simulating basis.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.SimulatesWithCost
items.doc: A simulation with a gate budget for each primitive operation.
items.statement:
def Interpretation.SimulatesWithCost (J : Interpretation τ U) (I : Interpretation σ U)
    (cost : σ.Op → ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.Simulates
items.doc: `J` simulates `I` if it can compute every primitive operation of `I`, with some gate budget.
items.statement: def Interpretation.Simulates (J : Interpretation τ U) (I : Interpretation σ U) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.SimulatesWithCost.simulates
items.statement:
theorem Interpretation.SimulatesWithCost.simulates {cost : σ.Op → ℕ}
    (h : J.SimulatesWithCost I cost) : J.Simulates I

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.simulates_iff
items.statement:
theorem Interpretation.simulates_iff :
    J.Simulates I ↔ ∀ op : σ.Op, ∃ c : Circuit τ (σ.Arity op) 1,
      c.Computes J (single (I op))

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.cost
items.doc: Given a cost per operation, this is the sum of the costs along a straight-line program.
items.statement: def Program.cost {g : ℕ} (p : Program σ n g) (cost : σ.Op → ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.cost_empty
items.statement:
theorem Program.cost_empty (cost : σ.Op → ℕ) :
(Program.empty : Program σ n 0).cost cost = 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.cost_gate
items.statement:
theorem Program.cost_gate (p : Program σ n g) (line : Line σ n g)
(cost : σ.Op → ℕ) : (p.gate line).cost cost = p.cost cost + cost line.op

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.cost_const
items.statement:
theorem Program.cost_const (p : Program σ n g) (b : ℕ) :
p.cost (fun _ => b) = b * g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.cost_mono
items.statement:
theorem Program.cost_mono (p : Program σ n g) {cost cost' : σ.Op → ℕ}
    (h : ∀ op, cost op ≤ cost' op) : p.cost cost ≤ p.cost cost'

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.simulate
items.doc:
Replace each operation by its supplied circuit, returning the resulting program and
a map from the original wires to their replacements. The gate count is the sum of the
sizes of the replacement circuits.
items.statement:
def Program.simulate {g : ℕ} (p : Program σ n g)
    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (σ.Arity op) 1) :
    Program τ n (p.cost fun op => (impl op).size) ×
      Wire.Renaming n g (p.cost fun op => (impl op).size)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.simulateProgram
items.doc: The program obtained by replacing each operation by its supplied circuit.
items.statement:
abbrev Program.simulateProgram (p : Program σ n g)
    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (σ.Arity op) 1) :
    Program τ n (p.cost fun op => (impl op).size)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.simulateRenaming
items.doc: The map from original wires to their replacements in `Program.simulateProgram`.
items.statement:
abbrev Program.simulateRenaming (p : Program σ n g)
    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (σ.Arity op) 1) :
    Wire.Renaming n g (p.cost fun op => (impl op).size)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.trace_simulate
items.doc: Replacing each operation by a circuit computing it preserves every wire value.
items.statement:
theorem Program.trace_simulate (p : Program σ n g)
    (impl : ∀ op : σ.Op, Circuit τ (σ.Arity op) 1)
    (h : ∀ op, (impl op).Computes J (single (I op))) (x : Fin n → U) :
    (p.simulateProgram impl).trace J x ∘ p.simulateRenaming impl = p.trace I x

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.exists_simulationWithCost
items.doc:
Simulate a program over `σ` by a program over `τ`, with a bound on the number of gates.

Assume that each operation `op` under `I` is computed by a circuit under `J` using at most
`cost op` gates. Replacing the gates of `p : Program σ n g` by these circuits produces a
program `q : Program τ n k` with `k ≤ p.cost cost`.

The returned map `ρ : Wire.Renaming n g k` fixes the input wires and maps every gate wire of
`p` to a wire of `q` carrying the same value. For every input `x`, the equality
`q.trace J x ∘ ρ = p.trace I x` says that all input and intermediate values are preserved.
items.statement:
theorem Program.exists_simulationWithCost (p : Program σ n g) (cost : σ.Op → ℕ)
    (h : J.SimulatesWithCost I cost) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ q : Program τ n k, ∃ ρ : Wire.Renaming n g k,
      k ≤ p.cost cost ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → U, q.trace J x ∘ ρ = p.trace I x

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Program.exists_simulation
items.doc: Replace the gates of a program, preserving every input and intermediate value.
items.statement:
theorem Program.exists_simulation (p : Program σ n g) (h : J.Simulates I) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ q : Program τ n k, ∃ ρ : Wire.Renaming n g k,
      ∀ x : Fin n → U, q.trace J x ∘ ρ = p.trace I x

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.exists_simulationWithCost
items.doc: The total replacement cost bounds the size of an equivalent circuit.
items.statement:
theorem Circuit.exists_simulationWithCost (c : Circuit σ n m) (cost : σ.Op → ℕ)
    (h : J.SimulatesWithCost I cost) :
    ∃ d : Circuit τ n m, d.eval J = c.eval I ∧ d.size ≤ c.program.cost cost

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.exists_simulation_le
items.doc: A uniform per-gate simulation budget gives a multiplicative circuit-size bound.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.SimulatesWithCost.refl
items.doc: Every basis simulates itself with a one-gate budget for each operation.
items.statement:
theorem Interpretation.SimulatesWithCost.refl (I : Interpretation σ U) :
    I.SimulatesWithCost I (fun _ => 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.SimulatesWithCost.trans
items.doc: Uniform simulation budgets multiply under composition.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.exists_simulation
items.doc: Gate replacement gives an equivalent circuit over the simulating basis.
items.statement:
theorem Circuit.exists_simulation (c : Circuit σ n m) (h : J.Simulates I) :
    ∃ d : Circuit τ n m, d.eval J = c.eval I

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.ComputesOn.simulation
items.doc: Simulation preserves computation on any support.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Circuit.Computes.simulation
items.doc: Simulation preserves computation on all inputs.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.Simulates.refl
items.doc: Every basis simulates itself.
items.statement: theorem Interpretation.Simulates.refl (I : Interpretation σ U) : I.Simulates I

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.Simulates.trans
items.doc: Compose simulations by replacing the gates of each implementing circuit.
items.statement:
theorem Interpretation.Simulates.trans (hK : K.Simulates J) (hJ : J.Simulates I) :
    K.Simulates I

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.Simulates.isComplete
items.doc: A basis that simulates a complete basis is itself complete.
items.statement:
theorem Interpretation.Simulates.isComplete (h : J.Simulates I) [I.IsComplete] :
    J.IsComplete

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Interpretation.IsComplete.simulates
items.doc: A complete basis simulates every interpretation on the same carrier.
items.statement:
theorem Interpretation.IsComplete.simulates [J.IsComplete] (I : Interpretation σ U) :
    J.Simulates I

modules.title: Simultaneous circuit synthesis
modules.doc:
`Synthesis I sources targets cost` bounds the number of additional gates needed to compute
`targets` from `sources` under an interpretation `I`. Every function already available in the
starting program remains available, so successive constructions can share intermediate results.
The signature and its carrier are arbitrary; neither needs to be finite or decidable.

The core rules compose bounds, combine finite families, and apply operations of the signature,
either to functions that are already available or to functions synthesized in turn. Composition
keeps everything built along the way available to later steps. The fold rules accept a bound
for combining two arguments, which may itself use several gates.
`Synthesis.exists_circuit_outputs` selects any tuple of outputs without adding gates;
`Synthesis.exists_circuit` specializes this to a single output.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.inputs
items.doc: The coordinate projections supplied by the circuit's inputs.
items.statement: def inputs (n : ℕ) : Set ((Fin n → U) → U)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.available
items.doc:
The functions computed by the wires of `p`, whether input wires or internal
gates.
items.statement: def available (I : Interpretation σ U) {g : ℕ} (p : Program σ n g) : Set ((Fin n → U) → U)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.mem_available
items.doc: A function is available exactly when some wire computes it pointwise.
items.statement:
theorem mem_available {g : ℕ} {p : Program σ n g} {f : (Fin n → U) → U} :
    f ∈ available I p ↔ ∃ w, ∀ x, p.trace I x w = f x

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.inputs_subset_available
items.doc: The input projections are available in every program.
items.statement:
theorem inputs_subset_available {g : ℕ} (p : Program σ n g) :
    inputs n ⊆ available I p

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis
items.doc:
`Synthesis I sources targets cost` says that `targets` can be computed from `sources`
using at most `cost` additional gates, without losing anything already computed.

Precisely: for every program `p₁` on whose wires every function in `sources` is available,
there is a program `p₂` such that
* `p₂` has at most `cost` more gates than `p₁`,
* every function available in `p₁` is still available in `p₂`, and
* every function in `targets` is available in `p₂`.

Quantifying over an arbitrary starting program, rather than the empty one, is what lets
constructions share intermediate results: `Synthesis.comp` adds budgets because the second
construction may reuse wires built by the first.
items.statement:
def Synthesis (I : Interpretation σ U) (sources targets : Set ((Fin n → U) → U))
    (cost : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.of_subset
items.doc: Available functions require no additional gates.
items.statement: theorem of_subset (h : t ⊆ s) : Synthesis I s t 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.of_mem
items.doc: An available function requires no additional gates.
items.statement: theorem of_mem (hf : f ∈ s) : Synthesis I s {f} 0

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.mono
items.doc: Enlarge the source family, narrow the target family, or increase the budget.
items.statement:
theorem mono (h : Synthesis I s t a) {s' t' : Set ((Fin n → U) → U)}
    (hs : s ⊆ s') (ht : t' ⊆ t) (hab : a ≤ b) : Synthesis I s' t' b

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.comp
items.doc:
Successive constructions add their gate budgets. The second construction may use the
targets of the first, and both target families remain available.
items.statement:
theorem comp (h : Synthesis I s t a) (h' : Synthesis I (s ∪ t) t₁ b) :
    Synthesis I s (t ∪ t₁) (a + b)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.trans
items.doc: Successive constructions, keeping only the final targets.
items.statement:
theorem trans (h : Synthesis I s t a) (h' : Synthesis I (s ∪ t) t₁ b) :
    Synthesis I s t₁ (a + b)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.union
items.doc: Combine two target families, preserving the first while constructing the second.
items.statement:
theorem union (h : Synthesis I s t a) (h' : Synthesis I s t₁ b) :
    Synthesis I s (t ∪ t₁) (a + b)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.gate
items.doc: Synthesize an operation whose arguments are already available.
items.statement:
theorem gate (op : σ.Op) (args : Fin (σ.Arity op) → (Fin n → U) → U)
    (hargs : ∀ i, args i ∈ s) :
    Synthesis I s {fun x => I op (fun i => args i x)} 1

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.biUnion
items.doc: Combine a finite family of target sets, retaining all earlier results.
items.statement:
theorem biUnion (indices : Finset ι) (targets : ι → Set ((Fin n → U) → U))
    (cost : ι → ℕ) (h : ∀ i ∈ indices, Synthesis I s (targets i) (cost i)) :
    Synthesis I s (⋃ i ∈ indices, targets i) (∑ i ∈ indices, cost i)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.iUnion
items.doc: Combine target sets indexed by a finite type.
items.statement:
theorem iUnion [Fintype ι] (targets : ι → Set ((Fin n → U) → U)) (cost : ι → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, Synthesis I s (targets i) (cost i)) :
    Synthesis I s (⋃ i, targets i) (∑ i, cost i)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.family
items.doc: Simultaneously synthesize an indexed finite family of functions.
items.statement:
theorem family [Fintype ι] (f : ι → (Fin n → U) → U) (cost : ι → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, Synthesis I s {f i} (cost i)) :
    Synthesis I s (Set.range f) (∑ i, cost i)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.gate_of_syntheses
items.doc: Synthesize every argument, then apply an operation with one further gate.
items.statement:
theorem gate_of_syntheses (op : σ.Op) (args : Fin (σ.Arity op) → (Fin n → U) → U)
    (cost : Fin (σ.Arity op) → ℕ) (h : ∀ i, Synthesis I s {args i} (cost i)) :
    Synthesis I s {fun x => I op (fun i => args i x)} ((∑ i, cost i) + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.nullary
items.doc: A nullary operation supplies its interpreted constant with one gate.
items.statement:
theorem nullary (op : σ.Op) (arity : σ.Arity op = 0) :
    Synthesis I s {fun _ => I op (fun i => Fin.elim0 (Fin.cast arity i))} 1

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.unary
items.doc:
Feed a synthesized function to every argument of an operation, using one further gate.
In particular, this applies a unary operation.
items.statement:
theorem unary (h : Synthesis I s {f} a) (op : σ.Op) :
    Synthesis I s {fun x => I op (fun _ => f x)} (a + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.binary
items.doc:
Feed `f` to argument zero and `g` to the remaining arguments, using one further gate.
For a binary operation, these are its two arguments.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.combine
items.doc:
Apply a synthesis bound to two previously synthesized arguments. The combining
construction can use several gates and can reuse either argument.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.foldr
items.doc:
Fold an ordered list of synthesized functions. No algebraic laws are needed for the
combining operation. The seed and the combining construction have their own gate budgets.
items.statement:
theorem foldr (op : U → U → U) (combineCost : ℕ)
    (hop : ∀ f g : (Fin n → U) → U,
      Synthesis I {f, g} {fun x => op (f x) (g x)} combineCost)
    (indices : List ι) {f : ι → (Fin n → U) → U} {cost : ι → ℕ}
    {seed : (Fin n → U) → U} (hseed : Synthesis I s {seed} a)
    (h : ∀ i ∈ indices, Synthesis I s {f i} (cost i)) :
    Synthesis I s {fun x => indices.foldr (fun i acc => op (f i x) acc) (seed x)}
      ((indices.map fun i => cost i + combineCost).sum + a)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.finset_fold
items.doc:
Fold a finite set of synthesized functions with a commutative associative operation.
The seed need not be an identity or a constant, and the combining construction may use
several gates.
items.statement:
theorem finset_fold (op : U → U → U) [Std.Commutative op] [Std.Associative op]
    (combineCost : ℕ) (hop : ∀ f g : (Fin n → U) → U,
      Synthesis I {f, g} {fun x => op (f x) (g x)} combineCost)
    (indices : Finset ι) {f : ι → (Fin n → U) → U} {cost : ι → ℕ}
    {seed : (Fin n → U) → U} (hseed : Synthesis I s {seed} a)
    (h : ∀ i ∈ indices, Synthesis I s {f i} (cost i)) :
    Synthesis I s {fun x => indices.fold op (seed x) (fun i => f i x)}
      ((∑ i ∈ indices, (cost i + combineCost)) + a)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.exists_circuit_outputs
items.doc:
Select a tuple of outputs from a synthesis bound. Selecting outputs, including repeated
outputs or none at all, requires no additional gates.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Synthesis.exists_circuit
items.doc: Extract a single-output circuit from a synthesis bound on the input projections.
items.statement:
theorem exists_circuit {cost : ℕ} (h : Synthesis I (inputs n) {f} cost) :
    ∃ c : Circuit σ n 1, c.Computes I (single f) ∧ c.size ≤ cost

modules.title: Circuit wires and renamings
modules.doc:
A `Wire inputCount gateCount` refers to an original input or an internal gate.
A valuation of wires is assembled with `Wire.elim` from values for the inputs and
values for the gates.

`Wire.Renaming` fixes the original inputs and maps each gate to an input or gate
in the target namespace. This file provides identity and composition, extension
by a gate, replacement of the last gate, and renaming by a permutation.

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire
items.doc: A wire is either an original input or the output of an earlier gate.
items.statement:
inductive Wire (inputCount gateCount : Nat) where
  /-- An original input. -/
  | input (input : Fin inputCount)
  /-- The output of an internal gate. -/
  | gate (gate : Fin gateCount)
  deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.elim
items.doc: Define a function on wires from its values on inputs and on gates.
items.statement:
protected def elim (inputs : Fin inputCount → α) (gates : Fin gateCount → α) :
    Wire inputCount gateCount → α

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.elim_input
items.statement:
theorem elim_input (inputs : Fin inputCount → α) (gates : Fin gateCount → α)
(i : Fin inputCount) : Wire.elim inputs gates (input i) = inputs i

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.elim_gate
items.statement:
theorem elim_gate (inputs : Fin inputCount → α) (gates : Fin gateCount → α)
(j : Fin gateCount) : Wire.elim inputs gates (gate j) = gates j

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.equiv
items.doc: A wire is an input or a gate.
items.statement:
def equiv (inputCount gateCount : Nat) :
    Wire inputCount gateCount ≃ Fin inputCount ⊕ Fin gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.card
items.statement: protected theorem card : Fintype.card (Wire inputCount gateCount) = inputCount + gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.mapInputs
items.doc: Map the input of a wire through a function, if it's connected to one.
items.statement:
def mapInputs {inputCount' : ℕ} (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount') :
    Wire inputCount gateCount → Wire inputCount' gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.mapInputs_input
items.statement:
theorem mapInputs_input {inputCount' : ℕ} (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount')
    (i : Fin inputCount) : (.input i : Wire inputCount gateCount).mapInputs f = .input (f i)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.mapInputs_gate
items.statement:
theorem mapInputs_gate {inputCount' : ℕ} (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount')
    (g : Fin gateCount) : (.gate g : Wire inputCount gateCount).mapInputs f = .gate g

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.mapInputs_id
items.statement:
theorem mapInputs_id :
(mapInputs id : Wire inputCount gateCount → Wire inputCount gateCount) = id

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.mapInputs_mapInputs
items.statement:
theorem mapInputs_mapInputs {inputCount' inputCount'' : ℕ} (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount')
    (g : Fin inputCount' → Fin inputCount'') (w : Wire inputCount gateCount) :
    (w.mapInputs f).mapInputs g = w.mapInputs (g ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.elim_mapInputs
items.doc: Evaluating a relabeled wire precomposes the input valuation with the relabeling.
items.statement:
theorem elim_mapInputs {inputCount' : ℕ} (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount')
(inputs : Fin inputCount' → α) (gates : Fin gateCount → α) (wire : Wire inputCount gateCount) :
Wire.elim inputs gates (wire.mapInputs f) = Wire.elim (inputs ∘ f) gates wire

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.elim_comp_mapInputs
items.doc: Function form of `elim_mapInputs`.
items.statement:
theorem elim_comp_mapInputs {inputCount' : ℕ} (f : Fin inputCount → Fin inputCount')
(inputs : Fin inputCount' → α) (gates : Fin gateCount → α) :
Wire.elim inputs gates ∘ Wire.mapInputs f = Wire.elim (inputs ∘ f) gates

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.castSucc
items.doc: Regard a wire as a wire in a namespace with one additional gate.
items.statement: def castSucc : Wire inputCount gateCount → Wire inputCount (gateCount + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.castSucc_input
items.statement:
theorem castSucc_input (i : Fin inputCount) :
(input i : Wire inputCount gateCount).castSucc = input i

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.castSucc_gate
items.statement:
theorem castSucc_gate (j : Fin gateCount) :
(gate j : Wire inputCount gateCount).castSucc = gate j.castSucc

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.castAdd
items.doc: Regard a wire as a wire of the same program continued by `extra` further gates.
items.statement: def castAdd (extra : Nat) : Wire inputCount gateCount → Wire inputCount (gateCount + extra)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.castAdd_input
items.statement:
theorem castAdd_input (extra : Nat) (i : Fin inputCount) :
(input i : Wire inputCount gateCount).castAdd extra = input i

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.castAdd_gate
items.statement:
theorem castAdd_gate (extra : Nat) (j : Fin gateCount) :
(gate j : Wire inputCount gateCount).castAdd extra = gate (j.castAdd extra)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.lastCases
items.doc:
A wire in a namespace with one additional gate is either the new last gate or an
earlier wire.
items.statement:
def lastCases {motive : Wire inputCount (gateCount + 1) → Sort*}
    (last : motive (gate (Fin.last gateCount)))
    (castSucc : ∀ wire : Wire inputCount gateCount, motive wire.castSucc) :
    ∀ wire, motive wire

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming
items.doc:
A renaming of gate wires that fixes every original input. Gate wires may be
sent to either inputs or gates in the target namespace.
items.statement:
structure Wire.Renaming (inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount : Nat) where
  /-- The target wire representing each source gate. -/
  gates : Fin sourceGateCount → Wire inputCount targetGateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.apply
items.doc: Apply an input-fixing wire renaming.
items.statement:
def apply (ρ : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount) :
    Wire inputCount sourceGateCount → Wire inputCount targetGateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.apply_input
items.statement:
theorem apply_input
(ρ : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount) (input : Fin inputCount) :
ρ (Wire.input input) = Wire.input input

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.apply_gate
items.statement:
theorem apply_gate
(ρ : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount) (gate : Fin sourceGateCount) :
ρ (Wire.gate gate) = ρ.gates gate

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.id
items.doc: The identity wire renaming.
items.statement: def id : Wire.Renaming inputCount gateCount gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.id_apply
items.statement:
theorem id_apply (wire : Wire inputCount gateCount) :
(id : Wire.Renaming inputCount gateCount gateCount) wire = wire

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.comp
items.doc: Compose input-fixing wire renamings.
items.statement:
def comp
    (outer : Wire.Renaming inputCount middleGateCount targetGateCount)
    (inner : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount middleGateCount) :
    Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.comp_apply
items.statement:
theorem comp_apply
(outer : Wire.Renaming inputCount middleGateCount targetGateCount)
(inner : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount middleGateCount)
(wire : Wire inputCount sourceGateCount) :
(outer.comp inner) wire = outer (inner wire)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.castSucc
items.doc: Include all wires into a namespace with one additional gate.
items.statement: def castSucc : Wire.Renaming inputCount gateCount (gateCount + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.castSucc_apply
items.statement:
theorem castSucc_apply (wire : Wire inputCount gateCount) :
(castSucc : Wire.Renaming inputCount gateCount (gateCount + 1)) wire = wire.castSucc

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.skipLast
items.doc: Extend a renaming while replacing the new last gate by an existing wire.
items.statement:
def skipLast
    (prior : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount)
    (replacement : Wire inputCount targetGateCount) :
    Wire.Renaming inputCount (sourceGateCount + 1) targetGateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.skipLast_gates_last
items.statement:
theorem skipLast_gates_last
(prior : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount)
(replacement : Wire inputCount targetGateCount) :
(prior.skipLast replacement).gates (Fin.last sourceGateCount) = replacement

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.skipLast_castSucc
items.statement:
theorem skipLast_castSucc
(prior : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount)
(replacement : Wire inputCount targetGateCount)
(wire : Wire inputCount sourceGateCount) :
prior.skipLast replacement wire.castSucc = prior wire

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.appendLast
items.doc: Extend a renaming and retain the new last gate as a fresh target gate.
items.statement:
def appendLast
    (prior : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount) :
    Wire.Renaming inputCount (sourceGateCount + 1) (targetGateCount + 1)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.appendLast_gates_last
items.statement:
theorem appendLast_gates_last
(prior : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount) :
prior.appendLast.gates (Fin.last sourceGateCount) = Wire.gate (Fin.last targetGateCount)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.appendLast_castSucc
items.statement:
theorem appendLast_castSucc
(prior : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount)
(wire : Wire inputCount sourceGateCount) :
prior.appendLast wire.castSucc = (prior wire).castSucc

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.ofPermutation
items.doc: Rename gate wires by a permutation.
items.statement:
def ofPermutation (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin gateCount)) :
    Wire.Renaming inputCount gateCount gateCount

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.ofPermutation_gate
items.statement:
theorem ofPermutation_gate
    (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin gateCount)) (gate : Fin gateCount) :
    (ofPermutation permutation : Wire.Renaming inputCount gateCount gateCount) (Wire.gate gate) =
      Wire.gate (permutation gate)

items.name: Cslib.Circuits.Wire.Renaming.value_apply
items.doc:
A source and target gate valuation agree along a renaming when they agree
