on the image of every source gate. Original inputs agree automatically.
items.statement:
theorem value_apply
    (ρ : Wire.Renaming inputCount sourceGateCount targetGateCount)
    (inputs : Fin inputCount → U)
    (oldGates : Fin sourceGateCount → U)
    (newGates : Fin targetGateCount → U)
    (preservesGates : ∀ gate, Wire.elim inputs newGates (ρ.gates gate) = oldGates gate)
    (wire : Wire inputCount sourceGateCount) :
    Wire.elim inputs newGates (ρ wire) = Wire.elim inputs oldGates wire

modules.title: Consistency hierarchy
modules.doc:
We prove a number of results about the various notions of consistency for replicated data types.
In paricular, we prove that:

  Linearizability → SequentialConsistency → CausalConsistency → BasicEventualConsistency

Our proofs follow closely the proofs of Lemma 5.1 and Proposition 5.1 of [Burckhardt2014].

## References

* [*Principles of Eventual Consistency*][Burckhardt2014]

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.isTrans_ar
items.statement: instance isTrans_ar : IsTrans Event a.ar

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.so_iff_se_rb
items.statement:
lemma so_iff_se_rb (s : Session) (x y : Event) :
    a.so s x y ↔ a.se x = s ∧ a.se y = s ∧ a.rb x y

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.so_le_rb
items.statement: lemma so_le_rb (s : Session) : a.so s ≤ a.rb

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.se_rval_eq_none
items.statement:
lemma se_rval_eq_none {s : Session} {x : Event} (h1 : a.se x = s) (h2 : a.rval x = none) :
    {y | a.se y = s} = {y | a.se y = s ∧ a.rb y x } ∪ {x}

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.singleOrder_vis_ar_rval_ne_none
items.statement:
lemma singleOrder_vis_ar_rval_ne_none (h : a.SingleOrder) (x y : Event) :
    (a.vis x y → a.ar x y) ∧ (a.ar x y → a.rval x ≠ none → a.vis x y)

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.singleOrder_realTime_imp_readMyWrites
items.statement:
lemma singleOrder_realTime_imp_readMyWrites
    (h1 : a.SingleOrder) (h2 : a.RealTime) : a.ReadMyWrites

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.linearizability_imp_sequentialConsistency
items.statement:
theorem linearizability_imp_sequentialConsistency
    (h : a.Linearizability d) : a.SequentialConsistency d

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.readMyWrites_imp_hb_le_trans_vis
items.statement:
lemma readMyWrites_imp_hb_le_trans_vis
    (h : a.ReadMyWrites) : a.hb ≤ TransGen a.vis

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.singleOrder_readMyWrites_imp_causalArbitration
items.statement:
lemma singleOrder_readMyWrites_imp_causalArbitration
    (h1 : a.SingleOrder) (h2 : a.ReadMyWrites) : a.CausalArbitration

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.causalVisibility_imp_readMyWrites
items.statement:
lemma causalVisibility_imp_readMyWrites
    (h : a.CausalVisibility) : a.ReadMyWrites

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.causalVisibility_imp_monotonicReads
items.statement:
lemma causalVisibility_imp_monotonicReads
    (h : a.CausalVisibility) : a.MonotonicReads

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.causalVisibility_imp_noCircularCausality
items.statement:
lemma causalVisibility_imp_noCircularCausality
    (h : a.CausalVisibility) : a.NoCircularCausality

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.singleOrder_readMyWrites_imp_causalVisibility
items.statement:
lemma singleOrder_readMyWrites_imp_causalVisibility
    (h1 : a.SingleOrder) (h2 : a.ReadMyWrites) : a.CausalVisibility

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.singleOrder_imp_eventualVisibility
items.statement:
lemma singleOrder_imp_eventualVisibility
    (h : a.SingleOrder) : a.EventualVisibility

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.sequentialConsistency_imp_causalConsistency
items.statement:
theorem sequentialConsistency_imp_causalConsistency
    (h : a.SequentialConsistency d) : a.CausalConsistency d

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.causalConsistency_imp_basicEventualConsistency
items.statement:
theorem causalConsistency_imp_basicEventualConsistency
    (h : a.CausalConsistency d) : a.BasicEventualConsistency d

modules.title: Consistency specifications
modules.doc:
We formalize several notions of consistency for replicated data types defined in [Burckhardt2014],
listed below in decreasing order of strength:
* Linearizability,
* Sequential consistency.
* Causal consistency,
* Basic eventual consistency,

We follow [Burckhardt2014] closely in the formalization except for one detail:
instead of using an equivalence relation "same-session" to model the notion of sessions,
we use a map `se : Event → Session` and regard two events `x` and `y` to belong to the
same session iff `se x = se y`.  These two approaches are clearly equivalent and `se` is
chosen because it is easier to work with.

NOTE: We left out the definition of quiescent consistency, for two reasons:
* Quiescent consistency is too weak a notion to be practically useful (see the remark
  on page 44 of [Burckhardt2014]).
* We found during the process of formalization that the only theoretic result about
  quiescent consistency in [Burckhardt2014], that it is implied by causal consistency,
  is incorrect given the definitions in [Burckhardt2014].

## References

* [*Principles of Eventual Consistency*][Burckhardt2014]

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.BaseHistory
items.doc: `BaseHistory` is an auxiliary definition containing all data fields of `History` below.
items.statement:
structure BaseHistory (Event Operation Value Session : Type*) where
  /-- `op` assigns each event its operation. -/
  op : Event → Operation
  /-- `se` assigns each event its session. -/
  se : Event → Session
  /-- `rval` assigns each event its return value, where `none` indicates that
  the event never returns. -/
  rval : Event → Option Value
  /-- `rb` is the "returns before" order on events. -/
  rb : Event → Event → Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.BaseHistory.so
items.doc: `so` (for "session order") is `rb` restricted to a single session.
items.statement: def BaseHistory.so (h : BaseHistory Event Operation Value Session) (s : Session)

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.History
items.doc: `History` extends `BaseHistory` with well-formedness conditions.
items.statement:
structure History (Event Operation Value Session : Type*)
    extends bh : BaseHistory Event Operation Value Session where
  /-- `rb` is a strict order on events (namely, it is irreflexive and transitive). -/
  rb_strict_order : IsStrictOrder Event rb
  /-- Each event has only a finite number of predecessors in the `rb` order. -/
  rb_pred_finite : ∀ x, (predecessors rb x).Finite
  /-- The `rb` order is an interval order. -/
  rb_interval_order : IsIntervalOrder rb
  /-- If an event `x` returns before another event `y`, then `x` cannot return `none`. -/
  rb_rval_ne_none : ∀ x y, rb x y → rval x ≠ none
  /-- The `so` order is a strict total order of the events of each session. -/
  so_strict_total_order : ∀ s, IsStrictTotalOrder {x | se x = s} (bh.so s)

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution
items.doc:
`AbstractExecution` extends `History` with two more orders and additional
well-formedness conditions.
items.statement:
structure AbstractExecution (Event Operation Value Session : Type*)
    extends History Event Operation Value Session where
  /-- `vis x y` means that `x` is visible to `y`. -/
  vis : Event → Event → Prop
  /-- `ar` is the arbitration order of the whole system. -/
  ar : Event → Event → Prop
  /-- The visibility order `vis` is acyclic. -/
  vis_acyclic : Acyclic vis
  /-- Each event has only a finite number of predecessors in the `vis` order. -/
  vis_pred_finite : ∀ x, (predecessors vis x).Finite
  /-- The arbitration order is a strict total order of all events. -/
  ar_strict_total_order : IsStrictTotalOrder Event ar

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.History.Satisfies
items.doc:
A history satisfies a predicte `p` on abstract executions iff it can be extended
to an abstract execution satisfying `p`.
items.statement:
def History.Satisfies (h : History Event Operation Value Session)
    (p : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.ReadMyWrites
items.doc:
`ReadMyWrites` says that if two events are ordered by `so`,
then they are also ordered by `vis`.
items.statement: def ReadMyWrites (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.MonotonicReads
items.doc:
`MonotonicReads` says that if `x` is visible to `y`, then `x` is also visible to all
successors of `y` under the `so` order.
items.statement: def MonotonicReads (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.ConsistentPrefix
items.doc:
`ConsistentPrefix` says that if `x` is visible to `y` in a different session,
then all predecessors of `x` in the arbitration order are also visible to `y`.
items.statement: def ConsistentPrefix (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.hb
items.doc:
The `happens before` order is transitive closure of the union of the `vis` order
and the `so s` orders for all sessions `s`.
items.statement: def hb (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Event → Event → Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.NoCircularCausality
items.doc: `NoCircularCausality` says that the `hb` order is acyclic.
items.statement: def NoCircularCausality (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.CausalArbitration
items.doc:
`CausalArbitration` says that if two events are ordered by `hb`,
then they are also ordered by `ar`.
items.statement: def CausalArbitration (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.CausalVisibility
items.doc:
`CausalVisibility` says that if two events are ordered by `hb`,
then they are also ordered by `vis`.
items.statement: def CausalVisibility (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.Causality
items.doc: `Causality` is the conjunction of `CausalArbitration` and `CausalVisibility`.
items.statement: def Causality (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.SingleOrder
items.doc:
`SingleOrder` says that `vis` and `ar` are the same order except that there may be
a set of events which never returns and are not visible.
items.statement: def SingleOrder (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.RealTime
items.doc: `RealTime` says that if two events are ordered by `rb`, then they are also ordered by `ar`.
items.statement: def RealTime (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.nonVisibleEvents
items.doc:
`a.nonVisibleEvents x s` is the set of events in session `s` which returns after `x`
but does not see `x`.
items.statement:
def nonVisibleEvents (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session)
    (x : Event) (s : Session) : Set Event

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.EventualVisibility
items.doc:
`EventualVisibility` says that for any event `x` and any session `s`, there can be at most
finitely many events in `s` that return after `x` and do not see `x`.
items.statement: def EventualVisibility (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.OperationContext
items.doc:
An `OperationContext` is the data used by a replicated data type to determine the
return value of an operation.  It is an abstraction of the notion of states.
items.statement:
structure OperationContext (Event Operation : Type*) where
  /-- The set of events in the operation context. -/
  events : Set Event
  /-- Operation labeling of events. -/
  op : Event → Operation
  /-- Visibility order. -/
  vis : Event → Event → Prop
  /-- Arbitration order. -/
  ar : Event → Event → Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.OperationContext.Equiv
items.doc:
The notion of equivalence on `OperationContext`, which is essentially an isomorphism
that ignores the identities of events and the behavior of `op`, `vis`, and `ar` outside
the set of events in the operation context.
items.statement:
structure OperationContext.Equiv (c1 c2 : OperationContext Event Operation) where
  /-- A bijection from `c1`'s events to `c2`'s events. -/
  equiv : { x // x ∈ c1.events } ≃ { x // x ∈ c2.events }
  /-- `op` is preserved by the bijection. -/
  op_equiv : ∀ x, c1.op x.val = c2.op (equiv x).val
  /-- `vis` is preserved by the bijection. -/
  vis_equiv : ∀ x y, c1.vis x.val y.val ↔ c2.vis (equiv x).val (equiv y).val
  /-- `ar` is preserved by the bijection. -/
  ar_equiv : ∀ x y, c1.ar x.val y.val ↔ c2.ar (equiv x).val (equiv y).val

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.ReplicatedDataType
items.doc: The notion of a replicated data type.
items.statement:
structure ReplicatedDataType (Event Operation Value : Type*) where
  /-- `rval` takes an operation and an operation context and returns a value. -/
  rval : Operation → OperationContext Event Operation → Option Value
  /-- For any operation, `rval` must returns the same value on equivalent operation contexts. -/
  rval_equiv : ∀ o c1 c2, ∀ _ : c1.Equiv c2, rval o c1 = rval o c2

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.context
items.doc: `a.context xs` is the operation context obtained by restricting `a` to `xs`.
items.statement:
def context (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session)
    (xs : Set Event) : OperationContext Event Operation

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.RVal
items.doc:
`a.RVal d` says that the return value of any event in the abstract execution `a` is
the same as the value returned by the replicated data type `d` in the context consisting of
the predecessors of the event.
items.statement:
def RVal (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session)
    (d : ReplicatedDataType Event Operation Value) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.Linearizability
items.doc: `Linearizability` is the conjunction of `SingleOrder`, `RealTime`, and `RVal`.
items.statement:
def Linearizability (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session)
    (d : ReplicatedDataType Event Operation Value) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.SequentialConsistency
items.doc: `SequentialConsistency` is the conjunction of `SingleOrder`, `ReadMyWrites`, and `RVal`.
items.statement:
def SequentialConsistency (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session)
    (d : ReplicatedDataType Event Operation Value) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.CausalConsistency
items.doc: `CausalConsistency` is the conjunction of `EventualVisibility`, `Causality`, and `RVal`.
items.statement:
def CausalConsistency (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session)
    (d : ReplicatedDataType Event Operation Value) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.DistributedConsistency.AbstractExecution.BasicEventualConsistency
items.doc:
`BasicEventualConsistency` is the conjunction of `EventualVisibility`, `NoCircularCausality`,
and `RVal`.
items.statement:
def BasicEventualConsistency (a : AbstractExecution Event Operation Value Session)
    (d : ReplicatedDataType Event Operation Value) : Prop

modules.title: Distributed algorithms for solving the consensus problem
modules.doc:
In the consensus problem, each process of a distributed algorithm is given a boolean value
at the beginning.  Then by exchanging messages asynchronously, they are supposed to agree on
one of the initial boolean values. This file contains a very general definition of such
a distributed algorithm.

Borrowing an idea from Leslie Lamport, we allow the LTS defined by such an algorithm to
"stutter" at any time, in the sense of taking a dummy step without changing the
global state of the distributed algorithm.  This idea enables us to focus on infinite
executions alone without loss of generality, because an algorithm that has run out of
useful steps to take can always take the stuttering step.  Pathological executions in which
the stuttering step is taken forever when there is useful work to be done are outlawed by
the fairness assumptions defined in `Consensus.lean`.

The types `P`, `M`, and `S` below are the types of processes (more precisely, process identifiers),
messages contents, and process states.  Eventually `P` will be assumed to be finite in the form of
`[Fintype P]`, but that assumption will be added only where necessary.  No assumption whatsoever
will be made about `M` and `S`.  In particular, they could be infinite.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Message
items.doc: The type of messages that processes send to each other.
items.statement:
structure Message (P M : Type*) where
  /-- The destination of a message. -/
  dest : P
  /-- The content of the message, where the `Bool` option is used to carry to the
      initial boolean value to each process. -/
  msg : Bool ⊕ M
deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ProcState
items.doc: The type of a process's local state.
items.statement:
structure ProcState (S : Type*) where
  /-- The internal state of a process. -/
  state : S
  /-- The state component used by a process to signal the boolean value it decides on. -/
  out : Option Bool

items.name: Cslib.FLP.State
items.doc: The global state of the distributed algorithm.
items.statement:
structure State (P M S : Type*) where
  /-- A multiset containing all messages that are in-flight (namely, they have been sent but
  not yet received). Note that being a multiset implies that the messages are not ordered. -/
  msgs : Multiset (Message P M)
  /-- A map giving the local states of all processes. -/
  proc : P → ProcState S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm
items.doc:
The specification of a distributed algorithm for solving the consensus problem.
Note that each field below can depend on a process's identifier (recall that each `Message`
contains its destination's identifier), so the algorithm is not required to be uniform
across processes.
items.statement:
structure Algorithm (P M S : Type*) where
  /-- A map specifying the initial state of each process. -/
  init : P → S
  /-- A map specifying how a process changes its internal state upon receiving a message. -/
  next : Message P M → ProcState S → S
  /-- A map specifying what messages a process sends out upon receiving a message. -/
  send : Message P M → ProcState S → Multiset (Message P M)
  /-- A map specifying the boolean decision a process makes upon receiving a message,
      where `none` means that no decision is made. -/
  out : Message P M → ProcState S → Option Bool

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Action
items.doc:
The type of labels of the LTS defined by an `Algorithm`, where `some m` denotes
the reception of message `m` and `none` denotes a stuttering step.
items.statement: abbrev Action (P M : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.DestIn
items.doc: `DestIn ps x` means that if `x ≠ none`, then `x = some m` with `m.dest ∈ ps`.
items.statement: def DestIn (ps : Set P) : Action P M → Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.start
items.doc:
Given `inp : P → Bool`, the initial state of the algorithm `a` contains a single message
carrying the boolean value `inp p` to each process `p`, where the initial internal state is
`a.init p` and no decision has been made.  The assumption `[Fintype P]` is made because
a multiset may contain only finitely many elements.
items.statement: def Algorithm.start [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) (inp : P → Bool) : State P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.recvMsg
items.doc:
The specification of how the global state of the algorithm changes when a process `p`
receives a message `m`.  (This function will be used only when such a message `m` exists.)
Note that once `p` has made a boolean decision in its `out` field, it is not allowed to
"change its mind" anymore.
items.statement: def Algorithm.recvMsg (a : Algorithm P M S) (m : Message P M) (s : State P M S) : State P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.lts
items.doc:
The transition relation of the LTS defined by the algorithm `a`.
Note that the stuttering step is always allowed.
items.statement: def Algorithm.lts (a : Algorithm P M S) : LTS (State P M S) (Action P M)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.Reachable
items.doc: `a.Reachable inp s` means that `s` is a reachable state of `a` given the initial `inp`.
items.statement:
def Algorithm.Reachable [Fintype P]
    (a : Algorithm P M S) (inp : P → Bool) (s : State P M S) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.State.ProcDecided
items.doc:
`s.ProcDecided p b` means that process `p` is decided on the boolean value `b`
in the state `s`.
items.statement: abbrev State.ProcDecided (s : State P M S) (p : P) (b : Bool) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.State.Decided
items.doc:
`s.Decided b` means that at least one process is decided on the boolean value `b`
in the state `s`.
items.statement: def State.Decided (s : State P M S) (b : Bool) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.State.Agreed
items.doc: `s.Agreed` says that all boolean values decided on in state `s` must agree with each other.
items.statement: def State.Agreed (s : State P M S) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.SafeConsensus
items.doc:
`a.SafeConsensus` says that in any reachable state of `a`, (1) all boolean values decided on
in that state must agree with each other and (2) that boolean value (if it exists) must be
one of the boolean values given by `inp` at the beginning.  `a.SafeConsensus` is the minimal
correctness requirement on `a` and is a safety property (hence its name).
items.statement: def Algorithm.SafeConsensus [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.tr_none
items.doc: The stuttering step does not change the global state.
items.statement: theorem tr_none {s s' : State P M S} (h : a.lts.Tr s none s') : s = s'

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.reachable_start
items.doc: The initial state is reachable.
items.statement:
theorem reachable_start [Fintype P] :
    a.Reachable inp (a.start inp)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.reachable_stable
items.doc:
If `s` is reachable from the initial state and `s'` is reachable from `s`,
then `s'` is reachable from the initial state.
items.statement:
theorem reachable_stable [Fintype P] {s s' : State P M S}
    (hr : a.Reachable inp s) (hc : a.lts.CanReach s s') : a.Reachable inp s'

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.procDecided_stable
items.doc:
If `p` is decided on the boolean value `b` in `s` and `s'` is reachable from `s`,
then `p` is still decided on `b` in `s'`.
items.statement:
theorem procDecided_stable {s s' : State P M S} {p : P} {b : Bool}
    (hd : s.ProcDecided p b) (hc : a.lts.CanReach s s') : s'.ProcDecided p b

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.decided_stable
items.doc:
If at least one process is decided on the boolean value `b` in `s` and `s'` is reachable
from `s`, then at least one process is still decided on `b` in `s'`.
items.statement:
theorem decided_stable {s s' : State P M S} {b : Bool}
    (hd : s.Decided b) (hc : a.lts.CanReach s s') : s'.Decided b

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.recvMsg_comm
items.doc:
If `m1` and `m2` are both inflight and they have different destinations,
then receiving them in either order produces the same end state.
items.statement:
theorem recvMsg_comm {m1 m2 : Message P M} {s : State P M S}
    (hd : m1.dest ≠ m2.dest) (h1 : m1 ∈ s.msgs) (h2 : m2 ∈ s.msgs) :
    m2 ∈ (a.recvMsg m1 s).msgs ∧ m1 ∈ (a.recvMsg m2 s).msgs ∧
    a.recvMsg m2 (a.recvMsg m1 s) = a.recvMsg m1 (a.recvMsg m2 s)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.tr_diamond
items.doc: A diamond property for the transition relation `a.lts.Tr`.
items.statement:
theorem tr_diamond {ps : Set P} {x1 x2 : Action P M} {s s1 s2 : State P M S}
    (hx1 : DestIn ps x1) (hs1 : a.lts.Tr s x1 s1)
    (hx2 : DestIn psᶜ x2) (hs2 : a.lts.Tr s x2 s2) :
    ∃ s', a.lts.Tr s1 x2 s' ∧ a.lts.Tr s2 x1 s'

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.mTr_notRcvd_enabled
items.doc:
A message that is in-flight stays in-flight as long as it is not received
(finite execution version).
items.statement:
theorem mTr_notRcvd_enabled {s t : State P M S} {xl : List (Action P M)} {m : Message P M}
    (hst : a.lts.MTr s xl t) (hs : m ∈ s.msgs) (hxl : ¬ some m ∈ xl) : m ∈ t.msgs

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.omega_notRcvd_enabled
items.doc:
A message that is in-flight stays in-flight as long as it is not received
(infinite execution version).
items.statement:
theorem omega_notRcvd_enabled
    {ss : ωSequence (State P M S)} {xs : ωSequence (Action P M)} {k : ℕ} {m : Message P M}
    (he : a.lts.OmegaExecution ss xs) (hm : m ∈ (ss k).msgs) (hn : ∀ j, k ≤ j → xs j ≠ some m) :
    ∀ j, k ≤ j → m ∈ (ss j).msgs

modules.title: Reachability via a subset of processes
modules.doc:
This file develops a theory of reachability via a subset of processes, that is, what happens
when only a subset of processes can receive messages and take steps.  It culminates with two
"diamond properties" of this more refined reachability relation.

## References

* [Volzer2004] H. Völzer, A constructive proof for FLP.
  Information Processing Letters 92(2), (October 2004) 83–87.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.CanReachVia
items.doc:
`a.CanReachVia ps s1 s2` means that state `s2` is reachable from state `s1` via a finite
execution of algorithm `a` in which all messages received have destinations in `ps`.
items.statement: def Algorithm.CanReachVia (a : Algorithm P M S) (ps : Set P) (s1 s2 : State P M S) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.CanReachVia.iff_exists_mTr
items.doc: Restricted reachability is witnessed by a finite trace whose destinations lie in `ps`.
items.statement:
theorem iff_exists_mTr {ps : Set P} {s s' : State P M S} :
    a.CanReachVia ps s s' ↔ ∃ xs, a.lts.MTr s xs s' ∧ xs.Forall (DestIn ps)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.CanReachVia.canReach
items.doc: `a.CanReachVia ps s s'` implies `a.lts.CanReach s s'` for any `ps`.
items.statement:
theorem canReach {ps : Set P} {s s' : State P M S}
    (h : a.CanReachVia ps s s') : a.lts.CanReach s s'

items.name: Cslib.FLP.CanReachVia.refl
items.doc: `a.CanReachVia ps s s` is true for any `ps`.
items.statement:
theorem refl (ps : Set P) (s : State P M S) :
    a.CanReachVia ps s s

items.name: Cslib.FLP.CanReachVia.stepL
items.doc: Extending `CanReachVia` on the left by one step.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.CanReachVia.diamond
items.doc: A diamond property for `CanReachVia`. This theorem formalizes Proposition 1 of [Volzer2004].

items.name: Cslib.FLP.CanReachVia.subset_inp
items.doc:
If inputs `inp1` and `inp2` agree on all processes in `ps` and state `s` is reachable from
the initial state determined by `inp1` by receiving messages with destinations in `ps` only,
then there exists a state `s2` that agrees with `s` on the states of all processes and is
reachable from the initial state determined by `inp2` by receiving messages with destinations
in `ps` only. This theorem is implicitly used in the proof of Lemma 1 of [Volzer2004].

modules.title: Fault-tolerant consensus
modules.doc:
Roughly speaking, a distributed consensus algorithm can tolerate `f` faults if up to `f`
processes can be "faulty" and yet the non-faulty processes can still reach a consensus.
The fault we consider here is limited to the crash fault, in which a process stops responding
to messages from some point onward.  We do not consider Byzantine faults.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ProcFaulty
items.doc:
A process `p` is faulty in an infinite execution iff there is a time `k` from which onward
there is a message in-flight to `p` but `p` has stopped receiving messages.
items.statement: def ProcFaulty (p : P) (ss : ωSequence (State P M S)) (xs : ωSequence (Action P M)) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ProcFair
items.doc:
A process `p` is fair in an infinite execution iff every message in-flight to `p` is
received by `p`.
items.statement: def ProcFair (p : P) (ss : ωSequence (State P M S)) (xs : ωSequence (Action P M)) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.not_procFaulty_and_procFair
items.doc:
A process `p` cannot be both faulty and fair in an infinite execution.  Note, however, that
it is possible for `p` to be neither faulty nor fair, because `p` can keep on receiving messages
but at the same time keep ignoring some messages sent to it.
items.statement:
theorem not_procFaulty_and_procFair (p : P)
    (ss : ωSequence (State P M S)) (xs : ωSequence (Action P M)) :
    ¬ (ProcFaulty p ss xs ∧ ProcFair p ss xs)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairRun
items.doc:
An infinite execution is fair iff every process is either faulty or fair
(cf. the comment for the theorem `not_procFaulty_and_procFair`).
items.statement: def FairRun (ss : ωSequence (State P M S)) (xs : ωSequence (Action P M)) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.numProcFaulty
items.doc: The number of faulty processes in an infinite execution.
items.statement: noncomputable def numProcFaulty (ss : ωSequence (State P M S)) (xs : ωSequence (Action P M)) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.FLP.not_procFaulty_of_numProcFaulty
items.doc:
If the number of faulty processes in an infinite execution is less than the total number
of processes, then at least one process is not faulty.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.numProcFaulty_le_not_procFair
items.doc:
If every process in a set `ps` is fair, then the number of faulty processes is bounded by
the total number of processes minus the cardinality of `ps`.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.AdmissibleRun
items.doc:
The notion of an infinite admissible execution for an algorithm `a` with input `inp`
and containing at most `f` faulty processes.
items.statement:
def Algorithm.AdmissibleRun [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) (inp : P → Bool) (f : ℕ)
    (ss : ωSequence (State P M S)) (xs : ωSequence (Action P M)) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ProcTermination
items.doc:
A process terminates in an infinite execution iff either it crashes or it decides on
a boolean value at some point.
items.statement: def ProcTermination (p : P) (ss : ωSequence (State P M S)) (xs : ωSequence (Action P M)) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.Termination
items.doc:
An algorithm `a` terminates with up to `f` faulty processes iff all its processes terminate
in every infinite admissible execution containing at most `f` faulty processes.
items.statement: def Algorithm.Termination [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) (f : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.Consensus
items.doc:
An algorithm `a` is a consensus algorithm tolerating up to `f` faulty processes iff
it both satisfies the consensus safety property `a.SafeConsensus` and terminates
with up to `f` faulty processes.
items.statement: def Algorithm.Consensus [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) (f : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.AdmissibleRun.fault_zero
items.doc: Specialize the definition of `Algorithm.AdmissibleRun` to the case of zero fault.
items.statement:
theorem AdmissibleRun.fault_zero [Fintype P]
    {xs : ωSequence (Action P M)} {ss : ωSequence (State P M S)} :
    a.AdmissibleRun inp 0 ss xs ↔
    ss 0 = a.start inp ∧ a.lts.OmegaExecution ss xs ∧ ∀ p, ProcFair p ss xs

items.name: Cslib.FLP.AdmissibleRun.fault_mono
items.doc:
If an infinite execution is admissible with up to `f` faulty processes,
then it is also admissible with up to `f' ≥ f` faulty processes.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Consensus.fault_mono
items.doc:
If `a` is a consensus algorithm tolerating up to `f` faulty processes,
then it is also a consensus algorithm tolerating up to `f' ≤ f` faulty processes.
items.statement:
theorem Consensus.fault_mono [Fintype P] {f f' : ℕ}
    (hle : f' ≤ f) (hc : a.Consensus f) : a.Consensus f'

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.not_fair_stay_enabled
items.doc:
If a process `p` is not fair in an infinite execution of an algorithm `a`, then there is
a message that is in-flight to, but never received, by `p` from some point onward.
items.statement:
theorem Algorithm.not_fair_stay_enabled
    {ss : ωSequence (State P M S)} {xs : ωSequence (Action P M)} {p : P}
    (he : a.lts.OmegaExecution ss xs) (hnf : ¬ ProcFair p ss xs) :
    ∃ m, m.dest = p ∧ ∃ k, m ∈ (ss k).msgs ∧ ∀ j, k ≤ j → m ∈ (ss j).msgs ∧ (xs j) ≠ some m

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.drop_procFair_iff
items.doc:
In an infinite execution of an algorithm `a`, a process `p` is fair iff `p` is fair in
all suffixes of the execution.
items.statement:
theorem Algorithm.drop_procFair_iff
    {ss : ωSequence (State P M S)} {xs : ωSequence (Action P M)}
    (he : a.lts.OmegaExecution ss xs) (p : P) (n : ℕ) :
    ProcFair p (ss.drop n) (xs.drop n) ↔ ProcFair p ss xs

modules.title: Machinery for constructing infinite fair executions
modules.doc:
The main goal of this file is to define a `fairScheduler` that, given a function `d`
of type `DeliverMsg`, a state predicate `q`, and a state `s0` of an algorithm `a`,
constructs an infinite execution of `a` starting from state `s0` in which all processes
from a set `ps` are fair and `q` is true infinitely often.  With additional assumptions,
we may also want to require that all actions in the infinite execution satisfy an action
predicate `r`.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.DeliverMsg
items.doc:
Given a state `s` and a message `m`, a function `d` of type `DeliverMsg` is supposed to
return `(xs, t)` where `xs` is a finite execution from `s` to `t` in which `m` is delivered.
items.statement: def DeliverMsg P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.DeliverMsg.ForallActions
items.doc: `d.ForallActions r` requires that all actions returned by `d` satisfy `r`.
items.statement: def DeliverMsg.ForallActions (d : DeliverMsg P M S) (r : Action P M → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.DeliverMsg.foldList
items.doc:
`d.foldList s ml ms` uses `d` to deliver all messages that are in `ml` but not in `ms` from
state `s`. Note that if a message `m` in `ml` is delivered during the delivery of an earlier
message, `m` is added to `ms` so that it is not processed again.
items.statement:
def DeliverMsg.foldList (d : DeliverMsg P M S) (s : State P M S) :
    List (Message P M) → Finset (Message P M) → List (Action P M) × State P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.DeliverMsg.scheduleMsgs
items.doc:
`d.scheduleMsgs ps s` schedules and delivers all messages which are in-flight in state `s`
and have destinations in `ps` in some order (as determined by choice).  If no such message exists,
then the the stuttering step is taken.
items.statement:
noncomputable def DeliverMsg.scheduleMsgs (d : DeliverMsg P M S) (ps : Set P)
    (s : State P M S) : List (Action P M) × State P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.DeliverMsg.foldList_forallActions
items.doc: If `d.ForallActions r`, then `d.foldList s ml ms` can only use actions satisfying `r`.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.fairScheduler
items.doc:
Starting from state `s0`, `a.fairScheduler d ps s0` constructs an infinite sequence of
finite executions of `a` by repeatedly applying `d.scheduleMsgs ps`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def Algorithm.fairScheduler (a : Algorithm P M S) (d : DeliverMsg P M S) (ps : Set P)
    (s0 : State P M S) : ℕ → List (Action P M) × State P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.fairSegEnds
items.doc:
The infinite sequence of states forming the end states of the finite executions constructed
by `Algorithm.fairScheduler`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def Algorithm.fairSegEnds (a : Algorithm P M S) (d : DeliverMsg P M S)
    (ps : Set P) (s0 : State P M S) : ωSequence (State P M S)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.fairSegActions
items.doc:
The infinite sequence of finite action sequences from the finite executions constructed
by `Algorithm.fairScheduler`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def Algorithm.fairSegActions (a : Algorithm P M S) (d : DeliverMsg P M S)
    (ps : Set P) (s0 : State P M S) : ωSequence (List (Action P M))

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.FairDeliverMsg
items.doc:
`a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q` says that for any state `s` of `a` satisfying `q` and
any message `m` which is in-flight in `s` and whose destination is in `ps`, `d s m`
produces a legal finite execution of `a` in which `m` is delivered and which ends in
a state satisfying `q` again.
items.statement:
def Algorithm.FairDeliverMsg (a : Algorithm P M S) (d : DeliverMsg P M S)
    (ps : Set P) (q : State P M S → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.fairScheduler_init
items.doc:
Re-stating the definition of `Algorithm.fairScheduler` as a mutual recursion of
`Algorithm.fairSegEnds` and `Algorithm.fairSegActions`.
items.statement:
theorem fairScheduler_init {d : DeliverMsg P M S} (ps : Set P) (s0 : State P M S) :
    a.fairSegEnds d ps s0 0 = s0

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.fairScheduler_step
items.doc:
Re-stating the definition of `Algorithm.fairScheduler` as a mutual recursion of
`Algorithm.fairSegEnds` and `Algorithm.fairSegActions`.
items.statement:
theorem fairScheduler_step {d : DeliverMsg P M S} (ps : Set P) (s0 : State P M S) (k : ℕ) :
    d.scheduleMsgs ps (a.fairSegEnds d ps s0 k) =
    (a.fairSegActions d ps s0 k, a.fairSegEnds d ps s0 (k + 1))

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.fairSeg_forallActions
items.doc: If `d.ForallActions r`, then `a.fairSegActions d ps s0` can only use actions satisfying `r`.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.fairDeliverMsg_foldList
items.doc: The correctness of `d.foldList s ml ms` under the assumption `a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q`.
items.statement:
theorem fairDeliverMsg_foldList {d : DeliverMsg P M S} {ps : Set P} {q : State P M S → Prop}
    (hd : a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q) (s : State P M S)
    (ml : List (Message P M)) (ms : Finset (Message P M))
    (hs : q s ∧ ∀ m, m ∈ ml → ¬ m ∈ ms → m ∈ s.msgs ∧ m.dest ∈ ps) :
    let (xl, t) := d.foldList s ml ms
    a.lts.MTr s xl t ∧ q t ∧ ∀ m, m ∈ ml → ¬ m ∈ ms → some m ∈ xl

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.fairDeliverMsg_scheduleMsgs
items.doc: The correctness of `d.scheduleMsgs ps s` under the assumption `a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q`.
items.statement:
theorem fairDeliverMsg_scheduleMsgs {d : DeliverMsg P M S} {ps : Set P} {q : State P M S → Prop}
    (hd : a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q) (s : State P M S) (hs : q s) :
    let xl := (d.scheduleMsgs ps s).fst
    let t := (d.scheduleMsgs ps s).snd
    q t ∧ a.lts.MTr s xl t ∧ 0 < xl.length ∧ ∀ m, m ∈ s.msgs → m.dest ∈ ps → some m ∈ xl

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.fair_fairSegs
items.doc:
The correctness of `a.fairSegEnds d ps s0` and `a.fairSegActions d ps s0`
under the assumption `a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q`.
items.statement:
theorem fair_fairSegs {d : DeliverMsg P M S} {ps : Set P} {q : State P M S → Prop}
    (hd : a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q) (s0 : State P M S) (hs0 : q s0) :
    let ts := a.fairSegEnds d ps s0
    let xls := a.fairSegActions d ps s0
    ∀ k, q (ts k) ∧ a.lts.MTr (ts k) (xls k) (ts (k + 1)) ∧ 0 < (xls k).length ∧
      ∀ m, m ∈ (ts k).msgs → m.dest ∈ ps → some m ∈ xls k

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.flatten_fairSegs
items.doc:
Given an infinite sequence of non-empty finite executions of algorithm `a`,
if all messages with destinations in `ps` that are in-flight at the beginning of each
finite execution are delivered in that finite execution, then those finite executions can
be concatenated into an infinite execution of `a` in which every process in `ps` is fair.
items.statement:
theorem flatten_fairSegs {ps : Set P}
    {ts : ωSequence (State P M S)} {xls : ωSequence (List (Action P M))}
    (hmtr : ∀ k, a.lts.MTr (ts k) (xls k) (ts (k + 1)))
    (hpos : ∀ k, 0 < (xls k).length)
    (hsch : ∀ k m, m ∈ (ts k).msgs → m.dest ∈ ps → some m ∈ xls k) :
    ∃ ss, a.lts.OmegaExecution ss xls.flatten ∧ (∀ k, ss (xls.cumLen k) = ts k) ∧
      ∀ p, p ∈ ps → ProcFair p ss xls.flatten

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.fair_omegaExecution
items.doc:
Under the assumption `a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q`, the infinite sequence of finite executions
of `a` represented by `a.fairSegEnds d ps s0` and `a.fairSegActions d ps s0` can be concatenated
into an infinite execution of `a` in which every process in `ps` is fair and `q` is true at
the ends of all those finite executions.
items.statement:
theorem fair_omegaExecution {d : DeliverMsg P M S} {ps : Set P} {q : State P M S → Prop}
    (hd : a.FairDeliverMsg d ps q) (s0 : State P M S) (hs0 : q s0) :
    let ts := a.fairSegEnds d ps s0
    let xls := a.fairSegActions d ps s0
    ∃ ss, a.lts.OmegaExecution ss xls.flatten ∧
      ss 0 = s0 ∧ (∀ k, ss (xls.cumLen k) = ts k) ∧
      (∀ k, q (ss (xls.cumLen k))) ∧ (∀ k, 0 < (xls k).length) ∧
      ∀ p, p ∈ ps → ProcFair p ss xls.flatten

items.name: Cslib.FLP.FairScheduler.omega_forall_actions
items.doc:
If `d.ForallActions r`, then the concatenation of all `a.fairSegActions d ps s0` segments
can only use actions satisfying `r`.

modules.title: Impossibility of asynchronous distributed consensus in the presence of a single fault
modules.doc:
This file formalizes the main theorem (Theorem 1) of [Volzer2004] and uses it to prove the
impossibility of asynchronous distributed consensus in the presence of a single fault.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.ReachableNonUniform
items.doc:
`a.ReachableNonUniform inp s` means that `s` is a reachable and non-uniform state of
algorithm `a` on input `inp`.
items.statement:
abbrev Algorithm.ReachableNonUniform [Fintype P]
    (a : Algorithm P M S) (inp : P → Bool) (s : State P M S) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.nonUniformInp
items.doc: Choose an arbitrary non-uniform input.
items.statement:
noncomputable def Algorithm.nonUniformInp [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S)
    (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (hc : 2 ≤ card P) : P → Bool

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_init
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1` and there are at least 2 processes, the input chosen by
`a.nonUniformInp` does indeed give rise to a non-uniform initial state.
items.statement:
theorem OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_init [Fintype P]
    (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (hc : 2 ≤ card P) :
    let inp := a.nonUniformInp hpc1 hc
    a.ReachableNonUniform inp (a.start inp)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_step_exists
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, starting from any reachable non-uniform state of `a` and
any message `m` that is in-flight in `s`, there exists a finite execution of `a` in which `m`
is received and which ends in another non-uniform state.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_step_aux
items.statement:
lemma OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_step_aux [Fintype P] (inp : P → Bool)
    (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (s : State P M S) (m : Message P M) :
    ∃ xl_t, m ∈ s.msgs ∧ a.ReachableNonUniform inp s →
      let (xl, t) := xl_t
      a.lts.MTr s xl t ∧ some m ∈ xl ∧ a.ReachableNonUniform inp t

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.nonUniformStep
items.doc:
Choose an arbitrary finite execution guaranteed to exist by the theorem
`OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_step_exists`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def Algorithm.nonUniformStep [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) (inp : P → Bool)
    (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) : DeliverMsg P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.fair_nonUniform_step
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, `a.nonUniformStep` does have the property guaranteed by
the theorem `OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_step_exists`.
items.statement:
theorem OnePseudoConsensus.fair_nonUniform_step [Fintype P] (inp : P → Bool)
    (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) :
    a.FairDeliverMsg (a.nonUniformStep inp hpc1) univ (a.ReachableNonUniform inp)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.fair_nonUniform
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, starting from any reachable non-uniform state `s0` of `a`,
use the fair scheduler developed in `FairScheduler.lean` to construct an infinite fair execution
in which there are infinitely many non-uniform states.
items.statement:
theorem OnePseudoConsensus.fair_nonUniform [Fintype P] (inp : P → Bool)
    (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (s0 : State P M S) (hs0 : a.ReachableNonUniform inp s0) :
    ∃ ss xs, a.lts.OmegaExecution ss xs ∧ ss 0 = s0 ∧ (∀ p, ProcFair p ss xs) ∧
      ∃ᶠ n in atTop, a.ReachableNonUniform inp (ss n)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.not_terminating
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1` and there are at least 2 processes, there must exist an
infinite admissible execution in which no process is faulty but no process terminates, either.
This theorem formalizes Theorem 1 of [Volzer2004].
items.statement:
theorem OnePseudoConsensus.not_terminating [Fintype P]
    (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (hc : 2 ≤ card P) :
    ∃ inp ss xs, a.AdmissibleRun inp 0 ss xs ∧ ∀ p, ¬ ProcTermination p ss xs

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Consensus.one_not_exists
items.doc:
As long as there are at least 2 processes, there does not exist a distributed consensus
algorithm that can tolerate 1 fault.
items.statement:
theorem Consensus.one_not_exists [Fintype P] (hc : 2 ≤ card P) :
    ¬ ∃ a : Algorithm P M S, a.Consensus 1

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Consensus.ge_one_not_exists
items.doc:
As long as there are at least 2 processes, there does not exist a distributed consensus
algorithm that can tolerate `f` faults for any `f ≥ 1`.
items.statement:
theorem Consensus.ge_one_not_exists [Fintype P] {f : ℕ} (hc : 2 ≤ card P) (hf : f ≥ 1) :
    ¬ ∃ a : Algorithm P M S, a.Consensus f

modules.title: 1-tolerant pseudo-consensus
modules.doc:
This file develops the theory of pseudo-consensus algorithms that can tolerate up to 1 fault.
It formalizes section 3 of [Volzer2004] except Theorem 1.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.CanDecideWithout
items.doc:
`a.CanDecideWithout s p b` means that the boolean value `b` is decided on in a state that
is reachable from `s` without the participation of `p`. In the notation of [Volzer2004], this
is equivalent to `b ∈ val(p,s)`.
items.statement:
def Algorithm.CanDecideWithout (a : Algorithm P M S)
    (s : State P M S) (p : P) (b : Bool) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.Uniform
items.doc:
`a.Uniform s b` means that for every process `p`, `a.CanDecideWithout s p b` but
not `a.CanDecideWithout s p !b`.
items.statement: def Algorithm.Uniform (a : Algorithm P M S) (s : State P M S) (b : Bool) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.NonUniform
items.doc:
`a.NonUniform s` means that for each boolean value `b`, there is a process `p`
such that `a.CanDecideWithout s p b`.
items.statement: def Algorithm.NonUniform (a : Algorithm P M S) (s : State P M S) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.pseudoTermination
items.doc: Draw a consequence of `a.PseudoConsensus 1`.
items.statement:
theorem pseudoTermination [Fintype P] (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1)
    {s : State P M S} (hr : a.Reachable inp s) (p : P) :
    ∃ s' b, a.CanReachVia {p}ᶜ s s' ∧ s'.Decided b

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.canDecideWithout_exists
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, for any reachable state of `a` and for any process `p`,
there is a boolean value `b` such that `a.CanDecideWithout s p b`. This theorem formalizes
Proposition 2(a) of [Volzer2004].
items.statement:
theorem canDecideWithout_exists [Fintype P] (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1)
    {s : State P M S} (hr : a.Reachable inp s) (p : P) :
    ∃ b, a.CanDecideWithout s p b

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.not_uniform_and_nonUniform
items.doc: A state cannot be both uniform and non-uniform.
items.statement:
theorem not_uniform_and_nonUniform {s : State P M S} (b : Bool) :
    ¬ (a.Uniform s b ∧ a.NonUniform s)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.uniform_or_nonUniform
items.doc: Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, any reachable state of `a` is either uniform or non-uniform.
items.statement:
theorem uniform_or_nonUniform [Fintype P] (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1)
    {s : State P M S} (hr : a.Reachable inp s) :
    a.Uniform s false ∨ a.Uniform s true ∨ a.NonUniform s

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.decided_eq_canDecideWithout
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, if a reachable state of `a` has decided on a boolean value `b`
and `a.CanDecideWithout s p b'` for any process `p`, then `b = b'`.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.decided_imp_uniform
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, if a reachable state of `a` has decided on a boolean value `b`,
then `s` is uniform for `b`. This theorem formalizes Proposition 2(b) of [Volzer2004].
items.statement:
theorem decided_imp_uniform [Fintype P] (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1)
    {s : State P M S} (hr : a.Reachable inp s) {b : Bool} (hd : s.Decided b) :
    a.Uniform s b

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.canDecideWithout_dest
items.doc:
For any message `m`, if state `s'` is reached from state `s` by receiving `m`, then
`a.CanDecideWithout s m.dest b` implies `a.CanDecideWithout s' m.dest b` for any `b`.
This theorem formalizes Proposition 3(b) of [Volzer2004].

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.canDecideWithout_nondest
items.doc:
For any message `m`, if state `s'` is reached from state `s` by receiving `m`, then
`a.CanDecideWithout s' p b` implies `a.CanDecideWithout s p b` for any `b` and any `p ≠ m.dest`.
This theorem formalizes Proposition 3(a) of [Volzer2004].

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.canDecideWithout_uniform
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, if any reachable state `s` of `a` is uniform for `b` and
state `s'` is reached from `s` by receiving a message `m`, then `a.CanDecideWithout s' p b`.
This theorem formalizes Proposition 3(c) of [Volzer2004].

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_step
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, if any reachable state `s` of `a` that is non-uniform,
then for any process `p`, there exists a state `s'` reachable from `s` such that
`a.CanDecideWithout s' p b` for all `b`. This theorem formalizes Lemma 2 of [Volzer2004].
items.statement:
theorem nonUniform_step [Fintype P] (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1)
    {s : State P M S} (hr : a.Reachable inp s) (hn : a.NonUniform s) (p : P) :
    ∃ s', a.lts.CanReach s s' ∧ ∀ b, a.CanDecideWithout s' p b

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.inpN
items.doc:
Given a numbering `pn` of processes and `n : ℕ`, `inpN pn n` assigns `true` to the processes
numbered `0, ..., (n - 1)` and `false` to the rest.
items.statement: def inpN (pn : P ≃ Fin (card P)) (n : ℕ) : P → Bool

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.inpN_eqOn_except_singleton
items.doc:
Assuming `0 < n ≤ card P`, the inputs `inpN pn (n - 1)` and `inpN pn n` agree on all processes
except the one that is numbered `(n - 1)`.
items.statement:
theorem inpN_eqOn_except_singleton (pn : P ≃ Fin (card P))
    {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 0 < n) (hnc : n ≤ card P) :
    EqOn (inpN pn (n - 1)) (inpN pn n) {pn.symm ⟨n - 1, by grind⟩}ᶜ

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.inpN_zero_no_true
items.statement:
lemma inpN_zero_no_true (pn : P ≃ Fin (card P)) (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (p : P) :
    ¬ a.CanDecideWithout (a.start (inpN pn 0)) p true

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.inpN_zero_uniform
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, the initial state determined by the all-`false` input
is uniform for `false`.
items.statement:
theorem inpN_zero_uniform (pn : P ≃ Fin (card P)) (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) :
    a.Uniform (a.start (inpN pn 0)) false

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.inpN_card_not_false
items.statement:
lemma inpN_card_not_false (pn : P ≃ Fin (card P)) (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (p : P) :
    ¬ a.CanDecideWithout (a.start (inpN pn (card P))) p false

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.inpN_card_uniform
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1`, the initial state determined by the all-`true` input
is uniform for `true`.
items.statement:
theorem inpN_card_uniform (pn : P ≃ Fin (card P)) (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) :
    a.Uniform (a.start (inpN pn (card P))) true

items.name: Cslib.FLP.OnePseudoConsensus.nonUniform_inp
items.doc:
Assuming `a.PseudoConsensus 1` and there are at least 2 processes, there must exist an input
that gives rise to a non-uniform initial state. This theorem formalizes Lemma 1 of [Volzer2004].
items.statement:
theorem nonUniform_inp (hpc1 : a.PseudoConsensus 1) (hc : 2 ≤ card P) :
    ∃ inp : P → Bool, a.NonUniform (a.start inp)

modules.title: Fault-tolerant pseudo-consensus
modules.doc:
A central idea of [Volzer2004] is the notion of pseudo-consensus, which weakens the notion of
consensus by replacing the requirement of termination, which is stated in terms of infinite
executions, by that of pseudo-termination, which is stated in terms of finite executions.
This makes the notion of pseudo-consensus easier to work with than consensus.  This file
defines pseudo-consensus and proves that it is implied by consensus.  This result is intuitively
obvious and is stated without proof in [Volzer2004], but it turns out to require quite a bit
of formal machinery to prove.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.PseudoTermination
items.doc:
An algorithm `a` satisfies `f`-tolerant pseudo-termination iff for every reachable state `s`
of `a` and every `ps` of at least `card P - f` processes, there exists a state `s'` reachable from
`s` using only messages with destinations in `ps` which has decided on a boolean value.
In other words, from any reachable state of `a`, a decision can be made without the participation
of at most `f` processes.
items.statement: def Algorithm.PseudoTermination [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) (f : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.PseudoConsensus
items.doc:
An algorithm `a` is a pseudo-consensus algorithm tolerating up to `f` faults iff it satisfies
both the consensus safety property `a.SafeConsensus` and `f`-tolerant pseudo-termination.
items.statement: def Algorithm.PseudoConsensus [Fintype P] (a : Algorithm P M S) (f : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.Algorithm.simpleDeliver
items.doc: `a.simpleDeliver ps` delivers any message that is in-flight and has its destination in `ps`.
items.statement: noncomputable def Algorithm.simpleDeliver (a : Algorithm P M S) (ps : Set P) : DeliverMsg P M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.PseudoConsensus.simpleDeliver_fair
items.statement:
lemma simpleDeliver_fair (ps : Set P) :
    a.FairDeliverMsg (a.simpleDeliver ps) ps (fun _ ↦ True)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.PseudoConsensus.simpleDeliver_forallActions
items.statement:
lemma simpleDeliver_forallActions (ps : Set P) :
    (a.simpleDeliver ps).ForallActions (DestIn ps)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.PseudoConsensus.of_consensus
items.doc:
If an algorithm `a` is a consensus algorithm tolerating up to `f` faults, then `a` is also
a pseudo-consensus algorithm tolerating up to `f` faults.  The main difficulty in the proof of
this theorem is that we need to construct an infinite admissible execution starting from any
reachable state of `a` using any subset of non-faulty processes.  This is achieved using the
fair scheduler developed in `FairScheduler.lean`.
items.statement:
theorem of_consensus [Fintype P] (f : ℕ) (hf : f < card P)
    (hc : a.Consensus f) : a.PseudoConsensus f

modules.title: Asynchronous distributed consensus in the absence of faults
modules.doc:
This file presents an asynchronous distributed consensus algorithm and proves that it does achieve
consensus when there is no fault.  Assume that there are `n` processes numbered 0, 1, ..., `n - 1`.
The algorithm works as follows:
(1) Process 0 receives its input value and sends that value to all processes (including itself).
    All other processes ignore their inputs upon receiving them.
(2) Upon receiving the value sent by process 0 in the previous step, every process (including
    process 0) decides on that value.
Clearly, if there is no fault and all messages are eventually delivered, every process will
eventually decide on the same value, namely, the input value at process 0.

The contents of this file are not needed for proving the FLP impossibility result, but do show
that the notion of an `Algorithm` is not vacuous, in the sense that it allows a working
asynchronous consensus algorithm when there is no fault.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.M
items.doc:
The payload of a message is of type `Bool ⊕ Bool`, where `inl b` denotes an input value `b`
and `inr b` denotes a value `b` sent by process 0 to all processes (including itself).
items.statement: abbrev M

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.S
items.doc: The local state of a process is trivial.
items.statement: abbrev S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.alg
items.doc: `alg` is the asynchronous distributed consensus algorithm described above.
items.statement: def alg : Algorithm (Fin n) M S

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.Inv
items.doc: `Inv` is an invariant for `alg`.
items.statement: def Inv (inp : Fin n → Bool) (s : State (Fin n) M S) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.inv_start
items.doc: `Inv` is true at any initial state.
items.statement:
theorem inv_start (inp : Fin n → Bool) :
    Inv npos inp ((alg npos).start inp)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.inv_tr_left
items.doc: What happens when an `inl` message is received.
items.statement:
theorem inv_tr_left (inp : Fin n → Bool) {s t : State (Fin n) M S} {m : Message (Fin n) M}
    (hs : Inv npos inp s) (htr : (alg npos).lts.Tr s (some m) t) (hm : m.msg.isLeft) :
    t.msgs = s.msgs.erase m +
      ( if m.dest = ⟨0, npos⟩ then Multiset.map (fun p ↦ ⟨p, inr (inp ⟨0, npos⟩)⟩) Finset.univ.val
        else 0 ) ∧
    ∀ p, (t.proc p).out = (s.proc p).out

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.inv_tr_right
items.doc: What happens when an `inr` message is received.
items.statement:
theorem inv_tr_right (inp : Fin n → Bool) {s t : State (Fin n) M S} {m : Message (Fin n) M}
    (hs : Inv npos inp s) (htr : (alg npos).lts.Tr s (some m) t) (hm : m.msg.isRight) :
    t.msgs = s.msgs.erase m ∧ (t.proc m.dest).out = some (inp ⟨0, npos⟩) ∧
    ∀ p, p ≠ m.dest → (t.proc p).out = (s.proc p).out

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.trInv_inv
items.doc: The truth of `Inv` is preserved by every transition of `alg`.
items.statement: theorem trInv_inv (inp : Fin n → Bool) : (alg npos).lts.TrInv (Inv npos inp)

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.reachable_inv
items.doc: `Inv` is true in all reachable state of `alg`.
items.statement:
theorem reachable_inv (inp : Fin n → Bool) {s : State (Fin n) M S}
    (hr : (alg npos).Reachable inp s) : Inv npos inp s

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.safeConsensus
items.doc: `alg` satisfies the `SafeConsensus` property.
items.statement: theorem safeConsensus : (alg npos).SafeConsensus

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.always_inv
items.doc: `Inv` is true at every state in an admissible run of `alg`.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.init_left
items.doc: The message carrying the input value for process 0 is enabled in the initial state.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.left_leadsTo_right
items.doc:
Whenever the message carrying the input value for process 0 is enabled in a state,
a message carrying that value is eventually sent to every process `p` by process 0.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.right_leadsTo_out
items.doc:
Whenever a message carrying a value sent by process 0 is enabled at a process `p`,
`p` eventually decides on that value.

items.name: Cslib.FLP.ZeroFaultAlg.consensus_zero
items.doc: `alg` is a correct asynchronous distributed consensus algorithm when there is no fault.
items.statement: theorem consensus_zero : (alg npos).Consensus 0

modules.title: Right Congruence
modules.doc:
This file contains basic definitions about left, right, and (two-sided) congruences
on finite sequences.

items.name: Language.RightCongruence
items.doc:
A right congruence is an equivalence relation on finite sequences (represented by lists)
that is preserved by concatenation on the right.  The equivalence relation is represented
by a setoid to to enable ready access to the quotient construction.
items.statement:
class RightCongruence (α : Type*) extends eq : Setoid (List α) where
  right_cov : CovariantClass _ _ (fun x y => y ++ x) eq

items.name: Language.RightCongruence.eqvCls
items.doc: The equivalence class (as a language) corresponding to an element of the quotient type.
items.statement: abbrev eqvCls [c : RightCongruence α] (a : Quotient c.eq) : Language α

items.name: Language.LeftCongruence
items.doc:
A left congruence is an equivalence relation on finite sequences (represented by lists)
that is preserved by concatenation on the left.  The equivalence relation is represented
by a setoid to to enable ready access to the quotient construction.
items.statement:
class LeftCongruence (α : Type*) extends eq : Setoid (List α) where
  left_cov : CovariantClass _ _ (fun x y => x ++ y) eq

items.name: Language.LeftCongruence.eqvCls
items.doc: The equivalence class (as a language) corresponding to an element of the quotient type.
items.statement: abbrev eqvCls [c : LeftCongruence α] (a : Quotient c.eq) : Language α

items.name: Language.Congruence
items.doc:
A (two-sided) congruence is an equivalence relation on finite sequences (represented by lists)
that is both a left-congruence and a right-congruence.
items.statement: class Congruence (α : Type*) extends LeftCongruence α, RightCongruence α where

items.name: Language.Congruence.eqvCls
items.doc: The equivalence class (as a language) corresponding to an element of the quotient type.
items.statement: abbrev eqvCls [c : Congruence α] (a : Quotient c.eq) : Language α

modules.title: Buchi Congruence
modules.doc:
A special type of right congruences used by J.R. Büchi to prove the closure
of ω-regular languages under complementation.

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.BuchiCongruence
items.doc:
Given a Buchi automaton `na`, two finite words `u` and `v` are Buchi-congruent
according to `na` iff for every pair of states `s` and `t` of `na`, both of the
following two conditions hold:
(1) `u` can move `na` from `s` to `t` iff `v` can move `na` from `s` to `t`;
(2) `u` can move `na` from `s` to `t` via an accepting states iff `v` can move `na`
from `s` to `t` via an accepting states.
items.statement: def BuchiCongruence (na : Buchi State Symbol) : RightCongruence Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.BuchiCongrParam
items.doc:
`BuchiCongrParam` is a parameterization of the equivalence classes of `na.BuchiCongruence`
using the type `State → State → Prop × Prop`, which is finite if `State` is.
items.statement:
noncomputable def BuchiCongrParam (na : Buchi State Symbol)
    (f : State → State → Prop × Prop) : Quotient na.BuchiCongruence.eq

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.buchiCongrParam_surjective
items.doc: `BuchiCongrParam` is surjective.
items.statement: lemma buchiCongrParam_surjective : Surjective na.BuchiCongrParam

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.buchiCongruence_fin_index
items.doc: `na.BuchiCongruence` is of finite index if `na` has only finitely many states.
items.statement: theorem buchiCongruence_fin_index [Finite State] : Finite (Quotient na.BuchiCongruence.eq)

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.buchiCongruence_transfer
items.doc:
If `xl` and `yl` belong to the same equivalence class of `na.BuchiCongruence`
and `xl` can move `na` from state `s` to state `t`, then so can `yl` and, furthermore,
if `xl` makes `na` go through an accepting state of `na`, then so can `yl`.
items.statement:
lemma buchiCongruence_transfer
    {a : Quotient na.BuchiCongruence.eq} {xl yl : List Symbol} {s t : State}
    (hc : xl ∈ na.BuchiCongruence.eqvCls a) (hc' : yl ∈ na.BuchiCongruence.eqvCls a)
    (hp : xl ∈ na.pairLang s t) : ∃ sl, na.Execution s yl t sl ∧
      ( xl ∈ na.pairViaLang na.accept s t → ∃ r ∈ na.accept, r ∈ sl )

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.buchiFamily
items.doc:
`na.buchiFamily` is a family of ω-languages indexed by a pair of equivalence classes
of `na.BuchiCongruence` which will turn out to saturate the ω-language accepted by `na`
and cover all possible ω-sequences.
items.statement:
def buchiFamily [Inhabited Symbol] (na : Buchi State Symbol) :
    Quotient na.BuchiCongruence.eq × Quotient na.BuchiCongruence.eq → ωLanguage Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.mem_buchiFamily
items.statement:
theorem mem_buchiFamily [Inhabited Symbol]
    {xs : ωSequence Symbol} {a b : Quotient na.BuchiCongruence.eq} :
    xs ∈ na.buchiFamily (a, b) ↔ ∃ xl, ∃ xls : ωSequence (List Symbol),
      xl ∈ na.BuchiCongruence.eqvCls a ∧ (∀ k, xls k ∈ na.BuchiCongruence.eqvCls b - 1) ∧
      xl ++ω xls.flatten = xs

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.buchiFamily_cover
items.doc:
`na.buchiFamily` is a cover if `na` has only finitely many states.
This theorem uses the Ramsey theorem for infinite graphs and does not depend on any details
of `na.BuchiCongruence` other than that it is of finite index.
items.statement:
theorem buchiFamily_cover [Inhabited Symbol] [Finite State] :
    ⨆ i, na.buchiFamily i = ⊤

items.name: Cslib.Automata.NA.Buchi.buchiFamily_saturation
items.doc: `na.buchiFamily` saturates the ω-language accepted by `na`.
items.statement:
theorem buchiFamily_saturation [Inhabited Symbol] :
    Saturates (fun i ↦ (na.buchiFamily i).toSet) (language na).toSet

modules.title: Myhill congruence
modules.doc:
The Myhill congruence of a language `l` is a two-sided congruence that is finer than
the Nerode congruence of the same language `l` (which is a right congruence).  It will be
used to define the syntactic monoid of `l`.

## References

[Holcombe1982] Holcombe, W.M.L. (1982). Algebraic automata theory. Section 5.3

items.name: Language.MyhillCongruence
items.doc:
The Myhill congruence of a language `l` is the two-sided congruence on finite words
such that two words are related iff all their two-sided extensions are either both in `l`
or both not in `l`.
items.statement: def MyhillCongruence (l : Language α) : Congruence α

items.name: Language.MyhillQuotient
items.doc: The Myhill quotient of a language `l` is the quotient of its Myhill congruence.
items.statement: abbrev MyhillQuotient (l : Language α)

items.name: Language.nerodeMap
items.doc:
Given a language `l` and a finite word `x`, the Nerode map is a map from the Nerode quotient
to itself induced by the `x`-transition of the Nerode congruence deterministic automaton of `l`.
items.statement: def nerodeMap (l : Language α) (x : List α) : l.NerodeQuotient → l.NerodeQuotient

items.name: Language.nerodeMap_append
items.statement:
theorem nerodeMap_append (l : Language α) (x y : List α) :
    l.nerodeMap (x ++ y) = l.nerodeMap y ∘ l.nerodeMap x

items.name: Language.nerodeMap_accept
items.statement:
theorem nerodeMap_accept (l : Language α) (x : List α) :
    x ∈ l ↔ l.nerodeMap x l.NerodeCongruenceDA.start ∈ l.NerodeCongruenceDA.accept

items.name: Language.myhillCongruence_iff
items.doc: The Myhill congruence is in fact the congruence induced by the Nerode map.
items.statement:
theorem myhillCongruence_iff (l : Language α) (x y : List α) :
    l.MyhillCongruence.r x y ↔ l.nerodeMap x = l.nerodeMap y

items.name: Language.IsRegular.finite_myhillQuotient
items.doc: The Myhill quotient of a regular language is finite.
items.statement:
theorem IsRegular.finite_myhillQuotient {l : Language α}

items.name: Language.myhillCongruenceDA
items.doc: The deterministic automaton corresponding to the Myhill congruence of a language `l`.
items.statement: def myhillCongruenceDA (l : Language α) : DA.FinAcc (l.MyhillQuotient) α

items.name: Language.myhillCongruenceDA_language_eq
items.doc:
The deterministic automaton corresponding to the Myhill congruence of a language `l`
accepts the same language `l`.
items.statement:
theorem myhillCongruenceDA_language_eq (l : Language α) :
    language (l.myhillCongruenceDA) = l

items.name: Language.IsRegular.iff_finite_myhillQuotient
items.doc: A language is regular if and only if its Myhill quotient is finite.
items.statement:
theorem IsRegular.iff_finite_myhillQuotient (l : Language α) :
    l.IsRegular ↔ Finite (l.MyhillQuotient)
