the configuration the run ends in. An action can optionally output one symbol, which models the
write-only output tape.

The input head can move freely on the input, but any move attempt beyond one cell outside the input
results in no movement. Restricting the movement of the input head is not essential, but useful
because it allows us to easily bound the number of possible configurations of a space-bounded
machine. Most textbooks have this restriction.

This definition is adapted from the one in [Papadimitriou94], chapter 2.3 including
the sub-linear space modifications from chapter 2.5 with the following changes:

- We allow Turing machines to choose to not write on a tape. This is equivalent to
  writing the read symbol again but makes it easier to reason about the semantics.
- Our tapes are infinite in both directions instead of just to the right. This definition is
  equivalent (see [AroraBarak09], Claim 1.4). It saves us from having to add a "start marker" to
  the alphabet.
- We only have a single halting state. The different ways to halt (accepting, rejecting, etc) can
  be distinguished based on the output.
- The input-head restriction is enforced by `Action.apply`, rather than by restricting the
  transition relation. The two definitions are equivalent, but allowing all actions makes it
  easier to define a universal machine.

## Important Declarations

* `Cfg`: the configuration: the internal state, the tape contents and head positions, and the
    output tape
* `Action`: what a machine does in one step
* `Action.apply`: the effect of one action on a configuration
* `HeadSymbols`, `Cfg.headSymbols`: the symbols under the heads, which a transition reads
* `Cfg.Halted`, `Cfg.init`: halting, and the configuration a machine starts in

## References

* [C. Papadimitriou, *Computational Complexity*][Papadimitriou94]
* [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*][AroraBarak09]

items.name: Turing.Action
items.doc: What a machine does in one step.
items.statement:
structure Action (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*) where
  /-- The movement (attempt) of the input head. -/
  inputTape : SignType
  /-- Actions on the work tapes: optionally a symbol to write and the head movement. -/
  workTapes : Fin k → (Option (Option Symbol)) × SignType
  /-- An optional symbol to output. -/
  output : Option Symbol
  /-- The successor state or none to halt. -/
  state : Option State

items.name: Turing.Cfg
items.doc:
The configurations of a Turing machine is relative to the input of the machine and consist of:
- an `Option`al state (or none for the halting state),
- the position of the input head (shifted by one),
- the contents of the work tape,
- the positions of the work tape heads,
- the contents of the write-only output tape
items.statement:
structure Cfg (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*) (input : List Symbol) where
  /-- the state of the TM (or none for the halting state) -/
  state : Option State
  /-- the position of the input head, shifted by one -/
  inputPos : Fin (input.length + 2)
  /-- the work tapes -/
  workTapes : Fin k → ℤ → Option Symbol
  /-- the positions of the heads on the work tapes -/
  workTapePos : Fin k → ℤ
  /-- the contents of the write-only output tape -/
  output : List Symbol
deriving Inhabited

items.name: Turing.Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
items.doc:
Two configurations with no work tapes are equal when their state, input head and output
agree.
items.statement:
lemma Cfg.ext_zero_tapes {Symbol State : Type*} {input : List Symbol}
    {cfg₁ cfg₂ : Cfg 0 Symbol State input} (state : cfg₁.state = cfg₂.state)
    (inputPos : cfg₁.inputPos = cfg₂.inputPos) (output : cfg₁.output = cfg₂.output) :
    cfg₁ = cfg₂

items.name: Turing.moveInputPos
items.doc:
Attempt to move the input tape head.
The machine can only read one empty cell outside of the input,
any attempted movement beyond that results in no movement.

The addition is performed in `ℤ` before clamping. Performing it in `Fin (n + 2)` would wrap an
outward boundary move to the opposite end of the input.
items.statement: def moveInputPos {n : ℕ} (pos : Fin (n + 2)) (m : SignType) : Fin (n + 2)

items.name: Turing.moveInputPos_zero
items.statement:
lemma moveInputPos_zero {n : ℕ} (pos : Fin (n + 2)) :
    moveInputPos pos 0 = pos

items.name: Turing.moveInputPos_leftBoundary
items.statement:
lemma moveInputPos_leftBoundary {n : ℕ} :
    moveInputPos (0 : Fin (n + 2)) (-1) = 0

items.name: Turing.moveInputPos_rightBoundary
items.statement:
lemma moveInputPos_rightBoundary {n : ℕ} :
    moveInputPos (⟨n + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin (n + 2)) 1 = ⟨n + 1, by omega⟩

items.name: Turing.moveInputPos_neg_of_ne_left
items.doc: A left move away from the left input boundary decrements the native input position.
items.statement:
lemma moveInputPos_neg_of_ne_left {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 2)) (h : p ≠ 0) :
    moveInputPos p .neg = ⟨p.val - 1, by have := p.isLt; omega⟩

items.name: Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right
items.doc: A right move away from the right input boundary increments the native input position.
items.statement:
lemma moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 2)) (h : p.val ≠ n + 1) :
    moveInputPos p .pos = ⟨p.val + 1, by have := p.isLt; omega⟩

items.name: Turing.val_moveInputPos_eq
items.doc: The value of the input head after a move, as a clamped integer. `omega`-friendly.
items.statement:
lemma val_moveInputPos_eq {n : ℕ} (pos : Fin (n + 2)) (m : SignType) :
    ((moveInputPos pos m).val : ℤ) = min ((n : ℤ) + 1) (max 0 ((pos.val : ℤ) + (m.cast : ℤ)))

items.name: Turing.val_moveInputPos_le
items.doc: The input head moves by at most one position.
items.statement:
lemma val_moveInputPos_le {n : ℕ} (pos : Fin (n + 2)) (m : SignType) :
    (moveInputPos pos m).val ≤ pos.val + 1

items.name: Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol
items.doc: The symbol currently under the input tape head.
items.statement: def Cfg.inputSymbol (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Option Symbol

items.name: Turing.inputSymbol_eq_none_of_boundary
items.doc: At either boundary of the input, the head reads a blank.

items.name: Turing.inputSymbolInner
items.statement:
lemma inputSymbolInner {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (p : ℕ)
    (h₁ : cfg.inputPos.val = 1 + p)
    (h₂ : p < input.length) :
    cfg.inputSymbol = some input[p]

items.name: Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols
items.doc: The symbol read by work tape `i`.
items.statement: def Cfg.workTapeSymbols (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) : Option Symbol

items.name: Turing.HeadSymbols
items.doc: The symbols under the heads of a machine with `k` work tapes, which its transitions read.
items.statement:
structure HeadSymbols (k : ℕ) (Symbol : Type*) where
  /-- the symbol under the input head -/
  inputSymbol : Option Symbol
  /-- the symbols under the work-tape heads -/
  workTapeSymbols : Fin k → Option Symbol

items.name: Turing.Cfg.headSymbols
items.doc: The symbols under the heads of a configuration.
items.statement: def Cfg.headSymbols (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : HeadSymbols k Symbol

items.name: Turing.Cfg.Halted
items.doc: A configuration is halted when it has no state to continue from.
items.statement: abbrev Cfg.Halted (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Prop

items.name: Turing.Cfg.prependOutput
items.doc:
The same configuration with a word prepended to the output tape. A machine never reads its
output, so prepending to it preserves steps: cf. `Turing.MultiTapeNTM.prependOutputHom`.
items.statement:
def Cfg.prependOutput (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (pre : List Symbol) :
Cfg k Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.Cfg.withState
items.doc: The same configuration in a different control state, possibly of a different state type.
items.statement:
def Cfg.withState (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
{State' : Type*} (q : Option State') : Cfg k Symbol State' input

items.name: Turing.Cfg.mapState
items.doc:
Remap the (optional) state of a configuration through `φ`, leaving the input head, the work
tapes, the work-tape heads and the output alone. Control-flow combinators such as `seq` embed a
sub-machine's configurations into the combined machine by exactly such a state remap.
items.statement:
def Cfg.mapState {State' : Type*} (φ : Option State → Option State')
(c : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Cfg k Symbol State' input

items.name: Turing.Cfg.init
items.doc: The initial configuration for a starting state and an input string.
items.statement: def Cfg.init (q₀ : State) (input : List Symbol) : Cfg k Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.Action.apply
items.doc:
The effect of an action on a configuration: move the input head, write and move on the work tapes,
append the emitted symbol to the output tape, and go to the successor state. This is the part of a
step that does not depend on how the action was chosen.
items.statement:
def Action.apply (action : Action k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    Cfg k Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.workTapePos_apply_le
items.doc: A work tape head moves by at most one cell when an action is applied.
items.statement:
lemma workTapePos_apply_le (action : Action k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) :
    |(action.apply cfg).workTapePos i - cfg.workTapePos i| ≤ 1

modules.authors: Christian Reitwiessner, Samuel Schlesinger, Aviv Bar Natan
modules.title: Deterministic Multi-Tape Turing Machines
modules.doc:
A deterministic Turing machine is a nondeterministic machine whose transition relation has exactly
one action for every combination of state and symbols read. From the transition relation it derives
a transition function `tr` and a function `step` which maps each configuration to its unique
successor configuration (a halted configuration maps to itself).

The design choices for configurations and actions are documented in
`Cslib.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Configuration`.

## Important Declarations

We define a number of structures and concepts related to multi-tape Turing machine computation:

* `MultiTapeNTM.IsDeterministic`: the transition relation relates every state and tuple of read
    symbols to exactly one action
* `MultiTapeTM`: the TM itself
* `tr`, `ofTr`: the derived transition function and construction from a function
* `adapt`: the machine run through an adapter
* `combine`: two machines on the same tapes combined into one
* `step`, `runFrom`: the successor configuration and iteration of this function
* `MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.ofDeterministic`, `MultiTapeNTM.ComputationPath.ofDeterministic`:
    paths of a given length from an arbitrary or initial configuration
* `Computes`: the machine halts with the given output on an input
* `ComputesInTimeAndSpace`: the machine produces an output within the shared resource bounds
* `ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace`: function computation with the shared time and space bounds
* `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`: such a machine exists with binary alphabet and finitely many states.
* `ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength`: the specialization to bounds on encoded input length.
* `DecidableInTimeAndSpace`: a proof that a TM decides a language within a certain time
    and space bound.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.IsDeterministic
items.doc:
Every state and tuple of read symbols is related to exactly one action by `ntm`'s transition
relation.
items.statement: def MultiTapeNTM.IsDeterministic (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM
items.doc:
A multi-tape Turing machine with `k` work tapes over the alphabet of `Option Symbol` (where `none`
is the blank tape symbol). Note that it is not required that `Symbol` or `State` are finite
to keep the definition more general. The restriction will be introduced once we start talking about
computability by Turing machines in general.
items.statement:
structure MultiTapeTM (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*)
    extends MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State where
  /-- Every state and tuple of read symbols is related to exactly one action by the transition
  relation. -/
  deterministic : toMultiTapeNTM.IsDeterministic

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.tr
items.doc: The unique action related to the given state and read symbols by `Tr`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def tr (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (q : State) (input : Option Symbol)
    (work : Fin k → Option Symbol) : Action k Symbol State

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.tr_iff
items.doc: `Tr` relates a state and read symbols to an action exactly when `tr` returns that action.
items.statement:
lemma tr_iff {q : State} {input : Option Symbol} {work : Fin k → Option Symbol}
    {action : Action k Symbol State} : tm.Tr q input work action ↔ tm.tr q input work = action

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ofTr
items.doc: Construct a deterministic machine from an initial state and transition function.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.q₀_ofTr
items.doc: The initial state of `ofTr` is the supplied one.
items.statement:
lemma q₀_ofTr (q₀ : State)
    (tr : State → Option Symbol → (Fin k → Option Symbol) → Action k Symbol State) :
    (ofTr q₀ tr).q₀ = q₀

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.tr_ofTr
items.doc: Extracting the transition of `ofTr` recovers the supplied function.
items.statement:
lemma tr_ofTr (q₀ : State)
    (tr : State → Option Symbol → (Fin k → Option Symbol) → Action k Symbol State)
    (q : State) (input : Option Symbol) (work : Fin k → Option Symbol) :
    (ofTr q₀ tr).tr q input work = tr q input work

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.adaptedTr
items.doc:
The transitions of `tm` performed through `adapter`: it reads what `tm` reads through `adapter`
and performs the adaptation of the action of `tm`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def adaptedTr {k' : ℕ} {State' : Type*} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (adapter : MultiTapeNTM.Adapter k k' Symbol State State') (q : State) (inp : Option Symbol)
    (work : Fin k' → Option Symbol) : Action k' Symbol State'

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.adapt
items.doc:
`tm` run through `adapter`, a `MultiTapeNTM.Adapter`: the adapter computes what `tm` reads
from the symbols under the heads of the new machine, and gives the action of the new machine
performing each action of `tm`. In state `q`, `tm.adapt adapter` performs the adaptation of the
action of `tm` in `q` on what the adapter reads.
items.statement:
noncomputable def adapt {k' : ℕ} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (adapter : MultiTapeNTM.Adapter k k' Symbol State State) : MultiTapeTM k' Symbol State

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.follows_adapt
items.doc: `tm.adapt adapter` follows `tm`.
items.statement:
lemma follows_adapt {k' : ℕ} {adapter : MultiTapeNTM.Adapter k k' Symbol State State} :
    (tm.adapt adapter).Follows tm id adapter

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.combine
items.doc:
`tm₀` and `tm₁` combined into one machine on their shared tapes, which starts in `q₀`: in a
state `inl q` it performs the transition of `tm₀` in `q`, and in `inr q` that of `tm₁`. The maps
`next₀` and `next₁` say where the steps of each machine lead: within the same machine, to the other
machine, or to halting.
items.statement:
noncomputable def combine {State₀ State₁ : Type*} (tm₀ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State₀)
    (tm₁ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State₁) (next₀ : Option State₀ → Option (State₀ ⊕ State₁))
    (next₁ : Option State₁ → Option (State₀ ⊕ State₁)) (q₀ : State₀ ⊕ State₁) :
    MultiTapeTM k Symbol (State₀ ⊕ State₁)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.handOver
items.doc:
Where the steps of a first machine lead when it runs in its own states: halting hands over to
the second machine in its state `q₁`.
items.statement:
def handOver {State₀ State₁ : Type*} (q₁ : State₁) (state : Option State₀) :
    Option (State₀ ⊕ State₁)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.handOver_some
items.statement:
lemma handOver_some {State₀ State₁ : Type*} (q₁ : State₁) (q : State₀) :
handOver q₁ (some q) = some (.inl q)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.handOver_none
items.statement:
lemma handOver_none {State₀ State₁ : Type*} (q₁ : State₁) :
handOver (State₀ := State₀) q₁ none = some (.inr q₁)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.follows_combine_left
items.doc: In its states `inl q`, the combined machine follows `tm₀`, its steps leading along `next₀`.
items.statement: lemma follows_combine_left : (combine tm₀ tm₁ next₀ next₁ q₀).Follows tm₀ .inl (.mapState next₀)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.follows_combine_right
items.doc: In its states `inr q`, the combined machine follows `tm₁`, its steps leading along `next₁`.
items.statement: lemma follows_combine_right : (combine tm₀ tm₁ next₀ next₁ q₀).Follows tm₁ .inr (.mapState next₁)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.combineLeftHom
items.doc:
If `next₀` keeps the live states of `tm₀` in `tm₀`, the combined machine mirrors the running
steps of `tm₀`, its states relabeled along `next₀`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def combineLeftHom {input : List Symbol} (h : ∀ q, next₀ (some q) = some (.inl q)) :
    (tm₀.runningStepRel input).Hom ((combine tm₀ tm₁ next₀ next₁ q₀).stepRel input)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.combineRightHom
items.doc: If the steps of `tm₁` stay in `tm₁`, the combined machine mirrors them.
items.statement:
noncomputable def combineRightHom {input : List Symbol} :
    (tm₁.stepRel input).Hom ((combine tm₀ tm₁ next₀ (Option.map .inr) q₀).stepRel input)

items.note:
## Stepping a Turing Machine

The step function lets the machine transition from one configuration to the next, and `runFrom`
gives the configuration reached after a number of steps. Configurations themselves are defined in
`Cslib.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Configuration`.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.step
items.doc: The unique successor configuration related to `cfg` by the inherited step relation.
items.statement: noncomputable def step (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Cfg k Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_iff
items.doc: `Step` relates `c` to `c'` exactly when `step c = c'`.
items.statement: lemma step_iff {c c' : Cfg k Symbol State input} : tm.Step c c' ↔ tm.step c = c'

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_state
items.doc: A running configuration takes the action selected by the transition function.
items.statement:
lemma step_of_state {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {q : State} (h : cfg.state = some q) :
    tm.step cfg = (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).apply cfg

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_inputPos_of_state
items.doc: The input head after a live step.
items.statement:
public lemma step_inputPos_of_state {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {q : State}
    (h : cfg.state = some q) :
    (tm.step cfg).inputPos =
      moveInputPos cfg.inputPos (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).inputTape

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_workTapes_of_state
items.doc: A work tape after a live step.
items.statement:
public lemma step_workTapes_of_state {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {q : State}
    (h : cfg.state = some q) (i : Fin k) :
    (tm.step cfg).workTapes i =
      match (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).workTapes i |>.1 with
      | none => cfg.workTapes i
      | some s => Function.update (cfg.workTapes i) (cfg.workTapePos i) s

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_workTapePos_of_state
items.doc: A work tape head after a live step.
items.statement:
public lemma step_workTapePos_of_state {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {q : State}
    (h : cfg.state = some q) (i : Fin k) :
    (tm.step cfg).workTapePos i =
      cfg.workTapePos i + ((tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).workTapes i).2

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt
items.statement:
lemma step_of_halt {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.state = none) :
    tm.step cfg = cfg

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.ofDeterministic
items.doc: The path of the first `t` steps from `cfg`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def RunPath.ofDeterministic (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) : tm.RunPath input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.eq_ofDeterministic
items.doc: Every deterministic run path is the canonical path from its head for its duration.
items.statement:
lemma RunPath.eq_ofDeterministic (p : tm.RunPath input) :
    p = .ofDeterministic tm p.head p.time

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.ComputationPath.ofDeterministic
items.doc: The path of the first `t` steps on `input`, starting at the initial configuration.
items.statement:
noncomputable def ComputationPath.ofDeterministic (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (input : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) : tm.ComputationPath input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.ComputationPath.eq_ofDeterministic
items.doc: Every deterministic computation path is the canonical path for its duration.
items.statement:
lemma ComputationPath.eq_ofDeterministic (p : tm.ComputationPath input) :
    p = .ofDeterministic tm input p.time

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.eq_take
items.doc:
Deterministic run paths from the same configuration are prefixes of one another: the shorter one
is the longer one, cut at its length.
items.statement:
lemma RunPath.eq_take {p q : tm.RunPath input} (hhead : p.head = q.head) (h : p.length ≤ q.length) :
    p = q.take ⟨p.length, Nat.lt_succ_of_le h⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.ComputationPath.spaceUsedByTape_le_of_space_le
items.doc:
The computation paths of a deterministic machine are prefixes of one another, so a path visiting
at most as many cells as another visits at most as many on each tape.
items.statement:
lemma ComputationPath.spaceUsedByTape_le_of_space_le (p : tm.ComputationPath input)
    {q : tm.ComputationPath input} (h : p.space ≤ q.space) :
    p.spaceUsedByTape ≤ q.spaceUsedByTape

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.map_ofDeterministic
items.doc:
A step-preserving map sends the path of `t` steps from `cfg` to the path of `t` steps from the
image of `cfg`.
items.statement:
lemma RunPath.map_ofDeterministic {k' : ℕ} {State' : Type*} {input' : List Symbol}
    {tm' : MultiTapeTM k' Symbol State'} (f : (tm.stepRel input).Hom (tm'.stepRel input'))
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    (RunPath.ofDeterministic tm cfg t).map f = .ofDeterministic tm' (f cfg) t

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom
items.doc:
The configuration reached by running the Turing machine for `t` steps from `cfg`.
If the Turing machine halts, it will stay at the halting configuration.
items.statement: noncomputable def runFrom (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) : Cfg k Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runPath_apply_eq_runFrom
items.doc: Every path of a deterministic machine follows its iterated step function.
items.statement:
lemma runPath_apply_eq_runFrom (p : tm.RunPath input) (i : Fin (p.length + 1)) :
    p i = tm.runFrom p.head i

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.computationPath_last_eq_runFrom
items.doc: A deterministic computation ends at the corresponding iterate.
items.statement:
lemma computationPath_last_eq_runFrom (p : tm.ComputationPath input) :
    p.last = tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) p.time

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_map
items.doc:
Running from the image of a configuration under a step-preserving map reaches the image of the
original run.
items.statement:
lemma runFrom_map {k' : ℕ} {State' : Type*} {input' : List Symbol}
    {tm' : MultiTapeTM k' Symbol State'} (f : (tm.stepRel input).Hom (tm'.stepRel input'))
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    tm'.runFrom (f cfg) t = f (tm.runFrom cfg t)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_eq_of_halt
items.doc: Nothing changes after the machine has halted.
items.statement:
lemma runFrom_eq_of_halt
    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) {τ t : ℕ} (hle : τ ≤ t)
    (hhalt : (tm.runFrom cfg τ).state = none) :
    tm.runFrom cfg t = tm.runFrom cfg τ

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runsInTime_of_halted
items.doc: A deterministic machine halted after `t` steps satisfies the shared time bound.
items.statement:
lemma runsInTime_of_halted {input : List Symbol} {t : ℕ}
    (h : (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) t).Halted) : tm.RunsInTime input t

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inputPos_runFrom_le
items.doc: In `t` steps the input head moves at most `t` positions to the right.
items.statement:
lemma inputPos_runFrom_le (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    ((tm.runFrom cfg t).inputPos : ℕ) ≤ (cfg.inputPos : ℕ) + t

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.Computes
items.doc: The machine eventually halts on `input` with the given `output`.
items.statement: def Computes (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (input output : List Symbol) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesInTimeAndSpace
items.doc: The machine computes `output` from `input` within the shared time and space bounds.
items.statement:
def ComputesInTimeAndSpace (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (input output : List Symbol) (t s : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace
items.doc: The machine computes `f` relative to given encodings within the given time and space bounds.
items.statement:
def ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace {α β : Type*} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (encIn : α ↪ List Symbol) (encOut : β ↪ List Symbol) (f : α → β) (t s : α → ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace.mono
items.doc: Resource bounds can be weakened independently on every input.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInTimeAndSpace
items.doc:
Computability by a deterministic machine with a binary tape alphabet and finitely many states,
within the supplied input-indexed bounds.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength
items.doc:
There exists a binary Turing machine with finitely many states that, for every input `a`,
computes `encOut (f a)` from `encIn a` in at most `t (encIn a).length` steps,
using at most `s (encIn a).length` work-tape cells.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInTimeAndSpace.mono
items.doc: Computability is monotone in the resource bounds.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator
items.doc: The Boolean indicator function of a set.
items.statement: noncomputable def indicator {α : Type*} (L : Set α) : α → Bool

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.DecidableInTimeAndSpace
items.doc:
A set is decidable within the given input-indexed bounds when its Boolean indicator is
computable in those bounds.
items.statement:
def DecidableInTimeAndSpace {α : Type*} (L : Set α) (enc : α ↪ List Bool)
    (t s : α → ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.not_halts_of_repeat_nonhalt
items.doc:
If a deterministic machine repeats a non-halting configuration, it never halts,
because the sequence between the two configurations will loop forever.
Note that this can be applied to two arbitrary and different time steps `t` and `t + Δ`
using `Function.iterate_add_apply`.
items.statement:
lemma not_halts_of_repeat_nonhalt
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
    (h_not_halt : cfg.state ≠ none)
    (t : ℕ)
    (heq : tm.runFrom cfg (t + 1) = cfg) :
    ∀ t', (tm.runFrom cfg t').state ≠ none

modules.title: Nondeterministic Multi-Tape Turing Machines
modules.doc:
Defines nondeterministic Turing machines with a read-only input tape, `k` work tapes and one
write-only output tape, their computation paths, and time bounds.

## Design

The design choices for configurations and actions are documented in
`Cslib.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Configuration`.

Following [Papadimitriou94], chapter 2.7, a nondeterministic machine is a Turing machine whose
transition function is replaced by a transition relation: `Tr q input work action` holds when `Tr`
relates the state `q` and the read symbols `input` and `work` to `action`.

A halted configuration steps to itself, so once a machine has halted it has a run of every length.
A time bound is therefore an upper bound, with no separate account of the step at which it halted.

The transition relation may be empty at a running configuration. Such a configuration has no
successor configuration and is called stuck.

Time bounds apply to every computation path, regardless of its outcome. `RunsInTime input t`
requires every path of at least `t` steps to end in a halted configuration.

## Important Declarations

* `MultiTapeNTM`: the machine, an initial state and a transition relation
* `Step`: the one-step relation on configurations
* `RunPath`: finite relation series of steps
* `ComputationPath`: a run path starting at the initial configuration
* `Adapter`, `Follows`: a machine follows another when it performs each of its transitions,
  reading and acting through an adapter
* `Follows.step`, `Follows.runningStepHom`, `Follows.stepHom`: a configuration map that agrees with
  the adapter maps steps to steps, so it is a homomorphism of step relations and maps run paths
* `RunsInTime`: every computation path of at least the given length ends in a halted
  configuration

## References

* [C. Papadimitriou, *Computational Complexity*][Papadimitriou94]
* [M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*][Sipser2013]

items.name: RelSeries.exists_of_mem_map
items.doc: A member of a mapped series is the image of a member.
items.statement:
lemma exists_of_mem_map {p : RelSeries r} {f : r.Hom s} {b : β} (hb : b ∈ p.map f) :
    ∃ a ∈ p, f a = b

items.name: RelSeries.mem_or_mem_of_mem_smash
items.doc: A member of two joined series lies on one of them.
items.statement:
lemma mem_or_mem_of_mem_smash {p q : RelSeries r} {h : p.last = q.head} {a : α}
    (ha : a ∈ p.smash q h) : a ∈ p ∨ a ∈ q

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM
items.doc:
A nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with `k` work tapes over the alphabet of
`Option Symbol` (where `none` is the blank symbol). Neither `Symbol` nor `State` is required to be
finite.
items.statement:
structure MultiTapeNTM (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*) where
  /-- initial state -/
  q₀ : State
  /-- transition relation: which combinations of state, current input symbol, tuple of work head
  symbols and resulting actions are valid transitions -/
  Tr (q : State) (input : Option Symbol) (work : Fin k → Option Symbol)
    (action : Action k Symbol State) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.Step
items.doc:
The one-step relation on configurations. A halted configuration steps only to itself. A running
configuration steps by applying any action related to its state and read symbols by `Tr`.
items.statement: def Step (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (c₁ c₂ : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.step_of_halt
items.doc: A halted configuration steps only to itself.
items.statement:
lemma step_of_halt {c c' : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : c.Halted) :
    ntm.Step c c' ↔ c' = c

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.initCfg
items.doc: The initial configuration corresponding to an input string.
items.statement:
def initCfg (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) :
    Cfg k Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.stepRel
items.doc: The one-step relation on configurations for `input`, as a set of pairs.
items.statement:
abbrev stepRel (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) :
    SetRel (Cfg k Symbol State input) (Cfg k Symbol State input)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.runningStepRel
items.doc: The steps of `ntm` from running configurations: the steps within a run until it halts.
items.statement:
abbrev runningStepRel (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) :
    SetRel (Cfg k Symbol State input) (Cfg k Symbol State input)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath
items.doc: A nonempty list of configurations joined by steps of `ntm`.
items.statement: abbrev RunPath (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.map
items.doc:
A run path mapped along a step-preserving map of configurations: `RelSeries.map`, typed as a
run path of the target machine.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.length_output_mono
items.doc: The output only grows along a run path.
items.statement:
lemma length_output_mono (p : ntm.RunPath input) :
    Monotone fun i ↦ (p i).output.length

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.last_eq_of_head_halted
items.doc: Once a run path is halted, its configuration stays unchanged.
items.statement: lemma last_eq_of_head_halted (p : ntm.RunPath input) (h : p.head.Halted) : p.last = p.head

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.last_eq_of_halted
items.doc: The last configuration equals any earlier halted configuration.
items.statement:
lemma last_eq_of_halted (p : ntm.RunPath input) (i : Fin (p.length + 1))
    (h : (p i).Halted) : p.last = p i

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.time
items.doc: The number of steps taken by a run path.
items.statement: def time (p : ntm.RunPath input) : ℕ

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunPath.exists_running
items.doc:
A path that ends halted runs from its head to its last configuration in running steps, up to
its first halted configuration.
items.statement:
lemma exists_running (p : ntm.RunPath input) (h : p.last.Halted) :
    ∃ q : RelSeries (ntm.runningStepRel input), q.head = p.head ∧ q.last = p.last ∧
      q.length ≤ p.length ∧ ∀ c ∈ q, c ∈ p

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.ComputationPath
items.doc: A run path starting at the initial configuration for `input`.
items.statement:
structure ComputationPath (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol)
    extends toRunPath : ntm.RunPath input where
  /-- the path starts at the initial configuration -/
  head_eq : toRunPath.head = ntm.initCfg input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.ComputationPath.time
items.doc: The number of steps taken by a computation path.
items.statement: def time (p : ntm.ComputationPath input) : ℕ

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunsInTime
items.doc:
Every computation path on `input` of at least `t` steps ends in a halted configuration.
A path ending in a stuck configuration must have fewer than `t` steps.
items.statement: def RunsInTime (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.RunsInTime.mono
items.doc: A time bound can be increased.
items.statement:
lemma RunsInTime.mono {input : List Symbol} {t t' : ℕ}
    (h : ntm.RunsInTime input t) (ht : t ≤ t') : ntm.RunsInTime input t'

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.Adapter
items.doc:
How a machine with `k'` work tapes and states `State'` performs the transitions of a machine
with `k` work tapes and states `State`. A transition turns the symbols under the heads into an
action, so the outer machine translates both ends: `read` computes the symbols the inner machine
reads from those under the outer heads, and `action` turns the inner action into an outer one,
which may also depend on the outer symbols.
items.statement:
structure Adapter (k k' : ℕ) (Symbol State State' : Type*) where
  /-- the symbols the inner machine reads -/
  read : HeadSymbols k' Symbol → HeadSymbols k Symbol
  /-- the outer action performing an inner action -/
  action : HeadSymbols k' Symbol → Action k Symbol State → Action k' Symbol State'

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.Adapter.mapState
items.doc: The adapter that relabels the states through `φ` and reads and acts on the same tapes.
items.statement:
def Adapter.mapState {State' : Type*} (φ : Option State → Option State') :
    Adapter k k Symbol State State'

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.Follows
items.doc:
`ntm'` follows `ntm` through `adapter`, in state `state q` while `ntm` is in state `q`: whatever
`ntm` may do in `q` on what `adapter` reads, `ntm'` may do the adapted action in `state q`.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.Follows.step
items.doc:
**A follower mirrors a step.** If `ntm'` follows `ntm`, and the map `f` relabels the state of
`c` through `state`, reads through `adapter` what `c` reads, and carries the action of a step from
`c` to its adaptation, then `f` maps the step to a step of `ntm'`.
items.statement:
lemma step (h : ntm'.Follows ntm state adapter)
    (f : Cfg k Symbol State input → Cfg k' Symbol State' input') {c c' : Cfg k Symbol State input}
    (hstep : ntm.Step c c') (hstate : c.state.map state = (f c).state)
    (hread : adapter.read (f c).headSymbols = c.headSymbols)
    (haction : ∀ action, action.apply c = c' →
      (adapter.action (f c).headSymbols action).apply (f c) = f c') :
    ntm'.Step (f c) (f c')

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.Follows.runningStepHom
items.doc:
**A follower mirrors the running steps.** If `ntm'` follows `ntm`, and `f` sends a configuration
in state `q` to one in state `state q`, from which `adapter` reads what the configuration reads and
on which each adapted action acts as the action acts on the configuration, then `f` maps each
running step of `ntm` to a step of `ntm'`.
items.statement:
def runningStepHom (h : ntm'.Follows ntm state adapter)
    (f : Cfg k Symbol State input → Cfg k' Symbol State' input')
    (hstate : ∀ c q, c.state = some q → (f c).state = some (state q))
    (hread : ∀ c, adapter.read (f c).headSymbols = c.headSymbols)
    (haction : ∀ c action,
      (adapter.action (f c).headSymbols action).apply (f c) = f (action.apply c)) :
    (ntm.runningStepRel input).Hom (ntm'.stepRel input')

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.Follows.stepHom
items.doc:
**A follower mirrors the steps.** As `runningStepHom`, for an `f` that relabels every state
through `state`, so that it also keeps halted configurations halted.
items.statement:
def stepHom (h : ntm'.Follows ntm state adapter)
    (f : Cfg k Symbol State input → Cfg k' Symbol State' input')
    (hstate : ∀ c, c.state.map state = (f c).state)
    (hread : ∀ c, adapter.read (f c).headSymbols = c.headSymbols)
    (haction : ∀ c action,
      (adapter.action (f c).headSymbols action).apply (f c) = f (action.apply c)) :
    (ntm.stepRel input).Hom (ntm'.stepRel input')

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeNTM.prependOutputHom
items.doc: A machine never reads its output tape, so prepending a word to the output preserves steps.
items.statement:
def prependOutputHom (ntm : MultiTapeNTM k Symbol State) (pre : List Symbol) :
    (ntm.stepRel input).Hom (ntm.stepRel input)

modules.title: A machine that clears a work tape
modules.doc:
`clearWork Symbol` erases the word on its work tape and returns the head to the start. It never
moves the input head and never outputs. It is the sequential composition of two one-tape machines:

* `forwardWork Symbol` moves the head right over the word until it reads the first blank, the
  frontier just past the word, and halts there (see `Plumbing.ForwardWork`).
* `rewindWork Symbol (some none)` rewinds the head to the start, erasing every symbol it walks
  over.

On a word of length `l` the forward pass takes `l + 1` steps and the erasing rewind `l + 2` steps.
The head stays within the cells `-1, …, l`, so the machine runs in time `3 * (l + 1)` and space
`l + 2`; placed on tape `i` of `k` tapes, the remaining tapes contribute one cell each.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.clearWork`: the one-tape machine that clears its tape.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_clearWork`: `clearWork` replaces the word on its tape by the
  empty word.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_clearWork_tapeEmb`: placed on tape `i` of a `k`-tape machine
  it does so on that tape and leaves every other tape unchanged.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.clearWork
items.doc:
The one-tape machine that clears its tape: it moves to the end of the word and erases it on
the way back.
items.statement:
public noncomputable def clearWork (Symbol : Type*) :
    MultiTapeTM 1 Symbol (Unit ⊕ RewindWorkState)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_clearWork
items.doc:
**The machine that clears its work tape** replaces the word on it by the empty word, in at most
`3 * (w.length + 1)` steps and `w.length + 2` cells.
items.statement:
public theorem transformsTapes_clearWork (w : List Symbol) :
    TransformsTapes (clearWork Symbol) (fun _ ws => ws 0 = w)
      (fun _ _ ws' emitted => ws' = (fun _ => []) ∧ emitted = [])
      (3 * (w.length + 1)) (w.length + 2)

items.note: ### Clearing one of several work tapes

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_clearWork_tapeEmb
items.doc:
**The machine that clears a work tape**, placed on tape `i` of a `k`-tape machine, replaces the
word on that tape by the empty word and leaves every other tape unchanged, in at most
`3 * (w.length + 1)` steps and `w.length + 1 + k` cells.
items.statement:
public theorem transformsTapes_clearWork_tapeEmb (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) :
    TransformsTapes ((clearWork Symbol).extendTapes (tapeEmb i)) (fun _ ws => ws i = w)
      (fun _ ws ws' emitted => ws' = Function.update ws i [] ∧ emitted = [])
      (3 * (w.length + 1)) (w.length + 1 + k)

modules.title: Extending a machine with additional work tapes
modules.doc:
`extendTapes tm e`, for an embedding `e : Fin k ↪ Fin k'`, runs `tm` inside a machine with more
work tapes. The tapes selected by `e` are used by `tm`: target tape `e j` plays the role of source
tape `j`. The remaining tapes are left unchanged.

The configuration map `embed e cfg extraTapes extraPos` places `cfg` on the selected tapes and
initialises the remaining tapes from `extraTapes` and `extraPos`.

The configuration map is a homomorphism of step relations (`embedHom`), so each run path of `tm`
maps to a run path of the larger machine.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv`: the partial inverse of the tape embedding.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.extendTapes`: the machine with reindexed work tapes.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed`: the corresponding configuration map.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.embedHom`: the configuration map as a step-preserving map, which maps run
  paths.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.tapeEmb`: the embedding placing the only tape of a one-tape machine on
  tape `i`, and `Turing.MultiTapeTM.noTapes`: the embedding of a machine without work tapes.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.space_map_embedHom_le`: the space bound for a mapped path.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.oneTapeCfg`: the one-tape view of a configuration.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_tapeEmb`: the run of a one-tape machine placed on work tape `i`.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.TransformsTapes.tapeEmb`: a one-tape specification, read on tape `i`.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_noTapes`: the run of a machine without work tapes, placed in a machine
  with `k` of them.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv
items.doc:
The computable analogue of `Function.partialInv` for an embedding `e`: `partialInv e l = some j`
when `e j = l` (such `j` is unique by injectivity), and `none` when `l` lies outside the range of
`e`.
items.statement: public def partialInv (e : Fin k ↪ Fin k') (l : Fin k') : Option (Fin k)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv_isPartialInv
items.doc: `partialInv e` is a partial inverse of `e`.
items.statement:
public lemma partialInv_isPartialInv (e : Fin k ↪ Fin k') :
    Function.IsPartialInv e (partialInv e)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.extendTapes
items.doc:
`tm` run on the tapes selected by the embedding `e`, leaving other tapes untouched: work tape
`e j` plays the role of `tm`'s tape `j`, and any tape outside `range e` is never written and never
moves.
items.statement:
public noncomputable def extendTapes (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
(e : Fin k ↪ Fin k') : MultiTapeTM k' Symbol State

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.extendTapes_q₀
items.statement:
public lemma extendTapes_q₀ (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (e : Fin k ↪ Fin k') :
    (tm.extendTapes e).q₀ = tm.q₀

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed
items.doc:
A configuration of `tm`, embedded: tape `j` goes to tape `e j`, the tapes outside `range e`
carry the given `extraTapes` contents and `extraPos` head positions.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv_embed
items.doc: The partial inverse recovers the source tape of an embedded tape.
items.statement: public lemma partialInv_embed (e : Fin k ↪ Fin k') (j : Fin k) : partialInv e (e j) = some j

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv_eq_none
items.doc: Outside the range of `e`, the partial inverse is undefined.
items.statement:
public lemma partialInv_eq_none (e : Fin k ↪ Fin k') {l : Fin k'} (hl : l ∉ Set.range e) :
    partialInv e l = none

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv_eq_some
items.doc: If the partial inverse is `some j`, then `e j = l`.
items.statement:
public lemma partialInv_eq_some (e : Fin k ↪ Fin k') {l : Fin k'} {j : Fin k}
    (h : partialInv e l = some j) : e j = l

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed_workTapes_embed
Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed_workTapePos_embed
Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed_workTapeSymbols_embed
Turing.MultiTapeTM.embedHom
items.doc:
`embed` as a homomorphism of step relations: each step `c → c'` of `tm` becomes the step
`embed c → embed c'` of the reindexed machine, so a run path of `tm` maps to a run path of the
reindexed machine, with the extra tapes held fixed. `Follows.stepHom` builds it, since `embed`
agrees with the adapter defining `extendTapes`.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.space_map_embedHom_le
items.doc:
**Space bound for a reindexed path.** The embedded tapes visit what the original path visits,
while each of the remaining `k' - k` tapes never moves and contributes one cell.

items.note: ### Placing a one-tape machine on a single work tape

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.tapeEmb
items.doc: The embedding that places the only work tape of a one-tape machine on tape `i`.
items.statement: public def tapeEmb (i : Fin k) : Fin 1 ↪ Fin k

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.tapeEmb_apply
items.statement: public lemma tapeEmb_apply (i : Fin k) (j : Fin 1) : tapeEmb i j = i

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.range_tapeEmb
items.statement: public lemma range_tapeEmb (i : Fin k) : Set.range (tapeEmb i) = {i}

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv_tapeEmb
items.doc: Tape `i` is the image of the only tape of a one-tape machine, and no other tape is.
items.statement:
public lemma partialInv_tapeEmb (i l : Fin k) :
    partialInv (tapeEmb i) l = if l = i then some 0 else none

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed_tapeEmb
items.doc: A one-tape configuration placed on tape `i` leaves every other tape as it was.
items.statement:
public lemma embed_tapeEmb (i : Fin k) (cfg : Cfg 1 Symbol State input)
    (tapes : Fin k → ℤ → Option Symbol) (heads : Fin k → ℤ) :
    embed (tapeEmb i) cfg tapes heads =
      ⟨cfg.state, cfg.inputPos, Function.update tapes i (cfg.workTapes 0),
        Function.update heads i (cfg.workTapePos 0), cfg.output⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.oneTapeCfg
items.doc:
The one-tape view of a configuration of a machine with `k` work tapes: the tape and head of
tape `i`, with everything else as it is.
items.statement:
public def oneTapeCfg (i : Fin k) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
Cfg 1 Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed_oneTapeCfg
items.doc: A configuration is its own one-tape view on tape `i`, placed back on tape `i`.
items.statement:
public lemma embed_oneTapeCfg (i : Fin k) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    embed (tapeEmb i) (oneTapeCfg i cfg) cfg.workTapes cfg.workTapePos = cfg

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_tapeEmb
items.doc:
**Running a one-tape machine on work tape `i`.** The run is the run on the one-tape view of the
configuration, placed back on tape `i`; every other tape and head keeps its starting value. Combine
with `embed_tapeEmb` to read off the resulting configuration.
items.statement:
public lemma runFrom_tapeEmb (tm : MultiTapeTM 1 Symbol State) (i : Fin k)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (n : ℕ) :
    (tm.extendTapes (tapeEmb i)).runFrom cfg n =
      embed (tapeEmb i) (tm.runFrom (oneTapeCfg i cfg) n) cfg.workTapes cfg.workTapePos

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.TransformsTapes.tapeEmb
items.doc:
**A one-tape specification on tape `i`.** A one-tape machine placed on tape `i` transforms the
word on that tape as it did on its own tape and leaves every other word alone; each remaining tape
costs one cell.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.noTapes
items.doc: The embedding of a machine without work tapes into a machine with `k` of them.
items.statement: public def noTapes (k : ℕ) : Fin 0 ↪ Fin k

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.partialInv_noTapes
items.doc: No tape is in the range of `noTapes`.
items.statement: public lemma partialInv_noTapes (l : Fin k) : partialInv (noTapes k) l = none

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.noTapesCfg
items.doc: The view of a configuration as a configuration of a machine without work tapes.
items.statement: public def noTapesCfg (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Cfg 0 Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed_noTapes
items.doc:
A configuration without work tapes, placed in a machine with `k` of them, only contributes its
state, its input head and its output.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.embed_noTapesCfg
items.doc: A configuration is its tapeless view, placed back on its tapes.
items.statement:
public lemma embed_noTapesCfg (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    embed (noTapes k) (noTapesCfg cfg) cfg.workTapes cfg.workTapePos = cfg

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_noTapes
items.doc:
**Running a machine without work tapes inside a machine with `k` of them.** Only the state, the
input head and the output change; every work tape and work head keeps its starting value.
items.statement:
public lemma runFrom_noTapes (tm : MultiTapeTM 0 Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
    (n : ℕ) :
    (tm.extendTapes (noTapes k)).runFrom cfg n =
      ⟨(tm.runFrom (noTapesCfg cfg) n).state, (tm.runFrom (noTapesCfg cfg) n).inputPos,
        cfg.workTapes, cfg.workTapePos, (tm.runFrom (noTapesCfg cfg) n).output⟩

modules.title: A machine that moves to the end of a word
modules.doc:
`forwardWork Symbol` moves the head of its work tape to the right over the word it holds and halts
on the frontier, the first blank cell just past the word. It never modifies a tape, never moves the
input head and never outputs.

On a word of length `l`, started with the head at cell `p ≤ l`, the machine takes `l - p + 1` steps
and the head stays within the cells `p, …, l`.

This is a one-tape machine; to move the head of tape `i` of a `k`-tape machine to the end of its
word, place it there with `Turing.MultiTapeTM.tapeEmb` and transport its run with
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_tapeEmb`. The input head, the output and every other tape are then
untouched by construction.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.forwardWork`: the one-tape machine that moves its head to the frontier of
  its word.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_forwardWork`: its run from the initial state.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_runFrom_forwardWork`: its head stays within `[p, w.length]`.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.forwardWork
items.doc:
The one-tape machine that moves its head to the end of its word. Over a symbol it moves right;
on the first blank it halts without moving.
items.statement: public def forwardWork (Symbol : Type*) : MultiTapeTM 1 Symbol Unit

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ForwardWork.runFrom_walk
items.doc:
Walking right over the word: from cell `p`, after `n` steps with `p + n ≤ w.length` the head
is at cell `p + n`.
items.statement:
lemma runFrom_walk {w : List Symbol} {p : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (hn : p + n ≤ w.length) :
    (forwardWork Symbol).runFrom
        ⟨some (), inpos, fun _ => tapeOfList w, fun _ => (p : ℤ), out⟩ n =
      ⟨some (), inpos, fun _ => tapeOfList w, fun _ => (p : ℤ) + n, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_forwardWork
items.doc:
**The run of the machine that moves to the end of the word.** Started with the tape holding a
word `w` and the head at a cell `p` with `p + n = w.length`, after `n + 1` steps the machine has
halted with the head on the frontier `w.length` and nothing else changed.
items.statement:
public theorem runFrom_forwardWork (inpos : Fin (input.length + 2)) (w : List Symbol)
    (out : List Symbol) {p n : ℕ} (hpn : p + n = w.length) :
    (forwardWork Symbol).runFrom
        ⟨some (forwardWork Symbol).q₀, inpos, fun _ => tapeOfList w, fun _ => (p : ℤ), out⟩
        (n + 1) =
      ⟨none, inpos, fun _ => tapeOfList w, fun _ => (w.length : ℤ), out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_runFrom_forwardWork
items.doc: At every step, the head is within `[p, w.length]`.
items.statement:
public theorem workTapePos_runFrom_forwardWork (inpos : Fin (input.length + 2))
    (w : List Symbol) (out : List Symbol) {p : ℕ} (hp : p ≤ w.length) (m : ℕ) :
    ((forwardWork Symbol).runFrom
        ⟨some (forwardWork Symbol).q₀, inpos, fun _ => tapeOfList w, fun _ => (p : ℤ), out⟩
        m).workTapePos 0 ∈ Set.Icc (p : ℤ) w.length

modules.title: Reading the input from a work tape
modules.doc:
`inputFromTape tm` behaves like `tm`, except that it reads its input from a work tape — the
*virtual input tape* — instead of the real one, which it never touches. The virtual input head
lives at cell `p - 1` when the simulated input head is at position `p`, so the word cells
`0, …, len - 1` are the input positions `1, …, len` and the two boundary positions read the blanks
at cells `-1` and `len`.

The one thing a blank cell cannot tell the machine is *which* boundary it is at — and it must
know, because the input head clamps there. This ambiguity is resolved by tracking a boundary
classification. A second fresh work tape, the *flag tape*, moves in lockstep with the virtual input
head and carries a single non-blank `mark` at cell `-1`, so the left boundary is recognised by
reading the flag. Reading blank on both the virtual input tape and the flag tape means the right
boundary.

The configuration map `inCfg` places the simulated input on the virtual input tape, places the
marker on the flag tape, and leaves the real input tape unused. It is a homomorphism of step
relations (`inCfgHom`), so each run path of `tm` maps to a run path of the redirected machine.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.clampMove
items.doc:
The clamped move of the virtual input head: at the left boundary (blank under the virtual
head, flag marked) left moves are blocked, at the right boundary (blank on both) right moves
are.
items.statement: public def clampMove (wvip wflag : Option Symbol) (m : SignType) : SignType

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inputFromTape
items.doc:
`tm`, reading its input from the virtual input tape `Fin.natAdd k 0`, with the flag tape
`Fin.natAdd k 1` marking the cell left of the input. The real input tape is never read and never
moved.
items.statement:
public noncomputable def inputFromTape (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) :
MultiTapeTM (k + 2) Symbol State

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg
items.doc:
A configuration of `tm` on `input`, as the redirecting machine sees it, over an arbitrary
ambient input: `input` sits on the virtual input tape with the head at cell `inputPos - 1`, the flag
tape carries its mark at `-1` with its head in lockstep, and the ambient input head rests at
`1`.
items.statement:
public def inCfg (mark : Symbol) {input : List Symbol} (c : Cfg k Symbol State input)
(outerInput : List Symbol) : Cfg (k + 2) Symbol State outerInput

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_inputPos
items.statement:
public lemma inCfg_inputPos (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (inCfg mark c outerInput).inputPos = 1

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapes_castAdd
items.statement:
public lemma inCfg_workTapes_castAdd (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (j : Fin k) :
    (inCfg mark c outerInput).workTapes (j.castAdd 2) = c.workTapes j

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapes_vip
items.statement:
public lemma inCfg_workTapes_vip (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (inCfg mark c outerInput).workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 0) = tapeOfList input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapes_flag
Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapePos_castAdd
items.statement:
public lemma inCfg_workTapePos_castAdd (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (j : Fin k) :
    (inCfg mark c outerInput).workTapePos (j.castAdd 2) = c.workTapePos j

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapePos_natAdd
items.doc: The virtual input head and the flag head both stand at cell `inputPos - 1`.
items.statement:
public lemma inCfg_workTapePos_natAdd (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin 2) :
    (inCfg mark c outerInput).workTapePos (Fin.natAdd k i) = (c.inputPos.val : ℤ) - 1

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapeSymbols_castAdd
items.statement:
public lemma inCfg_workTapeSymbols_castAdd (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (j : Fin k) :
    (inCfg mark c outerInput).workTapeSymbols (j.castAdd 2) = c.workTapeSymbols j

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapeSymbols_vip
items.doc:
The virtual input head reads exactly what the simulated input head reads: the word cells are
the input positions, the two boundary cells are blank.
items.statement:
public lemma inCfg_workTapeSymbols_vip (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (inCfg mark c outerInput).workTapeSymbols (Fin.natAdd k 0) = c.inputSymbol

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapeSymbols_flag
items.doc: The flag head reads the mark exactly at the left boundary.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.val_moveInputPos_sub_one_eq_clampMove
items.doc: The clamped move of the virtual input head tracks the simulated input head exactly.
items.statement:
public lemma val_moveInputPos_sub_one_eq_clampMove (mark : Symbol) (c : Cfg k Symbol State input)
    (m : SignType) :
    ((moveInputPos c.inputPos m).val : ℤ) - 1 =
      ((c.inputPos.val : ℤ) - 1) +
        (clampMove c.inputSymbol (if c.inputPos.val = 0 then some mark else none) m : ℤ)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inCfgHom
items.doc:
The redirection preserves steps, so it maps run paths of `tm` to run paths of the redirected
machine.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.space_map_inCfgHom_le
items.doc:
**Space of the input-redirected path.** The `k` inner tapes visit exactly what the original
path visits; the two extra tapes (virtual input, flag) each move only with the simulated input
head, which stays within `[-1, input.length]`, so they add at most `2 * (input.length + 2)`.

modules.title: Redirecting the output to a work tape
modules.doc:
`outputToTape tm` behaves like `tm`, except that whatever `tm` would append to the write-only
output tape is written on a fresh work tape instead, whose head always stands at the write
frontier.

Since the output is append-only, the frontier position is a *function of the configuration* —
the length of the output so far — so the redirected machine mirrors the original through the
configuration map `outCfg`, a homomorphism of step relations (`outCfgHom`), so each run path of `tm`
maps to a run path of the redirected machine.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outputToTape
items.doc:
`tm`, with its output writes redirected onto a fresh last work tape, whose head always stands
at the write frontier.
items.statement:
public noncomputable def outputToTape (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) :
MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Symbol State

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outCfg
items.doc:
A configuration of `tm`, as the redirected machine sees it: the output so far sits on the
last work tape with the head at its end, and the real output is empty.
items.statement:
public def outCfg (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outCfg_workTapes_last
items.statement:
public lemma outCfg_workTapes_last (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (outCfg c).workTapes (Fin.last k) = tapeOfList c.output

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outCfg_workTapes_castSucc
items.statement:
public lemma outCfg_workTapes_castSucc (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (j : Fin k) :
    (outCfg c).workTapes j.castSucc = c.workTapes j

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outCfg_workTapePos_last
items.statement:
public lemma outCfg_workTapePos_last (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (outCfg c).workTapePos (Fin.last k) = (c.output.length : ℤ)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outCfg_workTapePos_castSucc
items.statement:
public lemma outCfg_workTapePos_castSucc (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (j : Fin k) :
    (outCfg c).workTapePos j.castSucc = c.workTapePos j

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outCfg_workTapeSymbols_castSucc
items.statement:
public lemma outCfg_workTapeSymbols_castSucc (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (j : Fin k) :
    (outCfg c).workTapeSymbols j.castSucc = c.workTapeSymbols j

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.outCfgHom
items.doc:
The redirection preserves steps, so it maps run paths of `tm` to run paths of the redirected
machine.
items.statement:
public noncomputable def outCfgHom (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) :
(tm.stepRel input).Hom (tm.outputToTape.stepRel input)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg_outputToTape
items.doc: The initial configuration of the redirected machine is the original's through `outCfg`.
items.statement:
public lemma initCfg_outputToTape (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) :
    tm.outputToTape.initCfg input = outCfg (tm.initCfg input)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.space_map_outCfgHom_le
items.doc:
**Space of the output-redirected path.** The `k` inner tapes visit exactly what the original
path visits, and the frontier head only walks up to the final length of the output, so the
redirection costs at most the final output length plus one.
items.statement:
public lemma space_map_outCfgHom_le (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (p : tm.RunPath input) :
    (p.map (outCfgHom tm)).space ≤ p.space + (p.last.output.length + 1)

modules.title: Repeating a machine until a tape goes blank
modules.doc:
`repeatUntilBlank i tm` runs `tm` repeatedly. After each round it reads the cell under the head of
work tape `i` and halts if that cell is blank. Each round of a `Turing.MultiTapeTM.TransformsTapes`
specification ends with every head on the first cell of its word, so the loop halts exactly when
the word on tape `i` is empty. The body always runs at least once.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_repeatUntilBlank`: a loop invariant preserved by every round
  gives a specification of `repeatUntilBlank i tm`, with time bound `(rounds + 1) * (t + 1)` and
  space bound `2 * k * s + k`.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RepeatUntilBlank.blankTest
items.doc:
The test of tape `i`: it halts if the cell under the head of tape `i` is blank and otherwise
stays in its only state, moving no head.
items.statement: public def RepeatUntilBlank.blankTest (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Symbol Unit

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.repeatUntilBlank
items.doc:
`tm` combined with the test of tape `i`: halting of `tm` goes to the test, which halts the loop
if the cell under the head of tape `i` is blank and otherwise restarts `tm`.
items.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev repeatUntilBlank (i : Fin k) (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) :
    MultiTapeTM k Symbol (State ⊕ Unit)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RepeatUntilBlank.step_check
items.doc:
From the test on a `wordsCfg` configuration, the machine halts if the word on tape `i` is empty
and otherwise restarts `tm`, leaving the words unchanged.
items.statement:
lemma step_check (ws : Fin k → List Symbol) (out : List Symbol) :
    (repeatUntilBlank i tm).step (wordsCfg input (some (.inr ())) ws out) =
      wordsCfg input (if ws i = [] then none else some (.inl tm.q₀)) ws out

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RepeatUntilBlank.exists_round
items.doc:
One round of the loop. If `tm` transforms words satisfying `P` within `t` steps and `s` cells,
then from `tm`'s initial state on such words `w` the loop has a run path of at most `t + 1` steps
within `[-s, s]` to the words `w'` that `tm` leaves: the running steps of `tm`, and then reading
tape `i`, which halts the loop if `w' i` is empty and otherwise starts the next round.
items.statement:
lemma exists_round {P : (input : List Symbol) → (Fin k → List Symbol) → Prop}
    {Q : (input : List Symbol) → (Fin k → List Symbol) → (Fin k → List Symbol) →
      List Symbol → Prop} {t s : ℕ}
    (h : TransformsTapes tm P Q t s) {w : Fin k → List Symbol} (out : List Symbol)
    (hP : P input w) :
    ∃ w' e, Q input w w' e ∧ ∃ p : (repeatUntilBlank i tm).RunPath input,
      p.head = wordsCfg input (some (.inl tm.q₀)) w out ∧
      p.last = wordsCfg input (if w' i = [] then none else some (.inl tm.q₀)) w' (out ++ e) ∧
      p.length ≤ t + 1 ∧ p.InWindow s

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_repeatUntilBlank
items.doc:
Let `P n` be a loop invariant after `n` rounds, on the words on the tapes and the word emitted
so far. If each round `n < rounds` takes `P n` to `P (n + 1)` and leaves tape `i` non-empty, and
the round after that takes `P rounds` to `R` and empties tape `i`, then `repeatUntilBlank i tm`
takes `P 0` to `R`.

Each of the `rounds + 1` rounds takes at most `t + 1` steps. No head leaves `[-s, s]`, since every
round starts with all heads at cell `0` and uses at most `s` cells.

modules.title: A machine that rewinds the input head
modules.doc:
A two-state machine that, when started in its initial state at any input-head position, returns the
head to position 1 (the first input symbol when the input is nonempty, otherwise the right boundary)
and halts there. It has no work tapes at all and never outputs, so running it in between two phases
of a computation re-normalizes the input head without disturbing anything else: place it inside a
machine with `k` work tapes with `Turing.MultiTapeTM.noTapes` and transport its run with
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_noTapes`, which leaves every work tape and work head where it was.

In its initial state `start` the machine moves the input head one cell left and enters state `walk`.
The input head is clamped at the left boundary, so this has no effect if the head already is at
position `0`, and it moves a head at the right boundary `input.length + 1` back onto the input.
In state `walk` the machine moves left over symbols. Since the input tape holds a list of
(non-blank) symbols, the first blank to the left of the head is the cell at position `0`; the
halting transition moves right, onto position `1`.

From position `p` the run halts after `p + 1` steps, or after `2` steps if `p = 0`.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.rewindInput`: the machine that rewinds the input head.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindInput`: its run from the initial state.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RewindState
items.doc:
The control states of the rewinding machine: `start` takes one unconditional step left,
`walk` moves left towards the left boundary of the input.
items.statement:
public inductive RewindState : Type
  | start
  | walk
  deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.inputAction
items.doc:
The only kind of action the rewinding machine takes: move the input head by `m` and enter
`state`, without output.
items.statement: abbrev inputAction (m : SignType) (state : Option RewindState) : Action 0 Symbol RewindState

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.rewindInput
items.doc:
The rewinding machine. In state `start` it moves the input head left, unconditionally, and
enters `walk`. In state `walk` it moves left over a symbol; on the first blank it moves right and
halts. The machine has no work tapes and nothing is output.
items.statement: public def rewindInput (Symbol : Type*) : MultiTapeTM 0 Symbol RewindState

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.Rewind.step_eq
items.doc: A live step moves the input head and changes the state; nothing else changes.
items.statement:
lemma step_eq {c : Cfg 0 Symbol RewindState input} {q : RewindState} (hc : c.state = some q) :
    (rewindInput Symbol).step c =
      let a := (rewindInput Symbol).tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols
      ⟨a.state, moveInputPos c.inputPos a.inputTape, c.workTapes, c.workTapePos, c.output⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.Rewind.runFrom_walk
items.doc:
From `walk` at position `p ≤ input.length` the machine halts with the input head at position `1`
after `p + 1` steps.
items.statement:
lemma runFrom_walk (p : Fin (input.length + 2)) (hp : p.val ≤ input.length) :
    (rewindInput Symbol).runFrom ⟨some .walk, p, tapes, heads, out⟩ (p.val + 1) =
      ⟨none, 1, tapes, heads, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindInput
items.doc:
From its initial state at input position `p` the machine halts after `p - 1 + 2` steps, with
the input head at position `1` and everything else unchanged.
items.statement:
public theorem runFrom_rewindInput (p : Fin (input.length + 2))
    (tapes : Fin 0 → ℤ → Option Symbol) (heads : Fin 0 → ℤ) (out : List Symbol) :
    (rewindInput Symbol).runFrom ⟨some (rewindInput Symbol).q₀, p, tapes, heads, out⟩
      (p.val - 1 + 2) = ⟨none, 1, tapes, heads, out⟩

modules.title: A machine that rewinds a work-tape head
modules.doc:
A machine that moves the head of its work tape to the left end of its contents and halts. It
optionally writes a certain symbol to or clears the cells it moves over while traveling to the
left. The input tape is not modified. This machine can be run between two phases of a computation
to re-normalise a work-tape head without disturbing anything else.

In its initial state `start` the machine takes one unconditional step left, into state `scan`. In
state `scan` it walks left over symbols, writing `write` to every cell it leaves; on the first
blank it moves the head right and halts. By default `write` is `none` and the machine writes
nothing; with `write := some none` it erases the part of the word it walks over.

This is a one-tape machine; to rewind tape `i` of a `k`-tape machine, place it there with
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.tapeEmb` and transport its run with
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_tapeEmb`. The input head, the output and every other tape are then
untouched by construction.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.rewindWork`: the one-tape machine that rewinds its head to the start of its
  word.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindWork`: its run from the initial state, with the special cases
  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindWork_none` (nothing is written) and
  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindWork_erase` (the whole word is erased).
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_runFrom_rewindWork`: the rewound head stays within `[-1, p]`.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RewindWorkState
items.doc:
The control states of the work-tape-rewinding machine: `start` takes one unconditional step
left, `scan` walks left towards the start of the word.
items.statement:
public inductive RewindWorkState : Type
  | start
  | scan
  deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.rewindWork
items.doc:
The one-tape rewinding machine. In state `start` it moves its head left, unconditionally, and
enters state `scan`. In state `scan` it writes `write` over a symbol and moves left, staying in
`scan`; on the first blank it moves right and halts. The input head never moves and nothing is
ever output.
items.statement:
public def rewindWork (Symbol : Type*) (write : Option (Option Symbol) := none) :
    MultiTapeTM 1 Symbol RewindWorkState

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RewindWork.step_start
items.doc: Moving the head left in state `start`, unconditionally, entering `scan`.
items.statement:
lemma step_start :
    (rewindWork Symbol write).step ⟨some .start, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => p, out⟩ =
      ⟨some .scan, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => p - 1, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RewindWork.step_scan_some
items.doc:
Walking left in state `scan`: over a symbol the machine writes `write` and the head moves left,
staying in `scan`.
items.statement:
lemma step_scan_some {s : Symbol} (hs : t p = some s) :
    (rewindWork Symbol write).step ⟨some .scan, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => p, out⟩ =
      ⟨some .scan, ip, fun _ => write.elim t (Function.update t p), fun _ => p - 1, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RewindWork.step_scan_none
items.doc:
Halting in state `scan`: on the first blank — the cell at position `-1` — the head moves right
and the machine halts.
items.statement:
lemma step_scan_none (hs : t p = none) :
    (rewindWork Symbol write).step ⟨some .scan, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => p, out⟩ =
      ⟨none, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => p + 1, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.RewindWork.runFrom_scan
items.doc:
The scanning phase: from `scan` at cell `l - 1` of the word, after `n ≤ l` steps the head has
walked left `n` cells, writing `write` to the cells it left.
items.statement:
lemma runFrom_scan {w : List Symbol} (hw : t = tapeOfList w) {l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ w.length) (n : ℕ)
    (hn : n ≤ l) :
    (rewindWork Symbol write).runFrom
        ⟨some .scan, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => (l : ℤ) - 1, out⟩ n =
      ⟨some .scan, ip, fun _ z => if (l : ℤ) - n ≤ z ∧ z < l then write.getD (t z) else t z,
        fun _ => (l : ℤ) - 1 - n, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindWork
items.doc:
**The run of the one-tape machine that rewinds its head.** Started with the tape holding a word
`w` and the head at a position `p ≤ w.length` — inside the word or at the frontier just past it —
after `p + 2` steps the machine has halted with the head back at position `0`, `write` applied to
the cells `0, …, p - 1` and nothing else changed.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindWork_none
items.doc: **Rewinding without writing** changes nothing but the position of the head.
items.statement:
public theorem runFrom_rewindWork_none (ip : Fin (input.length + 2)) (t : ℤ → Option Symbol)
    (out : List Symbol) {w : List Symbol} (hw : t = tapeOfList w) {p : ℕ} (hp : p ≤ w.length) :
    (rewindWork Symbol).runFrom
        ⟨some (rewindWork Symbol).q₀, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => (p : ℤ), out⟩ (p + 2) =
      ⟨none, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => 0, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_rewindWork_erase
items.doc: **Rewinding while erasing** from the frontier of the word leaves the tape blank.
items.statement:
public theorem runFrom_rewindWork_erase (ip : Fin (input.length + 2)) (t : ℤ → Option Symbol)
    (out : List Symbol) {w : List Symbol} (hw : t = tapeOfList w) :
    (rewindWork Symbol (some none)).runFrom
        ⟨some (rewindWork Symbol (some none)).q₀, ip, fun _ => t, fun _ => (w.length : ℤ), out⟩
        (w.length + 2) =
      ⟨none, ip, fun _ _ => none, fun _ => 0, out⟩

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_runFrom_rewindWork
items.doc:
At every step, the head is within `[-1, p]`: it walks from its start `p ≤ w.length` down to
`-1` and back to `0`, where it stays.

modules.title: Sequential composition of machines on shared tapes
modules.doc:
`seq tm₀ tm₁` behaves like `tm₀` until `tm₀` would halt, at which point it continues as `tm₁`,
started in its initial state on the tapes as `tm₀` left them. The state space is
`State₀ ⊕ State₁`, and the *halting transition* of the first phase is mapped to the initial state
of the second, so the handoff costs no extra step.

At the specification level this is `transformsTapes_seq`: transformations compose, with the time
and space bounds adding. The postcondition of `TransformsTapes` is what makes the proof direct:
the first machine halts in a full `wordsCfg`, which is exactly a starting configuration for the
second.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.seq`: the composed machine.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.exists_runPath_seq`: run paths compose, and the composed path visits only
  cells that the two paths visit.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_seq`: transformations compose, bounds adding.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.seq
items.doc:
The sequential composition of `tm₀` and `tm₁`: it behaves like `tm₀` until `tm₀` would halt,
at which point it switches to the initial state of `tm₁` and behaves like `tm₁`. The switch is
folded into the halting transition of `tm₀`, so it costs no step.
items.statement:
noncomputable abbrev seq (tm₀ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State₀) (tm₁ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State₁) :
    MultiTapeTM k Symbol (State₀ ⊕ State₁)

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.exists_runPath_seq
items.doc:
**Sequential composition of runs.** A run path of `tm₀` to a halted configuration and a run path
of `tm₁` started where `tm₀` halted combine into a run path of `seq`: the first path up to its first
halted configuration, followed by the second. It takes at most as many steps as the two paths
together, and visits only cells that they visit.
items.statement:
theorem exists_runPath_seq {p₀ : tm₀.RunPath input} (h₀ : p₀.last.Halted)
    {p₁ : tm₁.RunPath input} (h₁ : p₁.head = p₀.last.withState (some tm₁.q₀)) :
    ∃ p : (tm₀.seq tm₁).RunPath input, p.head = p₀.head.mapState (handOver tm₁.q₀) ∧
      p.last = p₁.last.mapState (Option.map .inr) ∧ p.length ≤ p₀.length + p₁.length ∧
      ∀ i, p.visitedByTapeHead i ⊆ p₀.visitedByTapeHead i ∪ p₁.visitedByTapeHead i

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.transformsTapes_seq
items.doc:
**Sequential composition of transformations.** If the postcondition of the first
transformation implies the precondition of the second, the composed machine performs the two
transformations one after the other, with the time and space bounds adding and the emitted words
concatenating.
items.statement:
theorem transformsTapes_seq
    {P₀ P₁ : (input : List Symbol) → (Fin k → List Symbol) → Prop}
    {Q₀ Q₁ : (input : List Symbol) → (Fin k → List Symbol) → (Fin k → List Symbol) →
      List Symbol → Prop}
    {t₀ s₀ t₁ s₁ : ℕ}
    (h₀ : TransformsTapes tm₀ P₀ Q₀ t₀ s₀) (h₁ : TransformsTapes tm₁ P₁ Q₁ t₁ s₁)
    (hmid : ∀ input ws ws' e, P₀ input ws → Q₀ input ws ws' e → P₁ input ws') :
    TransformsTapes (tm₀.seq tm₁) P₀
      (fun input ws ws'' e => ∃ ws' e₀ e₁, Q₀ input ws ws' e₀ ∧ Q₁ input ws' ws'' e₁ ∧
        e = e₀ ++ e₁)
      (t₀ + t₁) (s₀ + s₁)

modules.title: Tidy computations
modules.doc:
A machine computes *tidily* if it clears its work tapes before halting and moves all tape heads
to their initial position.
This means tidy computations can easily be iterated and when applied to a subset of work tapes,
a combinator can run a tidy machine as a subroutine and rely on nothing but the word it emits.

A tidy computation is defined as a `Turing.MultiTapeTM.TransformsTapes` from blank work tapes to
blank work tapes, so the lemmas about tape transformations apply to it directly. The three
notions below add tidiness to `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesInTimeAndSpace`,
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace` and `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInTimeAndSpace`.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace`: a machine computes an output tidily.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesFunTidilyInTimeAndSpace`: a machine computes a function tidily.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace`: some machine with binary alphabet and
  finitely many states computes a function tidily.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpaceOfLength`: the same, with bounds on the length
  of the encoded input.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.computesTidily_iff`: a tidy computation is a single run path between
  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.wordsCfg` configurations within the time and space bounds.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace
items.doc:
`ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace tm input output t s`: started on `input` with blank work tapes,
`tm` halts within `t` steps and `s` work-tape cells, having emitted `output`, with every work tape
blank and every head back at its starting cell.
items.statement:
abbrev ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (input output : List Symbol) (t s : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.computesTidily_iff
items.doc:
A tidy computation is a single run path between `Turing.MultiTapeTM.wordsCfg` configurations
with blank work tapes, which emits the output, within the time and space bounds.
items.statement:
theorem computesTidily_iff {input output : List Symbol} :
    tm.ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace input output t s ↔
      ∃ p : tm.RunPath input, p.head = wordsCfg input (some tm.q₀) (fun _ => []) [] ∧
        p.last = wordsCfg input none (fun _ => []) output ∧ p.time ≤ t ∧ p.space ≤ s

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace.mono
items.doc: Resource bounds can be weakened.

items.name: Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesFunTidilyInTimeAndSpace
items.doc:
