(2) s' is halted in p, and p.toStandardForm steps to a state that is also halted
    with the same registers (this only happens for jumps with unbounded targets).
items.statement:
theorem Step.toStandardForm {p : Program} {s s' : State} (hstep : Step p s s') :
    Step p.toStandardForm s s' ∨
    (s'.isHalted p ∧ ∃ s₂, Step p.toStandardForm s s₂ ∧
      s₂.isHalted p.toStandardForm ∧ s'.regs = s₂.regs)

items.name: Cslib.URM.Steps.toStandardForm_halts
items.doc:
Forward halting: if p reaches a halted state, p.toStandardForm reaches a halted state
with the same registers.
items.statement:
theorem Steps.toStandardForm_halts {p : Program} {s s' : State}
    (hsteps : Steps p s s') (hhalted : s'.isHalted p) :
    ∃ s₂, Steps p.toStandardForm s s₂ ∧
      s₂.isHalted p.toStandardForm ∧ s'.regs = s₂.regs

items.name: Cslib.URM.Halts.toStandardForm
items.doc: Forward halting theorem.
items.statement:
theorem Halts.toStandardForm {p : Program} {inputs : List ℕ} (h : Halts p inputs) :
    Halts p.toStandardForm inputs

items.name: Cslib.URM.Step.from_toStandardForm
items.doc:
Reverse step correspondence: if p.toStandardForm steps from s to s', then either:
(1) p steps from s to s' (same step), or
(2) s' is halted in p.toStandardForm, and p steps to a state that is also halted
    with the same registers (this only happens for jumps with unbounded targets).
items.statement:
theorem Step.from_toStandardForm {p : Program} {s s' : State} (hstep : Step p.toStandardForm s s') :
    Step p s s' ∨
    (s'.isHalted p.toStandardForm ∧ ∃ s₂, Step p s s₂ ∧ s₂.isHalted p ∧ s'.regs = s₂.regs)

items.name: Cslib.URM.Steps.from_toStandardForm_halts
items.doc:
Reverse halting: if p.toStandardForm reaches a halted state, p reaches a halted state
with the same registers.

items.name: Cslib.URM.Halts.of_toStandardForm
items.doc: Reverse halting theorem.
items.statement:
theorem Halts.of_toStandardForm {p : Program} {inputs : List ℕ}
    (h : Halts p.toStandardForm inputs) : Halts p inputs

items.name: Cslib.URM.Halts.toStandardForm_iff
items.doc: Halting equivalence: original halts iff standard form halts.
items.statement:
theorem Halts.toStandardForm_iff {p : Program} {inputs : List ℕ} :
    Halts p inputs ↔ Halts p.toStandardForm inputs

items.name: Cslib.URM.evalState_toStandardForm_regs
items.doc: Registers preservation: both reach states with the same registers.
items.statement:
theorem evalState_toStandardForm_regs {p : Program} {inputs : List ℕ}
    (hp : (evalState p inputs).Dom) (hq : (evalState p.toStandardForm inputs).Dom) :
    ((evalState p inputs).get hp).regs =
      ((evalState p.toStandardForm inputs).get hq).regs

items.name: Cslib.URM.eval_toStandardForm
items.doc: eval equality: both programs produce the same partial result.
items.statement:
theorem eval_toStandardForm {p : Program} {inputs : List ℕ} :
    eval p inputs = eval p.toStandardForm inputs

items.name: Cslib.URM.toStandardForm_equiv
items.doc: A program is equivalent to its standard form.
items.statement: theorem toStandardForm_equiv (p : Program) : p.toStandardForm ≈ p

modules.title: Straight-Line Programs
modules.doc:
This file defines straight-line programs (those without jumps) and proves
they always halt exactly at their length.

## Main definitions

- `Program.IsStraightLine`: a program contains no jump instructions

## Main results

- `straight_line_halts`: straight-line programs always halt
- `straightLinefinalState`: final state after running a straight-line program

items.name: Cslib.URM.Program.IsStraightLine
items.doc: A program is "straight-line" if it contains no jump instructions.
items.statement: def Program.IsStraightLine (p : Program) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.URM.Program.IsStraightLine.append
items.doc: Append preserves straight-line property.

items.name: Cslib.URM.Program.IsStraightLine.cons
items.doc: Cons of non-jumping instruction preserves straight-line.

items.name: Cslib.URM.Program.IsStraightLine.singleton
items.doc: Singleton non-jumping instruction is straight-line.
items.statement:
theorem Program.IsStraightLine.singleton {instr : Instr}
    (h : ¬instr.IsJump) : Program.IsStraightLine [instr]

items.name: Cslib.URM.Step.of_nonJump
items.doc: A non-jumping instruction produces a step that increments PC by 1.
items.statement:
theorem Step.of_nonJump {p : Program} {s : State} (hlt : s.pc < p.length)
    (hnonjump : ¬(p[s.pc]'hlt).IsJump) :
    ∃ s', Step p s s' ∧ s'.pc = s.pc + 1

items.name: Cslib.URM.straight_line_halts_from_regs
items.doc:
Straight-line programs halt from any starting registers, not just State.init.
Useful for chaining: after running one program, we can run the next
straight-line segment from whatever registers we're in.
items.statement:
theorem straight_line_halts_from_regs {p : Program} (hsl : p.IsStraightLine) (r : Regs) :
    ∃ s, Steps p ⟨0, r⟩ s ∧ s.isHalted p ∧ s.pc = p.length

items.name: Cslib.URM.straight_line_halts
items.doc: A straight-line program halts on any input.
items.statement:
theorem straight_line_halts {p : Program} (hsl : p.IsStraightLine) (inputs : List ℕ) :
    Halts p inputs

items.name: Cslib.URM.straightLinefinalState
items.doc:
The halting state for a straight-line program starting from registers r.
Wraps Classical.choose to hide it from the API.
items.statement:
noncomputable def straightLinefinalState {p : Program}
    (hsl : p.IsStraightLine) (r : Regs) : State

items.name: Cslib.URM.straightLinefinalState_spec
items.doc:
Specification: the state from straightLinefinalState satisfies Steps, isHalted,
and has pc = p.length.
items.statement:
theorem straightLinefinalState_spec {p : Program} (hsl : p.IsStraightLine) (r : Regs) :
    let s := straightLinefinalState hsl r
    Steps p ⟨0, r⟩ s ∧ s.isHalted p ∧ s.pc = p.length

items.name: Cslib.URM.straightLineFinalRegs
items.doc: The final registers after running a straight-line program from given starting registers.
items.statement: noncomputable def straightLineFinalRegs {p : Program} (hsl : p.IsStraightLine) (r : Regs) : Regs

items.name: Cslib.URM.straightLineFinalRegs_eq_of_halted
items.doc: For a straight-line program, s.regs equals straightLineFinalRegs if halted from r.
items.statement:
theorem straightLineFinalRegs_eq_of_halted {p : Program} (hsl : p.IsStraightLine)
    (r : Regs) (s : State) (hsteps : Steps p ⟨0, r⟩ s) (hhalted : s.isHalted p) :
    s.regs = straightLineFinalRegs hsl r

items.name: Cslib.URM.straight_line_state_at_pc
items.doc:
In a straight-line program, we can characterize the state at any intermediate pc.
This gives us the state after executing instructions 0..pc-1.
items.statement:
theorem straight_line_state_at_pc {p : Program} (hsl : p.IsStraightLine)
    (r : Regs) (targetPc : ℕ) (htarget : targetPc ≤ p.length) :
    ∃ s, Steps p ⟨0, r⟩ s ∧ s.pc = targetPc

modules.title: Negligible functions
modules.doc:
Negligible bounds are nonnegative real-valued functions with Mathlib's superpolynomial decay at
natural security parameters. This module supplies zero, addition, multiplication, fixed finite
sums, eventual comparison, and polynomial-loss bounds for security games. Changing finitely many
values preserves negligibility.

The decay bound may depend on the whole algorithm. Security definitions quantify over that
algorithm before asserting negligibility; this module does not change that quantifier order.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Negligible
items.statement: def Negligible (ε : ℕ → ℝ≥0) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.negligible_iff
items.statement:
theorem negligible_iff (ε : ℕ → ℝ≥0) :
    Negligible ε ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ δ > (0 : ℝ≥0), ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ m, n ^ k * ε n < δ

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.negligible_zero
items.doc: The zero advantage is negligible.
items.statement: theorem negligible_zero : Negligible (fun _ => 0)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Negligible.congr'
items.doc:
Changing the value of a negligible bound at finitely many security parameters preserves
negligibility.
items.statement:
theorem Negligible.congr' {ε δ : ℕ → ℝ≥0} (hε : Negligible ε)
    (h : ε =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] δ) : Negligible δ

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Negligible.add
items.doc: The sum of two negligible bounds is negligible.
items.statement:
theorem Negligible.add {ε δ : ℕ → ℝ≥0} (hε : Negligible ε) (hδ : Negligible δ) :
    Negligible (ε + δ)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Negligible.mul
items.doc: The product of two negligible bounds is negligible.
items.statement:
theorem Negligible.mul {ε δ : ℕ → ℝ≥0} (hε : Negligible ε) (hδ : Negligible δ) :
    Negligible (ε * δ)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Negligible.sum
items.doc: A sum over a fixed finite set of negligible bounds is negligible.
items.statement:
theorem Negligible.sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) {ε : ι → ℕ → ℝ≥0}
    (hε : ∀ i ∈ s, Negligible (ε i)) : Negligible (∑ i ∈ s, ε i)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.negligible_of_eventually_le
items.doc: An eventually smaller advantage is negligible.
items.statement:
theorem negligible_of_eventually_le {ε δ : ℕ → ℝ≥0} (hδ : Negligible δ)
    (hle : ε ≤ᶠ[Filter.atTop] δ) : Negligible ε

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.negligible_of_le
items.doc: A pointwise smaller advantage is negligible.
items.statement:
theorem negligible_of_le {ε δ : ℕ → ℝ≥0} (hδ : Negligible δ)
    (hle : ∀ n, ε n ≤ δ n) : Negligible ε

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Negligible.polynomiallyBounded_mul
items.doc: Polynomially bounded factors preserve negligible decay.

modules.title: Asymptotic pseudorandom generator security
modules.doc:
Security for families of generators means negligible advantage for each admissible
adversary family, following [BonehShoup2023], Definition 3.1. Negligibility uses Mathlib's
`Asymptotics.SuperpolynomialDecay`. Admissibility is a predicate on the whole adversary
family, so a downstream computational model can express a uniform resource restriction.
This model has a natural-number security parameter and no sampled public system parameters.
Efficiency of generation and sampling is not asserted by these semantic definitions.

`SecureWithError` bounds every admissible family's advantage at parameter `n` by `ε n`.
A negligible bound implies `Secure`.

A non-negligible lower bound on the fraction of outputs outside the image rules out security
when the range-test family is admissible. In particular, a bitstring family that eventually
stretches by at least one bit is insecure against any class admitting its range test.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family
items.doc: A security-parameter-indexed collection of deterministic generators.
items.statement: abbrev Family (Seed Output : ℕ → Type*)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.Secure
items.doc:
Every admissible adversary family has negligible distinguishing advantage.
The predicate can encode computational restrictions; `fun _ => True` permits all families.
items.statement:
def Secure (G : Family Seed Output)
    (Admissible : (∀ n, Adversary (Output n)) → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.Secure.of_admissible
items.doc: Restricting the admissible adversary families preserves asymptotic security.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.SecureWithError
items.doc: Every admissible adversary family has advantage at most `ε n` at each parameter `n`.
items.statement:
def SecureWithError (G : Family Seed Output)
    (Admissible : (∀ n, Adversary (Output n)) → Prop) (ε : ℕ → ℝ≥0) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.SecureWithError.secure
items.doc: A negligible error bound implies asymptotic security.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.not_secure_of_rangeAdversary
items.doc:
A non-negligible lower bound on the fraction of outputs outside the image rules out
security whenever exhaustive range testing is admissible.
items.statement:
theorem not_secure_of_rangeAdversary (G : Family Seed Output)
    {Admissible : (∀ n, Adversary (Output n)) → Prop}
    (ha : Admissible (fun n => (G n).rangeAdversary)) {δ : ℕ → ℝ≥0}
    (hδ : ¬ Asymptotics.SuperpolynomialDecay atTop (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))
      (fun n => (δ n : ℝ)))
    (hgap : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      (δ n : ℝ) ≤ 1 - Nat.card (Set.range (G n)) / (Fintype.card (Output n) : ℝ)) :
    ¬ G.Secure Admissible

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.not_secure_of_two_mul_card_le
items.doc:
If outputs eventually outnumber seeds by a factor of two, admissibility of exhaustive
seed enumeration and output comparison suffices to rule out security.
items.statement:
theorem not_secure_of_two_mul_card_le (G : Family Seed Output)
    {Admissible : (∀ n, Adversary (Output n)) → Prop}
    (ha : Admissible (fun n => (G n).rangeAdversary))
    (hsize : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 2 * Fintype.card (Seed n) ≤ Fintype.card (Output n)) :
    ¬ G.Secure Admissible

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.not_secure_of_bitstring_stretch
items.doc:
A bitstring generator that eventually stretches by at least one bit is insecure
against any class admitting its range-test family.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.not_exists_secure_bitstring_stretch
items.doc:
No bitstring generator family that eventually stretches by at least one bit is secure
against all adversary families.
items.statement:
theorem not_exists_secure_bitstring_stretch {seedLength outputLength : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hstretch : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, seedLength n < outputLength n) :
    ¬ ∃ G : Family (fun n => Fin (seedLength n) → Bool)
      (fun n => Fin (outputLength n) → Bool), G.Secure (fun _ => True)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.not_secure_of_bitVec_stretch
items.doc:
A `BitVec` generator that eventually stretches by at least one bit is insecure
against any class admitting its range-test family.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Family.not_exists_secure_bitVec_stretch
items.doc:
No `BitVec` generator family that eventually stretches by at least one bit is secure
against all adversary families.
items.statement:
theorem not_exists_secure_bitVec_stretch {seedLength outputLength : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hstretch : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, seedLength n < outputLength n) :
    ¬ ∃ G : Family (fun n => BitVec (seedLength n)) (fun n => BitVec (outputLength n)),
      G.Secure (fun _ => True)

modules.title: Pseudorandom generators against arbitrary adversaries
modules.doc:
The range-membership test accepts every generated output, whereas it accepts a uniform
output with probability `|range G| / |Output|`. Its advantage is therefore at least
`1 - |Seed| / |Output|`. This proves that an expanding generator cannot have zero
advantage against arbitrary adversaries, and gives a quantitative obstruction for
every smaller error bound. No injectivity assumption on the generator is needed.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.advantage_nonneg
items.doc: Advantage is nonnegative.
items.statement:
theorem advantage_nonneg (G : Generator Seed Output) (adversary : Adversary Output) :
    0 ≤ G.advantage adversary

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.advantage_le_one
items.doc: Advantage is at most one, with the normalization of Attack Game 3.1.
items.statement:
theorem advantage_le_one (G : Generator Seed Output) (adversary : Adversary Output) :
    G.advantage adversary ≤ 1

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.secure_one
items.doc: Error one imposes no restriction on a generator.
items.statement:
theorem secure_one (G : Generator Seed Output) (Admissible : Adversary Output → Prop) :
    G.Secure Admissible 1

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.advantage_const
items.doc: A test whose output distribution is independent of its input has zero advantage.
items.statement:
theorem advantage_const (G : Generator Seed Output) (p : PMF Bool) :
    G.advantage (fun _ => p) = 0

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.secure_zero_of_outputDist_eq
items.doc: A generator with exactly uniform output is secure with zero error against any tests.
items.statement:
theorem secure_zero_of_outputDist_eq (G : Generator Seed Output)
    (hG : G.outputDist = uniformOfFintype Output)
    (Admissible : Adversary Output → Prop) : G.Secure Admissible 0

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.secure_zero_iff_outputDist_eq_uniform
items.doc: Zero-error security against arbitrary tests is equivalent to exactly uniform output.
items.statement:
theorem secure_zero_iff_outputDist_eq_uniform (G : Generator Seed Output) :
    G.Secure (fun _ => True) 0 ↔ G.outputDist = uniformOfFintype Output

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.Secure.mono
items.doc: Enlarging the allowed advantage preserves security.
items.statement:
theorem Secure.mono {G : Generator Seed Output} {Admissible : Adversary Output → Prop} :
    Monotone (G.Secure Admissible)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.Secure.of_admissible
items.doc: Security against a larger class of adversaries implies security against a smaller class.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.rangeTest
items.doc: Decide range membership by finite seed enumeration and output comparison.
items.statement: def rangeTest (G : Generator Seed Output) (output : Output) : Bool

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.rangeAdversary
items.doc: The deterministic adversary that tests membership in the generator's range.
items.statement: noncomputable def rangeAdversary (G : Generator Seed Output) : Adversary Output

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.realExperiment_rangeAdversary
items.doc: The range test always accepts a generated output.
items.statement:
theorem realExperiment_rangeAdversary (G : Generator Seed Output) :
    G.realExperiment G.rangeAdversary = PMF.pure true

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.idealExperiment_rangeAdversary
items.doc:
The range test's acceptance probability under uniform sampling is the fraction
of outputs in the range.
items.statement:
theorem idealExperiment_rangeAdversary (G : Generator Seed Output) :
    (idealExperiment G.rangeAdversary true).toReal =
      Nat.card (Set.range G) / (Fintype.card Output : ℝ)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.advantage_rangeAdversary
items.doc: The exact advantage of the range-membership adversary.
items.statement:
theorem advantage_rangeAdversary (G : Generator Seed Output) :
    G.advantage G.rangeAdversary =
      1 - Nat.card (Set.range G) / (Fintype.card Output : ℝ)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.one_sub_card_div_le_advantage_rangeAdversary
items.doc:
Every generator has an unbounded distinguisher with advantage at least
`1 - |Seed| / |Output|`. Collisions can only improve this attack.
items.statement:
theorem one_sub_card_div_le_advantage_rangeAdversary (G : Generator Seed Output) :
    1 - Fintype.card Seed / (Fintype.card Output : ℝ) ≤
      G.advantage G.rangeAdversary

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.not_secure_of_rangeAdversary
items.doc: Security is impossible below the range-test bound whenever that test is admissible.
items.statement:
theorem not_secure_of_rangeAdversary (G : Generator Seed Output)
    {Admissible : Adversary Output → Prop} {ε : ℝ≥0}
    (ha : Admissible G.rangeAdversary)
    (hε : (ε : ℝ) < 1 - Fintype.card Seed / (Fintype.card Output : ℝ)) :
    ¬ G.Secure Admissible ε

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.not_secure_zero_of_isExpanding
items.doc: An expanding generator cannot be perfectly secure against arbitrary adversaries.
items.statement:
theorem not_secure_zero_of_isExpanding (G : Generator Seed Output) (hG : G.IsExpanding) :
    ¬ G.Secure (fun _ => True) 0

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.not_exists_isExpanding_secure_zero
items.doc: There is no expanding, perfectly secure generator against arbitrary adversaries.
items.statement:
theorem not_exists_isExpanding_secure_zero :
    ¬ ∃ G : Generator Seed Output, G.IsExpanding ∧ G.Secure (fun _ => True) 0

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.prod
items.doc: Apply `G` separately to each component of a pair of seeds.
items.statement: def prod (G : Generator Seed Output) : Generator (Seed × Seed) (Output × Output)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.outputDist_prod
items.doc: The output distribution of `G.prod` is two independent draws from `G.outputDist`.
items.statement:
theorem outputDist_prod (G : Generator Seed Output) :
    G.prod.outputDist =
      G.outputDist.bind fun y₁ => G.outputDist.map fun y₂ => (y₁, y₂)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.leftReduction
items.doc: First hybrid distinguisher: given `y₁`, sample `y₂ ← G.outputDist` and run `A (y₁, y₂)`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def leftReduction (G : Generator Seed Output)
    (A : Adversary (Output × Output)) : Adversary Output

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.rightReduction
items.doc: Second hybrid distinguisher: given `y₂`, sample `u₁ ←$ Output` and run `A (u₁, y₂)`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def rightReduction
    (A : Adversary (Output × Output)) : Adversary Output

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.realExperiment_prod
items.doc:
Real experiment for `G.prod` equals the real experiment for `G` against
`leftReduction`.
items.statement:
theorem realExperiment_prod (G : Generator Seed Output)
    (A : Adversary (Output × Output)) :
    G.prod.realExperiment A = G.realExperiment (G.leftReduction A)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.idealExperiment_leftReduction
items.doc:
Ideal experiment against `leftReduction` equals the real experiment against
`rightReduction` (both equal the hybrid distribution `(u₁, G(x₂))`).
items.statement:
theorem idealExperiment_leftReduction (G : Generator Seed Output)
    (A : Adversary (Output × Output)) :
    idealExperiment (G.leftReduction A) = G.realExperiment (rightReduction A)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.idealExperiment_rightReduction
items.doc: Ideal experiment against `rightReduction` equals the ideal experiment for `G.prod`.
items.statement:
theorem idealExperiment_rightReduction (A : Adversary (Output × Output)) :
    idealExperiment (rightReduction A) = idealExperiment A

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.advantage_prod_le
items.doc: Hybrid advantage bound: `Adv(G.prod, A) ≤ Adv(G, leftReduction) + Adv(G, rightReduction)`.
items.statement:
theorem advantage_prod_le (G : Generator Seed Output)
    (A : Adversary (Output × Output)) :
    G.prod.advantage A ≤
      G.advantage (G.leftReduction A) + G.advantage (rightReduction A)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.Secure.prod
items.doc: Concrete security of `H(x₁, x₂) = (G(x₁), G(x₂))` via a two-step hybrid argument.

modules.title: Pseudorandom generators: games and concrete security
modules.doc:
Attack Game 3.1 of [BonehShoup2023] compares a deterministic generator applied to a
uniform seed with a uniform output. Adversaries are randomized Boolean tests. Security
is relative to a caller-supplied predicate `Admissible`, with an explicit advantage bound.
No computational model or efficiency assumption is built into the generator or the tests.

`Generator.IsExpanding` records the cardinality condition separately from security.
In particular, a generator need not expand, and an expanding generator need not be secure.

## References

* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023], Section 3.1.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator
items.doc:
A deterministic generator with seed space `Seed` and output space `Output`.
Efficiency, expansion, and security are separate properties.
items.statement:
structure Generator (Seed Output : Type*) where
  /-- Generate an output from a seed. -/
  toFun : Seed → Output

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Adversary
items.doc: A randomized statistical test on the output space.
items.statement: abbrev Adversary (Output : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.coe_mk
items.statement: theorem coe_mk (f : Seed → Output) : ⇑(Generator.mk f) = f

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.IsExpanding
items.doc: A generator expands when its output space is strictly larger than its seed space.
items.statement: def IsExpanding [Fintype Seed] [Fintype Output] (_G : Generator Seed Output) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.outputDist
items.doc: The distribution obtained by applying the generator to a uniform seed.
items.statement: noncomputable def outputDist (G : Generator Seed Output) : PMF Output

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.realExperiment
items.doc: Experiment 0 of Attack Game 3.1: give the adversary a generated output.
items.statement:
noncomputable def realExperiment (G : Generator Seed Output)
    (adversary : Adversary Output) : PMF Bool

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.idealExperiment
items.doc: Experiment 1 of Attack Game 3.1: give the adversary a uniform output.
items.statement: noncomputable def idealExperiment (adversary : Adversary Output) : PMF Bool

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.advantage
items.doc:
The absolute difference of the probabilities of outputting `true` in the two
experiments, as in Attack Game 3.1 of [BonehShoup2023].
items.statement: noncomputable def advantage (G : Generator Seed Output) (adversary : Adversary Output) : ℝ

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.Secure
items.doc:
Concrete security against admissible adversaries. The predicate is supplied by the
caller, for example to restrict tests to a chosen computational resource bound.
Taking `Admissible := fun _ => True` allows arbitrary adversaries.
items.statement:
def Secure (G : Generator Seed Output) (Admissible : Adversary Output → Prop)
    (ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop

modules.title: Commitment Schemes
modules.doc:
Basic results about information-theoretic commitment schemes.

The main result is the hiding–binding trade-off: a perfectly binding scheme
places the commitment distributions of distinct messages at the maximum
statistical distance, so it cannot be statistically hiding for any error below
one. Hiding and binding can therefore not both hold unconditionally; real
schemes make at most one side information-theoretic and settle for a
computational version of the other.

## Main results

- `Scheme.subsingleton_of_statisticallyHiding_of_perfectlyBinding`: a scheme
  cannot be both statistically hiding with error below one and perfectly
  binding unless any two messages are equal
- `Scheme.PerfectlyBinding.dist_commitmentDist_eq_one`: perfect binding forces
  distinct messages' commitment distributions to the maximum statistical
  distance
- `Scheme.subsingleton_of_perfectlyHiding_of_perfectlyBinding`: the perfect
  hiding case, with no finiteness assumption on commitments
- `Scheme.perfectlyHiding_iff_statisticallyHiding_zero`: perfect hiding is
  statistical hiding with zero error

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.perfectlyHiding_iff_statisticallyHiding_zero
items.doc: Perfect hiding is exactly statistical hiding with zero error.
items.statement:
theorem perfectlyHiding_iff_statisticallyHiding_zero
    [Fintype Commitment] (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening) :
    scheme.PerfectlyHiding ↔ scheme.StatisticallyHiding 0

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.StatisticallyHiding.mono
items.doc: Enlarging the permitted error preserves statistical hiding.
items.statement:
theorem StatisticallyHiding.mono [Fintype Commitment]
    {scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening} :
    Monotone scheme.StatisticallyHiding

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.PerfectlyBinding.disjoint_support_commitmentDist
items.doc:
Distinct messages of a perfectly binding scheme have disjoint sets of
possible commitments.
items.statement:
theorem PerfectlyBinding.disjoint_support_commitmentDist
    {scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening} (hbind : scheme.PerfectlyBinding)
    {message₀ message₁ : Message} (hne : message₀ ≠ message₁) :
    Disjoint (scheme.commitmentDist message₀).support
      (scheme.commitmentDist message₁).support

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.PerfectlyBinding.dist_commitmentDist_eq_one
items.doc:
In a perfectly binding scheme, the commitment distributions of distinct
messages are at the maximum statistical distance: an unbounded observer can
read the message off the commitment.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.subsingleton_of_statisticallyHiding_of_perfectlyBinding
items.doc:
**The hiding–binding trade-off.** A scheme cannot be both statistically
hiding with error below one and perfectly binding unless any two messages are
equal. The error bound is sharp: statistical hiding with error one holds
vacuously for every scheme.
items.statement:
theorem subsingleton_of_statisticallyHiding_of_perfectlyBinding
    [Fintype Commitment] (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening) {ε : ℝ≥0}
    (hε : ε < 1) (hhide : scheme.StatisticallyHiding ε)
    (hbind : scheme.PerfectlyBinding) : Subsingleton Message

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.subsingleton_of_perfectlyHiding_of_perfectlyBinding
items.doc:
A scheme cannot be both perfectly hiding and perfectly binding unless any
two messages are equal. Unlike the statistical version, this needs no
finiteness assumption on the commitment type.
items.statement:
theorem subsingleton_of_perfectlyHiding_of_perfectlyBinding
    (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening)
    (hhide : scheme.PerfectlyHiding) (hbind : scheme.PerfectlyBinding) :
    Subsingleton Message

modules.title: Commitment Schemes: Information-Theoretic Security
modules.doc:
Hiding and binding for commitment schemes, in their information-theoretic forms
([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.12). Perfect hiding: every message yields the same
commitment distribution. Statistical hiding: any two commitment distributions
are within statistical distance `ε`. Perfect binding: no commitment can be
opened to two different messages, even by an unbounded committer.

Each definition is about a single, fixed scheme; statistical hiding carries an
explicit error bound, and the perfect notions have no error at all. The
asymptotic notions in the book — negligible statistical distance for families
of distributions ([BonehShoup2023], Definition 3.6), or security against
efficient adversaries (Section 8.12) — can be layered on top of these later.

## Main definitions

- `Scheme.PerfectlyHiding`: the commitment distributions are equal for every
  pair of messages
- `Scheme.StatisticallyHiding`: the commitment distributions are statistically
  close with error `ε`
- `Scheme.PerfectlyBinding`: no commitment has accepted openings to two
  different messages

## References

* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.PerfectlyHiding
items.doc:
A scheme is perfectly hiding when every message yields the same commitment
distribution, so a commitment reveals nothing about the message as long as its
opening is withheld ([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.12).
items.statement: def PerfectlyHiding (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.StatisticallyHiding
items.doc:
A scheme is statistically hiding with error `ε` when the commitment
distributions of any two messages are within statistical distance `ε`
([BonehShoup2023], Definition 3.5 and Section 8.12).
items.statement:
def StatisticallyHiding [Fintype Commitment]
    (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening) (ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.PerfectlyBinding
items.doc:
A scheme is perfectly binding when a commitment can be opened to at most
one message: any two accepted openings of the same commitment agree on the
message ([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.12). Different openings of the same
message are still allowed.
items.statement: def PerfectlyBinding (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening) : Prop

modules.title: Commitment Schemes: Syntax and Correctness
modules.doc:
The syntax of a commitment scheme ([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.12): committing
to a message samples a commitment-opening pair `(c, o)`, verification of a
claimed opening is deterministic, and honestly generated pairs always verify.

The algorithms are plain functions, with no efficiency or finiteness
assumptions. Security notions live in separate definitions, so the same syntax
can carry perfect, statistical, or computational security.

## Main definitions

- `Scheme`: commitment syntax with perfect correctness
- `Scheme.commitmentDist`: the public commitment distribution for a message
- `Scheme.mem_support_commitmentDist_iff`: a commitment is possible exactly
  when it has a possible opening
- `Scheme.Accepts`: the verifier's acceptance relation

## References

* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme
items.doc:
A noninteractive, unkeyed commitment scheme over message, commitment, and
opening types ([BonehShoup2023], Section 8.12).

Committing is randomized and produces the commitment and opening together,
since the two may be correlated. Correctness requires that every
commitment-opening pair the honest committer can output is accepted by the
verifier; for a `PMF`, this says honest openings verify with probability
one.
items.statement:
structure Scheme (Message Commitment Opening : Type*) where
  /-- Randomized commitment and opening generation. -/
  commit (message : Message) : PMF (Commitment × Opening)
  /-- Deterministic verification of a claimed opening. -/
  verify (message : Message) (commitment : Commitment) (opening : Opening) : Bool
  /-- Every honestly generated commitment-opening pair verifies. -/
  correct : ∀ message commitment opening,
    (commitment, opening) ∈ (commit message).support →
      verify message commitment opening = true

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.commitmentDist
items.doc: The public commitment distribution obtained by forgetting the opening.
items.statement:
noncomputable def commitmentDist (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening)
    (message : Message) : PMF Commitment

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.mem_support_commitmentDist_iff
items.doc:
A commitment lies in the public distribution's support exactly when some
opening makes the corresponding pair an honest possible output.
items.statement:
theorem mem_support_commitmentDist_iff
    (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening) {message : Message}
    {commitment : Commitment} :
    commitment ∈ (scheme.commitmentDist message).support ↔
      ∃ opening, (commitment, opening) ∈ (scheme.commit message).support

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.Accepts
items.doc: The proposition that an opening is accepted for a commitment and message.
items.statement:
def Accepts (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening) (message : Message)
    (commitment : Commitment) (opening : Opening) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.accepts_of_mem_support
items.doc: Every pair in the support of an honest commitment is accepted.
items.statement:
theorem accepts_of_mem_support (scheme : Scheme Message Commitment Opening)
    {message : Message} {commitment : Commitment} {opening : Opening}
    (h : (commitment, opening) ∈ (scheme.commit message).support) :
    scheme.Accepts message commitment opening

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.Commitment.Scheme.ofPure
items.doc: Build a commitment scheme from a deterministic commitment generation.
items.statement:
noncomputable def ofPure (commit : Message → Commitment × Opening)
    (verify : Message → Commitment → Opening → Bool)
    (correct : ∀ message, verify message (commit message).1 (commit message).2 = true) :
    Scheme Message Commitment Opening

modules.title: Perfect Secrecy
modules.doc:
Characterisation theorems for perfect secrecy following
[KatzLindell2020], Chapter 2: the equivalence with message-ciphertext
independence, the ciphertext indistinguishability characterization, and
Shannon's key-space bound.

## Main results

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.perfectlySecret_iff_indep`:
  perfect secrecy is exactly message-ciphertext independence
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.perfectlySecret_iff_ciphertextIndist`:
  ciphertext indistinguishability characterization ([KatzLindell2020], Lemma 2.5)
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.perfectlySecret_keySpace_ge`:
  Shannon's theorem, `|K| ≥ |M|` ([KatzLindell2020], Theorem 2.12)

## References

* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.jointDist_eq
items.doc: The joint distribution at `(m, c)` equals `msgDist m * ciphertextDist m c`.
items.statement:
theorem jointDist_eq (scheme : EncScheme M K C) (msgDist : PMF M)
    (m : M) (c : C) :
    scheme.jointDist msgDist (m, c) = msgDist m * scheme.ciphertextDist m c

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.jointDist_tsum_fst
items.doc:
Summing the joint distribution over messages gives the marginal ciphertext
distribution.
items.statement:
theorem jointDist_tsum_fst (scheme : EncScheme M K C) (msgDist : PMF M) (c : C) :
    ∑' m, scheme.jointDist msgDist (m, c) = scheme.marginalCiphertextDist msgDist c

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.perfectlySecret_iff_indep
items.doc:
Perfect secrecy is equivalent to message-ciphertext independence.
The two formulations are related by multiplying/dividing by `marginal(c)`.
items.statement:
theorem perfectlySecret_iff_indep (scheme : EncScheme M K C) :
    scheme.PerfectlySecret ↔
    ∀ (msgDist : PMF M) (m : M) (c : C),
      scheme.jointDist msgDist (m, c) =
        msgDist m * scheme.marginalCiphertextDist msgDist c

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.perfectlySecret_iff_ciphertextIndist
items.doc:
A scheme is perfectly secret iff the ciphertext distribution is
independent of the plaintext ([KatzLindell2020], Lemma 2.5).
items.statement:
theorem perfectlySecret_iff_ciphertextIndist (scheme : EncScheme M K C) :
    scheme.PerfectlySecret ↔ scheme.CiphertextIndist

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.indep_of_ciphertextIndist
items.doc: Ciphertext indistinguishability implies message-ciphertext independence.
items.statement:
theorem indep_of_ciphertextIndist (scheme : EncScheme M K C)
    (h : scheme.CiphertextIndist) (msgDist : PMF M) (m : M) (c : C) :
    scheme.jointDist msgDist (m, c) =
      msgDist m * scheme.marginalCiphertextDist msgDist c

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.perfectlySecret_keySpace_ge
items.doc:
Perfect secrecy requires `|K| ≥ |M|` — Shannon's theorem
([KatzLindell2020], Theorem 2.12).
items.statement:
theorem perfectlySecret_keySpace_ge [Finite K]
    (scheme : EncScheme M K C) (h : scheme.PerfectlySecret) :
    Nat.card M ≤ Nat.card K

modules.title: Perfect Secrecy: Definitions
modules.doc:
Core definitions for perfect secrecy following [KatzLindell2020], Chapter 2.

## Main definitions

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.ciphertextDist`:
  ciphertext distribution for a given message
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.jointDist`:
  joint (message, ciphertext) distribution given a message prior
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.marginalCiphertextDist`:
  marginal ciphertext distribution given a message prior
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.posteriorMsgDist`:
  posterior message distribution `Pr[M | C = c]` as a `PMF`
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.PerfectlySecret`:
  perfect secrecy ([KatzLindell2020], Definition 2.3)
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.CiphertextIndist`:
  ciphertext indistinguishability ([KatzLindell2020], Lemma 2.5)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.ciphertextDist
items.doc: The distribution of `Enc_K(m)` when `K ← Gen`.
items.statement: noncomputable def ciphertextDist (scheme : EncScheme M K C) (m : M) : PMF C

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.jointDist
items.doc: Joint distribution of `(M, C)` given a message prior.
items.statement: noncomputable def jointDist (scheme : EncScheme M K C) (msgDist : PMF M) : PMF (M × C)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.marginalCiphertextDist
items.doc: Marginal ciphertext distribution given a message prior.
items.statement:
noncomputable def marginalCiphertextDist (scheme : EncScheme M K C)
    (msgDist : PMF M) : PMF C

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.posteriorMsgDist
items.doc:
The posterior message distribution `Pr[M | C = c]` as a probability
distribution, given a message prior and a ciphertext in the support of
the marginal distribution.
items.statement:
noncomputable def posteriorMsgDist (scheme : EncScheme M K C)
    (msgDist : PMF M) (c : C)
    (hc : c ∈ (scheme.marginalCiphertextDist msgDist).support) : PMF M

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.posteriorMsgDist_apply
items.statement:
theorem posteriorMsgDist_apply (scheme : EncScheme M K C)
    (msgDist : PMF M) (c : C)
    (hc : c ∈ (scheme.marginalCiphertextDist msgDist).support) (m : M) :
    scheme.posteriorMsgDist msgDist c hc m =
      scheme.jointDist msgDist (m, c) / scheme.marginalCiphertextDist msgDist c

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.PerfectlySecret
items.doc:
An encryption scheme is perfectly secret if the posterior message
distribution equals the prior for every ciphertext with positive probability
([KatzLindell2020], Definition 2.3).
items.statement: def PerfectlySecret (scheme : EncScheme M K C) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.CiphertextIndist
items.doc:
Ciphertext indistinguishability: the ciphertext distribution is the same
for all messages ([KatzLindell2020], Lemma 2.5).
items.statement: def CiphertextIndist (scheme : EncScheme M K C) : Prop

modules.title: Private-Key Encryption Schemes (Information-Theoretic)
modules.doc:
An information-theoretic private-key encryption scheme following
[KatzLindell2020], Definition 2.1. Key generation and encryption are
probability distributions over arbitrary types, with no computational
constraints.

## Main definitions

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme`:
  a private-key encryption scheme (Gen, Enc, Dec) with correctness

## References

* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme
items.doc:
A private-key encryption scheme over message space `M`, key space `K`,
and ciphertext space `C` ([KatzLindell2020], Definition 2.1).
items.statement:
structure EncScheme (Message Key Ciphertext : Type*) where
  /-- Probabilistic key generation. -/
  gen : PMF Key
  /-- (Possibly randomized) encryption. -/
  enc (key : Key) (message : Message) : PMF Ciphertext
  /-- Deterministic decryption. -/
  dec (key : Key) (ciphertext : Ciphertext) : Message
  /-- Decryption inverts encryption for all keys in the support of `gen`. -/
  correct : ∀ key, key ∈ gen.support → ∀ message ciphertext,
    ciphertext ∈ (enc key message).support → dec key ciphertext = message

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.EncScheme.ofPure
items.doc:
Build an encryption scheme from deterministic pure encryption/decryption
where decryption is a left inverse of encryption for every key.
items.statement:
noncomputable def EncScheme.ofPure.{u} {Message Key Ciphertext : Type u} (gen : PMF Key)
    (enc : Key → Message → Ciphertext) (dec : Key → Ciphertext → Message)
    (h : ∀ key, Function.LeftInverse (dec key) (enc key)) :
    EncScheme Message Key Ciphertext

modules.title: One-Time Pad
modules.doc:
The one-time pad (Vernam cipher) over `BitVec l`
([KatzLindell2020], Construction 2.9).

## Main definitions

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.otp`: the one-time pad encryption scheme

## Main results

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.otp_perfectlySecret`:
  the one-time pad is perfectly secret ([KatzLindell2020], Theorem 2.10)

## References

* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.otp
items.doc:
The one-time pad over `l`-bit strings. Encryption and decryption
are XOR ([KatzLindell2020], Construction 2.9).
items.statement:
noncomputable def otp (l : ℕ) :
    EncScheme (BitVec l) (BitVec l) (BitVec l)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.otp_ciphertextDist_eq_uniform
items.doc:
The ciphertext distribution of the OTP is uniform, regardless of the
message: masking with a uniform key is the permutation `Equiv.xor` of the
uniform distribution.
items.statement:
theorem otp_ciphertextDist_eq_uniform (l : ℕ) (m : BitVec l) :
    (otp l).ciphertextDist m = uniformOfFintype (BitVec l)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.PerfectSecrecy.otp_perfectlySecret
items.doc: The one-time pad is perfectly secret ([KatzLindell2020], Theorem 2.10).
items.statement: theorem otp_perfectlySecret (l : ℕ) : (otp l).PerfectlySecret

modules.title: Secret Sharing: Definitions
modules.doc:
Privacy for secret sharing is part of the `Scheme` interface. This file exposes
the corresponding view and posterior distributions, plus theorem-friendly
consequences of the built-in privacy field.

## Main definitions

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.shareDist`:
  the full share distribution for one secret
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.viewDist`:
  the distribution of the restricted view for one coalition
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.posteriorSecretDist`:
  the posterior distribution on secrets after observing one view
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectlyPrivate`:
  posterior equals prior for unauthorized coalitions
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.perfectlyPrivate`:
  every scheme has posterior privacy

## References

* [Adi Shamir, *How to Share a Secret*][Shamir1979]
* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.shareDist
items.doc: The distribution of the full share assignment for one secret.
items.statement:
noncomputable def shareDist (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share)
    (secret : Secret) : PMF (Party → Share)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.viewDist
items.doc: The view distribution induced on the coalition `s`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def viewDist (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share)
    (s : Finset Party) (secret : Secret) : PMF (s → Share)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.viewDist_eq_of_not_authorized
items.doc: Unauthorized coalitions receive secret-independent view distributions.
items.statement:
theorem viewDist_eq_of_not_authorized
    (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share)
    {s : Finset Party} (hs : ¬ scheme.authorized s)
    (secret₀ secret₁ : Secret) :
    scheme.viewDist s secret₀ = scheme.viewDist s secret₁

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.posteriorSecretDist
items.doc:
The posterior distribution on secrets after observing the coalition view
`v`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def posteriorSecretDist
    (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share)
    (s : Finset Party) (secretDist : PMF Secret) (v : s → Share)
    (hv : v ∈ (secretDist.bind (scheme.viewDist s)).support) : PMF Secret

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.posteriorSecretDist_apply
items.statement:
theorem posteriorSecretDist_apply
    (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share)
    (s : Finset Party) (secretDist : PMF Secret) (v : s → Share)
    (hv : v ∈ (secretDist.bind (scheme.viewDist s)).support) (secret : Secret) :
    scheme.posteriorSecretDist s secretDist v hv secret =
      (secretDist.bind fun secret' =>
        (scheme.viewDist s secret').bind fun v' => PMF.pure (secret', v')) (secret, v) /
        (secretDist.bind (scheme.viewDist s)) v

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectlyPrivate
items.doc:
Perfect privacy for unauthorized coalitions: conditioning on a view does not
change the prior on secrets.
items.statement: def PerfectlyPrivate (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.perfectlyPrivate
items.doc: Every scheme has posterior privacy by definition of `Scheme`.
items.statement:
theorem perfectlyPrivate
    (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share) :
    scheme.PerfectlyPrivate

modules.title: Secret Sharing Schemes
modules.doc:
A secret-sharing scheme bundles the deterministic sharing/reconstruction
interface, the distribution on randomness, and privacy for unauthorized
coalitions.

## Main definitions

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme`:
  a secret-sharing scheme with correctness and privacy
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.view`:
  the restricted shares seen by one coalition

## References

* [Adi Shamir, *How to Share a Secret*][Shamir1979]
* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.viewDistOf
items.doc: The view distribution induced by raw sharing data.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme
items.doc:
A secret-sharing scheme over secret space `Secret`, randomness space
`Randomness`, party set `Party`, and share space `Share`.

Correctness is deterministic: every authorized coalition reconstructs the
secret from the shares generated using any randomness seed. Privacy is
distributional: unauthorized coalitions have the same view distribution for all
secrets.
items.statement:
structure Scheme (Secret Randomness Party Share : Type*) where
  /-- The distribution used to sample the protocol's randomness. -/
  gen : PMF Randomness
  /-- Sharing algorithm: one randomness seed determines one share per party. -/
  share : Randomness → Secret → Party → Share
  /-- Reconstruction from a coalition's observed shares. -/
  reconstruct (s : Finset Party) : (s → Share) → Secret
  /-- Authorized coalitions. -/
  authorized : Finset Party → Prop
  /-- Authorization is monotone in the coalition. -/
  authorized_mono : Monotone authorized
  /-- Authorized coalitions reconstruct the secret from the restricted view. -/
  correct :
    ∀ (r : Randomness) (secret : Secret) (s : Finset Party),
      authorized s → reconstruct s (fun i => share r secret i) = secret
  /-- Unauthorized coalitions receive secret-independent view distributions. -/
  view_indist :
    ∀ (s : Finset Party), ¬ authorized s → ∀ secret₀ secret₁ : Secret,
      viewDistOf gen share s secret₀ = viewDistOf gen share s secret₁

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.view
items.doc: The restricted shares observed by the coalition `s`.
items.statement:
def view (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share) (s : Finset Party)
    (r : Randomness) (secret : Secret) : s → Share

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.view_apply
items.statement:
theorem view_apply (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share) (s : Finset Party)
    (r : Randomness) (secret : Secret) (i : s) :
    scheme.view s r secret i = scheme.share r secret i

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.reconstruct_view_eq_secret
items.doc: Authorized coalitions reconstruct the secret from the restricted view.
items.statement:
theorem reconstruct_view_eq_secret
    (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share)
    (r : Randomness) (secret : Secret) {s : Finset Party}
    (hs : scheme.authorized s) :
    scheme.reconstruct s (scheme.view s r secret) = secret

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Scheme.not_authorized_of_subset
items.doc: Any sub-coalition of an unauthorized coalition is unauthorized as well.
items.statement:
theorem not_authorized_of_subset
    (scheme : Scheme Secret Randomness Party Share)
    {s t : Finset Party} (hst : s ⊆ t)
    (ht : ¬ scheme.authorized t) :
    ¬ scheme.authorized s

modules.title: Shamir Secret Sharing
modules.doc:
This module presents a secure-by-construction API for finite-party Shamir secret
sharing through the abstract `SecretSharing.Scheme` interface.

The public constructors require two pieces of data:

- public parameters consisting of a threshold together with distinct, nonzero
  evaluation points for a finite party set
- a translation-invariant sampler on the tail coefficients

Translation invariance is exactly the symmetry used in the privacy proof. The
canonical finite-field instance is obtained by taking the sampler to be uniform.

## Main definitions

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Params`:
  the threshold and public evaluation points
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Randomness`:
  the vector of tail coefficients
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.TailSampler`:
  a translation-invariant distribution on tail coefficients
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.schemeWith`:
  Shamir's scheme with a privacy-preserving tail sampler
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.scheme`:
  the corresponding finite-field scheme with uniform randomness

## Main results

- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.reconstruct_view_eq_secret`:
  any authorized coalition reconstructs the secret
- `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.authorized_univ`:
  the full party set is always authorized

## Notes

The public share type is just the field `F`: the evaluation points are fixed in
`Params`, so one share consists only of the corresponding field value.

## References

* [Adi Shamir, *How to Share a Secret*][Shamir1979]
* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020]

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Params
items.doc:
Public parameters for a finite Shamir secret-sharing instance. The threshold
is bundled with the evaluation points so the API can enforce the standard
non-vacuous `threshold < number of parties` side condition.
items.statement:
structure Params (F : Type*) [Zero F] (Party : Type*) [Fintype Party] where
  /-- A coalition of size `threshold + 1` is the first authorized size. -/
  threshold : ℕ
  /-- Standard Shamir sharing requires `threshold < number of parties`. -/
  threshold_lt_card : threshold < Fintype.card Party
  /-- The public evaluation point assigned to each party. -/
  point : Party → F
  /-- Distinct parties receive distinct evaluation points. -/
  point_injective : Function.Injective point
  /-- Standard Shamir sharing forbids the point `0`, which would reveal the
  secret directly. -/
  point_nonzero : ∀ i : Party, point i ≠ 0

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Randomness
items.doc: The random coefficients of the degree-`threshold - 1` tail polynomial.
items.statement: abbrev Randomness (params : Params F Party)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.authorized
items.doc:
A coalition is authorized exactly when it contains at least
`params.threshold + 1` parties.
items.statement: def authorized (params : Params F Party) (s : Finset Party) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.authorized_univ
items.doc:
Because `params.threshold < |Party|`, the full party set can always
reconstruct the secret.
items.statement:
theorem authorized_univ {F Party : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype Party]
    (params : Params F Party) :
    authorized params (Finset.univ : Finset Party)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.share
items.doc: The Shamir share value sent to one party.
items.statement:
noncomputable def share (params : Params F Party)
    (coeffs : Randomness params) (secretValue : F) (i : Party) : F

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.reconstruct
items.doc: Reconstruct the secret from one coalition's Shamir shares.
items.statement:
noncomputable def reconstruct (params : Params F Party)
    (s : Finset Party) (σ : s → F) : F

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.TailSampler
items.doc:
A sampler on Shamir tail coefficients is privacy-compatible when its
distribution is invariant under translation by any coefficient vector. This is
the exact symmetry needed in the privacy proof.
items.statement:
structure TailSampler (params : Params F Party) where
  /-- The underlying coefficient distribution. -/
  gen : PMF (Randomness params)
  /-- Translating the coefficients does not change the distribution. -/
  map_add_eq_self : ∀ δ : Randomness params, gen.map (fun coeffs => coeffs + δ) = gen

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.uniformTailSampler
items.doc: Uniform tail coefficients form the canonical privacy-compatible sampler.
items.statement:
noncomputable def uniformTailSampler (params : Params F Party)
    [Fintype F] [Nonempty F] : TailSampler params

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.view_indist_of_tailSampler
items.doc:
Translation-invariant Shamir tail samplers induce secret-independent views
for unauthorized coalitions.
items.statement:
theorem view_indist_of_tailSampler (params : Params F Party)
    (sampler : TailSampler params) :
    ∀ (s : Finset Party), ¬ authorized params s → ∀ secret₀ secret₁ : F,
      viewDistOf sampler.gen (share params) s secret₀ =
        viewDistOf sampler.gen (share params) s secret₁

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.schemeWith
items.doc: Shamir's scheme built from a privacy-compatible tail sampler.
items.statement:
noncomputable def schemeWith (params : Params F Party) (sampler : TailSampler params)
    :
    SecretSharing.Scheme F (Randomness params) Party F

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.scheme
items.doc:
The canonical finite-field Shamir scheme with uniformly sampled tail
coefficients.
items.statement:
noncomputable def scheme (params : Params F Party)
    [Fintype F] [Nonempty F] :
    SecretSharing.Scheme F (Randomness params) Party F

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.schemeWith_authorized_iff
items.statement:
theorem schemeWith_authorized_iff (params : Params F Party)
    (sampler : TailSampler params) (s : Finset Party) :
    (schemeWith params sampler).authorized s ↔ params.threshold + 1 ≤ s.card

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.scheme_authorized_iff
items.statement:
theorem scheme_authorized_iff (params : Params F Party)
    [Fintype F] [Nonempty F] (s : Finset Party) :
    (scheme params).authorized s ↔ params.threshold + 1 ≤ s.card

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.schemeWith_share_eq
items.statement:
theorem schemeWith_share_eq (params : Params F Party)
    (sampler : TailSampler params) (coeffs : Randomness params)
    (secretValue : F) (i : Party) :
    (schemeWith params sampler).share coeffs secretValue i =
      share params coeffs secretValue i

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.reconstruct_view_eq_secret
items.doc: Any authorized coalition reconstructs the secret from the shares it sees.
items.statement:
theorem reconstruct_view_eq_secret
    (params : Params F Party) (sampler : TailSampler params)
    (coeffs : Randomness params) (secretValue : F) {s : Finset Party}
    (hs : (schemeWith params sampler).authorized s) :
    (schemeWith params sampler).reconstruct s
      ((schemeWith params sampler).view s coeffs secretValue) = secretValue

modules.title: Shamir Secret Sharing: Polynomial Utilities
modules.doc:
This file contains the Shamir-specific polynomial and interpolation utilities
used to prove correctness and privacy of the public scheme construction.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.tailPolynomial
items.doc: The tail polynomial determined by the first `n` coefficients.
items.statement: def tailPolynomial (n : ℕ) (coeffs : Fin n → F) : _root_.Polynomial F

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.tailPolynomial_coeff
items.statement:
theorem tailPolynomial_coeff (n : ℕ) (coeffs : Fin n → F) (i : Fin n) :
    (tailPolynomial (F := F) n coeffs).coeff i = coeffs i

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.tailPolynomial_degree_lt
items.doc: `tailPolynomial n coeffs` has degree `< n` by construction.
items.statement:
theorem tailPolynomial_degree_lt (n : ℕ) (coeffs : Fin n → F) :
    (tailPolynomial (F := F) n coeffs).degree < n

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.tailPolynomial_add
items.doc: `tailPolynomial` is additive in its coefficient vector.
items.statement:
theorem tailPolynomial_add (n : ℕ) (a b : Fin n → F) :
    tailPolynomial (F := F) n (a + b) = tailPolynomial n a + tailPolynomial n b

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.sharingPolynomial
items.doc: The standard Shamir sharing polynomial `s + X * q(X)`.
items.statement: def sharingPolynomial (secretValue : F) (tail : _root_.Polynomial F) : _root_.Polynomial F

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.sharingPolynomial_eval
items.statement:
theorem sharingPolynomial_eval (secretValue x : F) (tail : _root_.Polynomial F) :
    (sharingPolynomial secretValue tail).eval x = secretValue + x * tail.eval x

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.coeff_zero_sharingPolynomial
items.statement:
theorem coeff_zero_sharingPolynomial (secretValue : F) (tail : _root_.Polynomial F) :
    (sharingPolynomial secretValue tail).coeff 0 = secretValue

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.constantCoeff_sharingPolynomial
items.statement:
theorem constantCoeff_sharingPolynomial (secretValue : F) (tail : _root_.Polynomial F) :
    (sharingPolynomial secretValue tail).constantCoeff = secretValue

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.natDegree_sharingPolynomial_le
items.doc:
If the tail polynomial has degree `< n`, then the sharing polynomial has
natural degree at most `n`.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.degree_sharingPolynomial_lt_succ
items.doc:
If the tail polynomial has degree `< n`, then the sharing polynomial has
degree `< n + 1`.

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.degree_sharingPolynomial_tailPolynomial_lt_succ
items.doc: The coefficient-vector version of `degree_sharingPolynomial_lt_succ`.
items.statement:
theorem degree_sharingPolynomial_tailPolynomial_lt_succ
    (secretValue : F) (n : ℕ) (coeffs : Fin n → F) :
    (sharingPolynomial secretValue (tailPolynomial n coeffs)).degree <
      (n + 1 : WithBot ℕ)

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.reconstruct
items.doc:
Reconstruct the secret from finitely indexed share values by interpolating
the unique low-degree polynomial that matches them.
items.statement: def reconstruct (x σ : ι → F) : F

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.reconstruct_eq_constantCoeff_of_eval_eq
items.doc:
Reconstruction recovers the constant coefficient of any low-degree
polynomial from its values at distinct points.
items.statement:
theorem reconstruct_eq_constantCoeff_of_eval_eq
    {x : ι → F} {p : _root_.Polynomial F}
    (hx : Function.Injective x)
    (hdeg : p.degree < Fintype.card ι) :
    reconstruct x (fun i => p.eval (x i)) = p.constantCoeff

items.name: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SecretSharing.Shamir.Polynomial.reconstruct_sharingPolynomial_eq_secret
items.doc:
Reconstruction succeeds on the values of a Shamir sharing polynomial once
the finite index type is large enough.
items.statement:
theorem reconstruct_sharingPolynomial_eq_secret
    {x : ι → F} {secretValue : F} {tail : _root_.Polynomial F}
    (hx : Function.Injective x)
    (hdeg : (sharingPolynomial secretValue tail).degree < Fintype.card ι) :
    reconstruct x
      (fun i => (sharingPolynomial secretValue tail).eval (x i)) = secretValue

modules.title: Ramsey theorem for infinite graphs
modules.doc:
This result really should be in Mathlib, but currently it is not. We do expect
the Ramsey theorem for infinite hypergraphs to appear in Mathlib eventually and
this result to be derived as a corollary of the more general result.

items.name: Cslib.infinite_pigeonhole_principle
items.doc: An infinite pigeonhole principle.
items.statement:
theorem infinite_pigeonhole_principle {X Y : Type*} [Finite Y] (f : X → Y) {s : Set X}
    (h_inf : s.Infinite) : ∃ y, ∃ t, t.Infinite ∧ t ⊆ s ∧ ∀ x ∈ t, f x = y

items.name: Cslib.infinite_graph_ramsey
items.doc:
If the edges of an infinite complete graph is assigned a finite number of colors,
then there must exist a color `c` and an infinite set `s` of vertices such that the edge
between any two vertices of `s` is assigned the same color `c`.
items.statement:
theorem infinite_graph_ramsey :
    ∃ c : Color, ∃ s : Set Vertex, s.Infinite ∧
      ∀ e : Finset Vertex, e.card = 2 → ↑e ⊆ s → color e = c

modules.title: Free Monad
modules.doc:
This file defines a general `FreeM` monad construction for representing effectful programs
as pure syntax trees, separate from their interpretation.

The `FreeM` monad generates a free monad from any type constructor `f : Type → Type`, without
requiring `f` to be a `Functor`. This implementation uses the "freer monad" approach as the
traditional free monad is not safely definable in Lean due to termination checking.

In this construction, **effectful programs are represented as trees of effects**.
Each node (`FreeM.liftBind`) represents a request to perform an effect, accompanied by a
continuation specifying how the computation proceeds after the effect.
The leaves (`FreeM.pure`) represent completed computations with final results.

This separation of syntax from semantics enables multiple interpretations of the same program:
execution, static analysis, optimization, pretty-printing, verification, and more.

A key insight is that `FreeM F` satisfies the **universal property of free monads**: for any monad
`M` and effect handler `f : F → M`, there exists a unique way to interpret `FreeM F` computations
in `M` that respects the effect semantics given by `f`.
This unique interpreter is `FreeM.liftM f`


## Main Definitions

- `FreeM`: The free monad construction
- `FreeM.liftM`: The canonical interpreter satisfying the universal property
- `FreeM.liftM_unique`: Proof of the universal property

For elimination and interpretation theory, see `Free/Fold.lean`.
For polynomial effect signatures with explicit operation shapes and positions, see
`Cslib.Foundations.Data.PFunctor.Free`.

See the Haskell [freer-simple](https://hackage.haskell.org/package/freer-simple) library for the
Haskell implementation that inspired this approach.

## Implementation Notes

The `FreeM` monad is defined using an inductive type with constructors `.pure` and `.liftBind`.
We implement `Functor` and `Monad` instances, and prove the corresponding `LawfulFunctor`
and `LawfulMonad` instances.


The file `Free/Effects.lean` demonstrates practical applications by implementing State, Writer, and
Continuations monads using `FreeM` with appropriate effect signatures.

The file `Free/Fold.lean` provides the theory of the fold operation for free monads.

## References

* [Oleg Kiselyov, Hiromi Ishii. *Freer Monads, More Extensible Effects*][Kiselyov2015]
* [Bartosz Milewski. *The Dao of Functional Programming*][MilewskiDao]

## Tags

Free monad, state monad

items.name: Cslib.FreeM
items.doc:
The Free monad over a type constructor `F`.

A `FreeM F a` is a tree of operations from the type constructor `F`, with leaves of type `a`.
It has two constructors: `pure` for wrapping a value of type `a`, and `liftBind` for
representing an operation from `F` followed by a continuation.

This construction provides a free monad for any type constructor `F`, allowing for composable
effect descriptions that can be interpreted later. Unlike the traditional free monad,
this does not require `F` to be a functor.
items.statement:
inductive FreeM.{u, v, w} (F : Type u → Type v) (α : Type w) where
  /-- The action that does nothing and returns `a`. -/
  | protected pure (a : α) : FreeM F α
  /-- Invoke the operation `op` with contuation `cont`.

  Note that Lean's inductive types prevent us splitting this into separate bind and lift
  constructors. -/
  | liftBind {ι : Type u} (op : F ι) (cont : ι → FreeM F α) : FreeM F α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.pure_eq_pure
items.statement: theorem pure_eq_pure : FreeM.pure = (pure : α → FreeM F α)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.bind
items.doc:
Bind operation for the `FreeM` monad.

The builtin `>>=` notation should be preferred when `α` and `β` are in the same universe.
items.statement: protected def bind (x : FreeM F α) (f : α → FreeM F β) : FreeM F β

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.bind_eq_bind
items.doc: Note that this lemma does not always apply, as it is universe-constrained by `Bind.bind`.
items.statement: theorem bind_eq_bind {α β : Type w} : (FreeM.bind : FreeM F α → _ → FreeM F β) = Bind.bind

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.map
items.doc:
Map a function over a `FreeM` monad.

The builtin `<$>` notation should be preferred when `α` and `β` are in the same universe.
items.statement: def map (f : α → β) : FreeM F α → FreeM F β

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.map_eq_map
items.doc: Note that this lemma does not always apply, as it is universe-constrained by `Functor.map`.
items.statement: theorem map_eq_map {α β : Type w} : FreeM.map (F := F) (α := α) (β := β) = Functor.map

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.lift
items.doc: Lift an operation from the effect signature `F` into the `FreeM F` monad.
items.statement: def lift (op : F ι) : FreeM F ι

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftBind_eq
items.statement:
lemma liftBind_eq (op : F ι) :
    liftBind op cont = (lift op : FreeM F ι).bind cont

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.induction
items.doc:
An override for the default induction principle that is in simp-normal form.

Note that when `α` and `ι` are in the same universe, this simplifies slightly further.
items.statement:
protected theorem induction {motive : FreeM F α → Prop}
    (pure : ∀ a, motive (pure a))
    (lift_bind : ∀ {ι} (op : F ι) (cont : ι → FreeM F α) (ih : ∀ i, motive (cont i)),
      motive ((lift op).bind cont)) : ∀ x, motive x

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.bind_assoc
items.statement:
protected theorem bind_assoc (x : FreeM F α) (f : α → FreeM F β) (g : β → FreeM F γ) :
    (x.bind f).bind g = x.bind (fun x => (f x).bind g)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.pure_bind
items.doc: `.pure a` followed by `bind` collapses immediately.
items.statement: lemma pure_bind (a : α) (f : α → FreeM F β) : (pure a : FreeM F α).bind f = f a

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.bind_pure
items.statement: lemma bind_pure : ∀ x : FreeM F α, x.bind pure = x

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.bind_pure_comp
items.statement: lemma bind_pure_comp (f : α → β) : ∀ x : FreeM F α, x.bind (pure ∘ f) = map f x

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.map_pure
items.statement: theorem map_pure (f : α → β) (x : α) : map f (pure x : FreeM F α) = pure (f x)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.map_bind
items.statement:
theorem map_bind (f : β → γ) (x : FreeM F α) (c : α → FreeM F β) :
    map f (x.bind c) = x.bind fun a => (c a).map f

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.id_map
items.statement: theorem id_map : ∀ x : FreeM F α, map id x = x

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.comp_map
items.statement: theorem comp_map (h : β → γ) (g : α → β) : ∀ x : FreeM F α, map (h ∘ g) x = map h (map g x)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM
items.doc:
Interpret a `FreeM F` computation into any monad `m` by providing an interpretation
function for the effect signature `F`.

This function defines the *canonical interpreter* from the free monad `FreeM F` into the target
monad `m`. It is the unique monad morphism that extends the effect handler
`interp : ∀ {β}, F β → m β` via the universal property of `FreeM`.
items.statement: protected def liftM (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) : FreeM F α → m α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_pure
items.statement:
lemma liftM_pure (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (a : α) :
    (pure a : FreeM F α).liftM interp = pure a

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_lift_bind
items.statement:
lemma liftM_lift_bind (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (op : F β) (cont : β → FreeM F α) :
    ((lift op) >>= cont).liftM interp = (do let b ← interp op; (cont b).liftM interp)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_lift
items.statement:
lemma liftM_lift [LawfulMonad m] (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (op : F β) :
    (lift op).liftM interp = interp op

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_bind
items.statement:
lemma liftM_bind [LawfulMonad m]
    (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (x : FreeM F α) (f : α → FreeM F β) :
    (x >>= f).liftM interp = (do let a ← x.liftM interp; (f a).liftM interp)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_freeMLiftM
items.doc: A morphism of monads moves inside `FreeM.liftM`.
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_freeMLiftM [Monad n]
    {f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n f)
    (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (x : FreeM F α) :
    f (x.liftM interp) = x.liftM (fun op => f (interp op))

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.isMonadHom_liftM
items.doc: `FreeM.liftM interp` is a morphism of monads.
items.statement:
theorem isMonadHom_liftM [LawfulMonad m] (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) :
    IsMonadHom (FreeM F) m (FreeM.liftM interp)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_map
items.statement:
lemma liftM_map [LawfulMonad m]
    (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (f : α → β) (x : FreeM F α) :
    (f <$> x).liftM @interp = f <$> x.liftM @interp

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_seq
items.statement:
lemma liftM_seq [LawfulMonad m]
    (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (x : FreeM F (α → β)) (y : FreeM F α) :
    (x <*> y).liftM interp = x.liftM interp <*> y.liftM interp

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_seqLeft
items.statement:
lemma liftM_seqLeft [LawfulMonad m]
    (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (x : FreeM F α) (y : FreeM F β) :
    (x <* y).liftM interp = x.liftM interp <* y.liftM interp

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_seqRight
items.statement:
lemma liftM_seqRight [LawfulMonad m]
    (interp : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (x : FreeM F α) (y : FreeM F β) :
    (x *> y).liftM interp = x.liftM interp *> y.liftM interp

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.Interprets
items.doc:
A predicate stating that `interp : FreeM F α → m α` is an interpreter for the effect
handler `handler : ∀ {α}, F α → m α`.

This means that `interp` is a monad morphism from the free monad `FreeM F` to the
monad `m`, and that it extends the interpretation of individual operations
given by `f`.

Formally, `interp` satisfies the two equations:
- `interp (pure a) = pure a`
- `interp (liftBind op k) = handler op >>= fun x => interp (k x)`
items.statement:
structure Interprets (handler : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (interp : FreeM F α → m α) : Prop where
  apply_pure (a : α) : interp (.pure a) = pure a
  apply_lift_bind {ι : Type u} (op : F ι) (cont : ι → FreeM F α) :
    interp (lift op >>= cont) = handler op >>= fun x => interp (cont x)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.Interprets.eq
Cslib.FreeM.Interprets.liftM
items.statement:
theorem Interprets.liftM (handler : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) :
    Interprets handler (·.liftM handler : FreeM F α → _)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.Interprets.iff
items.doc:
The universal property of the free monad `FreeM`.

That is, `liftM handler` is the unique interpreter that extends the effect handler `handler` to
interpret `FreeM F` computations in a monad `m`.
items.statement:
theorem Interprets.iff (handler : {ι : Type u} → F ι → m ι) (interp : FreeM F α → m α) :
    Interprets handler interp ↔ interp = (·.liftM handler)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_lift_eq_self
items.doc: Interpreting each operation by its lift into the free monad is the identity.
items.statement: theorem liftM_lift_eq_self {α : Type u} (x : FreeM F α) : FreeM.liftM lift x = x

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_comp
items.doc: Interpreting into a free monad and then into `m` composes the two handlers.
items.statement:
theorem liftM_comp {m : Type u → Type w} [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    {G : Type u → Type w'} {α : Type u} (x : FreeM F α)
    (first : {ι : Type u} → F ι → FreeM G ι) (second : {ι : Type u} → G ι → m ι) :
    (x.liftM first).liftM second = x.liftM fun op => (first op).liftM second

modules.title: Free Monad
modules.doc:
This file defines several canonical instances on the free monad.

## Main definitions

- `FreeState`, `FreeWriter`, `FreeCont`, `FreeReader`: Specific effect monads

## Implementation

To execute or interpret these computations, we provide two approaches:
1. **Hand-written interpreters** (`FreeState.run`, `FreeWriter.run`, `FreeCont.run`,
  `FreeReader.run`) that directly
  pattern-match on the tree structure
2. **Canonical interpreters** (`FreeState.toStateM`, `FreeWriter.toWriterT`, `FreeCont.toContT`,
  `FreeReader.toReaderM`)
  derived from the universal property via `liftM`

We prove that these approaches are equivalent, demonstrating that the implementation aligns with
the theory. We also provide uniqueness theorems for the canonical interpreters, which follow from
the universal property.

## Tags

Free monad, state monad, writer monad, continuation monad

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.StateF
items.doc: Type constructor for state operations.
items.statement:
inductive StateF (σ : Type u) : Type u → Type u where
  /-- Get the current state. -/
  | get : StateF σ σ
  /-- Set the state. -/
  | set : σ → StateF σ PUnit

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState
items.doc: State monad via the `FreeM` monad.
items.statement: abbrev FreeState (σ : Type u)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.get_def
items.statement: lemma get_def : (get : FreeState σ σ) = .lift .get

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.set_def
items.statement: lemma set_def (s : σ) : (set s : FreeState σ PUnit) = .lift (.set s)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.stateInterp
items.doc: Interpret `StateF` operations into `StateM`.
items.statement: def stateInterp {α : Type u} : StateF σ α → StateM σ α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.toStateM
items.doc:
Convert a `FreeState` computation into a `StateM` computation. This is the canonical
interpreter derived from `liftM`.
items.statement: abbrev toStateM {α : Type u} (comp : FreeState σ α) : StateM σ α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.toStateM_unique
items.doc: `toStateM` is the unique interpreter extending `stateInterp`.
items.statement:
theorem toStateM_unique {α : Type u} (g : FreeState σ α → StateM σ α)
    (h : Interprets stateInterp g) : g = toStateM

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run
items.doc: Run a state computation, returning both the result and final state.
items.statement: def run (comp : FreeState σ α) (s₀ : σ) : α × σ

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run_toStateM
items.doc:
The canonical interpreter `toStateM` derived from `liftM` agrees with the hand-written
recursive interpreter `run` for `FreeState`.
items.statement:
theorem run_toStateM {α : Type u} (comp : FreeState σ α) (s₀ : σ) :
    (toStateM comp).run s₀ = pure (run comp s₀)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run_pure
items.statement:
lemma run_pure (a : α) (s₀ : σ) :
    run (pure a : FreeState σ α) s₀ = (a, s₀)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run_get
items.statement:
lemma run_get (s₀ : σ) :
    run (lift .get) s₀ = (s₀, s₀)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run_set
items.statement:
lemma run_set (s' : σ) (s₀ : σ) :
    run (lift (.set s')) s₀ = (.unit, s')

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run_bind
items.statement:
lemma run_bind (x : FreeState σ α) (f : α → FreeState σ β) (s₀ : σ) :
    run (x.bind f) s₀ = let p := x.run s₀; (f p.1).run p.2

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run'
items.doc: Run a state computation, returning only the result.
items.statement: def run' (c : FreeState σ α) (s₀ : σ) : α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run'_toStateM
items.statement:
theorem run'_toStateM {α : Type u} (comp : FreeState σ α) (s₀ : σ) :
    (toStateM comp).run' s₀ = pure (run' comp s₀)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run'_pure
items.statement:
lemma run'_pure (a : α) (s₀ : σ) :
    run' (pure a : FreeState σ α) s₀ = a

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run'_get
items.statement:
lemma run'_get (s₀ : σ) :
    run' (lift .get) s₀ = s₀
