items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run'_set
items.statement:
lemma run'_set (s' : σ) (s₀ : σ) :
    run' (lift (.set s')) s₀ = .unit

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeState.run'_bind
items.statement:
lemma run'_bind (x : FreeState σ α) (f : α → FreeState σ β) (s₀ : σ) :
    run' (x.bind f) s₀ = let p := x.run s₀; (f p.1).run' p.2

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.WriterF
items.doc:
Type constructor for writer operations. Writer has a single effect, so the definition has just one
constructor.
items.statement:
inductive WriterF (ω : Type u) : Type v → Type u
  /-- Write a value to the log. -/
  | tell : ω → WriterF ω PUnit

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter
items.doc:
Writer monad implemented via the `FreeM` monad construction. This provides a more efficient
implementation than the traditional `WriterT` transformer, as it avoids buffering the log.
items.statement: abbrev FreeWriter (ω : Type u)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.writerInterp
items.doc: Interpret `WriterF` operations into `WriterT`.
items.statement: def writerInterp {α : Type u} : WriterF ω α → WriterT ω Id α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.toWriterT
items.doc:
Convert a `FreeWriter` computation into a `WriterT` computation. This is the canonical
interpreter derived from `liftM`.
items.statement: abbrev toWriterT {α : Type u} [Monoid ω] (comp : FreeWriter ω α) : WriterT ω Id α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.toWriterT_unique
items.doc: `toWriterT` is the unique interpreter extending `writerInterp`.
items.statement:
theorem toWriterT_unique {α : Type u} [Monoid ω] (g : FreeWriter ω α → WriterT ω Id α)
    (h : Interprets writerInterp g) : g = toWriterT

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.tell
items.doc: Writes a log entry. This creates an effectful node in the computation tree.
items.statement: abbrev tell (w : ω) : FreeWriter ω PUnit

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.tell_def
items.statement:
lemma tell_def (w : ω) :
    tell w = .lift (.tell w)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.run
items.doc:
Interprets a `FreeWriter` computation by recursively traversing the tree, accumulating
log entries with the monoid operation, and returns the final value paired with the accumulated log.
items.statement: def run [Monoid ω] : FreeWriter ω α → α × ω

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.run_pure
items.statement:
lemma run_pure [Monoid ω] (a : α) :
    run (pure a : FreeWriter ω α) = (a, 1)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.run_lift_tell
items.statement:
lemma run_lift_tell [Monoid ω] (w : ω) :
    run (lift (.tell w)) = (.unit, w)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.run_bind
items.statement:
lemma run_bind [Monoid ω] (x : FreeWriter ω α) (f : α → FreeWriter ω β) :
    run (x.bind f) = let p := run x; ((f p.1).run.1, p.2 * (f p.1).run.2)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.run_toWriterT
items.doc:
The canonical interpreter `toWriterT` derived from `liftM` agrees with the hand-written
recursive interpreter `run` for `FreeWriter`.
items.statement:
theorem run_toWriterT {α : Type u} [Monoid ω] (comp : FreeWriter ω α) :
    (toWriterT comp).run = pure (run comp)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.listen
items.doc:
`listen` captures the log produced by a subcomputation incrementally. It traverses the computation,
emitting log entries as encountered, and returns the accumulated log as a result.
items.statement: def listen [Monoid ω] : FreeWriter ω α → FreeWriter ω (α × ω)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.listen_pure
items.statement:
lemma listen_pure [Monoid ω] (a : α) :
    listen (pure a : FreeWriter ω α) = .pure (a, 1)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.listen_lift_tell_bind
items.statement:
lemma listen_lift_tell_bind [Monoid ω] (w : ω)
    (k : PUnit → FreeWriter ω α) :
    listen (lift (.tell w) >>= k) =
      lift (.tell w) >>= (fun _ =>
        listen (k .unit) >>= fun (a, w') =>
          pure (a, w * w'))

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.pass
items.doc:
`pass` allows a subcomputation to modify its own log. After traversing the computation and
accumulating its log, the resulting function is applied to rewrite the accumulated log
before re-emission.
items.statement: def pass [Monoid ω] (m : FreeWriter ω (α × (ω → ω))) : FreeWriter ω α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeWriter.pass_def
items.statement:
lemma pass_def [Monoid ω] (m : FreeWriter ω (α × (ω → ω))) :
    pass m = let ((a, f), w) := run m; liftBind (.tell (f w)) fun _ => .pure a

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.ContF
items.doc: Type constructor for continuation operations.
items.statement:
inductive ContF (r : Type u) (α : Type v) where
  /-- Call with current continuation: provides access to the current continuation. -/
  | callCC : ((α → r) → r) → ContF r α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont
items.doc: Continuation monad via the `FreeM` monad.
items.statement: abbrev FreeCont (r : Type u)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.contInterp
items.doc: Interpret `ContF r` operations into `ContT r Id`.
items.statement: def contInterp : ContF r α → ContT r Id α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.toContT
items.doc:
Convert a `FreeCont` computation into a `ContT` computation. This is the canonical
interpreter derived from `liftM`.
items.statement: abbrev toContT {α : Type u} (comp : FreeCont r α) : ContT r Id α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.toContT_unique
items.doc: `toContT` is the unique interpreter extending `contInterp`.
items.statement:
theorem toContT_unique {α : Type u} (g : FreeCont r α → ContT r Id α)
    (h : Interprets contInterp g) : g = toContT

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.run
items.doc: Run a continuation computation with the given continuation.
items.statement: def run : FreeCont r α → (α → r) → r

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.run_pure
items.statement:
lemma run_pure (a : α) (k : α → r) :
    run (pure a : FreeCont r α) k = k a

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.run_lift_callCC
items.statement:
lemma run_lift_callCC (g : (α → r) → r) (k : α → r) :
    run (lift (.callCC g)) k = g k

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.run_bind
items.statement:
lemma run_bind (x : FreeCont r α) (f : α → FreeCont r β) (k : β → r) :
    run (x.bind f) k = run x (fun i => run (f i) k)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.run_toContT
items.doc:
The canonical interpreter `toContT` derived from `liftM` agrees with the hand-written
recursive interpreter `run` for `FreeCont`.
items.statement:
theorem run_toContT {α : Type u} (comp : FreeCont r α) (k : α → r) :
    (toContT comp).run k = pure (run comp k)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.callCC
items.doc: Call with current continuation for the Free continuation monad.
items.statement:
def callCC (f : MonadCont.Label α (FreeCont r) β → FreeCont r α) :
    FreeCont r α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeCont.run_callCC
items.doc: `run` of a `callCC` node simplifies to running the handler with the current continuation.
items.statement:
lemma run_callCC (f : MonadCont.Label α (FreeCont r) β → FreeCont r α) (k : α → r) :
    run (callCC f) k = run (f ⟨fun x => lift (.callCC fun _ => k x)⟩) k

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.ReaderF
items.doc: Type constructor for reader operations.
items.statement:
inductive ReaderF (σ : Type u) : Type u → Type u where
  | read : ReaderF σ σ

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader
items.doc: Reader monad via the `FreeM` monad
items.statement: abbrev FreeReader (σ)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.read_def
items.statement: lemma read_def : (read : FreeReader σ σ) = .lift .read

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.readInterp
items.doc: Interpret `ReaderF` operations into `ReaderM`.
items.statement: def readInterp {α : Type u} : ReaderF σ α → ReaderM σ α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.toReaderM
items.doc:
Convert a `FreeReader` computation into a `ReaderM` computation. This is the canonical
interpreter derived from `liftM`.
items.statement: abbrev toReaderM {α : Type u} (comp : FreeReader σ α) : ReaderM σ α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.toReaderM_unique
items.doc: `toReaderM` is the unique interpreter extending `readInterp`.
items.statement:
theorem toReaderM_unique {α : Type u} (g : FreeReader σ α → ReaderM σ α)
    (h : Interprets readInterp g) : g = toReaderM

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.run
items.doc: Run a reader computation
items.statement: def run (comp : FreeReader σ α) (s₀ : σ) : α

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.run_toReaderM
items.doc:
The canonical interpreter `toReaderM` derived from `liftM` agrees with the hand-written
recursive interpreter `run` for `FreeReader`
items.statement:
theorem run_toReaderM {α : Type u} (comp : FreeReader σ α) (s : σ) :
    (toReaderM comp).run s = pure (run comp s)

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.run_pure
items.statement:
lemma run_pure (a : α) (s₀ : σ) :
    run (pure a : FreeReader σ α) s₀ = a

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.run_read
items.statement:
lemma run_read (s₀ : σ) :
    run read s₀ = s₀

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.run_bind
items.statement:
lemma run_bind (x : FreeReader σ α) (f : α → FreeReader σ β) (s₀ : σ) :
    run (x >>= f) s₀ = run (f <| run x s₀) s₀

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.FreeReader.instMonadWithReaderOf
items.statement: instance instMonadWithReaderOf : MonadWithReaderOf σ (FreeReader σ)

items.statement:
theorem run_withReader (f : σ → σ) (m : FreeReader σ α) (s : σ) :
run (withTheReader σ f m) s = run m (f s)

modules.title: Free Monad Catamorphism
modules.doc:
This file defines the fold operation for free monads and proves its universal property.

In computer science terms, `foldFreeM` provides **interpreters** for effectful syntax trees.
Given any "target algebra" (a type with handlers for values and effects), `foldFreeM`
constructs the unique interpreter that transforms `FreeM` programs into that target.

The theory is based on the fact that `FreeM F α` is the initial algebra for a specific functor, and
`foldFreeM` provides the unique way to eliminate free monad computations into any
algebra of this functor.

## Main Definitions

- `FreeM.foldFreeM`: Fold operation for free monads
- `FreeM.foldFreeM_unique`: Universal property showing uniqueness of the fold

## Universal Property

`FreeM F α` is the initial algebra of the functor `φ_F(β) = α ⊕ Σ_ι (F ι × (ι → β))`.

An algebra of this functor consists of a type `β` and functions:
- `onValue : α → β` (handles pure values)
- `onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → β) → β` (handles effects with continuations)

For any such algebra, `foldFreeM onValue onEffect` is the unique algebra morphism
from the initial algebra `FreeM F α` to `(β, onValue, onEffect)`.

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM
items.doc: Fold function for the `FreeM` monad
items.statement:
def foldFreeM
    (onValue : α → β)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → β) → β) :
    FreeM F α → β

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM_pure
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_pure
    (onValue : α → β)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → β) → β)
    (a : α) : foldFreeM onValue onEffect (pure a) = onValue a

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM_lift_bind
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_lift_bind
    (onValue : α → β)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → β) → β)
    (op : F ι) (k : ι → FreeM F α) :
      foldFreeM onValue onEffect ((lift op).bind k)
      = onEffect op (fun x => foldFreeM onValue onEffect (k x))

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM_lift_bind'
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_lift_bind' {F : Type w → Type v} {ι : Type w}
    (onValue : α → β)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type w} → F ι → (ι → β) → β)
    (op : F ι) (k : ι → FreeM F α) :
      foldFreeM onValue onEffect (lift op >>= k)
      = onEffect op (fun x => foldFreeM onValue onEffect (k x))

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM_lift
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_lift
    (onValue : ι → β)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → β) → β)
    (op : F ι) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect (lift op) = onEffect op onValue

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM_unique
items.doc:
**Universal Property**: If `h : FreeM F α → β` satisfies:
* `h (pure a) = onValue a`
* `h ((lift op).bind k) = onEffect op (fun x => h (k x))`

then `h` is equal to `foldFreeM onValue onEffect`.
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_unique
    (onValue : α → β)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → β) → β)
    (h : FreeM F α → β)
    (h_pure : ∀ a, h (pure a) = onValue a)
    (h_liftBind : ∀ {ι} (op : F ι) (k : ι → FreeM F α),
      h ((lift op).bind k) = onEffect op (fun x => h (k x))) :
    h = foldFreeM onValue onEffect

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM_bind
items.doc: Sequencing substitutes the fold of the continuation for the value handler.
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_bind (onValue : β → γ)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → γ) → γ)
    (x : FreeM F α) (k : α → FreeM F β) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect (x.bind k) =
      foldFreeM (fun a => foldFreeM onValue onEffect (k a)) onEffect x

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM_map
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_map (onValue : β → γ)
    (onEffect : {ι : Type u} → F ι → (ι → γ) → γ) (f : α → β) (x : FreeM F α) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect (map f x) = foldFreeM (onValue ∘ f) onEffect x

items.name: Cslib.FreeM.liftM_eq_foldFreeM
items.doc: Monadic interpretation is the fold whose effect handler uses `bind`.

modules.title: (unbundled) morphisms of monads
modules.doc:
This file defines predicates on functions `f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α` that preserve functor, applicative,
monadic, and alternative structure (`IsFunctorHom`, `IsApplicativeHom`, `IsMonadHom`,
`IsAlternativeHom`, `IsAlternativeMonadHom`).

Rather than assuming lawfulness, they explicitly require compatibility with every operator
defined by the corresponding typeclasses, with helper constructors that dismiss the derived
operators when the structures are lawful.

items.name: Id.pure_injective
items.statement: theorem _root_.Id.pure_injective : Function.Injective (pure : α → Id α)

items.name: Cslib.IsFunctorHom
items.doc: A function `f` is a morphism of functors if it preserves `<$>` and `Functor.mapConst`.
items.statement:
structure IsFunctorHom (m n) [Functor m] [Functor n] (f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α) : Prop where
  map_map {α β} (g : α → β) (x : m α) : f (g <$> x) = g <$> f x
  map_mapConst {α β} (a : α) (x : m β) : f (Functor.mapConst a x) = Functor.mapConst a (f x)

items.name: Cslib.IsFunctorHom.mk'
items.doc: Construct an `IsFunctorHom` for lawful functors from `map_map`.

items.name: Cslib.IsFunctorHom.id
items.statement: protected theorem id : IsFunctorHom m m id

items.name: Cslib.IsFunctorHom.comp
Cslib.IsApplicativeHom
items.doc: A function `f` is a morphism of applicatives if it preserves `pure`, `<$>`, `<*>`, `<*`, and `*>`.
items.statement:
structure IsApplicativeHom (m n) [Applicative m] [Applicative n] (f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α) : Prop
    extends IsFunctorHom m n f where
  map_pure {α} (a : α) : f (pure a) = pure a
  map_seq {α β} (x : m (α → β)) (y : Unit → m α) :
      f (Seq.seq x y) = Seq.seq (f x) (f <| y ·)
  map_seqLeft {α β} (x : m α) (y : Unit → m β) :
      f (SeqLeft.seqLeft x y) = SeqLeft.seqLeft (f x) (f <| y ·)
  map_seqRight {α β} (x : m α) (y : Unit → m β) :
      f (SeqRight.seqRight x y) = SeqRight.seqRight (f x) (f <| y ·)

items.name: Cslib.IsApplicativeHom.mk'
items.doc: Construct an `IsApplicativeHom` for lawful applicatives from `map_pure` and `map_seq`.
items.statement:
theorem mk' [LawfulApplicative m] [LawfulApplicative n] {f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α}
    (map_pure : ∀ {α} (a : α), f (pure a) = pure a)
    (map_seq : ∀ {α β} (x : m (α → β)) (y : Unit → m α),
      f (Seq.seq x y) = Seq.seq (f x) (f <| y ·)) :
    IsApplicativeHom m n f

items.name: Cslib.IsApplicativeHom.id
items.statement: protected theorem id : IsApplicativeHom m m id

items.name: Cslib.IsApplicativeHom.comp
Cslib.IsMonadHom
items.doc: A function `f` is a morphism of monads if it preserves `pure`, `>>=`, `<$>`, `<*>`, `<*`, and `*>`.
items.statement:
structure IsMonadHom (m n) [Monad m] [Monad n] (f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α) : Prop
    extends IsApplicativeHom m n f where
  map_bind {α β} (x : m α) (y : α → m β) : f (x >>= y) = f x >>= (f <| y ·)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.mk'
items.doc: Construct an `IsMonadHom` for lawful monads from `map_pure` and `map_bind`.
items.statement:
theorem mk' [LawfulMonad m] [LawfulMonad n] {f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α}
    (map_pure : ∀ {α} (a : α), f (pure a) = pure a)
    (map_bind : ∀ {α β} (x : m α) (y : α → m β), f (x >>= y) = f x >>= (f <| y ·)) :
    IsMonadHom m n f

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.id
items.statement: protected theorem id : IsMonadHom m m id

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.comp
Cslib.IsMonadHom.monadLift
items.statement:
protected theorem monadLift [LawfulMonad m] [LawfulMonad n]
    [MonadLift m n] [LawfulMonadLift m n] :
    IsMonadHom m n MonadLift.monadLift

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.monadLiftT
items.statement:
protected theorem monadLiftT [LawfulMonad m] [LawfulMonad n]
    [MonadLiftT m n] [LawfulMonadLiftT m n] :
    IsMonadHom m n monadLift

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeHom
items.doc:
A function `f` is a morphism of alternatives if it preserves `pure`, `<$>`, `<*>`, `<*`, `*>`,
`failure`, and `orElse`.
items.statement:
structure IsAlternativeHom (m n) [Alternative m] [Alternative n] (f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α) : Prop
    extends IsApplicativeHom m n f where
  map_failure {α} : f (Alternative.failure : m α) = Alternative.failure
  map_orElse {α} (x : m α) (y : Unit → m α) :
    f (HOrElse.hOrElse x y) = HOrElse.hOrElse (f x) (f <| y ·)

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeHom.mk'
items.doc:
Construct an `IsAlternativeHom` for lawful applicatives from `map_pure`, `map_seq`,
`map_failure`, and `map_orElse`.
items.statement:
theorem mk' [LawfulApplicative m] [LawfulApplicative n] {f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α}
    (map_pure : ∀ {α} (a : α), f (pure a) = pure a)
    (map_seq : ∀ {α β} (x : m (α → β)) (y : Unit → m α),
      f (Seq.seq x y) = Seq.seq (f x) (f <| y ·))
    (map_failure : ∀ {α}, f (Alternative.failure : m α) = Alternative.failure)
    (map_orElse : ∀ {α} (x : m α) (y : Unit → m α),
      f (HOrElse.hOrElse x y) = HOrElse.hOrElse (f x) (f <| y ·)) :
    IsAlternativeHom m n f

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeHom.id
items.statement: protected theorem id : IsAlternativeHom m m id

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeHom.comp
Cslib.IsAlternativeMonadHom
items.doc:
A function `f` is a morphism of alternative monads if it preserves monadic and alternative
structure.
items.statement:
structure IsAlternativeMonadHom (m n) [AlternativeMonad m] [AlternativeMonad n]
    (f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α) : Prop
    extends IsMonadHom m n f, IsAlternativeHom m n f

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeMonadHom.mk'
items.doc:
Construct an `IsAlternativeMonadHom` for lawful monads from `map_pure`, `map_bind`,
`map_failure`, and `map_orElse`.
items.statement:
theorem mk' [LawfulMonad m] [LawfulMonad n] {f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α}
    (map_pure : ∀ {α} (a : α), f (pure a) = pure a)
    (map_bind : ∀ {α β} (x : m α) (y : α → m β), f (x >>= y) = f x >>= (f <| y ·))
    (map_failure : ∀ {α}, f (Alternative.failure : m α) = Alternative.failure)
    (map_orElse : ∀ {α} (x : m α) (y : Unit → m α),
      f (HOrElse.hOrElse x y) = HOrElse.hOrElse (f x) (f <| y ·)) :
    IsAlternativeMonadHom m n f

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeMonadHom.id
items.statement: protected theorem id : IsAlternativeMonadHom m m id

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeMonadHom.comp
Cslib.IsMonadHom.wp
items.statement: theorem IsMonadHom.wp [Monad m] [WPMonad m ps] : IsMonadHom m (PredTrans ps) WP.wp

modules.title: List operations and monad morphisms
modules.doc:
This file proves that monadic operations on lists commute with monad homomorphisms
(and applicative homomorphisms), and that `List.reverse` is a monad homomorphism on `List`.

items.note: ### Preservation of list operations under applicative homomorphisms

items.name: Cslib.IsApplicativeHom.map_listMapA
items.statement:
theorem map_listMapA {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsApplicativeHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} {β : Type u} (f : α → m β) (l : List α) :
    F (l.mapA f) = l.mapA (F ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.IsApplicativeHom.map_listForA
items.statement:
theorem map_listForA {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsApplicativeHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} (l : List α) (f : α → m PUnit) :
    F (l.forA f) = l.forA (F ∘ f)

items.note: ### Preservation of list operations under monad homomorphisms

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listMapM'
items.statement:
theorem map_listMapM'
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} {β : Type u} (f : α → m β) (l : List α) :
    F (l.mapM' f) = l.mapM' (F ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listMapMLoop
items.statement:
theorem map_listMapMLoop
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} {β : Type u} (f : α → m β) (l : List α) (acc : List β) :
    F (List.mapM.loop f l acc) = List.mapM.loop (F ∘ f) l acc

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listMapM
items.statement:
theorem map_listMapM
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} {β : Type u} (f : α → m β) (l : List α) :
    F (l.mapM f) = l.mapM (F ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listForM
items.statement:
theorem map_listForM {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} (l : List α) (f : α → m PUnit) :
    F (l.forM f) = l.forM (F ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listFoldlM
items.statement:
theorem map_listFoldlM {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {s : Type u} {α : Type v} (f : s → α → m s) (init : s) (l : List α) :
    F (l.foldlM f init) = l.foldlM (fun s a => F (f s a)) init

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listFoldrM
items.statement:
theorem map_listFoldrM {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {s : Type u} {α : Type v} (f : α → s → m s) (init : s) (l : List α) :
    F (l.foldrM f init) = l.foldrM (fun a s => F (f a s)) init

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listFindSomeM?
items.statement:
theorem map_listFindSomeM?
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} {β : Type u} (f : α → m (Option β)) (l : List α) :
    F (l.findSomeM? f) = l.findSomeM? (F ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listFindM?
items.statement:
theorem map_listFindM? {m n : Type → Type v} [Monad m] [Monad n]
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type} (p : α → m Bool) (l : List α) :
    F (l.findM? p) = l.findM? (F ∘ p)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listAnyM
items.statement:
theorem map_listAnyM {m n : Type → Type v} [Monad m] [Monad n]
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} (p : α → m Bool) (l : List α) :
    F (l.anyM p) = l.anyM (F ∘ p)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listAllM
items.statement:
theorem map_listAllM {m n : Type → Type v} [Monad m] [Monad n]
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} (p : α → m Bool) (l : List α) :
    F (l.allM p) = l.allM (F ∘ p)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listFilterAuxM
items.statement:
theorem map_listFilterAuxM {m n : Type → Type v} [Monad m] [Monad n]
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type} (p : α → m Bool) (l acc : List α) :
    F (List.filterAuxM p l acc) = List.filterAuxM (F ∘ p) l acc

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listFilterM
items.statement:
theorem map_listFilterM {m n : Type → Type v} [Monad m] [Monad n]
    {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsMonadHom m n F)
    {α : Type} (p : α → m Bool) (l : List α) :
    F (l.filterM p) = l.filterM (F ∘ p)

items.note: ### Preservation of list operations under alternative homomorphisms

items.name: Cslib.IsAlternativeHom.map_listFirstM
items.statement:
theorem map_listFirstM {F : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : IsAlternativeHom m n F)
    {α : Type v} {β : Type u} (f : α → m β) (l : List α) :
    F (l.firstM f) = l.firstM (F ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.IsApplicativeHom.map_listSingleton
items.statement:
theorem IsApplicativeHom.map_listSingleton
    {F : ∀ {α}, List α → List α} (hf : IsApplicativeHom List List F) {α} (a : α) :
    F ([a] : List α) = [a]

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_listFlatMap
items.statement:
theorem IsMonadHom.map_listFlatMap
    {F : ∀ {α}, List α → List α} (hf : IsMonadHom List List F) {α β} (l : List α) (g : α → List β) :
    F (l.flatMap g) = (F l).flatMap (F <| g ·)

items.name: Cslib.IsFunctorHom.map_listNil
items.statement:
theorem IsFunctorHom.map_listNil {F : ∀ {α}, List α → List α} (hf : IsFunctorHom List List F) {α} :
    F ([] : List α) = []

items.name: List.isMonadHom_reverse
items.statement: protected theorem _root_.List.isMonadHom_reverse : IsMonadHom List List List.reverse

items.name: Cslib.isMonadHom_list_iff
items.doc: The only monad morphisms on lists are the identity and reversal.
items.statement:
theorem isMonadHom_list_iff (f : ∀ {α : Type u}, List α → List α) :
    IsMonadHom List List @f ↔ @f = (@id <| List ·) ∨ @f = @List.reverse

modules.title: BiTape: Bidirectionally infinite TM tape representation using StackTape
modules.doc:
This file defines `BiTape`, a tape representation for Turing machines
in the form of an `List` of `Option` values,
with the additional property that the list cannot end with `none`.

## Design

Note that Mathlib has a `Tape` type, but it requires the alphabet type to be inhabited,
and considers the ends of the tape to be filled with default values.

This design requires the tape elements to be `Option` values, and ensures that
`List`s of the base alphabet, rendered directly onto the tape by mapping over `some`,
will not collide.

## Main definitions

* `BiTape`: A tape with a head symbol and left/right contents stored as `StackTape`
* `BiTape.move`: Move the tape head left or right
* `BiTape.write`: Write a symbol at the current head position
* `BiTape.spaceUsed`: The space used by the tape

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape
items.doc:
A structure for bidirectionally-infinite Turing machine tapes
that eventually take on blank `none` values
items.statement:
structure BiTape (Symbol : Type*) where
  /-- The symbol currently under the tape head -/
  head : Option Symbol
  /-- The contents to the left of the head -/
  left : StackTape Symbol
  /-- The contents to the right of the head -/
  right : StackTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.nil
items.doc: The empty `BiTape`
items.statement: def nil : BiTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.empty_eq_nil
items.statement: lemma empty_eq_nil : (∅ : BiTape Symbol) = nil

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.mk₁
items.doc:
Given a `List` of `Symbol`s, construct a `BiTape` by mapping the list to `some` elements
and laying them out to the right side,
with the head under the first element of the list if it exists.
items.statement: def mk₁ (l : List Symbol) : BiTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.moveLeft
items.doc: Move the head left by shifting the left StackTape under the head.
items.statement: def moveLeft (t : BiTape Symbol) : BiTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.moveRight
items.doc: Move the head right by shifting the right StackTape under the head.
items.statement: def moveRight (t : BiTape Symbol) : BiTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.move
items.doc: Move the head to the left or right, shifting the tape underneath it.
items.statement: def move (t : BiTape Symbol) : Dir → BiTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.optionMove
items.doc: Optionally perform a `move`, or do nothing if `none`.
items.statement: def optionMove : BiTape Symbol → Option Turing.Dir → BiTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.moveLeft_moveRight
items.statement: lemma moveLeft_moveRight (t : BiTape Symbol) : t.moveLeft.moveRight = t

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.moveRight_moveLeft
items.statement: lemma moveRight_moveLeft (t : BiTape Symbol) : t.moveRight.moveLeft = t

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.write
items.doc: Write a value under the head of the `BiTape`.
items.statement: def write (t : BiTape Symbol) (a : Option Symbol) : BiTape Symbol

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.spaceUsed
items.doc:
The space used by a `BiTape` is the number of symbols
between and including the head, and leftmost and rightmost non-blank symbols on the `BiTape`.
items.statement: def spaceUsed (t : BiTape Symbol) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.spaceUsed_write
items.statement:
lemma spaceUsed_write (t : BiTape Symbol) (a : Option Symbol) :
    (t.write a).spaceUsed = t.spaceUsed

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.spaceUsed_mk₁
items.statement:
lemma spaceUsed_mk₁ (l : List Symbol) :
    (mk₁ l).spaceUsed = max 1 l.length

items.name: Cslib.Turing.BiTape.spaceUsed_move
items.statement:
lemma spaceUsed_move (t : BiTape Symbol) (d : Turing.Dir) :
    (t.move d).spaceUsed ≤ t.spaceUsed + 1

modules.title: Fixed-length bit strings and Boolean functions
modules.doc:
A bit string is indexed by its coordinates, so selecting or updating one bit uses the usual
functions on `Fin n → Bool`.

items.name: Cslib.BitString
items.doc: A string of `n` bits, indexed by its coordinates.
items.statement: abbrev BitString (n : ℕ) : Type

items.name: Cslib.BooleanFunction
items.doc: A Boolean function of `n` input bits.
items.statement: abbrev BooleanFunction (n : ℕ) : Type

items.name: Cslib.DecidableEqZero
items.doc: Equality to `Zero` is decidable for all elements of a type (`α`).
items.statement: abbrev DecidableEqZero (α : Type*) [Zero α]

modules.title: Appending tuples
modules.doc:
Lemmas about `Fin.append` not (yet) in Mathlib: the two parts of an appended tuple never overlap
and appending commutes with post-composition and with updating an entry on either side.

items.name: Fin.castAdd_ne_natAdd
items.doc: The two parts of `Fin.append` never overlap.
items.statement: theorem castAdd_ne_natAdd (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n) : castAdd n i ≠ natAdd m j

items.name: Fin.comp_append
items.doc: Post-composition commutes with `Fin.append`.
items.statement:
theorem comp_append (f : α → β) (a : Fin m → α) (b : Fin n → α) :
    f ∘ append a b = append (f ∘ a) (f ∘ b)

items.name: Fin.append_update_left
items.doc: Updating an entry of the left tuple is updating the appended tuple at `castAdd`.
items.statement:
theorem append_update_left (a : Fin m → α) (b : Fin n → α) (i : Fin m) (x : α) :
    append (Function.update a i x) b = Function.update (append a b) (castAdd n i) x

items.name: Fin.append_update_right
items.doc: Updating an entry of the right tuple is updating the appended tuple at `natAdd`.
items.statement:
theorem append_update_right (a : Fin m → α) (b : Fin n → α) (i : Fin n) (x : α) :
    append a (Function.update b i x) = Function.update (append a b) (natAdd m i) x

modules.title: Finite functions
modules.doc:
Given types `α` and `β`, and assuming that `β` has a `Zero` element,
a `FinFun α β` is a function from `α` to `β` where only a finite number of elements
in `α` are mapped to non-zero elements.

items.name: Cslib.FinFun
items.doc:
A `FinFun` is a function `fn` with a finite `support`.

This is similar to `Finsupp` in Mathlib, but definitions are computable.
items.statement:
structure FinFun (α β : Type*) [Zero β] where
  /-- The underlying function. -/
  fn : α → β
  /-- The finite support of the function. -/
  support : Finset α
  /-- Proof that `support` is the support of the underlying function. -/
  mem_support_fn {a : α} : a ∈ support ↔ fn a ≠ 0

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fromFun
items.doc:
Constructs a `FinFun` by restricting a function to a given support, filtering out all elements
not mapped to 0 in the support.
items.statement:
def fromFun {α β : Type*} [Zero β] [DecidableEq α]
  [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)] (fn : α → β) (support : Finset α) : α →₀ β

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.instFunLike
items.statement: instance instFunLike [Zero β] : FunLike (α →₀ β) α β

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.coe_fn
items.statement: theorem coe_fn [Zero β] {f : α →₀ β} : (f : α → β) = f.fn

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.coe_eq_fn
items.statement: theorem coe_eq_fn [Zero β] {f : α →₀ β} : f a = f.fn a

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.ext
items.doc: Extensional equality for `FinFun`.
items.statement: theorem ext [Zero β] {f g : α →₀ β} (h : ∀ (a : α), f a = g a) : f = g

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.mem_support_not_zero
items.statement: theorem mem_support_not_zero [Zero β] {f : α →₀ β} : a ∈ f.support ↔ f a ≠ 0

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.not_mem_support_zero
items.statement: theorem not_mem_support_zero [Zero β] {f : α →₀ β} : a ∉ f.support ↔ f a = 0

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.eq_fields_eq
items.doc: If two `FinFun`s are equal, their underlying functions and supports are equal.
items.statement: theorem eq_fields_eq [Zero β] {f g : α →₀ β} : f = g → f.fn = g.fn ∧ f.support = g.support

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fn_eq_eq
items.doc:
If two functions are equal, two `FinFun`s respectively using them as underlying functions
are equal.
items.statement: theorem fn_eq_eq [Zero β] {f g : α →₀ β} (h : f.fn = g.fn) : f = g

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.congrFinFun
items.statement: theorem congrFinFun [Zero β] {f g : α →₀ β} (h : f = g) (a : α) : f a = g a

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fromFun_eq
items.statement:
theorem fromFun_eq [Zero β] [DecidableEq α] [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)]
    (f : α → β) (support : Finset α) (h : ∀ a, a ∉ support → f a = 0) :
    (f ↾₀ support) = f

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fromFun_fn
items.statement:
theorem fromFun_fn [Zero β] [DecidableEq α] [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)]
    (f : α → β) (support : Finset α) :
    (f ↾₀ support).fn = (fun a => if a ∈ support then f a else 0)

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fromFun_support
items.statement:
theorem fromFun_support [Zero β] [DecidableEq α] [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)]
    (f : α → β) (support : Finset α) :
    (f ↾₀ support).support = support.filter (f · ≠ 0)

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fromFun_idem
items.doc: Restricting a function twice to the same support is idempotent.
items.statement:
theorem fromFun_idem [Zero β] [DecidableEq α]
    [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)] {f : α → β} {support : Finset α} :
    (f ↾₀ support) ↾₀ support = f ↾₀ support

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.coe_fromFun_id
items.doc: Restricting a `FinFun` to its own support is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem coe_fromFun_id [Zero β] [DecidableEq α] [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)] {f : α →₀ β} :
    (f ↾₀ f.support) = f

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fromFun_inter
items.doc: Restricting a function twice to two supports is equal to restricting to their intersection.
items.statement:
theorem fromFun_inter [Zero β] [DecidableEq α]
    [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)] {f : α → β} {support1 support2 : Finset α} :
    (f ↾₀ support1) ↾₀ support2 = f ↾₀ (support1 ∩ support2)

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.fromFun_comm
items.doc: Restricting a function is commutative.
items.statement:
theorem fromFun_comm [Zero β] [DecidableEq α]
    [∀ y : β, Decidable (y = 0)] {f : α → β} {support1 support2 : Finset α} :
    (f ↾₀ support1) ↾₀ support2 = (f ↾₀ support2) ↾₀ support1

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.instDecidableEq
items.doc: Decidable equality
items.statement: instance instDecidableEq [Zero β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] : DecidableEq (α →₀ β)

modules.title: Update for finite functions
modules.doc:
This module defines the update operation for finite functions, that is, the equivalent of
`Function.update` for `FinFun`.

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update
items.doc: `FinFun` equivalent of `Function.update`.
items.statement: def update (f : α →₀ β) (a : α) (b : β) : α →₀ β

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update_coe
items.doc: `FinFun.update` is consistent with `Function.update`.
items.statement: theorem update_coe (f : α →₀ β) : (f.update a b : α → β) = Function.update f a b

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update_apply
items.doc: Conditional characterisation of the functional interface of `FinFun.update`.
items.statement: theorem update_apply (f : α →₀ β) : ((f.update a' b) a) = if a = a' then b else f a

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update_support
items.doc: Conditional characterisation of the support of an updated `FinFun`.
items.statement:
theorem update_support (f : α →₀ β) :
    (f.update a b).support = if b = 0 then f.support \ {a} else f.support ∪ {a}

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update_idem
items.doc: Updating a finite function on the same key is the same as doing the last update.
items.statement: theorem update_idem (f : α →₀ β) : (f.update a b).update a b' = f.update a b'

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update_comm
items.doc: Updates on different keys commute.
items.statement:
theorem update_comm (f : α →₀ β) (h : a ≠ a') :
    (f.update a b).update a' b' = (f.update a' b').update a b

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update_self
items.doc: Updates that do not change mappings are redundant.
items.statement: theorem update_self (f : α →₀ β) : (f.update a (f a)) = f

items.name: Cslib.FinFun.update_support_subseteq
items.doc: Updating a function never grows its support more than adding the key.
items.statement: theorem update_support_subseteq (f : α →₀ β) : (f.update a b).support ⊆ f.support ∪ {a}

modules.title: Counting via involutions
modules.doc:
If `σ` is an involution on a finset `s` and every orbit `{x, σ x}` meets a
predicate `p`, then at least half of `s` satisfies `p`. This is the
combinatorial core of pairing arguments such as the Ehrenfeucht–Haussler–
Kearns–Valiant lower bound on PAC sample complexity.

## Main statements

- `Finset.card_filter_not_le_card_filter_of_involution`: the elements of `s`
  failing `p` inject via `σ` into those satisfying `p`.
- `Finset.card_div_two_le_card_filter_of_involution`: at least half of `s`
  satisfies `p`.

items.name: Finset.card_filter_not_le_card_filter_of_involution
items.doc:
If `σ` is an involution on `s` and every orbit `{x, σ x}` meets `p`, then
`σ` injects the elements of `s` failing `p` into those satisfying `p`.
items.statement:
theorem card_filter_not_le_card_filter_of_involution
    (hσ : ∀ x ∈ s, σ (σ x) = x) (hσs : ∀ x ∈ s, σ x ∈ s)
    (hp : ∀ x ∈ s, p x ∨ p (σ x)) :
    #(s.filter fun x => ¬ p x) ≤ #(s.filter p)

items.name: Finset.card_div_two_le_card_filter_of_involution
items.doc:
If `σ` is an involution on `s` and every orbit `{x, σ x}` meets `p`, then
at least half of `s` satisfies `p`.
items.statement:
theorem card_div_two_le_card_filter_of_involution
    (hσ : ∀ x ∈ s, σ (σ x) = x) (hσs : ∀ x ∈ s, σ x ∈ s)
    (hp : ∀ x ∈ s, p x ∨ p (σ x)) :
    #s / 2 ≤ #(s.filter p)

modules.doc: Computable chacterization of infinite types.

items.name: Cslib.HasFresh
items.doc:
A type `α` has a computable `fresh` function if it is always possible, for any finite set
of `α`, to compute a fresh element not in the set.
items.statement:
class HasFresh (α : Type u) where
  /-- Given a finite set, returns an element not in the set. -/
  fresh : Finset α → α
  /-- Proof that `fresh` returns a fresh element for its input set. -/
  fresh_notMem (s : Finset α) : fresh s ∉ s

items.name: Cslib.HasFresh.fresh_exists
items.doc:
An existential version of the `HasFresh` typeclass. This is useful for the sake of brevity
in proofs.
items.statement: theorem HasFresh.fresh_exists {α : Type u} [HasFresh α] (s : Finset α) : ∃ a, a ∉ s

items.name: Cslib.HasFresh.to_infinite
items.doc: `HasFresh α` implies a computably infinite type.
items.statement: instance HasFresh.to_infinite (α : Type u) [HasFresh α] : Infinite α

items.name: Cslib.HasFresh.ofNatEmbed
items.doc: Construct a fresh element from an embedding of `ℕ` using `Nat.find`.
items.statement: def HasFresh.ofNatEmbed {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] (e : ℕ ↪ α) : HasFresh α

items.name: Cslib.HasFresh.ofSucc
items.doc: Construct a fresh element given a function `f` with `x < f x`.
items.statement:
def HasFresh.ofSucc {α : Type u} [Inhabited α] [SemilatticeSup α] (f : α → α) (hf : ∀ x, x < f x) :
    HasFresh α

items.name: Cslib.FreeUnionConfig
items.doc: Configuration for the `free_union` term elaborator.
items.statement:
structure FreeUnionConfig where
  /-- For `free_union Var`, include all `x : Var`. Defaults to true. -/
  singleton : Bool := true
  /-- For `free_union Var`, include all `xs : Finset Var`. Defaults to true. -/
  finset : Bool := true

items.name: Cslib.HasFresh.freeUnion
items.doc: Elaborator for `free_union`.
items.statement: def HasFresh.freeUnion : TermElab

modules.title: Chains with a designated start and end
modules.doc:
This file defines `List.IsChainFromTo`, a variant of `List.IsChain` that also fixes the first and
last element of the chain. Such a chain is an explicit witness for the fact that its end point is
reachable from its start point, and its length bounds the number of steps that are needed.

## Main definitions

* `List.IsChainFromTo r chain a b`: `chain` is a non-empty list whose adjacent elements are related
  by `r`, whose first element is `a` and whose last element is `b`.

## Main results

* `List.IsChainFromTo.reflTransGen`: the start and the end of a chain are related by
  `Relation.ReflTransGen`.
* `List.IsChainFromTo.head_induction_on`: induction on a chain, peeling off elements at the start.
* `List.IsChainFromTo.exists_length_lt_of_not_nodup`: a chain with duplicates can always be
  shortened.
* `List.IsChainFromTo.exists_nodup`: iterating the above yields a chain without duplicates.

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo
items.doc:
A "chain from to" is a list of elements where adjacent elements relate to each other
(cf. `List.IsChain`) and start and end with specific elements.
items.statement:
structure IsChainFromTo {α : Type*} (r : α → α → Prop) (chain : List α) (a b : α) : Prop where
  isChain : chain.IsChain r
  ne_nil : chain ≠ []
  head_eq : chain.head ne_nil = a
  getLast_eq : chain.getLast ne_nil = b

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.length_pos
items.doc: A chain has at least one element.
items.statement: lemma IsChainFromTo.length_pos (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) : 0 < chain.length

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.getElem_zero
items.doc: The first element of an `r`-chain from `a` to `b` is `a`.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.getElem_zero (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) :
    chain[0]'hc.length_pos = a

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.getElem_length_sub_one
items.doc: The last element of an `r`-chain from `a` to `b` is `b`.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.getElem_length_sub_one (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) :
    chain[chain.length - 1]'(by have := hc.length_pos; lia) = b

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.reflTransGen
items.doc: The start and the end of an `r`-chain are reflexively-transitively related by `r`.
items.statement:
theorem IsChainFromTo.reflTransGen (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen r a b

items.name: List.IsChain.isChainFromTo_of_ne_nil
items.doc: Create a `List.IsChainFromTo` from a non-empty `List.IsChain`.
items.statement:
theorem IsChain.isChainFromTo_of_ne_nil
    {chain : List α} (hc : chain.IsChain r) (h_ne_nil : chain ≠ []) :
    List.IsChainFromTo r chain (chain.head h_ne_nil) (chain.getLast h_ne_nil)

items.name: List.isChainFromTo_singleton
items.doc: A one-element list is an `r`-chain from that element to itself.
items.statement: lemma isChainFromTo_singleton : List.IsChainFromTo r [a] a a

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.cons
items.doc: Prepend an `r`-related element to the start of the chain.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.cons (h : r a b) (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r b c) :
    (a :: chain).IsChainFromTo r a c

items.name: List.isChainFromTo_pair_iff
items.statement:
lemma isChainFromTo_pair_iff {a a' b b' : α} :
    List.IsChainFromTo r [a, b] a' b' ↔ r a b ∧ a = a' ∧ b = b'

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.of_cons_cons
items.doc: Removing the head yields a valid chain.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.of_cons_cons {x y : α} (hc : (x :: y :: chain).IsChainFromTo r a b) :
    (y :: chain).IsChainFromTo r y b

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.append_tail
items.doc:
Appending a chain and the tail of a second one whose start point equals the end point of the
first yields a valid chain.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.append_tail (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) {chain' : List α}
    (hc' : chain'.IsChainFromTo r b c) : (chain ++ chain'.tail).IsChainFromTo r a c

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.snoc
items.doc: Add an `r`-related element to the end of the chain.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.snoc (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) (h : r b c) :
    (chain ++ [c]).IsChainFromTo r a c

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.append_dropLast
items.doc:
Appending a chain, dropping its last element and another chain whose start point equals
the end point of the first chain yields a valid chain.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.append_dropLast (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) {chain' : List α}
    (hc' : chain'.IsChainFromTo r b c) : (chain.dropLast ++ chain').IsChainFromTo r a c

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.take
items.doc:
Taking the first `i + 1` elements of a chain yields a chain from the same start point to
`chain[i]`.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.take (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < chain.length) :
    (chain.take (i + 1)).IsChainFromTo r a chain[i]

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.drop
items.doc:
Dropping the first `i` elements of a chain yields a chain from `chain[i]` to the same end
point.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.drop (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < chain.length) :
    (chain.drop i).IsChainFromTo r chain[i] b

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.head_induction_on
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.head_induction_on
    {motive : ∀ {chain : List α} {a b : α}, chain.IsChainFromTo r a b → Prop}
    (h_refl : ∀ {a : α}, motive (isChainFromTo_singleton (r := r) (a := a)))
    (h_head : ∀ {a b c : α} {chain : List α} (hab : r a b) (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r b c),
      motive hc → motive (hc.cons hab))
    {chain : List α} {a b : α} (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) : motive hc

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.reflTransGen_of_mem
items.doc: Any element of an `r`-chain from `a` to `b` is reflexively-transitively related from `a`.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.reflTransGen_of_mem (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) {x : α} (mem : x ∈ chain) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen r a x

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.reflTransGen_of_mem'
items.doc: Any element of an `r`-chain from `a` to `b` is reflexively-transitively related to `b`.

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.exists_length_lt_of_not_nodup
items.doc:
If there is an `r`-chain from `a` to `b` with duplicates, then there is a shorter `r`-chain
from `a` to `b` (the one that skips the part between the duplicates).
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.exists_length_lt_of_not_nodup
    (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b)
    (h_dup : ¬ chain.Nodup) :
    ∃ chain' : List α, chain'.IsChainFromTo r a b ∧ chain'.length < chain.length

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.exists_nodup
items.doc: For any `r`-chain from `a` to `b` there is one without duplicates.
items.statement:
lemma IsChainFromTo.exists_nodup (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b) :
    ∃ chain' : List α, chain'.IsChainFromTo r a b ∧ chain'.Nodup

modules.title: Asymptotic bounds on natural numbers
modules.doc:
For any natural base greater than one, exponentials eventually dominate fixed multiples of
powers, and fixed multiples of logarithms are eventually at most the input. The inequalities
are stated in `ℕ`; the polynomial bound specializes Mathlib's
`isLittleO_pow_const_const_pow_of_one_lt`.

items.name: Nat.eventually_mul_pow_le_pow
items.doc:
Every fixed multiple of a power is eventually at most an exponential of base greater
than one.
items.statement:
theorem eventually_mul_pow_le_pow (c k : ℕ) {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * n ^ k ≤ b ^ n

items.name: Nat.eventually_add_one_le_pow_div
items.doc:
The quotient of an exponential of base greater than one by the input is eventually
at least the input plus one.
items.statement:
theorem eventually_add_one_le_pow_div {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, n + 1 ≤ b ^ n / n

items.name: Nat.eventually_mul_log_le
items.doc:
Every fixed multiple of the logarithm in a base greater than one is eventually at most
the input.
items.statement:
theorem eventually_mul_log_le (c : ℕ) {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * log b n ≤ n

items.name: Nat.eventually_mul_log2_le
items.doc: Every fixed multiple of the binary logarithm is eventually at most the input.
items.statement:
theorem eventually_mul_log2_le (c : ℕ) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * log2 n ≤ n

modules.title: A logarithmic lower bound for the factorial
modules.doc: Bounding one term of the exponential series gives `n log n - n ≤ log (n!)`, including at zero.

items.name: Nat.mul_log_sub_le_log_factorial
items.doc: The logarithm of the factorial is at least `n log n - n`.
items.statement:
theorem mul_log_sub_le_log_factorial (n : ℕ) :
    (n : ℝ) * Real.log n - n ≤ Real.log n.factorial

modules.title: Polynomial bounds on natural-valued functions
modules.doc:
`PolynomiallyBounded f` means that `f n ≤ n ^ d` eventually, for some fixed degree `d`.
This is equivalent to a real-valued `IsBigO` bound and to a bound `c * (n + 1) ^ d`
at every input. It is a growth condition and does not assert computability.

items.name: Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded
items.doc: A function is polynomially bounded if a fixed power eventually bounds its values.
items.statement: def PolynomiallyBounded (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.polynomiallyBounded_iff_isBigO
items.doc: Polynomial growth is equivalent to a big-O bound after casting to the reals.
items.statement:
theorem polynomiallyBounded_iff_isBigO {f : ℕ → ℕ} :
    PolynomiallyBounded f ↔
      ∃ d : ℕ, (fun n => (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ d)

items.name: Cslib.polynomiallyBounded_iff_le
items.doc: A polynomial bound can absorb every finite prefix into its constant factor.
items.statement:
theorem polynomiallyBounded_iff_le {f : ℕ → ℕ} :
    PolynomiallyBounded f ↔ ∃ c d : ℕ, ∀ n, f n ≤ c * (n + 1) ^ d

modules.title: Segments defined by a strictly monotonic function on Nat
modules.doc:
Given a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ` and `k : ℕ` with `k ≥ f 0`,
`Nat.segment f k` is the unique `m : ℕ` such that `f m ≤ k < f (m + 1)`.
`Nat.segment f k` is defined to be 0 for `k < f 0`.
This file defines `Nat.segment` and proves various properties about it.

items.name: Nat.segment
items.doc: The `f`-segment of `k`, where `f : ℕ → ℕ` will be assumed to be at least StrictMono.
items.statement: noncomputable def Nat.segment (f : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Nat.strictMono_infinite
items.doc: Any strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ` has an infinite range.
items.statement:
theorem strictMono_infinite (hm : StrictMono f) :
    (range f).Infinite

items.name: Nat.infinite_strictMono
items.doc: Any infinite subset of `ℕ` is the range of a strictly monotonic function.
items.statement:
theorem infinite_strictMono {ns : Set ℕ} (h : ns.Infinite) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono f ∧ range f = ns

items.name: Nat.nth_succ_gap
items.doc:
There is a gap between two successive occurrences of a predicate `p : ℕ → Prop`,
assuming `p` (as a set) is infinite.
items.statement:
theorem nth_succ_gap {p : ℕ → Prop} (hf : (ofPred p).Infinite) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ k < nth p (n + 1) - nth p n, 0 < k → ¬ p (k + nth p n)

items.name: Nat.nth_of_strictMono
items.doc:
For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, `f n` is exactly the n-th
element of the range of `f`.
items.statement:
theorem nth_of_strictMono (hm : StrictMono f) (n : ℕ) :
    f n = nth (· ∈ range f) n

items.name: Nat.count_notMem_range_pos
items.doc: If `f 0 = 0`, then `0` is below any `n` not in the range of `f`.
items.statement:
theorem count_notMem_range_pos (h0 : f 0 = 0) (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∉ range f) :
    0 < count (· ∈ range f) n

items.name: Nat.strictMono_range_gap
items.doc:
For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, no number (strictly) between
`f m` and ` f (m + 1)` is in the range of `f`.
items.statement:
theorem strictMono_range_gap (hm : StrictMono f) {m k : ℕ}
    (hl : f m < k) (hu : k < f (m + 1)) : k ∉ range f

items.name: Nat.segment_idem
items.doc: For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, the segment of `f k` is `k`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_idem (hm : StrictMono f) (k : ℕ) :
    segment f (f k) = k

items.name: Nat.segment_pre_zero
items.doc: For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, `segment f k = 0` for all `k < f 0`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_pre_zero (hm : StrictMono f) {k : ℕ} (h : k < f 0) :
    segment f k = 0

items.name: Nat.segment_zero
items.doc: For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ` with `f 0 = 0`, `segment f 0 = 0`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_zero (hm : StrictMono f) (h0 : f 0 = 0) :
    segment f 0 = 0

items.name: Nat.segment_plus_one
items.doc: A slight restatement of the definition of `segment` which has proven useful.
items.statement:
theorem segment_plus_one (h0 : f 0 = 0) (k : ℕ) :
    segment f k + 1 = count (· ∈ range f) (k + 1)

items.name: Nat.segment_upper_bound
items.doc:
For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ` with `f 0 = 0`,
`k < f (segment f k + 1)` for all `k : ℕ`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_upper_bound (hm : StrictMono f) (h0 : f 0 = 0) (k : ℕ) :
    k < f (segment f k + 1)

items.name: Nat.segment_lower_bound
items.doc:
For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ` with `f 0 = 0`,
`f (segment f k) ≤ k` for all `k : ℕ`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_lower_bound (hm : StrictMono f) (h0 : f 0 = 0) (k : ℕ) :
    f (segment f k) ≤ k

items.name: Nat.segment_range_val
items.doc:
For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, all `k` satisfying `f m ≤ k < f (m + 1)`
has `segment f k = m`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_range_val (hm : StrictMono f) {m k : ℕ}
    (hl : f m ≤ k) (hu : k < f (m + 1)) : segment f k = m

items.name: Nat.segment_galois_connection
items.doc:
For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ` with `f 0 = 0`,
`f` and `segment f` form a Galois connection.
items.statement:
theorem segment_galois_connection (hm : StrictMono f) (h0 : f 0 = 0) :
    GaloisConnection f (segment f)

items.name: Nat.segment'
items.doc:
`segment'` is a helper function that will be proved to be equal to `segment`.
It facilitates the proofs of some theorems below.
items.statement: noncomputable def segment' (f : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Nat.base_zero_strictMono
items.statement:
theorem base_zero_strictMono (hm : StrictMono f) :
    StrictMono (f · - f 0)

items.name: Nat.segment'_eq_segment
items.doc:
For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`,
`segment' f` and `segment f` are actually equal.
items.statement:
theorem segment'_eq_segment (hm : StrictMono f) :
    segment' f = segment f

items.name: Nat.segment_zero'
items.doc: For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, `segment f k = 0` for all `k ≤ f 0`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_zero' (hm : StrictMono f) {k : ℕ} (h : k ≤ f 0) :
    segment f k = 0

items.name: Nat.segment_upper_bound'
items.doc: For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, `k < f (segment f k + 1)` for all `k ≥ f 0`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_upper_bound' (hm : StrictMono f) {k : ℕ} (h : f 0 ≤ k) :
    k < f (segment f k + 1)

items.name: Nat.segment_lower_bound'
items.doc: For a strictly monotonic function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, `f (segment f k) ≤ k` for all `k ≥ f 0`.
items.statement:
theorem segment_lower_bound' (hm : StrictMono f) {k : ℕ} (h : f 0 ≤ k) :
    f (segment f k) ≤ k

modules.title: Definition of `ωSequence` and functions on infinite sequences
modules.doc:
An `ωSequence α` is an infinite sequence of elements of `α`.  It is basically
a wrapper around the type `ℕ → α` which supports the dot-notation and
the analogues of many familiar API functions of `List α`.  In particular,
the element at position `n : ℕ` of `s : ωSequence α` is obtained using the
function application notation `s n`.

In this file we define `ωSequence` and its API functions.
Most code below is adapted from Mathlib.Data.Stream.Defs.

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence
items.doc: An `ωSequence α` is an infinite sequence of elements of `α`.
items.statement:
structure ωSequence (α : Type u) where
  /-- The function that defines this infinite sequence. -/
  get : ℕ → α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.head
items.doc: Head of an ω-sequence: `ωSequence.head s = ωSequence s 0`.
items.statement: abbrev head (s : ωSequence α) : α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail
items.doc: Tail of an ω-sequence: `ωSequence.tail (h :: t) = t`.
items.statement: def tail (s : ωSequence α) : ωSequence α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop
items.doc: Drop first `n` elements of an ω-sequence.
items.statement: def drop (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : ωSequence α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take
items.doc: `take n s` returns a list of the `n` first elements of ω-sequence `s`
items.statement: def take : ℕ → ωSequence α → List α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract
items.doc: Get the list containing the elements of `xs` from position `m` to `n - 1`.
items.statement: def extract (xs : ωSequence α) (m n : ℕ) : List α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cons
items.doc: Prepend an element to an ω-sequence.
items.statement: def cons (a : α) (s : ωSequence α) : ωSequence α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.appendωSequence
items.doc: Append an ω-sequence to a list.
items.statement: def appendωSequence : List α → ωSequence α → ωSequence α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.const
items.doc: The constant ω-sequence: `ωSequence n (ωSequence.const a) = a`.
items.statement: def const (a : α) : ωSequence α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map
items.doc: Apply a function `f` to all elements of an ω-sequence `s`.
items.statement: def map (f : α → β) (s : ωSequence α) : ωSequence β

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.zip
items.doc:
Zip two ω-sequences using a binary operation:
`ωSequence n (ωSequence.zip f s₁ s₂) = f (ωSequence s₁) (ωSequence s₂)`.
items.statement: def zip (f : α → β → δ) (s₁ : ωSequence α) (s₂ : ωSequence β) : ωSequence δ

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.iterate
items.doc: Iterates of a function as an ω-sequence.
items.statement: def iterate (f : α → α) (a : α) : ωSequence α

modules.title: Flattening an infinite sequence of lists
modules.doc:
Given `ls : ωSequence (List α)`, `ls.flatten` is the infinite sequence formed by
concatenating all members of `ls`.  For this definition to make proper sense,
we will consistently assume that all lists in `ls` are nonempty.  Furthermore,
in order to simplify the definition, we will also assume [Inhabited α].

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cumLen
items.doc:
Given an ω-sequence `ls` of lists, `ls.cumLen k` is the cumulative sum
of `(ls k).length` for `k = 0, ..., k - 1`.
items.statement: def cumLen (ls : ωSequence (List α)) : ℕ → ℕ

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cumLen_zero
items.statement:
theorem cumLen_zero {ls : ωSequence (List α)} :
    ls.cumLen 0 = 0

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cumLen_succ
items.statement:
theorem cumLen_succ (ls : ωSequence (List α)) (k : ℕ) :
    ls.cumLen (k + 1) = ls.cumLen k + (ls k).length

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cumLen_one_add_drop
items.statement:
theorem cumLen_one_add_drop (ls : ωSequence (List α)) (k : ℕ) :
    ls.cumLen (1 + k) = (ls 0).length + (ls.drop 1).cumLen k

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cumLen_strictMono
items.doc: If all lists in `ls` are nonempty, then `ls.cumLen` is strictly monotonic.
items.statement:
theorem cumLen_strictMono {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length) :
    StrictMono ls.cumLen

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cumLen_segment_zero
items.statement:
theorem cumLen_segment_zero {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length)
    (n : ℕ) (h_n : n < (ls 0).length) : segment ls.cumLen n = 0

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cumLen_segment_one_add
items.statement:
theorem cumLen_segment_one_add {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length)
    (n : ℕ) (h_n : (ls 0).length ≤ n) :
    segment ls.cumLen n = 1 + segment (ls.drop 1).cumLen (n - (ls 0).length)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.flatten
items.doc:
Given an ω-sequence `ls` of lists, `ls.flatten` is the infinite sequence
formed by the concatenation of all of them.  For the definition to make proper
sense, we will consistently assume that all lists in `ls` are nonempty.
items.statement: noncomputable def flatten [Inhabited α] (ls : ωSequence (List α)) : ωSequence α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.flatten_def
items.statement:
theorem flatten_def [Inhabited α] (ls : ωSequence (List α)) (n : ℕ) :
    flatten ls n = (ls (segment ls.cumLen n))[n - ls.cumLen (segment ls.cumLen n)]!

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.flatten_get_add
Cslib.ωSequence.flatten_get_cumLen
items.statement:
theorem flatten_get_cumLen [Inhabited α] (ls : ωSequence (List α)) {n : ℕ}
    (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < (ls n).length) : ls.flatten (ls.cumLen n) = (ls n)[0]'(hpos n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cons_flatten
items.doc: `ls.flatten` equals the concatenation of `ls.head` and `ls.tail.flatten`.
items.statement:
theorem cons_flatten [Inhabited α] {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length) :
    ls.head ++ω ls.tail.flatten = ls.flatten

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_flatten
items.doc: `ls.flatten` equals the concatenation of `(ls.take n).flatten` and `(ls.drop n).flatten`.
items.statement:
theorem append_flatten [Inhabited α] {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length)
    (n : ℕ) : (ls.take n).flatten ++ω (ls.drop n).flatten = ls.flatten

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_length_take_sum
items.doc: The sum of `List.map List.length (take n ls)` is `ls.cumLen n`.
items.statement:
theorem map_length_take_sum {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (n : ℕ) :
    (List.map List.length (take n ls)).sum = ls.cumLen n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.flatten_take_drop
items.doc:
In fact, `(ls.take n).flatten` is `ls.flatten.take (ls.cumLen n)`
and `(ls.drop n).flatten` is `ls.flatten.drop (ls.cumLen n)`.
items.statement:
theorem flatten_take_drop [Inhabited α]
    {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length) (n : ℕ) :
    (ls.take n).flatten = ls.flatten.take (ls.cumLen n) ∧
    (ls.drop n).flatten = ls.flatten.drop (ls.cumLen n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.flatten_take
items.statement:
theorem flatten_take [Inhabited α]
    {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length) (n : ℕ) :
    (ls.take n).flatten = ls.flatten.take (ls.cumLen n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.flatten_drop
items.statement:
theorem flatten_drop [Inhabited α]
    {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length) (n : ℕ) :
    (ls.drop n).flatten = ls.flatten.drop (ls.cumLen n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_flatten
items.doc:
`ls n` is the segment from position `ls.cumLen n` to position `ls.cumLen (n + 1) - 1`
of `ls.flatten`
items.statement:
theorem extract_flatten [Inhabited α] {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length)
    (n : ℕ) : ls.flatten.extract (ls.cumLen n) (ls.cumLen (n + 1)) = ls n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.forall_flatten_iff
items.doc: Distributivity of "forall" over `flatten`.
items.statement:
theorem forall_flatten_iff [Inhabited α] {ls : ωSequence (List α)} (h_ls : ∀ k, 0 < (ls k).length)
    (p : α → Prop) : (∀ n, p (ls.flatten n)) ↔ ∀ k, (ls k).Forall p

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.toSegs
items.doc:
Given an ω-sequence `s` and a function `f : ℕ → ℕ`, `s.toSegs f` is the ω-sequence
whose `n`-th element is the list `s.extract (f n) (f (n + 1))`.  In all its uses, the
function `f` will always be assumed to be strictly monotonic with `f 0 = 0`.
items.statement: def toSegs (s : ωSequence α) (f : ℕ → ℕ) : ωSequence (List α)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.toSegs_def
items.statement:
theorem toSegs_def (s : ωSequence α) (f : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    s.toSegs f n = s.extract (f n) (f (n + 1))

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.segment_toSegs_cumLen
items.doc: `(s.toSegs f).cumLen` is `f` itself.

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.strictMono_flatten
items.doc: `(s.toSegs f).flatten` is `s` itself.

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.infOcc
items.doc: The set of elements that appear infinitely often in an ω-sequence.
items.statement: def infOcc (xs : ωSequence α) : Set α

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.frequently_iff_strictMono
items.doc: An alternative characterization of "infinitely often".
items.statement:
theorem frequently_iff_strictMono {p : ℕ → Prop} :
    (∃ᶠ n in atTop, p n) ↔ ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono f ∧ ∀ m, p (f m)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.frequently_in_finite_type
items.doc:
In a finite type, the elements of a set occurs infinitely often iff
some element in the set occurs infinitely often.
items.statement:
theorem frequently_in_finite_type [Finite α] {s : Set α} {xs : ωSequence α} :
    (∃ᶠ k in atTop, xs k ∈ s) ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ᶠ k in atTop, xs k = x

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.frequently_in_strictMono
items.doc:
If `p` is true infinitely often, then `p` is true in infinitely many segments
of any strictly monotonic function `f`.

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.strictMono_of_infinite
items.doc: Every infinite subset of ℕ is the range of a strictly monotonic function from ℕ to ℕ.
items.statement:
theorem strictMono_of_infinite {ns : Set ℕ} (h : ns.Infinite) :
    ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ range φ = ns

modules.title: ω-sequences a.k.a. infinite sequences
modules.doc: Most code below is adapted from Mathlib.Data.Stream.Init.

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.eta
items.statement: protected theorem eta (s : ωSequence α) : head s ::ω tail s = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cons_head_tail
items.doc: Alias for `ωSequence.eta` to match `List` API.
items.statement: alias cons_head_tail

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.ext
items.statement: protected theorem ext {s₁ s₂ : ωSequence α} : (∀ n, s₁ n = s₂ n) → s₁ = s₂

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_fun
items.statement: theorem get_fun (f : ℕ → α) (n : ℕ) : ωSequence.mk f n = f n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_zero_cons
items.statement: theorem get_zero_cons (a : α) (s : ωSequence α) : (a ::ω s) 0 = a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.head_cons
items.statement: theorem head_cons (a : α) (s : ωSequence α) : head (a ::ω s) = a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_cons
items.statement: theorem tail_cons (a : α) (s : ωSequence α) : tail (a ::ω s) = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_drop
items.statement: theorem get_drop (n m : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : (drop m s) n = s (m + n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_eq_drop
items.statement: theorem tail_eq_drop (s : ωSequence α) : tail s = drop 1 s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_drop
items.statement: theorem drop_drop (n m : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : drop n (drop m s) = drop (m + n) s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_tail
items.statement: theorem get_tail {n : ℕ} {s : ωSequence α} : s.tail n = s (n + 1)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_drop'
items.statement: theorem tail_drop' {i : ℕ} {s : ωSequence α} : tail (drop i s) = s.drop (i + 1)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_tail'
items.statement: theorem drop_tail' {i : ℕ} {s : ωSequence α} : drop i (tail s) = s.drop (i + 1)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_drop
items.statement: theorem tail_drop (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : tail (drop n s) = drop n (tail s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_succ
items.statement: theorem get_succ (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : s (succ n) = (tail s) n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_succ_cons
items.statement: theorem get_succ_cons (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) (x : α) : (x ::ω s) n.succ = s n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_cons_append_zero
items.statement:
lemma get_cons_append_zero {a : α} {x : List α} {s : ωSequence α} :
    (a :: x ++ω s) 0 = a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_get_zero_of_ne_nil
items.statement:
lemma append_get_zero_of_ne_nil {x : List α} {s : ωSequence α} (h : x ≠ []) :
    (x ++ω s) 0 = x.head h

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_eq_cons
items.statement: lemma append_eq_cons {a : α} {as : ωSequence α} : [a] ++ω as = a ::ω as

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_zero
items.statement: theorem drop_zero {s : ωSequence α} : s.drop 0 = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_succ
items.statement: theorem drop_succ (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : drop (succ n) s = drop n (tail s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.head_drop
items.statement: theorem head_drop (a : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ) : (a.drop n).head = a n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cons_injective2
items.statement: theorem cons_injective2 : Function.Injective2 (cons : α → ωSequence α → ωSequence α)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cons_injective_left
items.statement: theorem cons_injective_left (s : ωSequence α) : Function.Injective fun x => cons x s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cons_injective_right
items.statement: theorem cons_injective_right (x : α) : Function.Injective (cons x)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_map
items.statement: theorem drop_map (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : drop n (map f s) = map f (drop n s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_map
items.statement: theorem get_map (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : (map f s) n = f (s n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_map
items.statement: theorem tail_map (s : ωSequence α) : tail (map f s) = map f (tail s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.head_map
items.statement: theorem head_map (s : ωSequence α) : head (map f s) = f (head s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_eq
items.statement: theorem map_eq (s : ωSequence α) : map f s = f (head s) ::ω map f (tail s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_cons
items.statement: theorem map_cons (a : α) (s : ωSequence α) : map f (a ::ω s) = f a ::ω map f s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_id
items.statement: theorem map_id (s : ωSequence α) : map id s = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_map
items.statement: theorem map_map (g : β → δ) (f : α → β) (s : ωSequence α) : map g (map f s) = map (g ∘ f) s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_tail
items.statement: theorem map_tail (s : ωSequence α) : map f (tail s) = tail (map f s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_zip
items.statement:
theorem drop_zip (n : ℕ) (s₁ : ωSequence α) (s₂ : ωSequence β) :
    drop n (zip f s₁ s₂) = zip f (drop n s₁) (drop n s₂)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_zip
items.statement:
theorem get_zip (n : ℕ) (s₁ : ωSequence α) (s₂ : ωSequence β) :
    (zip f s₁ s₂) n = f (s₁ n) (s₂ n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.head_zip
items.statement:
theorem head_zip (s₁ : ωSequence α) (s₂ : ωSequence β) :
    head (zip f s₁ s₂) = f (head s₁) (head s₂)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_zip
items.statement:
theorem tail_zip (s₁ : ωSequence α) (s₂ : ωSequence β) :
    tail (zip f s₁ s₂) = zip f (tail s₁) (tail s₂)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.zip_eq
items.statement:
theorem zip_eq (s₁ : ωSequence α) (s₂ : ωSequence β) :
    zip f s₁ s₂ = f (head s₁) (head s₂) ::ω zip f (tail s₁) (tail s₂)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.const_eq
items.statement: theorem const_eq (a : α) : const a = a ::ω const a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_const
items.statement: theorem tail_const (a : α) : tail (const a) = const a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_const
items.statement: theorem map_const (f : α → β) (a : α) : map f (const a) = const (f a)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_const
items.statement: theorem get_const (n : ℕ) (a : α) : (const a) n = a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_const
items.statement: theorem drop_const (n : ℕ) (a : α) : drop n (const a) = const a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.head_iterate
items.statement: theorem head_iterate (f : α → α) (a : α) : head (iterate f a) = a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_iterate
items.statement:
theorem get_iterate (f : α → α) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
    iterate f a n = f^[n] a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_succ_iterate'
items.statement:
theorem get_succ_iterate' (n : ℕ) (f : α → α) (a : α) :
    iterate f a (succ n) = f (iterate f a n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.tail_iterate
items.statement: theorem tail_iterate (f : α → α) (a : α) : tail (iterate f a) = iterate f (f a)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.iterate_eq
items.statement: theorem iterate_eq (f : α → α) (a : α) : iterate f a = a ::ω iterate f (f a)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_zero_iterate
items.statement: theorem get_zero_iterate (f : α → α) (a : α) : (iterate f a) 0 = a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_succ_iterate
items.statement:
theorem get_succ_iterate (n : ℕ) (f : α → α) (a : α) :
    iterate f a (succ n) = iterate f (f a) n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.iterate_id
items.statement: theorem iterate_id (a : α) : iterate id a = const a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_iterate
items.statement: theorem map_iterate (f : α → α) (a : α) : iterate f (f a) = map f (iterate f a)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.nil_append_ωSequence
items.statement: theorem nil_append_ωSequence (s : ωSequence α) : appendωSequence [] s = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cons_append_ωSequence
items.statement:
theorem cons_append_ωSequence (a : α) (l : List α) (s : ωSequence α) :
    appendωSequence (a :: l) s = a ::ω appendωSequence l s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.singleton_append_ωSequence
items.statement:
theorem singleton_append_ωSequence (a : α) (s : ωSequence α) :
[a] ++ω s = a ::ω s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_append_ωSequence
items.statement:
theorem append_append_ωSequence : ∀ (l₁ l₂ : List α) (s : ωSequence α),
    l₁ ++ l₂ ++ω s = l₁ ++ω (l₂ ++ω s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_append_left
items.statement: lemma get_append_left (h : n < x.length) : (x ++ω a) n = x[n]

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_append_right
items.statement: lemma get_append_right : (x ++ω a) (x.length + n) = a n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_append_right'
items.statement:
theorem get_append_right' {xl : List α} {xs : ωSequence α} {k : ℕ} (h : xl.length ≤ k) :
    (xl ++ω xs) k = xs (k - xl.length)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_append_length
items.statement: lemma get_append_length : (x ++ω a) x.length = a 0

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_right_injective
items.statement: lemma append_right_injective (h : x ++ω a = x ++ω b) : a = b

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_right_inj
items.statement: lemma append_right_inj : x ++ω a = x ++ω b ↔ a = b

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_left_injective
items.statement: lemma append_left_injective (h : x ++ω a = y ++ω b) (hl : x.length = y.length) : x = y

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_left_right_injective
items.statement:
theorem append_left_right_injective (l1 l2 : List α) (s1 s2 : ωSequence α)
    (h1 : l1 ++ω s1 = l2 ++ω s2) (h2 : l1.length = l2.length) : l1 = l2 ∧ s1 = s2

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_append_ωSequence
items.statement:
theorem map_append_ωSequence (f : α → β) :
    ∀ (l : List α) (s : ωSequence α), map f (l ++ω s) = List.map f l ++ω map f s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_append_ωSequence
items.statement: theorem drop_append_ωSequence : ∀ (l : List α) (s : ωSequence α), drop l.length (l ++ω s) = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_ωSequence_head_tail
items.statement: theorem append_ωSequence_head_tail (s : ωSequence α) : [head s] ++ω tail s = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_zero
items.statement: theorem take_zero (s : ωSequence α) : take 0 s = []

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_succ
items.statement: theorem take_succ (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : take (succ n) s = head s :: take n (tail s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_succ_cons
items.statement:
theorem take_succ_cons {a : α} (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) :
    take (n+1) (a ::ω s) = a :: take n s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_succ'
items.statement: theorem take_succ' {s : ωSequence α} : ∀ n, s.take (n+1) = s.take n ++ [s n]

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_one
items.statement:
theorem take_one {xs : ωSequence α} :
    xs.take 1 = [xs 0]

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.length_take
items.statement: theorem length_take (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : (take n s).length = n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_take
items.statement: theorem take_take {s : ωSequence α} : ∀ {m n}, (s.take n).take m = s.take (min n m)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.concat_take_get
items.statement: theorem concat_take_get {n : ℕ} {s : ωSequence α} : s.take n ++ [s n] = s.take (n + 1)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.getElem?_take
items.statement: theorem getElem?_take {s : ωSequence α} : ∀ {k n}, k < n → (s.take n)[k]? = s k

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.getElem?_take_succ
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_take_succ (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) :
    (take (succ n) s)[n]? = some (s n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.dropLast_take
items.statement:
theorem dropLast_take {n : ℕ} {xs : ωSequence α} :
    (ωSequence.take n xs).dropLast = ωSequence.take (n-1) xs

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_take_drop
items.statement: theorem append_take_drop (n : ℕ) (s : ωSequence α) : appendωSequence (take n s) (drop n s) = s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_take
items.statement: lemma append_take : x ++ (a.take n) = (x ++ω a).take (x.length + n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_get
items.statement: lemma take_get (h : m < (a.take n).length) : (a.take n)[m] = a m

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_append_of_le_length
items.statement:
theorem take_append_of_le_length (h : n ≤ x.length) :
    (x ++ω a).take n = x.take n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_add
items.statement: lemma take_add : a.take (m + n) = a.take m ++ (a.drop m).take n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_prefix_take_left
items.statement: lemma take_prefix_take_left (h : m ≤ n) : a.take m <+: a.take n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_prefix
items.statement: lemma take_prefix : a.take m <+: a.take n ↔ m ≤ n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.map_take
items.statement: lemma map_take (f : α → β) : (a.take n).map f = (a.map f).take n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_drop
items.statement: lemma take_drop : (a.drop m).take n = (a.take (m + n)).drop m

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_append_of_le_length
items.statement:
lemma drop_append_of_le_length (h : n ≤ x.length) :
    (x ++ω a).drop n = x.drop n ++ω a

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_append_of_ge_length
items.statement:
theorem drop_append_of_ge_length {xl : List α} {xs : ωSequence α} {n : ℕ} (h : xl.length ≤ n) :
    (xl ++ω xs).drop n = xs.drop (n - xl.length)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_theorem
items.statement: theorem take_theorem (s₁ s₂ : ωSequence α) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, take n s₁ = take n s₂) : s₁ = s₂

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_eq_drop_take
items.statement:
theorem extract_eq_drop_take {xs : ωSequence α} {m n : ℕ} :
    xs.extract m n = take (n - m) (xs.drop m)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_eq_ofFn
items.statement:
theorem extract_eq_ofFn {xs : ωSequence α} {m n : ℕ} :
    xs.extract m n = List.ofFn (fun k : Fin (n - m) ↦ xs (m + k))

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_eq_extract
Cslib.ωSequence.extract_eq_take
items.statement:
theorem extract_eq_take {xs : ωSequence α} {n : ℕ} :
    xs.extract 0 n = xs.take n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_extract_drop
items.statement:
theorem append_extract_drop {xs : ωSequence α} {n : ℕ} :
    (xs.extract 0 n) ++ω (xs.drop n) = xs

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_append_right_right
items.statement:
theorem extract_append_right_right {xl : List α} {xs : ωSequence α} {m n : ℕ} (h : xl.length ≤ m) :
    (xl ++ω xs).extract m n = xs.extract (m - xl.length) (n - xl.length)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_append_zero_right
items.statement:
theorem extract_append_zero_right {xl : List α} {xs : ωSequence α} {n : ℕ} (h : xl.length ≤ n) :
    (xl ++ω xs).extract 0 n = xl ++ (xs.extract 0 (n - xl.length))

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_drop
items.statement:
theorem extract_drop {xs : ωSequence α} {k m n : ℕ} :
    (xs.drop k).extract m n = xs.extract (k + m) (k + n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.length_extract
items.statement:
theorem length_extract {xs : ωSequence α} {m n : ℕ} :
    (xs.extract m n).length = n - m

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_eq_nil
items.statement:
theorem extract_eq_nil {xs : ωSequence α} {n : ℕ} :
    xs.extract n n = []

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_eq_nil_iff
items.statement:
theorem extract_eq_nil_iff {xs : ωSequence α} {m n : ℕ} :
    xs.extract m n = [] ↔ n ≤ m

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.get_extract
items.statement:
theorem get_extract {xs : ωSequence α} {m n k : ℕ} (h : k < n - m) :
    (xs.extract m n)[k]'(by simp [h]) = xs (m + k)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.append_extract_extract
items.statement:
theorem append_extract_extract {xs : ωSequence α} {k m n : ℕ} (h_km : k ≤ m) (h_mn : m ≤ n) :
    (xs.extract k m) ++ (xs.extract m n) = xs.extract k n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_succ_right
items.statement:
theorem extract_succ_right {xs : ωSequence α} {m n : ℕ} (h_mn : m ≤ n) :
    xs.extract m (n + 1) = xs.extract m n ++ [xs n]

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_lu_extract_lu
items.statement:
theorem extract_lu_extract_lu {xs : ωSequence α} {m n i j : ℕ} (h : j ≤ n - m) :
