    (xs.extract m n).extract i j = xs.extract (m + i) (m + j)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_0u_extract_lu
items.statement:
theorem extract_0u_extract_lu {xs : ωSequence α} {n i j : ℕ} (h : j ≤ n) :
    (xs.extract 0 n).extract i j = xs.extract i j

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.extract_0u_extract_l
items.statement:
theorem extract_0u_extract_l {xs : ωSequence α} {n i : ℕ} :
    (xs.extract 0 n).extract i = xs.extract i n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.take_extract
items.statement:
theorem take_extract {xs : ωSequence α} {m n k : ℕ} (h : k ≤ n - m) :
    (xs.extract m n).take k = xs.extract m (m + k)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_extract
items.statement:
theorem drop_extract {xs : ωSequence α} {m n k : ℕ} (h : k ≤ n - m) :
    (xs.extract m n).drop k = xs.extract (m + k) n

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.Step
items.doc:
`Step p q` means that whenever `p` holds at a position in `xs`, `q` holds at the next position
in `xs`.
items.statement: def Step (xs : ωSequence α) (p q : Set α) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.Step.mk
items.statement: theorem Step.mk {xs : ωSequence α} (h : ∀ k, xs k ∈ p → xs (k + 1) ∈ q) : Step xs p q

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.LeadsTo
items.doc:
"`p` leads to `q`" means that whenever `p` holds at a position in `xs`, `q` holds at the same
or a later position in `xs`.
items.statement: def LeadsTo (xs : ωSequence α) (p q : Set α) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.LeadsTo.mk
items.statement:
theorem LeadsTo.mk {xs : ωSequence α} (h : ∀ k, xs k ∈ p → ∃ k', k ≤ k' ∧ xs k' ∈ q) :
    LeadsTo xs p q

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.step_leadsTo
items.doc: `Step` implies `LeadsTo`.
items.statement: theorem step_leadsTo {p q : Set α} (h : xs.Step p q) : xs.LeadsTo p q

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.leadsTo_trans
items.doc: `LeadsTo` is transitive.
items.statement:
theorem leadsTo_trans {p q r : Set α}
    (h1 : xs.LeadsTo p q) (h2 : xs.LeadsTo q r) : xs.LeadsTo p r

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.leadsTo_cases_or
items.doc: If `p ∩ q` leads to `r` and `p ∩ qᶜ` leads to `s`, then `p` leads to `r ∪ s`.
items.statement:
theorem leadsTo_cases_or {p q r s : Set α}
    (h1 : xs.LeadsTo (p ∩ q) r) (h2 : xs.LeadsTo (p ∩ qᶜ) s) : xs.LeadsTo p (r ∪ s)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.until_frequently_not_leadsTo
items.doc: If `p` holds until `q` and `p` fails infinitely often, then `p` leads to `q`.
items.statement:
theorem until_frequently_not_leadsTo {p q : Set α}
    (h1 : xs.Step (p ∩ qᶜ) p) (h2 : ∃ᶠ k in atTop, xs k ∉ p) : xs.LeadsTo p q

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.until_frequently_leadsTo_and
items.doc: If `p` holds until `q` and `q` holds infinite often, then `p` leads to `p ∩ q`.
items.statement:
theorem until_frequently_leadsTo_and {p q : Set α}
    (h1 : xs.Step (p ∩ qᶜ) p) (h2 : ∃ᶠ k in atTop, xs k ∈ q) : xs.LeadsTo p (p ∩ q)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.frequently_leadsTo_frequently
items.doc: If `p` holds infinitely often and `p` leads to `q`, then `q` holds infinite often as well.
items.statement:
theorem frequently_leadsTo_frequently {p q : Set α}
    (h1 : ∃ᶠ k in atTop, xs k ∈ p) (h2 : xs.LeadsTo p q) : ∃ᶠ k in atTop, xs k ∈ q

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.drop_frequently_iff_frequently
items.statement:
theorem drop_frequently_iff_frequently {p : Set α} (n : ℕ) :
    (∃ᶠ k in atTop, (xs.drop n) k ∈ p) ↔ (∃ᶠ k in atTop, xs k ∈ p)

modules.title: Topology on ω-sequences
modules.doc:
The topology on ω-sequences is essentially the product topology when `ωSequence α` is
viewed as the product space `Π (n : ℕ), α`, where `α` is equipped with the discrete
topology.  The notion of "cylinders" are also ported from `Π (n : ℕ), α` and they form
a topological basis.

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.homeomorph
items.doc: The homeomorphisim from `ωSequence α` to `ℕ → WithDiscreteTopology α`.
items.statement: def homeomorph : ωSequence α ≃ₜ (ℕ → WithDiscreteTopology α)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.homeomorph_apply
items.statement:
lemma homeomorph_apply (xs : ωSequence α) (i : Nat) :
    homeomorph xs i = .toTopology ⊥ (xs i)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.homeomorph_symm_apply
items.statement:
lemma homeomorph_symm_apply (f : ℕ → WithDiscreteTopology α) :
    homeomorph.symm f = ωSequence.mk fun i => (f i).ofTopology

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cylinder
items.doc: Port the notion of "cylinders" from `ℕ → WithDiscreteTopology α` to `ωSequence α`.
items.statement: def cylinder (xs : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ) : Set (ωSequence α)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cylinder_def
items.doc: An alternative characterization of cylinders in terms of `ωSequence α` alone.
items.statement:
theorem cylinder_def (xs : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ) :
    xs.cylinder n = { ys | ∀ k, k < n → ys k = xs k }

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.cylinder_eq_prepend_range
items.doc: Yet another alternative characterization of cylinders in terms of `ωSequence α` alone.
items.statement:
theorem cylinder_eq_prepend_range (xs : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ) :
    xs.cylinder n = range (xs.take n ++ω ·)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.isTopologicalBasis_cylinders
items.doc: The cylinders form a topological basis.
items.statement:
theorem isTopologicalBasis_cylinders :
    IsTopologicalBasis { s | ∃ (xs : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ), s = xs.cylinder n }

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.isOpen_cylinder
items.doc: All cylinders are open sets.
items.statement:
theorem isOpen_cylinder (xs : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ) :
    IsOpen (xs.cylinder n)

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.nhds_cylinders
items.doc: Every ω-sequence in an open set belongs to a cylinder which is contained in the set.
items.statement:
theorem nhds_cylinders {xs : ωSequence α} {s : Set (ωSequence α)} (hx : xs ∈ s) (hs : IsOpen s) :
    ∃ (ys : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ), xs ∈ ys.cylinder n ∧ ys.cylinder n ⊆ s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.isOpen_iff
items.doc:
A set is open iff any ω-sequence in the set has a finite prefix all of whose infinite
extensions are also in the set.
items.statement:
theorem isOpen_iff (s : Set (ωSequence α)) :
    IsOpen s ↔ ∀ xs, xs ∈ s → ∃ n, ∀ ys, (xs.take n) ++ω ys ∈ s

items.name: Cslib.ωSequence.dense_iff
items.doc: A set is dense iff any finite sequence can be extended to an infinite sequence in the set.
items.statement:
theorem dense_iff (s : Set (ωSequence α)) :
    Dense s ↔ ∀ (xs : ωSequence α) (n : ℕ), ∃ ys, (xs.take n) ++ω ys ∈ s

modules.authors: Fabrizio Montesi, Devon Tuma, Quang Dao
modules.title: Polynomial Functors
modules.doc:
Definitions of common `PFunctor` constructions:
- `monomial A B`: constant direction `B` for any shape `a : A`
- `P + Q`: shapes are a disjoint sum, directions are defined by sum elimination on `a : P.A ⊕ Q.A`
- `P * Q`: shapes are pairs of underlying shapes, directions are a disjoint sum over both shapes.

Special cases `C`, `linear`, `selfMonomial`, `purePower`, the indeterminate `y`,
and canonical choices of `0` and `1` are defined as abbreviations or instances over `monomial`.
The scoped notations `A y^ B` and `y^ B` denote `monomial A B` and `purePower B`, respectively.

The child-map API includes `const`, `Unary`, and `DecidableEqChildren`.

items.name: PFunctor.ext
items.doc:
Two polynomial functors are equal if their head types are equal and their child types
agree over that equality.
items.statement:
theorem ext {P Q : PFunctor.{uA, uB}} (h : P.A = Q.A) (h' : ∀ a, P.B a = Q.B (h ▸ a)) :
    P = Q

items.name: PFunctor.const
items.doc: The constant child map for `a`.
items.statement: def const {P : PFunctor} (a : P.A) (x : α) : P.B a → α

items.name: PFunctor.const_apply
items.statement: theorem const_apply {P : PFunctor} (a : P.A) (x : α) (i : P.B a) : PFunctor.const a x i = x

items.name: PFunctor.monomial
items.doc: The monomial `PFunctor` with head type `A` and constant `B` for any `a : A`.
items.statement: abbrev monomial (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) : PFunctor

items.name: PFunctor.monomial_A
items.statement: lemma monomial_A (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) : (monomial A B).A = A

items.name: PFunctor.monomial_B
items.statement:
lemma monomial_B (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) (a : (monomial A B).A) :
    (monomial A B).B a = B

items.name: PFunctor.instZeroPFunctor
items.doc:
The zero polynomial functor, defined as `A = PEmpty` and `B _ = PEmpty`, is the identity with
respect to sum (up to equivalence).
items.statement: instance instZeroPFunctor : Zero PFunctor

items.name: PFunctor.instIsEmptyZeroPFunctor
items.statement: instance instIsEmptyZeroPFunctor : IsEmpty (0 : PFunctor.{uA, 0}).A

items.name: PFunctor.instOnePFunctor
items.doc:
The unit polynomial functor, defined as `A = PUnit` and `B _ = PEmpty`, is the identity with
respect to product (up to equivalence).
items.statement: instance instOnePFunctor : One PFunctor

items.name: PFunctor.instUniqueOneA
items.statement: instance instUniqueOneA : Unique (1 : PFunctor.{uA, 0}).A

items.name: PFunctor.instIsEmptyOneB
items.statement: instance instIsEmptyOneB (a : (1 : PFunctor.{uA, uB}).A) : IsEmpty ((1 : PFunctor.{uA, uB}).B a)

items.name: PFunctor.C
items.doc: The constant polynomial functor `P(y) = A y^ PEmpty = A`.
items.statement: abbrev C (A : Type uA) : PFunctor

items.name: PFunctor.linear
items.doc: The linear polynomial functor `P(y) = A y`.
items.statement: abbrev linear (A : Type uA) : PFunctor

items.name: PFunctor.selfMonomial
items.doc: The self-monomial polynomial functor `P(y) = S y^ S`.
items.statement: abbrev selfMonomial (S : Type uA) : PFunctor.{uA, uA}

items.name: PFunctor.purePower
items.doc: The pure-power polynomial functor `y^ B`, representable on `B`.
items.statement: abbrev purePower (B : Type uB) : PFunctor

items.name: PFunctor.y
items.doc:
The indeterminate polynomial functor `P(y) = y`, the identity with respect to
composition and tensor product (up to equivalence).
items.statement: abbrev y : PFunctor

items.name: PFunctor.C_pempty
items.statement: lemma C_pempty : C PEmpty = 0

items.name: PFunctor.C_punit
items.statement: lemma C_punit : C PUnit = 1

items.name: PFunctor.linear_punit
items.statement: lemma linear_punit : linear PUnit = y

items.name: PFunctor.selfMonomial_punit
items.statement: lemma selfMonomial_punit : selfMonomial PUnit = y

items.name: PFunctor.purePower_punit
items.statement: lemma purePower_punit : purePower PUnit = y

items.name: PFunctor.add
items.doc:
The sum of two polynomial functors `P` and `Q`, written as `P + Q`,
defined as the sum of the head types and the dependent sum recursor for the child types.

The child universes must agree. The named spelling `P.add Q` can elaborate in contexts where
`P + Q` fails to infer universes, such as under `PFunctor.W`; see `CslibTests.PFunctor`.
items.statement:
def add (P : PFunctor.{uA₁, uB}) (Q : PFunctor.{uA₂, uB}) :
PFunctor.{max uA₁ uA₂, uB}

items.name: PFunctor.instHAddPFunctor
items.statement:
instance instHAddPFunctor :
HAdd PFunctor.{uA₁, uB} PFunctor.{uA₂, uB} PFunctor.{max uA₁ uA₂, uB}

items.name: PFunctor.add_eq_add
items.statement:
lemma add_eq_add (P : PFunctor.{uA₁, uB}) (Q : PFunctor.{uA₂, uB}) :
P.add Q = P + Q

items.name: PFunctor.prod
items.doc:
The product of two polynomial functors `P` and `Q`, written as `P * Q`,
defined as the product of the head types and the sum of the child types.
items.statement:
def prod (P : PFunctor.{uA₁, uB₁}) (Q : PFunctor.{uA₂, uB₂}) :
PFunctor.{max uA₁ uA₂, max uB₁ uB₂}

items.name: PFunctor.instHMulPFunctor
items.statement:
instance instHMulPFunctor :
HMul PFunctor.{uA₁, uB₁} PFunctor.{uA₂, uB₂} PFunctor.{max uA₁ uA₂, max uB₁ uB₂}

modules.title: Free Monad of a Polynomial Functor
modules.doc:
We define the free monad on a **polynomial functor** (`PFunctor`), and prove some basic properties.

The free monad `PFunctor.FreeM P` extends the W-type construction with an extra `pure`
constructor, yielding a monad that is free over the polynomial functor `P`.

## Comparison with `Cslib.FreeM`

`Cslib.FreeM F` (in `Cslib/Foundations/Control/Monad/Free.lean`) builds a free monad over an
arbitrary type constructor `F : Type u → Type v`, which need not be functorial.
Its `liftBind` constructor abstracts over the intermediate type `ι`:
```
| liftBind {ι : Type u} (op : F ι) (cont : ι → FreeM F α) : FreeM F α
```

`PFunctor.FreeM P` instead takes a polynomial functor `P : PFunctor`, where the shapes
`P.A` and positions `P.B a` are given explicitly.
Its `liftBind` constructor uses the shape and continuation directly:
```
| liftBind (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) : P.FreeM α
```

When the effect signature is naturally polynomial (a fixed set of operations, each with a
known return type), `PFunctor.FreeM` avoids the universe bump that the abstract `ι` in
`Cslib.FreeM` introduces.
Concretely, `PFunctor.FreeM P` is a genuine endofunctor on a single universe: for a ground
`P`, `P.FreeM α : Type` whenever `α : Type`, whereas `Cslib.FreeM F α : Type 1` for
`F : Type → Type`, since `liftBind` stores the intermediate type `ι : Type`.

This matters when a program must itself be a first-class value of the same kind, i.e. for
higher-order effects whose operations consume or return computations of the same monad
(schedulers, exception handlers, staged interpreters, higher-order oracles).
Such an effect's response type can be another `P.FreeM` computation, staying in one universe:
```
def coin : PFunctor.{0,0} := ⟨Bool, fun b => if b then Bool else Nat⟩
-- a `coin`-program is itself `Type 0`, so it can be another effect's response type:
def scheduler : PFunctor.{0,0} := ⟨Unit, fun _ => coin.FreeM Bool⟩  -- `Type 0`
```
With the abstract `ι`, the analogous program lives in `Type 1`, so an effect `Type → Type`
cannot return it; bumping the effect to `Type 1 → Type 1` pushes its programs to `Type 2`,
and so on without bound.

This construction is ported from the [VCV-io](https://github.com/dtumad/VCV-io) library.

## Main Definitions

- `PFunctor.FreeM`: The free monad on a polynomial functor.
- `PFunctor.FreeM.lift`: Lift a shape of the base polynomial functor into the free monad.
- `PFunctor.FreeM.liftObj`: Lift an object of the base polynomial functor into the free monad.
- `PFunctor.FreeM.liftM`: Interpret `FreeM P` into any other monad.

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM
items.doc:
The free monad on a polynomial functor.
This extends `WType` with an extra `pure` constructor.
items.statement:
inductive FreeM (P : PFunctor.{uA, uB}) : Type v → Type (max uA uB v)
  /-- A leaf node wrapping a pure value. -/
  | protected pure {α} (a : α) : P.FreeM α
  /-- Invoke the operation `a : P.A` with continuation `cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α`. -/
  | liftBind {α} (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) : P.FreeM α
deriving Inhabited

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.pure_eq_pure
items.statement: theorem pure_eq_pure : (FreeM.pure : α → P.FreeM α) = pure

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.lift
items.doc: Lift a shape of the base polynomial functor into the free monad.
items.statement: def lift (a : P.A) : P.FreeM (P.B a)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.lift_ne_pure
items.statement:
lemma lift_ne_pure (a : P.A) (y : P.B a) :
(lift a : P.FreeM (P.B a)) ≠ pure y

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.pure_ne_lift
items.statement:
lemma pure_ne_lift (a : P.A) (y : P.B a) :
pure y ≠ (lift a : P.FreeM (P.B a))

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.bind
items.doc:
Bind operation for the `FreeM` monad.

The builtin `>>=` notation should be preferred when `α` and `β` are in the same universe.
items.statement: protected def bind : P.FreeM α → (α → P.FreeM β) → P.FreeM β

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.bind_eq_bind
items.doc: Note that this lemma does not always apply, as it is universe-constrained by `Bind.bind`.
items.statement:
theorem bind_eq_bind {α β : Type v} :
    (FreeM.bind : P.FreeM α → _ → P.FreeM β) = Bind.bind

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.map
items.doc:
Map a function over a `FreeM` computation.

The builtin `<$>` notation should be preferred when `α` and `β` are in the same universe.
items.statement: def map (f : α → β) : P.FreeM α → P.FreeM β

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.map_eq_map
items.doc: Note that this lemma does not always apply, as it is universe-constrained by `Functor.map`.
items.statement:
theorem map_eq_map {α β : Type v} :
    FreeM.map (P := P) (α := α) (β := β) = Functor.map

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftBind_eq
items.statement:
lemma liftBind_eq (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) :
    FreeM.liftBind a cont = (FreeM.lift a).bind cont

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftObj
items.doc:
Lift an object of the base polynomial functor into the free monad.

This lifts the shape `x.1` with `lift` and relabels the responses with `x.2`. We use the
universe-polymorphic `FreeM.map` rather than `<$>`, since the response type `P.B x.1` and the
target `α` need not lie in the same universe.
items.statement: abbrev liftObj (x : P.Obj α) : P.FreeM α

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftObj_ne_pure
items.statement:
lemma liftObj_ne_pure (x : P.Obj α) (y : α) :
(liftObj x : P.FreeM α) ≠ pure y

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.pure_ne_liftObj
items.statement:
lemma pure_ne_liftObj (x : P.Obj α) (y : α) :
pure y ≠ (liftObj x : P.FreeM α)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.monadLift_eq_liftObj
items.statement: lemma monadLift_eq_liftObj (x : P.Obj α) : (x : P.FreeM α) = FreeM.liftObj x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.induction
items.doc:
An override for the default induction principle that is in simp-normal form.

Note that when `α` and `P.B a` are in the same universe, this simplifies slightly further.
items.statement:
protected theorem induction {motive : P.FreeM α → Prop}
    (pure : ∀ a, motive (pure a))
    (lift_bind : ∀ (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) (ih : ∀ i, motive (cont i)),
      motive ((FreeM.lift a).bind cont)) : ∀ x, motive x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.bind_assoc
items.statement:
protected theorem bind_assoc (x : P.FreeM α) (f : α → P.FreeM β) (g : β → P.FreeM γ) :
    (x.bind f).bind g = x.bind (fun a => (f a).bind g)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.pure_bind
items.doc: `.pure a` followed by `bind` collapses immediately.
items.statement:
lemma pure_bind (a : α) (f : α → P.FreeM β) :
    (pure a : P.FreeM α).bind f = f a

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.bind_pure
items.statement: lemma bind_pure : ∀ x : P.FreeM α, x.bind pure = x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.bind_pure_comp
items.statement: lemma bind_pure_comp (f : α → β) : ∀ x : P.FreeM α, x.bind (pure ∘ f) = map f x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.map_pure
items.statement: theorem map_pure (f : α → β) (x : α) : map f (pure x : P.FreeM α) = pure (f x)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.map_bind
items.statement:
theorem map_bind (f : β → γ) (x : P.FreeM α) (cont : α → P.FreeM β) :
    map f (x.bind cont) = x.bind fun a => (cont a).map f

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftBind_bind
items.statement:
lemma liftBind_bind (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM β) (f : β → P.FreeM γ) :
    ((FreeM.lift a).bind cont).bind f = (FreeM.lift a).bind (fun u ↦ (cont u).bind f)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftObj_bind
items.statement:
lemma liftObj_bind (x : P.Obj α) (f : α → P.FreeM β) :
    (FreeM.liftObj x).bind f = FreeM.liftBind x.1 (fun a ↦ f (x.2 a))

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.bind_eq_pure_iff
items.statement:
lemma bind_eq_pure_iff (x : P.FreeM α) (f : α → P.FreeM β) (b : β) :
x.bind f = pure b ↔ ∃ a, x = pure a ∧ f a = pure b

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.pure_eq_bind_iff
items.statement:
lemma pure_eq_bind_iff (x : P.FreeM α) (f : α → P.FreeM β) (b : β) :
pure b = x.bind f ↔ ∃ a, x = pure a ∧ pure b = f a

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.id_map
items.statement: theorem id_map : ∀ x : P.FreeM α, map id x = x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.comp_map
items.statement:
theorem comp_map (h : β → γ) (g : α → β) :
    ∀ x : P.FreeM α, map (h ∘ g) x = map h (map g x)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.pure_inj
items.statement: lemma pure_inj (a b : α) : (pure a : P.FreeM α) = pure b ↔ a = b

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftBind_inj
items.statement:
lemma liftBind_inj (a a' : P.A)
    (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) (cont' : P.B a' → P.FreeM α) :
    FreeM.liftBind a cont = FreeM.liftBind a' cont' ↔ ∃ h : a = a', h ▸ cont = cont'

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM
items.doc:
Interpret a `FreeM P` computation into any monad `m` by providing an interpretation
`interp : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)` for each operation.
items.statement: protected def liftM [Pure m] [Bind m] (interp : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)) : P.FreeM α → m α

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_pure
items.statement: lemma liftM_pure (a : α) : (Pure.pure a : P.FreeM α).liftM interp = Pure.pure a

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_lift_bind
items.statement:
lemma liftM_lift_bind (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) :
    FreeM.liftM interp (FreeM.lift a >>= cont) =
      (do let u ← interp a; (cont u).liftM interp)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.Interprets
items.doc:
A predicate stating that `eval : P.FreeM α → m α` is an interpreter for the polynomial
effect handler `handler : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)`.

This means that `eval` is a monad morphism from the free monad `P.FreeM` to the
monad `m`, and that it extends the interpretation of individual operations given by
`handler`.
items.statement:
structure Interprets (handler : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)) (eval : P.FreeM α → m α) : Prop where
  apply_pure (a : α) : eval (.pure a) = pure a
  apply_lift_bind (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) :
    eval ((FreeM.lift a).bind cont) = handler a >>= fun x => eval (cont x)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.Interprets.eq
PFunctor.FreeM.Interprets.liftM
items.statement:
theorem Interprets.liftM (handler : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)) :
    Interprets handler (·.liftM handler : P.FreeM α → _)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.Interprets.iff
items.doc:
The universal property of the free monad `P.FreeM`.

That is, `liftM handler` is the unique interpreter that extends the effect handler `handler` to
interpret `P.FreeM` computations in a monad `m`.
items.statement:
theorem Interprets.iff (handler : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)) (eval : P.FreeM α → m α) :
    Interprets handler eval ↔ eval = (·.liftM handler)

items.name: Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_pfunctorFreeMLiftM
items.doc: A morphism of monads moves inside `FreeM.liftM`.
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Cslib.IsMonadHom.map_pfunctorFreeMLiftM [Monad n]
    {f : ∀ {α}, m α → n α} (hf : Cslib.IsMonadHom m n f) (interp : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a))
    (x : P.FreeM α) :
    f (x.liftM interp) = x.liftM (fun op => f (interp op))

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_bind
items.statement:
lemma liftM_bind {α β : Type uB} (x : P.FreeM α) (f : α → P.FreeM β) :
    (x >>= f).liftM interp = (do let u ← x.liftM interp; (f u).liftM interp)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.isMonadHom_liftM
items.doc: `FreeM.liftM interp` is a morphism of monads.
items.statement: theorem isMonadHom_liftM : Cslib.IsMonadHom P.FreeM m (FreeM.liftM interp)

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_map
items.statement:
lemma liftM_map {α β : Type uB} (f : α → β) (interp : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)) (x : P.FreeM α) :
    (f <$> x).liftM interp = f <$> x.liftM interp

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_seq
PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_seqLeft
PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_seqRight
PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_lift
items.statement:
lemma liftM_lift (interp : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)) (a : P.A) :
    (FreeM.lift a).liftM interp = interp a

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_liftObj
items.statement:
lemma liftM_liftObj (interp : (a : P.A) → m (P.B a)) (x : P.Obj α) :
    (FreeM.liftObj x).liftM interp = x.2 <$> interp x.1

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_lift_eq_self
items.doc: Interpreting each operation by its lift into the free monad is the identity.
items.statement: theorem liftM_lift_eq_self {α : Type uB} (x : P.FreeM α) : FreeM.liftM FreeM.lift x = x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_comp
items.doc: Interpreting into a free monad and then into `m` composes the two handlers.
items.statement:
theorem liftM_comp {m : Type uB → Type v} [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    {Q : PFunctor.{u, uB}} {α : Type uB} (x : P.FreeM α)
    (first : (a : P.A) → Q.FreeM (P.B a)) (second : (a : Q.A) → m (Q.B a)) :
    (x.liftM first).liftM second = x.liftM fun a => (first a).liftM second

modules.title: Folding polynomial free monads
modules.doc:
`PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM` evaluates a free polynomial tree in an algebra given by handlers
for values and operations. It satisfies the same universal property and substitution laws
as `Cslib.FreeM.foldFreeM`.

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM
items.doc: Fold a free polynomial tree into an algebra of its signature.
items.statement: def foldFreeM (onValue : α → β) (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → β) → β) : P.FreeM α → β

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM_pure
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_pure (onValue : α → β) (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → β) → β) (a : α) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect (pure a) = onValue a

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM_lift_bind
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_lift_bind (onValue : α → β) (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → β) → β)
    (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect ((lift a).bind (α := no_index (P.B a)) cont) =
      onEffect a (fun b => foldFreeM onValue onEffect (cont b))

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM_lift_bind'
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_lift_bind' {α : Type uB} (onValue : α → β)
    (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → β) → β) (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect (Bind.bind (α := no_index (P.B a)) (lift a) cont) =
      onEffect a (fun b => foldFreeM onValue onEffect (cont b))

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM_lift
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_lift (a : P.A) (onValue : P.B a → β)
    (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → β) → β) :
    foldFreeM (α := no_index (P.B a)) onValue onEffect (lift a) = onEffect a onValue

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM_unique
items.doc: A function agreeing with the algebra on values and operations is the fold.
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_unique (onValue : α → β) (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → β) → β)
    (h : P.FreeM α → β) (h_pure : ∀ a, h (pure a) = onValue a)
    (h_lift_bind : ∀ (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α),
      h ((lift a).bind cont) = onEffect a (fun b => h (cont b))) :
    h = foldFreeM onValue onEffect

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM_bind
items.doc: Sequencing substitutes the fold of the continuation for the value handler.
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_bind (onValue : β → γ) (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → γ) → γ)
    (x : P.FreeM α) (k : α → P.FreeM β) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect (x.bind k) =
      foldFreeM (fun a => foldFreeM onValue onEffect (k a)) onEffect x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.foldFreeM_map
items.statement:
theorem foldFreeM_map (onValue : β → γ) (onEffect : (a : P.A) → (P.B a → γ) → γ)
    (f : α → β) (x : P.FreeM α) :
    foldFreeM onValue onEffect (map f x) = foldFreeM (onValue ∘ f) onEffect x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.liftM_eq_foldFreeM
items.doc: Monadic interpretation is the fold whose effect handler uses `bind`.

modules.title: Polynomial free monads with an empty result type
modules.doc:
When `α` is empty, a tree in `P.FreeM α` has only operation nodes. The equivalence
`PFunctor.FreeM.equivWOfIsEmpty` identifies these trees with the W-type `P.W`.

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty
items.doc: Regard a free polynomial tree with no return values as a W-type.
items.statement: def FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty [IsEmpty α] : P.FreeM α → P.W

items.name: PFunctor.W.toFreeM
items.doc: Regard a W-type as a free polynomial tree with no return nodes.
items.statement: def W.toFreeM : P.W → P.FreeM α

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty_lift_bind
items.statement:
theorem FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty_lift_bind [IsEmpty α] (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) :
    toWOfIsEmpty ((lift a).bind (α := no_index (P.B a)) cont) =
      W.mk (.mk a fun b => toWOfIsEmpty (cont b))

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty_lift_bind'
items.statement:
theorem FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty_lift_bind' {α : Type uB} [IsEmpty α] (a : P.A)
    (cont : P.B a → P.FreeM α) :
    toWOfIsEmpty (Bind.bind (α := no_index (P.B a)) (lift a) cont) =
      W.mk (.mk a fun b => toWOfIsEmpty (cont b))

items.name: PFunctor.W.toFreeM_mk
items.statement:
theorem W.toFreeM_mk (a : P.A) (cont : P.B a → P.W) :
    toFreeM (α := α) (W.mk (.mk a cont)) =
      (FreeM.lift a).bind (fun b => toFreeM (cont b))

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty_toFreeM
items.statement:
theorem FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty_toFreeM [IsEmpty α] (x : P.W) :
    toWOfIsEmpty (W.toFreeM (α := α) x) = x

items.name: PFunctor.W.toFreeM_toWOfIsEmpty
items.statement:
theorem W.toFreeM_toWOfIsEmpty [IsEmpty α] (x : P.FreeM α) :
    toFreeM (FreeM.toWOfIsEmpty x) = x

items.name: PFunctor.FreeM.equivWOfIsEmpty
items.doc: With an empty result type, the free polynomial monad is equivalent to its W-type.
items.statement: def FreeM.equivWOfIsEmpty [IsEmpty α] : P.FreeM α ≃ P.W

modules.title: Monotonicity of polynomial evaluation
modules.doc:
Over a canonically ordered semiring (such as `ℕ`), every coefficient of a polynomial is
nonnegative, so evaluation of the polynomial is a monotone function. This is useful for
reasoning about polynomial time bounds.

items.name: Polynomial.monotone_eval
items.doc: Over a canonically ordered semiring, evaluation of a polynomial is monotone.
items.statement: theorem monotone_eval : Monotone (fun x : R => p.eval x)

items.name: Polynomial.eval_mono
items.doc: Over a canonically ordered semiring, evaluation of a polynomial preserves `≤`.
items.statement: theorem eval_mono {a b : R} (hab : a ≤ b) : p.eval a ≤ p.eval b

items.name: Set.Saturates
items.doc:
`f : ι → Set α` saturates `s : Set α` iff `f i` is a subset of `s`
whenever `f i` and `s` has any intersection at all.
items.statement: def Saturates (f : ι → Set α) (s : Set α) : Prop

items.name: Set.saturates_compl
items.doc: If `f` saturates `s`, then `f` saturates its complement `sᶜ` as well.
items.statement: theorem saturates_compl (hs : Saturates f s) : Saturates f sᶜ

items.name: Set.saturates_eq_biUnion
items.doc: If `f` is a cover and saturates `s`, then `s` is the union of all `f i` that intersects `s`.
items.statement:
theorem saturates_eq_biUnion (hs : Saturates f s) (hc : ⋃ i, f i = univ) :
    s = ⋃ i ∈ {i | (f i ∩ s).Nonempty}, f i

modules.title: StackTape: Infinite, eventually-`none` lists of `Option`s
modules.doc:
This file defines `StackTape`, a stack-like data structure of `Option` values,
where the tape is considered to be infinite and eventually all `none`s.
This is useful as a data structure with a simple API for manipulation by Turing machines.

## Design

`StackTape` is represented as a list of `Option` values where the list cannot end with `none`.
The end of the list is then treated as the start of an infinite sequence of `none` values
by the low-level API.
This design makes it convenient to express the length of the tape in terms of the list length.

An alternative design would be to represent the tape as a `Stream' (Option Symbol)`,
with additional fields tracking the length and the fact that the stream eventually becomes `none`.
This design might complicate reasoning about the length of the tape, but could make other operations
more straightforward.

Future design work might explore this alternative representation and compare its
advantages and disadvantages.

…

items.name: Cslib.Turing.StackTape
items.doc:
An infinite tape representation using a list of `Option` values,
where the list is eventually `none`.

Represented as a `List (Option Symbol)` that does not end with `none`.
items.statement:
structure StackTape (Symbol : Type*) where
  /-- The underlying list representation -/
  toList : List (Option Symbol)
  /--
  The list can be empty (i.e. `none`),
  but if it is not empty, the last element is not (`some`) `none`
  -/

modules.title: Inference systems
modules.doc:
This module defines the basic classes and notation for *inference systems* -- systems for deriving
conclusions from premises.

We intend inference systems broadly, as in theory of programming languages. In applications to
logic, for example, we use inference systems to capture both the concepts of satisfiability and
proof systems.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem
items.doc:
The notation typeclass for inference systems.
This enables the notation `S⇓a`, where `S` is a tag for the inference system and `a : α`
is a derivable value.
items.statement:
class InferenceSystem (S : Type*) (α : Type*) where
  /--
  `S⇓a` is a derivation of `a`, that is, a witness that `a` is derivable in the system `S`.
  The meaning of this notation is type-dependent.
  -/
  derivation (a : α) : Sort v

modules.title: Measures supported on finite sets
modules.doc:
For a measure that vanishes off a finite set, every set is null-measurable if
singletons are measurable. Finite support is preserved by finite products of
finite measures. These facts let sample-complexity arguments in learning
theory measure failure events of *arbitrary* (non-measurable) learners under
finitely supported adversarial distributions.

`HasFiniteSupport` records this property as a typeclass, with an instance for
finite products.

The [PFR project](https://github.com/teorth/pfr/blob/master/PFR/ForMathlib/Entropy/Measure.lean)
has an equivalent `ProbabilityTheory.FiniteSupport` class, expressed using an almost-everywhere
`Finset` witness.

## Main statements

- `MeasureTheory.HasFiniteSupport`: a measure vanishes off some finite set.
- `MeasureTheory.HasFiniteSupport.exists_eq_sum_smul_dirac`: on a space with measurable
  singletons, a measure with finite support is a finite sum of Dirac measures weighted by
  its singleton masses.
- `MeasureTheory.HasFiniteSupport.isFiniteMeasure`: a sigma-finite measure with finite
  support is finite.
- `MeasureTheory.NullMeasurableSet.of_hasFiniteSupport`: on a space with measurable
  singletons, every set is null-measurable for a measure with finite support,
  including finite products.

items.name: MeasureTheory.HasFiniteSupport
items.doc: A measure vanishes off a finite set.
items.statement:
class HasFiniteSupport {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) : Prop where
  /-- Some finite set has null complement. -/
  exists_finite_measure_compl_zero : ∃ s : Set α, s.Finite ∧ μ sᶜ = 0

items.name: MeasureTheory.HasFiniteSupport.exists_eq_sum_smul_dirac
items.doc:
On a space with measurable singletons, a measure with finite support is a finite sum
of Dirac measures weighted by its singleton masses. This is `Measure.ae_mem_finset_iff`
applied to a finite support.
items.statement:
theorem HasFiniteSupport.exists_eq_sum_smul_dirac {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass α] (μ : Measure α) [HasFiniteSupport μ] :
    ∃ s : Finset α, μ = ∑ a ∈ s, μ {a} • Measure.dirac a

items.name: MeasureTheory.HasFiniteSupport.isFiniteMeasure
items.doc: A sigma-finite measure with finite support is finite.
items.statement:
instance (priority := 100) HasFiniteSupport.isFiniteMeasure {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    (μ : Measure α) [HasFiniteSupport μ] [SigmaFinite μ] : IsFiniteMeasure μ

items.name: MeasureTheory.NullMeasurableSet.of_hasFiniteSupport
items.doc:
On a space with measurable singletons, every set is null-measurable for a measure
with finite support.
items.statement:
theorem NullMeasurableSet.of_hasFiniteSupport {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass α] {μ : Measure α} [HasFiniteSupport μ]
    (t : Set α) : NullMeasurableSet t μ

modules.title: Huntington's axioms for Boolean Algebras
modules.doc:
In this file we derive an instance of Mathlib's `BooleanAlgebra` on an inhabited type, starting
from operations of binary supremum `· ⊔ ·` and complementation `·ᶜ`, obeying the three axioms
laid out in [Huntington1933a] and [Huntington1933b]:

* Supremum is associative: `a ⊔ b ⊔ c = a ⊔ (b ⊔ c)`,
* Supremum is commutative: `a ⊔ b = b ⊔ a`, and
* Huntington's axiom: `(aᶜ ⊔ b)ᶜ ⊔ (aᶜ ⊔ bᶜ)ᶜ = a`.

These axioms are packaged in the class `HuntingtonAlgebra`, which should only be used for its
instance `HuntingtonAlgebra.instBooleanAlgebra`.

## References

* [E. V. Huntington, "New Sets of Independent Postulates for the Algebra of Logic, With Special
  Reference to Whitehead and Russell's Principia Mathematica"][Huntington1933a]
* [E. V. Huntington, "Boolean Algebra. A Correction"][Huntington1933b]

items.name: HuntingtonAlgebra
items.doc: A class for types obeying Huntington's axioms for Boolean algebras.
items.statement:
public class HuntingtonAlgebra (α : Type*) extends Max α, Compl α, Inhabited α,
    Std.Associative (α := α) (· ⊔ ·), Std.Commutative (α := α) (· ⊔ ·) where
  /-- Huntington's axiom. -/
  huntington (a b : α) : (aᶜ ⊔ b)ᶜ ⊔ (aᶜ ⊔ bᶜ)ᶜ = a

modules.authors: Fabrizio Montesi, Thomas Waring, Chris Henson
modules.title: Relations: Confluence
modules.doc:
This module proves some properties regarding confluence that are used for both lambda calculi and
combinatory logic. Some notable theorems:

* `Diamond.to_confluent`: the diamond property implies confluence
* `LocallyConfluent.terminating_toConfluent`: Newman's lemma

We prove most results first for two relations, where `Confluent r` becomes `Commute r₁ r₂`, then
specialize to the classical case where `r₁ = r₂`.

## References

* [*Term Rewriting and All That*][Baader1998]

items.name: Relation.emptyHRelation
items.doc: The empty (heterogeneous) relation, which always returns `False`.
items.statement: def emptyHRelation {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (_ : α) (_ : β)

items.name: Relation.dom
items.doc: Domain of a relation.
items.statement: def dom (r : α → β → Prop) : Set α

items.name: Relation.cod
items.doc: Codomain of a relation, aka range.
items.statement: def cod (r : α → β → Prop) : Set β

items.name: Relation.Join₂
items.doc: Generalisation of `Join` to two relations.
items.statement: def Join₂ (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop) (a b : α) : Prop

items.name: Relation.MJoin
items.doc:
The join of the reflexive transitive closure. This is not named in Mathlib, but see
`#loogle Relation.Join (Relation.ReflTransGen ?r)`
items.statement: abbrev MJoin (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.UpTo
items.doc: The relation `r` 'up to' the relation `s`.
items.statement: def UpTo (r s : α → α → Prop) : α → α → Prop

items.name: Relation.Preserves
items.doc: Relation `r` preserves predicate `P`.
items.statement: def Preserves (r : α → α → Prop) (P : α → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Relation.Diamond
items.doc: A relation has the diamond property when all reductions with a common origin are joinable
items.statement: abbrev Diamond (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.DiamondCommute
items.doc: Generalization of `Diamond` to two relations.
items.statement: abbrev DiamondCommute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.Confluent
items.doc: A relation is confluent when its reflexive transitive closure has the diamond property.
items.statement: abbrev Confluent (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.Commute
items.doc: Generalization of `Confluent` to two relations.
items.statement: abbrev Commute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.SemiConfluent
items.doc:
A relation is semi-confluent when single and multiple steps with common origin
are multi-joinable.
items.statement: abbrev SemiConfluent (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.SemiCommute
items.doc: Generalisation of `SemiConfluent` to two relations.
items.statement: abbrev SemiCommute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.ChurchRosser
items.doc: A relation has the Church Rosser property when equivalence implies multi-joinability.
items.statement: abbrev ChurchRosser (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.LocallyConfluent
items.doc: A relation is locally confluent when all reductions with a common origin are multi-joinable
items.statement: abbrev LocallyConfluent (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.LocallyCommute
items.doc: Generalization of `LocallyConfluent` to two relations.
items.statement: def LocallyCommute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.StronglyConfluent
items.doc: A relation is strongly confluent when single steps are reflexive- and multi-joinable.
items.statement: abbrev StronglyConfluent (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.StronglyCommute
items.doc: Generalization of `StronglyConfluent` to two relations.
items.statement: def StronglyCommute (r₁ r₂ : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.Reducible
items.doc: An element is reducible with respect to a relation if there is a value it is related to.
items.statement: abbrev Reducible (r : α → α → Prop) (x : α) : Prop

items.name: Relation.Normal
items.doc: An element is normal if it is not reducible.
items.statement: abbrev Normal (r : α → α → Prop) (x : α) : Prop

items.name: Relation.Normalizable
items.doc: An element is normalizable if it is related to a normal element.
items.statement: abbrev Normalizable (r : α → α → Prop) (x : α) : Prop

items.name: Relation.Normalizing
items.doc: A relation is normalizing when every element is normalizable.
items.statement: abbrev Normalizing (r : α → α → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Relation.SN
items.doc:
An element `x` is `SN` (for strongly-normalising) for a relation `r` if it is accessible under
the inverse of `r`.
items.statement: abbrev SN (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.Terminating
items.doc:
A relation is terminating when the inverse of its transitive closure is well-founded.
Note that this is also called Noetherian or strongly normalizing in the literature.
items.statement: abbrev Terminating (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.Acyclic
items.doc:
A relation is acyclic if its transitive closure is irreflexive, equivalently if it admits no
nonempty cycle.
items.statement: abbrev Acyclic (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.Convergent
items.doc: A relation is convergent when it is both confluent and terminating.
items.statement: abbrev Convergent (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Relation.RightEuclidean
items.doc: A relation `r` is (right) Euclidean if `r a b` and `r a c` guarantee `r b c`.
items.statement:
class RightEuclidean (r : α → α → Prop) where
  rightEuclidean : r a b → r a c → r b c

items.name: Relation.LeftEuclidean
items.doc: A relation `r` is (left) Euclidean if `r a c` and `r b c` guarantee `r a b`.

modules.title: Relations Across Steps
modules.doc:
This file defines `Relation.RelatesInSteps` (and `Relation.RelatesWithinSteps`).
These are inductively defined propositions that communicate whether a relation forms a
chain of length `n` (or at most `n`) between two elements.

The lemma `RelatesInSteps.exists_isChainFromTo` allows to obtain a chain
(`List.IsChainFromTo`) of related elements that witness the reachability, and
`List.IsChainFromTo.relatesInSteps` is the converse direction.
`Relation.relatesInSteps_iff_exists_isChainFromTo` combines both.

Another result is `Relation.ReflTransGen.relatesInSteps_lt_encard`, which states that any element
reachable from `a` is reachable in fewer steps than there are elements reachable from `a`.

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps
items.statement:
inductive RelatesInSteps (r : α → α → Prop) : α → α → ℕ → Prop
  | refl (a : α) : RelatesInSteps r a a 0
  | tail (t t' t'' : α) (n : ℕ) (h₁ : RelatesInSteps r t t' n) (h₂ : r t' t'') :
      RelatesInSteps r t t'' (n + 1)

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.reflTransGen
items.statement: theorem RelatesInSteps.reflTransGen (h : RelatesInSteps r a b n) : ReflTransGen r a b

items.name: Relation.ReflTransGen.relatesInSteps
items.doc:
If `b` is reachable from `a` via `r`, then they relate to each other for some number
of steps.
items.statement: theorem ReflTransGen.relatesInSteps (h : ReflTransGen r a b) : ∃ n, RelatesInSteps r a b n

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.single
items.statement: lemma RelatesInSteps.single {a b : α} (h : r a b) : RelatesInSteps r a b 1

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.head
items.statement:
theorem RelatesInSteps.head (t t' t'' : α) (n : ℕ) (h₁ : r t t')
    (h₂ : RelatesInSteps r t' t'' n) : RelatesInSteps r t t'' (n+1)

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.head_induction_on
items.statement:
theorem RelatesInSteps.head_induction_on {motive : ∀ (a : α) (n : ℕ), RelatesInSteps r a b n → Prop}
    {a : α} {n : ℕ} (h : RelatesInSteps r a b n) (hrefl : motive b 0 (.refl b))
    (hhead : ∀ {a c n} (h' : r a c) (h : RelatesInSteps r c b n),
      motive c n h → motive a (n + 1) (h.head a c b n h')) :
    motive a n h

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.zero
items.statement: lemma RelatesInSteps.zero {a b : α} (h : RelatesInSteps r a b 0) : a = b

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.zero_iff
items.statement: lemma RelatesInSteps.zero_iff {a b : α} : RelatesInSteps r a b 0 ↔ a = b

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.trans
Relation.RelatesInSteps.succ
items.statement:
lemma RelatesInSteps.succ {n : ℕ} (h : RelatesInSteps r a b (n + 1)) :
    ∃ t', RelatesInSteps r a t' n ∧ r t' b

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.succ_iff
items.statement:
lemma RelatesInSteps.succ_iff {a b : α} {n : ℕ} :
    RelatesInSteps r a b (n + 1) ↔ ∃ t', RelatesInSteps r a t' n ∧ r t' b

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.succ'
items.statement:
lemma RelatesInSteps.succ' {a b : α} {n : ℕ} (h : RelatesInSteps r a b (n + 1)) :
    ∃ t', r a t' ∧ RelatesInSteps r t' b n

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.succ'_iff
items.statement:
lemma RelatesInSteps.succ'_iff {a b : α} {n : ℕ} :
    RelatesInSteps r a b (n + 1) ↔ ∃ t', r a t' ∧ RelatesInSteps r t' b n

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.apply_le_apply_add
items.doc:
If `h : α → ℕ` increases by at most 1 on each step of `r`,
then the value of `h` at the output is at most `h` at the input plus the number of steps.
items.statement:
lemma RelatesInSteps.apply_le_apply_add {a b : α} {m : ℕ} (hevals : RelatesInSteps r a b m)
    (h : α → ℕ) (h_step : ∀ a b, r a b → h b ≤ h a + 1) :
    h b ≤ h a + m

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.map
items.doc:
If `g` is a homomorphism from `r` to `r'` (i.e., it preserves the reduction relation),
then `RelatesInSteps` is preserved under `g`.

items.name: Relation.RelatesInSteps.exists_isChainFromTo
items.doc:
If `b` is related to `a` via `r` in `n` steps, then there is an `r`-chain of `n + 1` elements
starting at `a` and ending at `b`.
This is similar to `List.exists_isChain_ne_nil_of_relationReflTransGen`, but also provides
a length guarantee.
items.statement:
lemma RelatesInSteps.exists_isChainFromTo {a b : α} {n : ℕ} (h : RelatesInSteps r a b n) :
    ∃ chain : List α, chain.IsChainFromTo r a b ∧ chain.length = n + 1

items.name: List.IsChain.relatesInSteps_getElem
items.doc:
Any two elements along an `r`-chain are related in as many steps as their distance in the
chain.
items.statement:
lemma _root_.List.IsChain.relatesInSteps_getElem {chain : List α} (hc : chain.IsChain r)
    (i k : ℕ) (hik : i + k < chain.length) :
    RelatesInSteps r chain[i] chain[i + k] k

items.name: List.IsChainFromTo.relatesInSteps
items.doc:
If there is an `r`-chain of `n + 1` elements from `a` to `b`, then `a` and `b` are related
to each other in `n` steps.

items.name: Relation.relatesInSteps_iff_exists_isChainFromTo
items.doc:
`a` and `b` are related in `n` steps exactly when there is an `r`-chain of `n + 1` elements
from `a` to `b`.
items.statement:
lemma relatesInSteps_iff_exists_isChainFromTo :
    RelatesInSteps r a b n ↔ ∃ chain : List α, chain.IsChainFromTo r a b ∧ chain.length = n + 1

items.note: ## RelatesWithinSteps - only requires an upper bound on the number of steps

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps
items.doc:
`RelatesWithinSteps` is a variant of `RelatesInSteps` that allows for a loose bound.
It states that `a` relates to `b` in *at most* `n` steps.
items.statement: def RelatesWithinSteps (r : α → α → Prop) (a b : α) (n : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.of_relatesInSteps
items.doc: `RelatesInSteps` implies `RelatesWithinSteps` with the same bound.
items.statement:
lemma RelatesWithinSteps.of_relatesInSteps {a b : α} {n : ℕ} (h : RelatesInSteps r a b n) :
    RelatesWithinSteps r a b n

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.refl
items.statement: lemma RelatesWithinSteps.refl (a : α) : RelatesWithinSteps r a a 0

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.single
items.statement: lemma RelatesWithinSteps.single {a b : α} (h : r a b) : RelatesWithinSteps r a b 1

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.zero
items.statement: lemma RelatesWithinSteps.zero {a b : α} (h : RelatesWithinSteps r a b 0) : a = b

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.zero_iff
items.statement: lemma RelatesWithinSteps.zero_iff {a b : α} : RelatesWithinSteps r a b 0 ↔ a = b

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.trans
items.doc: Transitivity of `RelatesWithinSteps` in the sum of the step bounds.

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.mono
items.doc:
If two elements `a` and `b` are related in at most `n₁` steps in the relation `r` and
`n₁ ≤ n₂`, then they are also related in at most `n₂` steps.
items.statement: lemma RelatesWithinSteps.mono {a b : α} : Monotone (RelatesWithinSteps r a b ·)

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.apply_le_apply_add
items.doc:
If `h : α → ℕ` increases by at most 1 on each step of `r`,
then the value of `h` at the output is at most `h` at the input plus the step bound.
items.statement:
lemma RelatesWithinSteps.apply_le_apply_add {a b : α} {m : ℕ}
    (hevals : RelatesWithinSteps r a b m)
    (h : α → ℕ)
    (h_step : ∀ a b, r a b → h b ≤ h a + 1) :
    h b ≤ h a + m

items.name: Relation.RelatesWithinSteps.map
items.doc:
If `g` is a homomorphism from `r` to `r'` (i.e., it preserves the reduction relation),
then `RelatesWithinSteps` is preserved under `g`.
items.statement:
lemma RelatesWithinSteps.map {α α' : Type*} {r : α → α → Prop} {r' : α' → α' → Prop}
    (g : α → α') (hg : ∀ a b, r a b → r' (g a) (g b))
    {a b : α} {n : ℕ} (h : RelatesWithinSteps r a b n) :
    RelatesWithinSteps r' (g a) (g b) n

items.note: ## Reachability under a bound on the number of reachable elements

items.name: Relation.ReflTransGen.relatesInSteps_lt_encard
items.doc:
A more precise version of `ReflTransGen.relatesInSteps`: if `b` is reachable from `a`, then it
is related to `a` in fewer steps than there are elements reachable from `a`.
Note that this cardinality is an `ℕ∞`, and if it is infinite, no bound on the number of steps
is stated.
items.statement:
theorem ReflTransGen.relatesInSteps_lt_encard {b : α} (h : ReflTransGen r a b) :
    ∃ n, RelatesInSteps r a b n ∧ (n : ℕ∞) < {x | ReflTransGen r a x}.encard

modules.title: Relation algebras
modules.doc:
A relation algebra in the sense of Tarski (not to be confused with a relational algebra) is an
extension of Boolean algebras that are designed to form an algebraic analysis of relations,
`α → α → Prop` in Lean. They have applications in computer science such as the theory of constraint
satisfaction as well as mathematical connections such as combinatorics.

## References

* [R. Maddux, *Relation Algebras*][Maddux2006]

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra
items.doc:
The class of relation algebras. Note the notational differences from the literature. In addition
to inheriting Mathlib's notations for Boolean algebras, `star` is used for converse, and the monoid
reduct for composition uses multiplicative notation.
items.statement:
class RelationAlgebra (α : Type*) extends BooleanAlgebra α, Monoid α, StarMul α where
  sup_mul (a b c : α) : (a ⊔ b) * c = a * c ⊔ b * c
  star_sup (a b : α) : star (a ⊔ b) = star a ⊔ star b
  tarski (a b : α) : star a * (a * b)ᶜ ≤ bᶜ

items.name: Cslib.CompleteRelationAlgebra
items.doc: The relation algebra of a complete Boolean algebra.
items.statement: class CompleteRelationAlgebra (α : Type*) extends RelationAlgebra α, CompleteBooleanAlgebra α

items.name: Cslib.CompleteAtomicRelationAlgebra
items.doc: The relation algebra of a complete and atomic Boolean algebra.
items.statement:
class CompleteAtomicRelationAlgebra (α : Type*) extends CompleteRelationAlgebra α,
    CompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra α

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.ofTarski
items.doc: A `RelationAlgebra` can be constructed using Tarski's original ten axioms.
items.statement:
def ofTarski {α : Type*} [Max α] [Compl α] [Mul α] [One α] [Star α]
    (sup_comm : ∀ a b : α, a ⊔ b = b ⊔ a)
    (sup_assoc : ∀ a b c : α, (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c = a ⊔ (b ⊔ c))
    (huntington : ∀ a b : α, (aᶜ ⊔ b)ᶜ ⊔ (aᶜ ⊔ bᶜ)ᶜ = a)
    (mul_assoc : ∀ a b c : α, (a * b) * c = a * (b * c))
    (mul_one : ∀ a : α, a * 1 = a)
    (star_involutive : ∀ a : α, star (star a) = a)
    (star_mul : ∀ a b : α, star (a * b) = star b * star a)
    (sup_mul : ∀ a b c : α, (a ⊔ b) * c = a * c ⊔ b * c)
    (star_sup : ∀ a b : α, star (a ⊔ b) = star a ⊔ star b)
    (tarski : ∀ a b : α, star a * (a * b)ᶜ ⊔ bᶜ = bᶜ) : RelationAlgebra α

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.star_mono
items.statement: theorem star_mono : Monotone (star : α → α)

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.starOrderIso
items.doc: Converse as an automorphism of a relation algebra.
items.statement: def starOrderIso : α ≃o α

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.star_bot
items.statement: theorem star_bot : star (⊥ : α) = ⊥

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.star_le_star_iff
items.statement: theorem star_le_star_iff {a b : α} : star a ≤ star b ↔ a ≤ b

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.star_lt_star_iff
items.statement: theorem star_lt_star_iff {a b : α} : star a < star b ↔ a < b

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.star_inf
items.statement: theorem star_inf (a b : α) : star (a ⊓ b) = star a ⊓ star b

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.star_compl
items.statement: theorem star_compl (a : α) : star aᶜ = (star a)ᶜ

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.star_sdiff
items.statement: theorem star_sdiff (a b : α) : star (a \ b) = star a \ star b

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.mul_sup
items.statement: theorem mul_sup (a b c : α) : a * (b ⊔ c) = a * b ⊔ a * c

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.mul_bot
items.statement: theorem mul_bot (a : α) : a * ⊥ = ⊥

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.isAtom_star_iff
items.statement: theorem isAtom_star_iff {a : α} : IsAtom (star a) ↔ IsAtom a

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.atom_cycle_left
items.statement:
theorem atom_cycle_left {r s p : α} (hs : IsAtom s) (hp : p ≠ ⊥) (h : p ≤ r * s) :
    s ≤ star r * p

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.left_modular
items.statement: theorem left_modular (a b c : α) : a * b ⊓ c ≤ a * (b ⊓ star a * c)

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.exists_atom_le_mul_right
items.doc: If an atom lies below a product, its right factor can be replaced by an atom below it.
items.statement:
theorem exists_atom_le_mul_right [IsAtomic α] {a b p : α} (hp : IsAtom p) (h : p ≤ a * b) :
    ∃ s, IsAtom s ∧ s ≤ b ∧ p ≤ a * s

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.exists_atom_le_mul_left
items.doc: If an atom lies below a product, its left factor can be replaced by an atom below it.
items.statement:
theorem exists_atom_le_mul_left [IsAtomic α] {a b p : α} (hp : IsAtom p) (h : p ≤ a * b) :
    ∃ r, IsAtom r ∧ r ≤ a ∧ p ≤ r * b

items.doc: A relation algebra is *integral* when its identity is an atom.
items.statement: def IsIntegral (α : Type*) [RelationAlgebra α] : Prop

items.statement: def identityAtoms (α : Type*) [RelationAlgebra α] : Set α

items.statement: def symmetricDiversityAtoms (α : Type*) [RelationAlgebra α] : Set α

items.statement: def nonsymmetricDiversityAtoms (α : Type*) [RelationAlgebra α] : Set α

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebraHom

The type of relation algebra homomorphisms from `α` to `β`, preserving both the Boolean algebra

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebraHom.ext
items.statement: theorem ext {f g : RelationAlgebraHom α β} (h : ∀ a, f a = g a) : f = g

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebraHom.id

items.statement: protected def id (α : Type*) [RelationAlgebra α] : RelationAlgebraHom α α

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebraHom.comp
items.doc: Composition of `RelationAlgebraHom`
items.statement: def comp (f : RelationAlgebraHom β γ) (g : RelationAlgebraHom α β) : RelationAlgebraHom α γ

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebraHom.id_apply

items.statement: theorem ext {f g : RelationAlgebraEquiv α β} (h : ∀ a, f a = g a) : f = g

items.statement: protected def refl (α : Type*) [RelationAlgebra α] : RelationAlgebraEquiv α α

items.doc: The symmetric `RelationAlgebraEquiv`
items.statement: def symm (f : RelationAlgebraEquiv α β) : RelationAlgebraEquiv β α

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebraEquiv.trans
items.doc: The transitive `RelationAlgebraEquiv`
items.statement:

modules.title: Representable relation algebras
modules.doc:
One of the primary notions of interest in the study of relation algebras is the notion of
*representation* by a relation algebra of concrete relations.

Recall Stone's representation for Boolean algebras which (at a low level of
generality) states that every Boolean algebra has an isomorphism into a particuliar "field of sets".
Tarski's hope was that an analogous property would hold for abstract relation algebras, with the
isomorphism desired being into a relation algebra of concrete relations. This turns out to be false,
with the clasification and conditions for the representation of a relation algebra thus being a
matter of much interest.

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.SquareRelations
items.doc:
Relations over a type `α`. This definition exists because we need to prevent some instances from
from Mathlib being included.
items.statement: def SquareRelations (α : Type u) : Type u

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.Representation
items.doc: A representation of a relation algebra is an injective morphism into a product of relations.
items.statement:
structure Representation (α : Type u) [RelationAlgebra α] (ι : Type v) (β : ι → Type w) where
  /-- A `RelationAlgebraHom` into a product of relations. -/
  hom : RelationAlgebraHom α (∀ i, SquareRelations (β i))
  injective : Function.Injective hom

items.name: Cslib.RelationAlgebra.Representable
items.doc: A relation algebra is representable if a `Representation` exists.
items.statement: def Representable (α : Type u) [RelationAlgebra α] : Prop

modules.title: Functional Labelled Transition System (FLTS)
modules.doc:
A Functional Labelled Transition System is a special case of an `LTS` where transitions are
determined by a function.

This is a generalisation of deterministic finite-state machines.

## References

* [J. E. Hopcroft, R. Motwani, J. D. Ullman,
  *Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation*][Hopcroft2006]

items.name: Cslib.FLTS
items.doc:
A Functional Labelled Transition System (`FLTS`) for a type of states (`State`) and a type of
transition labels (`Label`) consists of a labelled transition function (`tr`).
items.statement:
structure FLTS (State Label : Type*) where
  /-- The transition function. -/
  tr : State → Label → State

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.mtr
items.doc:
Extended transition function.

Implementation note: compared to [Hopcroft2006], the definition consumes the input list of symbols
from the left (instead of the right), in order to match the way lists are constructed.
items.statement: def mtr (flts : FLTS State Label) (s : State) (μs : List Label)

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.mtr_nil_eq
items.statement: theorem mtr_nil_eq {flts : FLTS State Label} {s : State} : flts.mtr s [] = s

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.mtr_concat_eq
items.statement:
theorem mtr_concat_eq {flts : FLTS State Label} {s : State} {μs : List Label} {μ : Label} :
    flts.mtr s (μs ++ [μ]) = flts.tr (flts.mtr s μs) μ

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.mtr_append_eq
items.statement:
theorem mtr_append_eq {flts : FLTS State Label} {s : State} {μs1 μs2 : List Label} :
    flts.mtr s (μs1 ++ μs2) = flts.mtr (flts.mtr s μs1) μs2

modules.doc: Converting from `FLTS` to `LTS`

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.toLTS
items.doc: `FLTS` is a special case of `LTS`.
items.statement: def toLTS (flts : FLTS State Label) : LTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.toLTS_tr
items.doc: `FLTS.toLTS` correctly characterises transitions.
items.statement:
theorem toLTS_tr {flts : FLTS State Label} {s1 : State} {μ : Label} {s2 : State} :
  flts.toLTS.Tr s1 μ s2 ↔ flts.tr s1 μ = s2

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.toLTS_deterministic
items.doc: The transition system of a FLTS is deterministic.
items.statement: instance toLTS_deterministic (flts : FLTS State Label) : flts.toLTS.Deterministic

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.toLTS_imageFinite
items.doc: The transition system of a FLTS is image-finite.
items.statement: instance toLTS_imageFinite (flts : FLTS State Label) : flts.toLTS.ImageFinite

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.toLTS_mtr
items.doc: Characterisation of multistep transitions.
items.statement:
theorem toLTS_mtr {flts : FLTS State Label} {s1 : State} {μs : List Label} {s2 : State} :
    flts.toLTS.MTr s1 μs s2 ↔ flts.mtr s1 μs = s2

modules.doc: Converting from `LTS` to `FLTS`

items.name: Cslib.LTS.toFLTS
items.doc: Converts an `LTS` into an `FLTS` using the subset construction.
items.statement: def toFLTS (lts : LTS State Label) : FLTS (Set State) Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.toFLTS_mem_tr
items.doc: Characterisation of transitions in `LTS.toFLTS` wrt transitions in the original `LTS`.
items.statement:
theorem toFLTS_mem_tr {lts : LTS State Label} {S : Set State} {s' : State} {μ : Label} :
  s' ∈ lts.toFLTS.tr S μ ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, lts.Tr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.toFLTS_mem_mtr
items.doc:
Characterisation of multistep transitions in `LTS.toFLTS` wrt multistep transitions in the
original `LTS`.
items.statement:
theorem toFLTS_mem_mtr {lts : LTS State Label} {S : Set State} {s' : State} {μs : List Label} :
    s' ∈ lts.toFLTS.mtr S μs ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, lts.MTr s μs s'

items.doc: Characterisation of multistep transitions in `LTS.toFLTS` as image transitions in `LTS`.
items.statement:
theorem toFLTS_mtr_setImageMultistep {lts : LTS State Label} :
  lts.toFLTS.mtr = lts.setImageMultistep

modules.title: Product of functional labelled transition systems

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.prod
items.doc: The product of two FLTS with the same label type.
items.statement:
def prod (flts1 : FLTS State1 Label) (flts2 : FLTS State2 Label) :
    FLTS (State1 × State2) Label

items.name: Cslib.FLTS.prod_mtr_eq
items.doc:
A state is reachable by the product FLTS iff its components are reachable by
the respective FLTS components.
items.statement:
theorem prod_mtr_eq (flts1 : FLTS State1 Label) (flts2 : FLTS State2 Label)
    (s : State1 × State2) (μs : List Label) :
    (flts1.prod flts2).mtr s μs = (flts1.mtr s.fst μs, flts2.mtr s.snd μs)

items.statement: def IsSyncTrace (flts : FLTS State Label) (μs : List Label) : Prop

modules.title: Modal Frames
modules.doc:
A frame is a structure of relations, each with its own arity.

## Implementation notes

Frames for general modal logic were formulated with modal similarity types [Blackburn2001], which
we generalise here to arbitrary polynomial functors.

## References

* [P. Blackburn, M. de Rijke, Y. Venema, *Modal Logic*][Blackburn2001]

items.name: Cslib.Frame
items.doc:
A frame is an indexed structure of general relations that can differ in argument positions.

Frames are typically used in combination with modal logics or akin concepts. This is why we use
`op` (for operator) to range over relation indexes.

The definition generalises Definition 1.23 in [Blackburn2001] to general operator signatures given
as `PFunctor`s and possibly-empty world types.
items.statement:
structure Frame (World : Type u) (τ : PFunctor) where
  /-- Accessibility relations. -/
  r : (op : τ.A) → World → (τ.B op → World) → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Frame.project
items.doc: The binary relation obtained by observing position `i` of the worlds accessible via `op`.
items.statement: def project (f : Frame World τ) (op : τ.A) (i : τ.B op) : World → World → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Frame.diagonal
items.doc:
The binary relation induced by restricting the accessibility relation of `op`
to constant tuples of worlds.
items.statement: def diagonal (f : Frame World τ) (op : τ.A) : World → World → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Frame.r_const_of_diagonal
items.statement:
theorem r_const_of_diagonal {f : Frame World τ} (h : f.diagonal op w w') :
    f.r op w (fun _ => w')

items.name: Cslib.Frame.diagonal_of_r
items.statement:
theorem diagonal_of_r [PFunctor.Unary τ] {f : Frame World τ} (h : f.r op w ws) :
    f.diagonal op w (ws default)

items.name: Cslib.Frame.DiagonalInverse
items.doc: Two operators in a frame have inverse diagonal relations.
items.statement:
class DiagonalInverse (f : Frame World τ) (op₁ op₂ : τ.A) where
  diagonalInverse : ∀ w w', f.diagonal op₁ w w' ↔ f.diagonal op₂ w' w

items.name: Cslib.Frame.DiagonalSymm
items.doc:
A frame is diagonally symmetric at `op` if, whenever `w` accesses `ws`, some component of `ws`
accesses the constant sequence at `w`.
items.statement:
class DiagonalSymm (f : Frame World τ) (op : τ.A) where
  symm w ws : f.r op w ws → ∃ i, f.r op (ws i) (fun _ => w)

items.name: Cslib.Frame.Trans
items.doc:
A frame is transitive at `op` if accessibility can be composed through any accessible component:
whenever `w` accesses `ws₁` and `ws₁ i` accesses `ws₂`, then `w` accesses `ws₂`.
items.statement:
class Trans (f : Frame World τ) (op : τ.A) where
  trans w ws₁ i ws₂ : f.r op w ws₁ → f.r op (ws₁ i) ws₂ → f.r op w ws₂

items.name: Cslib.Frame.RightEuclidean
items.doc:
A frame is right Euclidean at `op` if, whenever a world `w` accesses two tuples `ws₁` and
`ws₂`, some component of `ws₂` accesses `ws₁`.
items.statement:
class RightEuclidean (f : Frame World τ) (op : τ.A) where
  rightEuclidean w ws₁ ws₂ : f.r op w ws₁ → f.r op w ws₂ → ∃ i, f.r op (ws₂ i) ws₁

items.name: Cslib.Frame.PreservesMap
items.doc:
A predicate map `Ps` is preserved from `P` by `op` if, whenever `P` holds at a world `w`,
then for every tuple `ws` accessible from `w` via `op`, each component `ws i` satisfies the
corresponding predicate `Ps i`.
items.statement: def PreservesMap (f : Frame α τ) (op : τ.A) (P : α → Prop) (Ps : τ.B op → α → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelations
items.doc: Builds a unary frame from an indexed family of binary relations.
items.statement:
def ofRelations {τ : PFunctor} [τ.Unary] (r : τ.A → World → World → Prop) :
    Frame World τ

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelations_iff
items.statement:
lemma ofRelations_iff {τ : PFunctor} [τ.Unary] (r : τ.A → World → World → Prop) (i : τ.A)
    (w : World) (ws : τ.B i → World) : (ofRelations r).r i w ws ↔ r i w (ws default)

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelations_diagonal_iff
items.statement:
lemma ofRelations_diagonal_iff {τ : PFunctor} [τ.Unary]
    (r : τ.A → World → World → Prop) (i : τ.A) (w w' : World) :
    (ofRelations r).diagonal i w w' ↔ r i w w'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.toFrame
items.doc: Transforms `lts` into a corresponding unary `Frame`.
items.statement: def toFrame : Frame State (mkUnary Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.toFrame_r_iff_tr
items.statement: lemma toFrame_r_iff_tr : lts.toFrame.r μ s f ↔ lts.Tr s μ (f default)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.toFrame_diagonal_iff_tr
items.statement: lemma toFrame_diagonal_iff_tr : lts.toFrame.diagonal μ s s' ↔ lts.Tr s μ s'

modules.title: Labelled Transition System (LTS)
modules.doc:
A Labelled Transition System (`LTS`) models the observable behaviour of the possible states of a
system. They are particularly popular in the fields of concurrency theory, logic, and programming
languages.

## Main definitions

- `LTS` is a structure for labelled transition systems, consisting of a labelled transition
relation `Tr` between states. We follow the style and conventions in [Sangiorgi2011].

- `LTS.MTr` extends the transition relation of any LTS to a multistep transition relation,
formalising the inference system and admissible rules for such relations in [Montesi2023].

- `LTS.BoundedUpTo` records an explicit global execution-length bound. `LTS.Bounded`,
`LTS.Terminating`, and `LTS.Acyclic` distinguish globally bounded execution length, absence of
infinite executions, and absence of nonempty cycles.

- Definitions for all the common classes of LTSs: image-finite, finitely branching, finite-state,
and deterministic.

## Main statements

- A series of results on `LTS.MTr` that allow for obtaining and composing multistep transitions in
different ways.

- `LTS.deterministic_imageFinite`: every deterministic LTS is also image-finite.

- `LTS.finiteState_imageFinite`: every finite-state LTS is also image-finite.

- `LTS.finiteState_finitelyBranching`: every finite-state LTS is also finitely-branching, if the
type of labels is finite.

## References

* [F. Montesi, *Introduction to Choreographies*][Montesi2023]
* [D. Sangiorgi, *Introduction to Bisimulation and Coinduction*][Sangiorgi2011]

items.name: Cslib.LTS
items.doc:
A Labelled Transition System (LTS) for a type of states (`State`) and a type of transition
labels (`Label`) consists of a labelled transition relation (`Tr`).
items.statement:
structure LTS (State : Type u) (Label : Type v) where
  /-- The transition relation. -/
  Tr : State → Label → State → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.UnlabelledTr
items.doc: The unlabelled transition relation underlying an LTS.
items.statement: def UnlabelledTr (lts : LTS State Label) : State → State → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsTerminal
items.doc: A state is terminal if it has no outgoing transitions.
items.statement: def IsTerminal (lts : LTS State Label) (s : State) : Prop

items.note:
## Multistep transitions and executions with finite traces

This section treats executions with a finite number of steps.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr
items.doc:
Definition of a multistep transition.

(Implementation note: compared to [Montesi2023], we choose stepL instead of stepR as fundamental
rule. This makes working with lists of labels more convenient, because we follow the same
construction. It is also similar to what is done in the `SimpleGraph` library in mathlib.)
items.statement:
inductive MTr (lts : LTS State Label) : State → List Label → State → Prop where
  | refl {s : State} : lts.MTr s [] s
  | stepL {s1 : State} {μ : Label} {s2 : State} {μs : List Label} {s3 : State} :
    lts.Tr s1 μ s2 → lts.MTr s2 μs s3 →
    lts.MTr s1 (μ :: μs) s3

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.nil_eq
items.doc: In any zero-steps multistep transition, the origin and the derivative are the same.
items.statement: theorem MTr.nil_eq (h : lts.MTr s1 [] s2) : s1 = s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.nil_iff
items.statement: theorem MTr.nil_iff (s1 s2 : State) : lts.MTr s1 [] s2 ↔ s1 = s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.single
items.doc: Any transition is also a multistep transition.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.single {s1 : State} {μ : Label} {s2 : State} :
  lts.Tr s1 μ s2 → lts.MTr s1 [μ] s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.cons_iff
items.doc:
A multistep transition along `μ :: μs` is a transition labelled by `μ` plus a multistep
transition labelled by `μs`.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.cons_iff {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.MTr s1 (μ :: μs) s2 ↔ ∃ s, lts.Tr s1 μ s ∧ lts.MTr s μs s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.stepR
items.doc: Any multistep transition can be extended by adding a transition.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.stepR {s1 : State} {μs : List Label} {s2 : State} {μ : Label} {s3 : State} :
  lts.MTr s1 μs s2 → lts.Tr s2 μ s3 → lts.MTr s1 (μs ++ [μ]) s3

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.comp
items.doc: Multistep transitions can be composed.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.comp {s1 : State} {μs1 : List Label} {s2 : State} {μs2 : List Label} {s3 : State} :
  lts.MTr s1 μs1 s2 → lts.MTr s2 μs2 s3 →
  lts.MTr s1 (μs1 ++ μs2) s3

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.single_invert
items.doc: Any 1-sized multistep transition implies a transition with the same states and label.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.single_invert (s1 : State) (μ : Label) (s2 : State) :
  lts.MTr s1 [μ] s2 → lts.Tr s1 μ s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.singleton_iff
items.doc: A 1-sized multistep transition is exactly a single transition with the given label.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.singleton_iff (s1 : State) (μ : Label) (s2 : State) :
lts.MTr s1 [μ] s2 ↔ lts.Tr s1 μ s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.split
items.doc: A multistep transition over a concatenation can be split into two multistep transitions.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.split {lts : LTS State Label} (h : lts.MTr s1 (μs ++ μs') s2) :
    ∃ s, lts.MTr s1 μs s ∧ lts.MTr s μs' s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.append_iff
items.doc:
Multistep-transitions over `μs ++ μs'` are exactly multistep transitions over `μs` and `μs'`
with a common end & start state (respectively).
items.statement: theorem MTr.append_iff : lts.MTr s1 (μs ++ μs') s2 ↔ ∃ s, lts.MTr s1 μs s ∧ lts.MTr s μs' s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TrInv
items.doc: Single-step invariant.
items.statement: def TrInv (p : State → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTrInv
items.doc: Multistep invariant.
items.statement: def MTrInv (p : State → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mtrInv_of_trInv
items.doc: Any single-step invariant is also a multistep invariant.
items.statement:
theorem mtrInv_of_trInv {lts : LTS State Label} {p : State → Prop}
    (htr : lts.TrInv p) : lts.MTrInv p

items.name: Cslib.LTS.CanReach
items.doc:
A state `s1` can reach a state `s2` if there exists a multistep transition from
`s1` to `s2`.
items.statement: def CanReach (s1 s2 : State) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.CanReach.refl
items.doc: Any state can reach itself.
items.statement: theorem CanReach.refl (s : State) : lts.CanReach s s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.generatedBy
items.doc: The LTS generated by a state `s` is the LTS given by all the states reachable from `s`.
items.statement: def generatedBy (s : State) : LTS {s' : State // lts.CanReach s s'} Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.traces
items.doc:
The traces of a state `s` is the set of all lists of labels `μs` such that there is a multi-step
transition labelled by `μs` originating from `s`.
items.statement: def traces (s : State)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.completeTraces
items.doc:
The complete traces of a state `s` is the set of all lists of labels `μs` such that there is a
multi-step transition labelled by `μs` from `s` to a state with no outgoing transitions.
items.statement: def completeTraces (s : State)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_traces_iff
items.doc: Definition of `LTS.traces` for general label sequences, ...
items.statement:
theorem mem_traces_iff {lts : LTS State Label} (μs : List Label) :
  μs ∈ lts.traces s ↔ ∃ s', lts.MTr s μs s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_traces_singleton_iff
items.doc: ... singleton sequences, ...
items.statement:
theorem mem_traces_singleton_iff {lts : LTS State Label} (μ : Label) :
    [μ] ∈ lts.traces s ↔ ∃ s', lts.Tr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_traces_cons_iff
items.doc: ... and sequences extended with a single transition.
items.statement:
theorem mem_traces_cons_iff {lts : LTS State Label} (μ : Label) (μs : List Label) :
    (μ :: μs) ∈ lts.traces s ↔ ∃ s', lts.Tr s μ s' ∧ μs ∈ lts.traces s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.traces_in
items.doc:
If there is a multi-step transition from `s` labelled by `μs`, then `μs` is in the traces of
`s`.
items.statement: theorem traces_in {lts : LTS State Label} (h : lts.MTr s μs s') : μs ∈ lts.traces s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.image
items.doc: The `μ`-image of a state `s` is the set of all `μ`-derivatives of `s`.
items.statement: def image (s : State) (μ : Label) : Set State

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DeterministicStateLabel
items.doc: A state `s` is deterministic for a label `μ` if `s` has at most one `μ`-derivative.
items.statement: def DeterministicStateLabel (s : State) (μ : Label) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.deterministicStateLabel_iff_subsingleton_image
items.doc: Determinism at a state and label means that its image is a subsingleton.
items.statement:
theorem deterministicStateLabel_iff_subsingleton_image {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.DeterministicStateLabel s μ ↔ (lts.image s μ).Subsingleton

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DeterministicState
items.doc: A state `s` is deterministic if it is deterministic for all labels.
items.statement: def DeterministicState (s : State) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.deterministicState_iff_subsingleton_image
items.doc: A state is deterministic exactly when each of its labelled images is a subsingleton.
items.statement:
theorem deterministicState_iff_subsingleton_image {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.DeterministicState s ↔ ∀ μ, (lts.image s μ).Subsingleton

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic
items.doc: An lts is deterministic if it is deterministic at every state.
items.statement:
class Deterministic (lts : LTS State Label) where
  /-- For all states and labels, there is at most one state reachable from a given state
  with a given label. -/
  deterministic : ∀ s, lts.DeterministicState s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.deterministic_iff_subsingleton_image
items.doc: An LTS is deterministic exactly when every labelled image is a subsingleton.
items.statement:
theorem deterministic_iff_subsingleton_image {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.Deterministic ↔ ∀ s μ, (lts.image s μ).Subsingleton

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic.eq_of_tr
items.statement:
theorem Deterministic.eq_of_tr {lts : LTS State Label} [h : lts.Deterministic]
    (htr : lts.Tr s1 μ s2) (htr' : lts.Tr s1 μ s2') : s2 = s2'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic.eq_of_mTr
items.doc:
In a deterministic lts, multistep transitions with a given start state and trace reach a unique
end state.
items.statement:
theorem Deterministic.eq_of_mTr {lts : LTS State Label} [lts.Deterministic]
    (hmtr : lts.MTr s1 μs s2) (hmtr' : lts.MTr s1 μs s2') : s2 = s2'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.imageMultistep
items.doc:
The `μs`-image of a state `s`, where `μs` is a list of labels, is the set of all
`μs`-derivatives of `s`.
items.statement: def imageMultistep (s : State) (μs : List Label) : Set State

items.name: Cslib.LTS.ImageFinite
items.doc: An lts is image-finite if all images of its states are finite.
items.statement: abbrev ImageFinite

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DeterministicStateLabel.not_tr_of_ne
items.doc:
In a deterministic LTS, if a state has a `μ`-derivative, then it can have no other
`μ`-derivative.
items.statement:
theorem DeterministicStateLabel.not_tr_of_ne (hdet : lts.DeterministicStateLabel s μ)
    (hne : s₁ ≠ s₂) (htr₁ : lts.Tr s μ s₁) : ¬lts.Tr s μ s₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DeterministicStateLabel.image_singleton_iff_tr
items.statement:
theorem DeterministicStateLabel.image_singleton_iff_tr (h : lts.DeterministicStateLabel s μ) :
    lts.image s μ = {s'} ↔ lts.Tr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DeterministicStateLabel.image_char
items.doc:
If `s` is deterministic for `μ`, then the `μ`-image of `s` is either a singleton or the empty
set.
items.statement:
theorem DeterministicStateLabel.image_char (h : lts.DeterministicStateLabel s μ) :
    (∃ s', lts.image s μ = { s' }) ∨ (lts.image s μ = ∅)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DeterministicStateLabel.finite_image
items.doc: If `s` is deterministic at `μ`, then the `μ`-image of `s` is finite.
items.statement:
theorem DeterministicStateLabel.finite_image (h : lts.DeterministicStateLabel s μ) :
    Finite (lts.image s μ)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.deterministic_imageFinite
items.doc: Every deterministic LTS is also image-finite.
items.statement: instance deterministic_imageFinite [lts.Deterministic] : lts.ImageFinite

items.name: Cslib.LTS.finiteState_imageFinite
items.doc: Every finite-state LTS is also image-finite.
items.statement: instance finiteState_imageFinite [Finite State] : lts.ImageFinite

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HasOutLabel
items.doc: A state has an outgoing label `μ` if it has a `μ`-derivative.
items.statement: def HasOutLabel (s : State) (μ : Label) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.outgoingLabels
items.doc: The set of outgoing labels of a state.
items.statement: def outgoingLabels (s : State)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.FinitelyBranching
items.doc:
An LTS is finitely branching if it is image-finite and all states have finite sets of
outgoing labels.
items.statement:
class FinitelyBranching where
  [image_finite : lts.ImageFinite]
  [finite_state : ∀ s, Finite (lts.outgoingLabels s)]

items.name: Cslib.LTS.FinitelyBranching.of_finite
items.doc: Every LTS with finite types for states and labels is also finitely branching.
items.statement: instance FinitelyBranching.of_finite [Finite State] [Finite Label] : lts.FinitelyBranching

items.name: Cslib.LTS.BoundedUpTo
items.doc: An LTS is bounded up to `n` if every finite execution has length strictly less than `n`.
