items.statement: def BoundedUpTo (lts : LTS State Label) (n : ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bounded
items.doc: An LTS is bounded if there is a global bound on the length of all of its finite executions.
items.statement:
class Bounded (lts : LTS State Label) where
  bounded : ∃ n, lts.BoundedUpTo n

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Terminating
items.doc:
An LTS is terminating if its underlying unlabelled transition relation is terminating,
equivalently if it admits no infinite execution.
items.statement:
class Terminating (lts : LTS State Label) where
  terminating : Relation.Terminating lts.UnlabelledTr

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Acyclic
items.doc:
An LTS is acyclic if its underlying unlabelled transition relation contains no nonempty
cycle.
items.statement:
class Acyclic (lts : LTS State Label) where
  [acyclic : Relation.Acyclic lts.UnlabelledTr]

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic.traces_of_mTr
items.doc: In a deterministic lts, a state's traces are determined by any of its multi-step predecessors.
items.statement:
theorem Deterministic.traces_of_mTr {lts : LTS State Label} [lts.Deterministic]
    (h : lts.MTr s μs s') : lts.traces s' = {μs' | μs ++ μs' ∈ lts.traces s}

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic.traces_of_tr
items.doc: In a deterministic lts, a state's traces are determined by any of its predecessors.
items.statement:
theorem Deterministic.traces_of_tr {lts : LTS State Label} [lts.Deterministic]
    (h : lts.Tr s μ s') : lts.traces s' = {μs | μ :: μs ∈ lts.traces s}

modules.title: Bisimulation and Bisimilarity
modules.doc:
A bisimulation is a binary relation on the states of two `LTS`s, which establishes a tight semantic
correspondence. More specifically, if two states `s₁` and `s₂` are related by a bisimulation, then
`s₁` can mimic all transitions of `s₂` and vice versa. Furthermore, the derivatives reached through
these transitions remain related by the bisimulation.

Bisimilarity is the largest bisimulation between two LTSs: it relates any two states that are
related by some bisimulation between those LTSs.

Weak bisimulation (resp. bisimilarity) is the relaxed version of bisimulation (resp. bisimilarity)
whereby internal actions performed by processes can be ignored.

For an introduction to theory of bisimulation, we refer to [Sangiorgi2011].

## Main definitions

- `IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r`: the relation `r` is a bisimulation between `lts₁` and `lts₂`.
- `Bisimilarity lts₁ lts₂`: states related by some bisimulation between `lts₁` and `lts₂`.
- `UpToHomBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ r`: the closure of `r` under bisimilarity in each LTS.
- `IsBisimulationUpTo lts₁ lts₂ r`: transitions from states related by `r` can be matched with
  derivatives in `UpToHomBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ r`.
- `IsWeakBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r`: the relation `r` is a weak bisimulation.
- `WeakBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂`: states related by some weak bisimulation.
- `IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r`: a characterization of weak bisimulation using single-transition
  challenges, which we prove to be sound and complete.

The `Hom` variants specialize these definitions to comparing states in the same LTS.

## Notations

- `s₁ ~[lts₁,lts₂] s₂`: the states `s₁` and `s₂` are bisimilar under `lts₁` and `lts₂`.
- `s₁ ≈[lts₁,lts₂] s₂`: the states `s₁` and `s₂` are weakly bisimilar under `lts₁` and `lts₂`.
- `s₁ ~[lts] s₂` and `s₁ ≈[lts] s₂`: the corresponding homogeneous relations.

## Main statements

- `LTS.IsBisimulation.inv`: the inverse of a bisimulation is a bisimulation.
- `HomBisimilarity.eqv`: homogeneous bisimilarity is an equivalence relation (see `Equivalence`).
- `Bisimilarity.isBisimulation`: bisimilarity is itself a bisimulation.
- `IsBisimulation.le_bisimilarity`: bisimilarity is the largest bisimulation.
- `Bisimilarity.gfp`: the union of bisimilarity and any bisimulation is equal to bisimilarity.
- `LTS.IsBisimulationUpTo.isBisimulation`: if `r` is a bisimulation up to bisimilarity,
  `UpToHomBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ r` is a bisimulation.
- `LTS.IsBisimulationUpTo.le_bisimilarity`: a bisimulation up to bisimilarity relates only
  bisimilar states.
- `LTS.IsBisimulation.traceEq`: any bisimulation that relates two states implies that they are
trace equivalent (see `TraceEq`).
- `Bisimilarity.deterministic_bisim_eq_traceEq`: in a deterministic LTS, bisimilarity and trace
equivalence coincide.
- `HomBisimilarity.symm_simulation`: homogeneous bisimilarity can be characterized through
  symmetric simulations.
- `WeakBisimilarity.weakBisim_eq_swBisim`: weak bisimulation and sw-bisimulation coincide.
- `HomWeakBisimilarity.eqv`: homogeneous weak bisimilarity is an equivalence relation.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation
items.doc:
A relation is a bisimulation if, whenever it relates two states,
the transitions originating from these states mimic each other and the reached
derivatives are themselves related.
items.statement:
def IsBisimulation (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label)
    (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.isSimulation
items.doc: Any bisimulation is also a simulation.
items.statement: theorem IsBisimulation.isSimulation : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r → IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.flip_isSimulation
items.doc: The inverse of a bisimulation is a simulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.flip_isSimulation :
    IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r → IsSimulation lts₂ lts₁ (flip r)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.isSimulation_iff
items.doc: A relation is a bisimulation iff both it and its inverse are simulations.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.isSimulation_iff :
    IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r ↔ (IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r ∧ IsSimulation lts₂ lts₁ (flip r))

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.follow_fst
items.doc: Helper for following a transition by the first state in a pair of a `Bisimulation`.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.follow_fst
    (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂) (htr : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁') :
    ∃ s₂', lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.follow_snd
items.doc: Helper for following a transition by the second state in a pair of a `Bisimulation`.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.follow_snd
    (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂) (htr : lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂') :
    ∃ s₁', lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.match_deterministic
items.doc:
If the unique transition of a state is matched by a related state in a bisimulation,
then the derivatives are still in the bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.match_deterministic
    (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r)
    (hr : r s₁ s₂)
    (hdet : lts₁.DeterministicStateLabel s₁ μ)
    (htr₁ : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁')
    (htr₂ : lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂') : r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.match_deterministic₂
items.doc:
If the unique transition of a state is matched by a related state in the inverse of a
bisimulation, then the derivatives are still in the bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.match_deterministic₂
    (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r)
    (hr : r s₁ s₂)
    (hdet : lts₂.DeterministicStateLabel s₂ μ)
    (htr₁ : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁')
    (htr₂ : lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂') : r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.follow_fst_deterministic
items.doc:
If a state is deterministic for `μ`, then any transition made by a related state in a
bisimulation is matched by a unique transition (left variant).
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.follow_fst_deterministic (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂)
    (hdet : lts₂.DeterministicStateLabel s₂ μ) (htr : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁') :
    ∃! s₂', lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.follow_snd_deterministic
items.doc:
If a state is deterministic for `μ`, then any transition made by a related state in a
bisimulation is matched by a unique transition (right variant).
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.follow_snd_deterministic
    (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r)
    (hr : r s₁ s₂)
    (hdet : lts₁.DeterministicStateLabel s₁ μ)
    (htr : lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂') : ∃! s₁', lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsHomBisimulation
items.doc: A homogeneous bisimulation is a bisimulation where the underlying LTSs are the same.
items.statement: abbrev IsHomBisimulation (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity
items.doc: Two states are bisimilar if they are related by some bisimulation.
items.statement: def Bisimilarity (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) : State₁ → State₂ → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomBisimilarity
items.doc: Homogeneous bisimilarity is bisimilarity where the underlying LTSs are the same.
items.statement: abbrev HomBisimilarity (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.follow_fst
items.doc: Helper for following a transition by the first state in a pair of a `Bisimilarity`.
items.statement:
theorem Bisimilarity.follow_fst (hr : s₁ ~[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) (htr : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁') :
    ∃ s₂', lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂' ∧ s₁' ~[lts₁,lts₂ ] s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.follow_snd
items.doc: Helper for following a transition by the first state in a pair of a `Bisimilarity`.
items.statement:
theorem Bisimilarity.follow_snd (hr : s₁ ~[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) (htr : lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂') :
    ∃ s₁', lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁' ∧ s₁' ~[lts₁,lts₂] s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomBisimilarity.refl
items.doc: Homogeneous bisimilarity is reflexive.
items.statement: theorem HomBisimilarity.refl (s : State) : s ~[lts] s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomBisimilarity.of_image_eq
items.doc: States with the same image function are bisimilar.
items.statement:
theorem HomBisimilarity.of_image_eq {lts : LTS State Label} {s₁ s₂ : State}
    (h : lts.image s₁ = lts.image s₂) : s₁ ~[lts] s₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.inv
items.doc: The inverse of a bisimulation is a bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.inv (h : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
  IsBisimulation lts₂ lts₁ (flip r)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.symm
items.doc: Bisimilarity is symmetric.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.comp
items.doc: The composition of two bisimulations is a bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.comp
    (h1 : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r1) (h2 : IsBisimulation lts₂ lts₃ r2) :
  IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₃ (Relation.Comp r1 r2)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.trans
items.doc: Bisimilarity is transitive.
items.statement:
theorem Bisimilarity.trans
    (h1 : s₁ ~[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) (h2 : s₂ ~[lts₂,lts₃] s₃) :
  s₁ ~[lts₁,lts₃] s₃

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomBisimilarity.eqv
items.doc: Homogeneous bisimilarity is an equivalence relation.
items.statement:
theorem HomBisimilarity.eqv :
  Equivalence (HomBisimilarity lts)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.simulationEquiv
items.doc: Bisimulation implies simulation equivalence.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.simulationEquiv (h : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hrel : r s₁ s₂) :
    s₁ ≤≥[lts₁,lts₂] s₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.sup
items.doc: The union of two bisimulations is a bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.sup (hrb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hsb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ s) :
    IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ (r ⊔ s)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.isBisimulation
items.doc: Bisimilarity is a bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem Bisimilarity.isBisimulation (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) :
  IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ (Bisimilarity lts₁ lts₂)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.le_bisimilarity
items.doc: Bisimilarity is the largest bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.le_bisimilarity (h : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
    r ≤ (Bisimilarity lts₁ lts₂)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.gfp
items.doc: The union of bisimilarity with any bisimulation is bisimilarity.
items.statement:
theorem Bisimilarity.gfp (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) (h : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
    (Bisimilarity lts₁ lts₂) ⊔ r = Bisimilarity lts₁ lts₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.coe_sup
items.statement:
lemma coe_sup (r s : {r // IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r}) :
(↑(r ⊔ s) : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) = (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) ⊔ s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.bot
items.doc: The empty (heterogeneous) relation is a bisimulation.
items.statement: theorem IsBisimulation.bot : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ Relation.emptyHRelation

items.name: Cslib.LTS.UpToHomBisimilarity
items.doc:
The closure of `r` under bisimilarity in each LTS: `s₁` and `s₂` are related if there are
`t₁` and `t₂` with `s₁ ~[lts₁] t₁`, `r t₁ t₂`, and `t₂ ~[lts₂] s₂`.
items.statement:
def UpToHomBisimilarity (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label)
    (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) : State₁ → State₂ → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulationUpTo
items.doc:
A relation `r` is a bisimulation up to homogeneous bisimilarity if, whenever it relates two
states, their transitions can be matched with derivatives related by
`UpToHomBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ r`.
items.statement:
def IsBisimulationUpTo (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label)
    (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulationUpTo.isBisimulation
items.doc:
If `r` is a bisimulation up to bisimilarity, its closure
`UpToHomBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ r` is a bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulationUpTo.isBisimulation (h : IsBisimulationUpTo lts₁ lts₂ r) :
    IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ (UpToHomBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ r)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulationUpTo.le_bisimilarity
items.doc: A bisimulation up to bisimilarity relates only bisimilar states.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulationUpTo.le_bisimilarity (h : IsBisimulationUpTo lts₁ lts₂ r) :
    r ≤ Bisimilarity lts₁ lts₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.bisim_trace
items.doc:
If two states are related by a bisimulation, they can mimic each other's multi-step
transitions.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.bisim_trace (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂) :
    ∀ μs s₁', lts₁.MTr s₁ μs s₁' → ∃ s₂', lts₂.MTr s₂ μs s₂' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.traceEq
items.doc: Any bisimulation implies trace equivalence.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.traceEq (hb : IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂) :
    s₁ ~tr[lts₁,lts₂] s₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.le_traceEq
items.doc: Bisimilarity is included in trace equivalence.
items.statement: theorem Bisimilarity.le_traceEq : Bisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ ≤ TraceEq lts₁ lts₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.traceEq_not_bisim
items.doc:
In general, trace equivalence is not a bisimulation (extra conditions are needed, see for
example `Bisimulation.deterministic_trace_eq_is_bisim`).
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.traceEq_not_bisim :
    ∃ (State : Type) (Label : Type) (lts : LTS State Label),
      ¬(IsHomBisimulation lts (HomTraceEq lts))

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.bisimilarity_neq_traceEq
items.doc: In general, bisimilarity and trace equivalence are distinct.
items.statement:
theorem Bisimilarity.bisimilarity_neq_traceEq :
    ∃ (State : Type) (Label : Type) (lts : LTS State Label),
      HomBisimilarity lts ≠ HomTraceEq lts

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsBisimulation.deterministic_traceEq_isBisimulation
items.doc: In any deterministic LTS, trace equivalence is a bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsBisimulation.deterministic_traceEq_isBisimulation
    {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label}
    [lts₁.Deterministic] [lts₂.Deterministic] :
    (IsBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ (TraceEq lts₁ lts₂))

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.deterministic_traceEq_bisim
items.doc: In deterministic LTSs, trace equivalence implies bisimilarity.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic.bisim_tfae
items.doc:
In a deterministic lts, bisimilarity, trace equivalence, and simulation equivalence are
equivalent to one-another.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bisimilarity.deterministic_bisim_eq_traceEq
items.doc: In deterministic LTSs, bisimilarity and trace equivalence coincide.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomBisimilarity.symm_simulation
items.doc: Homogeneous bisimilarity can also be characterized through symmetric simulations.
items.statement:
theorem HomBisimilarity.symm_simulation :
  HomBisimilarity lts =
    fun s₁ s₂ => ∃ r, r s₁ s₂ ∧ Std.Symm r ∧ IsHomSimulation lts r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsWeakBisimulation
items.doc:
A weak bisimulation is similar to a `Bisimulation`, but allows for the related processes to do
internal work. Technically, this is defined as a `Bisimulation` on the saturation of the LTSs.
items.statement:
def IsWeakBisimulation [HasTau Label] (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label)
    (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsHomWeakBisimulation
items.doc: A homogeneous bisimulation is a bisimulation where the underlying LTSs are the same.
items.statement: abbrev IsHomWeakBisimulation [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.WeakBisimilarity
items.doc: Two states are weakly bisimilar if they are related by some weak bisimulation.
items.statement:
def WeakBisimilarity [HasTau Label] (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) :
    State₁ → State₂ → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomWeakBisimilarity
items.doc: Homogeneous bisimilarity is bisimilarity where the underlying LTSs are the same.
items.statement: abbrev HomWeakBisimilarity [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSWBisimulation
items.doc:
An `SWBisimulation` is a more convenient definition of weak bisimulation, because the challenge
is a single transition. We prove later that this technique is sound, following a strategy inspired
by [Sangiorgi2011].
items.statement:
def IsSWBisimulation [HasTau Label] (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label)
    (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSWBisimulation.isSimulation
items.statement:
lemma IsSWBisimulation.isSimulation [HasTau Label] (h : IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
    IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂.saturate r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSWBisimulation.isSimulation_flip
items.statement:
lemma IsSWBisimulation.isSimulation_flip [HasTau Label] (h : IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
    IsSimulation lts₂ lts₁.saturate (flip r)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSWBisimulation.iff_isSimulation
items.statement:
theorem IsSWBisimulation.iff_isSimulation [HasTau Label] :
    IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r ↔
      IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂.saturate r ∧ IsSimulation lts₂ lts₁.saturate (flip r)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.isWeakBisimulation_iff_isSWBisimulation
items.doc:
We can now prove that any relation is a `WeakBisimulation` iff it is an `SWBisimulation`.
This formalises lemma 4.2.10 in [Sangiorgi2011].
items.statement:
theorem isWeakBisimulation_iff_isSWBisimulation
    [HasTau Label] {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label} :
    IsWeakBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r ↔ IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsWeakBisimulation.isSwBisimulation
items.statement:
theorem IsWeakBisimulation.isSwBisimulation
    [HasTau Label] {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label} {r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop}
    (h : IsWeakBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
  IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSWBisimulation.isWeakBisimulation
items.statement:
theorem IsSWBisimulation.isWeakBisimulation
    [HasTau Label] {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label} {r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop}
    (h : IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
  IsWeakBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.WeakBisimilarity.weakBisim_eq_swBisim
items.doc: Weak bisimilarity can also be characterized through sw-bisimulations.
items.statement:
theorem WeakBisimilarity.weakBisim_eq_swBisim [HasTau Label]
    (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) :
    WeakBisimilarity lts₁ lts₂ =
      fun s₁ s₂ => ∃ r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop, r s₁ s₂ ∧ IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomWeakBisimilarity.refl
items.doc: Homogeneous weak bisimilarity is reflexive.
items.statement:
theorem HomWeakBisimilarity.refl [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} (s : State) :
    s ≈[lts] s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsWeakBisimulation.inv
items.doc: The inverse of a weak bisimulation is a weak bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsWeakBisimulation.inv [HasTau Label]
    {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label}
    (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) (h : IsWeakBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) :
    IsWeakBisimulation lts₂ lts₁ (flip r)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.WeakBisimilarity.symm
items.doc: Weak bisimilarity is symmetric.
items.statement:
theorem WeakBisimilarity.symm [HasTau Label] {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label}
    (h : s₁ ≈[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) : s₂ ≈[lts₂,lts₁] s₁

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsWeakBisimulation.comp
items.doc: The composition of two weak bisimulations is a weak bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsWeakBisimulation.comp
    [HasTau Label] {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label} {lts₃ : LTS State₃ Label}
    (h1 : IsWeakBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r1) (h2 : IsWeakBisimulation lts₂ lts₃ r2) :
    IsWeakBisimulation lts₁ lts₃ (Relation.Comp r1 r2)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSWBisimulation.comp
items.doc: The composition of two sw-bisimulations is an sw-bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsSWBisimulation.comp
    [HasTau Label] {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label} {lts₃ : LTS State₃ Label}
    (h1 : IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₂ r1) (h2 : IsSWBisimulation lts₂ lts₃ r2) :
    IsSWBisimulation lts₁ lts₃ (Relation.Comp r1 r2)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.WeakBisimilarity.trans
items.doc: Weak bisimilarity is transitive.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomWeakBisimilarity.eqv
items.doc: Homogeneous weak bisimilarity is an equivalence relation.
items.statement:
theorem HomWeakBisimilarity.eqv [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} :
    Equivalence (HomWeakBisimilarity lts)

items.note: ## Reindex an LTS by an equivalence between two state types

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reindex
items.doc: Reindex an LTS by an equivalence between two state types.
items.statement: def reindex (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (e : State₁ ≃ State₂) : LTS State₂ Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reindex.tr
items.statement:
theorem reindex.tr (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (e : State₁ ≃ State₂) (s₁ t₁ : State₁) (μ : Label) :
    (lts₁.reindex e).Tr (e s₁) μ (e t₁) ↔ lts₁.Tr s₁ μ t₁

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reindex.isBisimulation
items.statement:
theorem reindex.isBisimulation (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (e : State₁ ≃ State₂) :
    IsBisimulation lts₁ (lts₁.reindex e) (fun s s' ↦ s' = e s)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reindex.bisim_trace
items.statement:
theorem reindex.bisim_trace (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (e : State₁ ≃ State₂)
    (s₁ t₁ : State₁) (μs : List Label) :
    lts₁.MTr s₁ μs t₁ → (lts₁.reindex e).MTr (e s₁) μs (e t₁)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reindex.bisim_trace_iff
items.statement:
theorem reindex.bisim_trace_iff (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (e : State₁ ≃ State₂)
    (s₁ t₁ : State₁) (μs : List Label) :
    lts₁.MTr s₁ μs t₁ ↔ (lts₁.reindex e).MTr (e s₁) μs (e t₁)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DivergentTrace
items.doc: An infinite trace is divergent if every label within it is τ.
items.statement: def DivergentTrace [HasTau Label] (μs : ωSequence Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Divergent
items.doc: A state is divergent if there is a divergent execution from it.
items.statement: def Divergent [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) (s : State) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.divergentTrace_drop
items.doc: If a trace is divergent, then any 'suffix' is also divergent.
items.statement:
theorem divergentTrace_drop
    [HasTau Label] {μs : ωSequence Label}
    (h : DivergentTrace μs) (n : ℕ) :
    DivergentTrace (μs.drop n)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.DivergenceFree
items.doc: An LTS is divergence-free if it has no divergent state.
items.statement:
class DivergenceFree [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) where
  divergence_free : ¬∃ s, lts.Divergent s

modules.title: Examples separating boundedness, termination, and acyclicity
modules.doc:
On infinite state spaces, boundedness, termination, and acyclicity are distinct properties.
This file gives concrete LTSs witnessing that the converses in
`Bounded → Terminating → Acyclic` do not hold in general.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.countdownLTS
items.doc: The countdown LTS takes a natural number to its predecessor.
items.statement: def countdownLTS : LTS ℕ Unit

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.countdownLTS_terminating
items.statement: instance countdownLTS_terminating : countdownLTS.Terminating

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.countdownLTS_not_bounded
items.doc: The countdown LTS is not bounded.
items.statement: theorem countdownLTS_not_bounded : ¬ countdownLTS.Bounded

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.successorLTS
items.doc: The successor LTS takes each natural number to its successor.
items.statement: def successorLTS : LTS ℕ Unit

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.successorLTS_acyclic
items.statement: instance successorLTS_acyclic : successorLTS.Acyclic

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.successorLTS_not_terminating
items.doc: The successor LTS is not terminating.
items.statement: theorem successorLTS_not_terminating : ¬ successorLTS.Terminating

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.selfLoopLTS
items.doc: The self-loop LTS has a transition from its unique state to itself.
items.statement: def selfLoopLTS : LTS Unit Unit

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Example.selfLoopLTS_not_acyclic
items.doc: The self-loop LTS is not acyclic.
items.statement: theorem selfLoopLTS_not_acyclic : ¬ selfLoopLTS.Acyclic

modules.authors: Fabrizio Montesi, Ching-Tsun Chou, Thomas Waring
modules.title: Finite executions of LTS
modules.doc:
A finite execution of `lts : LTS State Label`, a proposition `lts.Execution s μs t ss`, which says
that `lts` can transition from `s` to `t` through `ss` using the transition labels `μ`. That is,
the lists have the form `μs = [μ₀, μ₁, ..., μₙ]` and `ss = [s, s₁, s₂, ..., sₙ, t]`, and there are
transitions `lts.Tr s μ₀ s₁`, `lts.Tr s₁ μ₁ s₂`, ..., `lts.Tr sₙ μₙ t`.

We define `Cslib.LTS.Execution` as an inductive proposition, which is equivalent to the definition
in terms of indicies: see `Cslib.LTS.Execution.mk` and `Cslib.LTS.execution_iff_index`.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution
items.doc:
`Execution` extends `MTr` by providing the intermediate states of a multistep transition:
`lts.Execution s₁ μs s₂ ss` means that `lts` can transition from `s₁` to `s₂` through `ss` using
the transition labels `μ`. This is equivalent to the proposition:
```lean
∃ _ : ss.length = μs.length + 1, ss[0] = s₁ ∧ ss[ss.length - 1] = s₂ ∧
  ∀ k < μs.length, lts.Tr ss[k] μ[k] ss[k + 1].
```
Access that formulation as a constructor using `Cslib.LTS.Execution.mk`, and its projections as
`Cslib.LTS.Execution.length`, `Cslib.LTS.Execution.start`, `Cslib.LTS.Execution.last` and
`Cslib.LTS.Execution.trans`.
items.statement:
inductive Execution (lts : LTS State Label) :
    (s : State) → (μs : List Label) → (t : State) → (ss : List State) → Prop where
  /-- Every state has an execution of zero steps terminating in itself. -/
  | refl (s : State) : lts.Execution s [] s [s]
  /-- Equivalent of `MTr.stepL` for executions. -/
  | stepL {r s t : State} {μ : Label} {μs : List Label} {ss : List State}
      (htr : lts.Tr r μ s) (hex : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
      lts.Execution r (μ :: μs) t (r :: ss)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.of_tr
items.statement: theorem of_tr (h : lts.Tr s μ t) : lts.Execution s [μ] t [s, t]

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.length
items.doc:
The lengths of `μs` and `ss` are constrained by the fact that each label `μ ∈ μs` represents
a transition between two states in `ss`.
items.statement: theorem length (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) : ss.length = μs.length + 1

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.length'
items.statement:
theorem length' (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
  μs.length = ss.length - 1

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.length_ss_pos
items.doc: Transitions have positive length.
items.statement: theorem length_ss_pos (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) : 0 < ss.length

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.ss_ne_nil
items.doc: Every execution has at least one intermediate state.
items.statement: theorem ss_ne_nil (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) : ss ≠ []

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.nonEmpty_states
items.statement: alias nonEmpty_states

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.head
items.doc: `s` is the first state of the execution.
items.statement: theorem head (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) : ss.head h.ss_ne_nil = s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.start
items.doc: Alternative accessor for `Cslib.LTS.Execution.head`.
items.statement: theorem start (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) : ss[0]'(h.length_ss_pos) = s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.getLast
items.doc: `t` is the last state of the execution.
items.statement:
theorem getLast (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
    ss.getLast h.ss_ne_nil = t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.last
items.doc: Alternative accessor for `Cslib.LTS.Execution.getLast`.
items.statement:
theorem last (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
    ss[ss.length - 1]'(by lia [h.length_ss_pos]) = t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.last'
items.doc: Alternative accessor for `Cslib.LTS.Execution.getLast`.
items.statement:
theorem last' (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
  ss[μs.length]'(by grind) = t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.trans
items.doc:
`lts` transitions along the `k`th label in `μs` between the `k`th and `(k + 1)`th states in
`ss`.
items.statement:
theorem trans (h : lts.Execution s μs t ss) (k : ℕ) (hk : k < μs.length) :
    lts.Tr (ss[k]'(by lia [h.length])) μs[k] (ss[k + 1]'(by lia [h.length]))

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.mk
items.doc:
Alternative constructor for `Cslib.LTS.Execution`, in terms of the indexed collections of
states and labels.
items.statement:
protected theorem mk {s t : State} {μs : List Label} {ss : List State}
    (length : ss.length = μs.length + 1) (start : ss[0] = s) (last : ss[ss.length - 1] = t)
    (trans : ∀ k (hk : k < μs.length), lts.Tr ss[k] μs[k] ss[k + 1]) :
    lts.Execution s μs t ss

items.name: Cslib.LTS.execution_iff_index
items.doc: The inductive definition of `Cslib.LTS.Execution` is equivalent to that in terms of indices.
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Cslib.LTS.execution_iff_index :
    lts.Execution s μs t ss ↔
      ∃ (_ : ss.length = μs.length + 1), ss[0] = s ∧ ss[ss.length - 1] = t ∧
        ∀ k (_ : k < μs.length), lts.Tr ss[k] μs[k] ss[k + 1]

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.cons_invert
items.doc: Deconstruction of executions with `List.cons`.
items.statement:
theorem cons_invert (h : lts.Execution s (μ :: μs) t (s :: ss)) :
    lts.Execution (ss[0]'(by grind)) μs t ss

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.cons_cons_invert
items.doc:
Deconstruct a positive-length execution, with a specific value for the second state in the
sequence.
items.statement:
theorem cons_cons_invert (h : lts.Execution r (μ :: μs) t (r' :: s :: ss)) :
    lts.Execution s μs t (s :: ss)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.tail_of_length_pos
items.doc: Trim the first state from a positive-length execution.
items.statement:
theorem tail_of_length_pos (he : lts.Execution s μs t ss) (hlen : 0 < μs.length) :
    lts.Execution (ss[1]'(by grind)) μs.tail t ss.tail

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.of_mTr
items.doc: A multistep transition implies the existence of an execution.
items.statement:
theorem of_mTr {lts : LTS State Label} {s : State} {μs : List Label} {t : State}
    (h : lts.MTr s μs t) : ∃ ss : List State, lts.Execution s μs t ss

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.to_mTr
items.doc: Converts an execution into a multistep transition.
items.statement:
theorem to_mTr (hex : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
    lts.MTr s μs t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.isChainFromTo
items.doc:
The states visited by an execution form a chain from the initial to the final state
in the underlying unlabelled relation.
items.statement:
theorem isChainFromTo (hex : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
    ss.IsChainFromTo lts.UnlabelledTr s t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.isChain
items.doc: The states visited by an execution form a chain in the underlying unlabelled relation.
items.statement:
theorem isChain (hex : lts.Execution s μs t ss) :
    ss.IsChain lts.UnlabelledTr

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mTr_iff_execution
items.doc: Correspondence of multistep transitions and executions.
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Cslib.LTS.mTr_iff_execution :
    lts.MTr s μs t ↔ ∃ ss : List State, lts.Execution s μs t ss

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.comp
items.doc: The composition of two executions is an execution.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.take
items.doc: The states up to `ss[n]` form an execution.
items.statement:
theorem take (he : lts.Execution s μs t ss) (n : ℕ) (hn : n < ss.length) :
    lts.Execution s (μs.take n) ss[n] (ss.take (n + 1))

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.drop
items.doc: The states from `ss[n]` onward form an execution.
items.statement:
theorem drop (he : lts.Execution s μs t ss) (n : ℕ) (hn : n < ss.length) :
    lts.Execution ss[n] (μs.drop n) t (ss.drop n)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.split
items.doc: Split an execution at an intermediate state `ss[n]`.
items.statement:
theorem split (he : lts.Execution s μs t ss) {n : ℕ} (hn : n < ss.length) :
    lts.Execution s (μs.take n) ss[n] (ss.take (n + 1)) ∧
      lts.Execution ss[n] (μs.drop n) t (ss.drop n)

items.name: Cslib.HasTau
items.doc: A type of transition labels that includes a special 'internal' transition `τ`.
items.statement:
class HasTau (Label : Type v) where
  /-- The internal transition label, also known as τ. -/
  τ : Label

items.name: Cslib.DecidableEqTau
items.doc: Checking whether an element is `τ` is decidable.
items.statement: abbrev DecidableEqTau (α : Type*) [HasTau α]

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τSTr
items.doc: Saturated τ-transition relation.
items.statement: def τSTr [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) : State → State → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τSTr.refl
items.statement: theorem τSTr.refl [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} : lts.τSTr s s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.STr
items.doc: Saturated transition relation.
items.statement:
inductive STr [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) : State → Label → State → Prop where
  | refl : lts.STr s HasTau.τ s
  | tr : lts.τSTr s1 s2 → lts.Tr s2 μ s3 → lts.τSTr s3 s4 → lts.STr s1 μ s4

items.name: Cslib.LTS.saturate
items.doc: The `LTS` obtained by saturating the transition relation in `lts`.
items.statement: def saturate [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) : LTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.saturate_tr_sTr
items.statement:
theorem saturate_tr_sTr [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} :
  lts.saturate.Tr = lts.STr

items.name: Cslib.LTS.STr.single
items.doc: Any transition is also a saturated transition.
items.statement:
theorem STr.single [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.Tr s μ s' → lts.STr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.tr_le_tr_saturate
items.statement: lemma tr_le_tr_saturate [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) : lts.Tr ≤ lts.saturate.Tr

items.name: Cslib.LTS.sTr_τSTr_iff
items.doc: STr transitions labeled by HasTau.τ are exactly the τSTr transitions.
items.statement:
theorem sTr_τSTr_iff [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) :
    lts.STr s HasTau.τ s' ↔ lts.τSTr s s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.saturate_τsTr_τSTr_iff
items.doc: Saturating an LTS does not change its saturated τ-transition relation.
items.statement:
theorem saturate_τsTr_τSTr_iff [hHasTau : HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) :
    lts.saturate.τSTr = lts.τSTr

items.name: Cslib.LTS.STr.trans_τ
items.doc: Saturated transitions labelled by τ can be composed.
items.statement:
theorem STr.trans_τ
    [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label}
    (h1 : lts.STr s1 HasTau.τ s2) (h2 : lts.STr s2 HasTau.τ s3) :
    lts.STr s1 HasTau.τ s3

items.name: Cslib.LTS.STr.comp
items.doc: Saturated transitions can be composed.
items.statement:
theorem STr.comp
    [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label}
    (h1 : lts.STr s1 HasTau.τ s2)
    (h2 : lts.STr s2 μ s3)
    (h3 : lts.STr s3 HasTau.τ s4) :
  lts.STr s1 μ s4

items.name: Cslib.LTS.saturate_tr_saturate_sTr
items.doc: In a saturated LTS, transitions and saturated transitions agree for every label.
items.statement:
theorem saturate_tr_saturate_sTr [hHasTau : HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) :
    lts.saturate.Tr s μ = lts.saturate.STr s μ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_saturate_image_τ
items.doc: In a saturated LTS, every state is in its τ-image.
items.statement:
lemma mem_saturate_image_τ [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) :
  s ∈ lts.saturate.image s HasTau.τ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.subset_saturate_setImage_τ
items.doc: Monotonicity of `setImage` on `HasTau.τ`.
items.statement:
lemma subset_saturate_setImage_τ [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) :
    S ⊆ lts.saturate.setImage S HasTau.τ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.empty_saturate_setImage_τ
items.doc: `setImage` preserves (non-)emptyness.
items.statement:
lemma empty_saturate_setImage_τ [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) :
    lts.saturate.setImage S HasTau.τ = ∅ ↔ S = ∅

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τClosure
items.doc:
The `τ`-closure of a set of states `S` is the set of states reachable by any state in `S`
by performing only `τ`-transitions.
items.statement: def τClosure [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) (S : Set State) : Set State

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τClosure_subset
items.doc: Monotonicity of `setImage` on `HasTau.τ`.
items.statement:
lemma τClosure_subset [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) :
    S ⊆ lts.τClosure S

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_τClosure_iff
items.doc: The `τ`-closure of `S` consists of the states reachable from `S` by `τ`-transitions.
items.statement:
theorem mem_τClosure_iff [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} {S : Set State} {s' : State} :
    s' ∈ lts.τClosure S ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, lts.τSTr s s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τClosure_empty
items.doc: The `τ`-closure of the empty set is empty.
items.statement: theorem τClosure_empty [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) : lts.τClosure ∅ = ∅

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τClosure_union
items.doc: The `τ`-closure distributes over binary unions.
items.statement:
theorem τClosure_union [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) (S T : Set State) :
    lts.τClosure (S ∪ T) = lts.τClosure S ∪ lts.τClosure T

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τClosure_mono
items.doc: Taking the `τ`-closure is monotone.
items.statement:
theorem τClosure_mono [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) {S T : Set State} (h : S ⊆ T) :
    lts.τClosure S ⊆ lts.τClosure T

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τClosure_τClosure
items.doc: The `τ`-closure is idempotent.
items.statement:
theorem τClosure_τClosure [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) (S : Set State) :
    lts.τClosure (lts.τClosure S) = lts.τClosure S

items.name: Cslib.LTS.saturate_setImage_of_ne_τ
items.doc:
For a label other than `τ`, the saturated image of `S` is the `τ`-closure of the image of the
`τ`-closure of `S`.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SMTr
items.doc: Saturated multistep transition relation.
items.statement:
inductive SMTr [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) : State → List Label → State → Prop where
  | τ : lts.STr s HasTau.τ s' → lts.SMTr s [] s'
  | stepL : lts.STr s1 μ s2 → lts.SMTr s2 μs s3 → lts.SMTr s1 (μ :: μs) s3

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SMTr.refl
items.doc: The saturated multistep transition relation is reflexive.
items.statement:
theorem SMTr.refl [HasTau Label] (lts : LTS State Label) (s : State) :
    lts.SMTr s [] s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SMTr.comp
items.doc: The saturated multistep transition relation is transitive.
items.statement:
theorem SMTr.comp [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label}
    (h₁ : lts.SMTr s₁ μs₁ s₂) (h₂ : lts.SMTr s₂ μs₂ s₃) : lts.SMTr s₁ (μs₁ ++ μs₂) s₃

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SMTr.fromMTr
items.doc: A multistep transition implies a saturated multistep transition.
items.statement:
theorem SMTr.fromMTr [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label}
    (h : lts.MTr s μs s') : lts.SMTr s μs s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.sMTr_τSTr_iff
items.statement:
theorem sMTr_τSTr_iff [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.τSTr s s' ↔ lts.SMTr s [] s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.saturate_mTr_sMTr_not_nil_iff
items.doc: A saturated multistep transition with a nonempty label list implies a multistep transition.
items.statement:
theorem saturate_mTr_sMTr_not_nil_iff [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label}
    (hμs : μs ≠ []) : lts.saturate.MTr s μs s' ↔ lts.SMTr s μs s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.τSTr_iff_exists_mTr_replicate
items.doc: A saturated `τ`-transition is a run along a list of `τ`s.
items.statement:
theorem τSTr_iff_exists_mTr_replicate [HasTau Label] {lts : LTS State Label} {s t : State} :
    lts.τSTr s t ↔ ∃ n, lts.MTr s (List.replicate n HasTau.τ) t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.sMTr_iff_exists_mTr_filter
items.doc:
A saturated run along a list of visible labels is a run whose labels, once the `τ`s are
dropped, are that list.
items.statement:
theorem sMTr_iff_exists_mTr_filter [HasTau Label] [DecidableEqTau Label]
    {lts : LTS State Label} {s t : State} {μs : List Label} (hμs : ∀ μ ∈ μs, μ ≠ HasTau.τ) :
    lts.SMTr s μs t ↔ ∃ νs : List Label, νs.filter (· ≠ HasTau.τ) = μs ∧ lts.MTr s νs t

modules.title: Category of Labelled Transition Systems
modules.doc:
This file contains the definition of the category of labelled transition systems
as defined in Winskel and Nielsen's handbook chapter [WinskelNielsen1995].

## References

* [N. Winskel and M. Nielsen, *Models for concurrency*][WinskelNielsen1995]

items.name: Cslib.LTS.withIdle
items.doc:
We first define what is denoted `Tran*` in [WinskelNielsen1995]: the extension of
a transition relation with idle transitions.
items.statement: def LTS.withIdle (lts : LTS State Label) : LTS State (Option Label)

items.note: ## LTSs and LTS morphisms form a category

items.name: Cslib.LTSCat
items.doc:
The definition of labelled transition system (with the type of states and the
type of labels as part of the structure).
items.statement:
structure LTSCat : Type (max u v + 1) where
  /-- Type of states of an LTS -/
  State : Type u
  /-- Type of labels of an LTS -/
  Label : Type v
  /-- Transition relation of an LTS -/
  lts : LTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Morphism
items.doc:
A morphism between two labelled transition systems consists of (1) a function on
states, (2) a partial function on labels, and a proof that (1) preserves each
transition along (2).
items.statement:
structure LTS.Morphism (lts₁ lts₂ : LTSCat.{u, v}) : Type (max u v) where
  /-- Mapping of states of `lts₁` to states of `lts₂` -/
  stateMap : lts₁.State → lts₂.State
  /-- Mapping of labels of `lts₁` to labels of `lts₂` -/
  labelMap : lts₁.Label → Option lts₂.Label
  /-- Stipulation that `stateMap` preserve transitions -/
  labelMap_tr (s s' : lts₁.State) (l : lts₁.Label) :
    lts₁.lts.Tr s l s' → (withIdle lts₂.lts).Tr (stateMap s) (labelMap l) (stateMap s')

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Morphism.id
items.doc: The identity LTS morphism.
items.statement: def LTS.Morphism.id (lts : LTSCat) : LTS.Morphism lts lts

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Morphism.comp
items.doc:
Composition of LTS morphisms.

We use Kleisli composition to define this.
items.statement:
def LTS.Morphism.comp {lts₁ lts₂ lts₃} (f : LTS.Morphism lts₁ lts₂) (g : LTS.Morphism lts₂ lts₃) :
    LTS.Morphism lts₁ lts₃

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mapHom
items.doc:
Given a language homomorphism `f` from `Label₂` to `Label₁` and an LTS `lts` that
uses `Label₁`, `lts.mapHom f` is an LTS with the same state space but uses `Label₂`, whose
step on a single label `μ` is the composition of the steps taken by `lts` on the sequence of
labels `f [μ]`.  Note that `f [μ]` can be empty or consists of many labels.
items.statement: def mapHom (lts : LTS State Label₁) (f : Hom Label₂ Label₁) : LTS State Label₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mapHom_tr
items.statement:
theorem mapHom_tr {lts : LTS State Label₁} {μ : Label₂} :
    (lts.mapHom f).Tr s μ s' ↔ lts.MTr s (f [μ]) s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mapHom_mTr
items.doc:
This theorem says basically that `lts.mapHom f` is well-defined because `f` is
a language homomorphism.
items.statement:
theorem mapHom_mTr {lts : LTS State Label₁} {μs : List Label₂} :
    (lts.mapHom f).MTr s μs s' ↔ lts.MTr s (f μs) s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mapLabel
items.doc:
This is the special case of `LTS.mapHom` when the language homomorphism maps
single labels to single labels.
items.statement: def mapLabel (lts : LTS State Label₁) (f : Label₂ → Label₁) : LTS State Label₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mapLabel_tr
items.statement:
theorem mapLabel_tr {lts : LTS State Label₁} :
    (lts.mapLabel f).Tr s μ s' ↔ lts.Tr s (f μ) s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mapLabel_mTr
items.statement:
theorem mapLabel_mTr {lts : LTS State Label₁} {f : Label₂ → Label₁} :
    (lts.mapLabel f).MTr s μs s' ↔ lts.MTr s (μs.map f) s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution
items.doc:
An infinite execution is conceptually an infinite sequence of transitions. But it is
technically more convenient to separate the states and the labels into two ω-sequences.
items.statement:
def OmegaExecution (lts : LTS State Label)
    (ss : ωSequence State) (μs : ωSequence Label) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.extract_execution
items.doc: Any finite execution extracted from an infinite execution is valid.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.extract_execution
    (h : lts.OmegaExecution ss μs) {n m : ℕ} (hnm : n ≤ m) :
    lts.Execution (ss n) (μs.extract n m) (ss m) (ss.extract n (m + 1))

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.extract_mTr
items.doc: Any multistep transition extracted from an infinite execution is valid.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.extract_mTr
    (h : lts.OmegaExecution ss μs) {n m : ℕ} (hnm : n ≤ m) :
    lts.MTr (ss n) (μs.extract n m) (ss m)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.cons
items.doc: Prepends an infinite execution with a transition.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.cons (htr : lts.Tr s μ t)
    (hωtr : lts.OmegaExecution ss μs) (hm : ss 0 = t) :
    lts.OmegaExecution (s ::ω ss) (μ ::ω μs)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.prepend_execution_tr
items.doc: Prepend an infinite execution with a finite one, bridged with a transition.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.prepend_execution_tr (he_head : lts.Execution s μl t sl)
    (he_tail : lts.OmegaExecution ss μs) (htr : lts.Tr t μ (ss 0)) :
    lts.OmegaExecution (sl ++ω ss) (μl ++ω μ ::ω μs)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.prepend_execution
items.doc: Glue a finite execution and an infinite execution together on a common first and last state.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.prepend_execution (he_head : lts.Execution s μl t sl)
    (he_tail : lts.OmegaExecution ss μs) (hm : ss 0 = t) :
    lts.OmegaExecution (sl ++ω ss.tail) (μl ++ω μs)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.append
items.doc: Prepends an infinite execution with a finite execution.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.append
    (hmtr : lts.MTr s μl t) (hωtr : lts.OmegaExecution ss μs) (hm : ss 0 = t) :
    ∃ ss', lts.OmegaExecution ss' (μl ++ω μs) ∧
      ss' 0 = s ∧ ss' μl.length = t ∧ ss'.drop μl.length = ss

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.flatten_execution'
items.doc:
Concatenating an infinite sequence of finite executions, with an explicit expression for the
state sequence.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.flatten_execution' [Inhabited Label] [Inhabited State]
    {ts : ωSequence State} {μls : ωSequence (List Label)} {sls : ωSequence (List State)}
    (hexec : ∀ k, lts.Execution (ts k) (μls k) (ts (k + 1)) (sls k))
    (hpos : ∀ k, 0 < (μls k).length) :
    lts.OmegaExecution (sls.map List.dropLast).flatten μls.flatten

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.flatten_execution
items.doc: Concatenating an infinite sequence of finite executions.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.flatten_execution [Inhabited Label]
    {ts : ωSequence State} {μls : ωSequence (List Label)} {sls : ωSequence (List State)}
    (hexec : ∀ k, lts.Execution (ts k) (μls k) (ts (k + 1)) (sls k))
    (hpos : ∀ k, 0 < (μls k).length) :
    ∃ ss, lts.OmegaExecution ss μls.flatten ∧
      ∀ k, ss.extract (μls.cumLen k) (μls.cumLen (k + 1)) = (sls k).take (μls k).length

items.name: Cslib.LTS.OmegaExecution.flatten_mTr
items.doc: Concatenating an infinite sequence of multistep transitions.
items.statement:
theorem OmegaExecution.flatten_mTr [Inhabited Label]
    {ts : ωSequence State} {μls : ωSequence (List Label)}
    (hmtr : ∀ k, lts.MTr (ts k) (μls k) (ts (k + 1))) (hpos : ∀ k, 0 < (μls k).length) :
    ∃ ss, lts.OmegaExecution ss μls.flatten ∧ ∀ k, ss (μls.cumLen k) = ts k

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Tr.toRelation
items.doc: Returns the relation that relates all states `s1` and `s2` via a fixed transition label `μ`.
items.statement: def Tr.toRelation (lts : LTS State Label) (μ : Label) : State → State → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Relation.toLTS
items.doc: Any homogeneous relation can be seen as an LTS where all transitions have the same label.
items.statement:
def Relation.toLTS [DecidableEq Label] (r : State → State → Prop) (μ : Label) :
  LTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.toRelation
items.doc:
Returns the relation that relates all states `s1` and `s2` via a fixed list of transition
labels `μs`.
items.statement: def MTr.toRelation (lts : LTS State Label) (μs : List Label) : State → State → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.toReflTransGen
items.doc:
A multistep transition induces a reflexive-transitive path in the underlying unlabelled
transition relation.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.toReflTransGen (h : lts.MTr s1 μs s2) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen lts.UnlabelledTr s1 s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MTr.toTransGen
items.doc:
A nonempty multistep transition induces a nonempty path in the underlying unlabelled
transition relation.
items.statement:
theorem MTr.toTransGen (h : lts.MTr s1 μs s2) (hne : μs ≠ []) :
    Relation.TransGen lts.UnlabelledTr s1 s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reflTransGen_unlabelledTr_iff
items.doc:
The reflexive-transitive closure of the underlying unlabelled transition relation is exactly
reachability in the LTS.
items.statement:
theorem reflTransGen_unlabelledTr_iff :
    Relation.ReflTransGen lts.UnlabelledTr s1 s2 ↔ lts.CanReach s1 s2

items.name: Cslib.LTS.transGen_unlabelledTr_iff
items.doc:
The transitive closure of the underlying unlabelled transition relation is exactly the
nonempty multistep transitions of the LTS.
items.statement:
theorem transGen_unlabelledTr_iff :
    Relation.TransGen lts.UnlabelledTr s1 s2 ↔
      ∃ μs, μs ≠ [] ∧ lts.MTr s1 μs s2

modules.title: Reverse operation for LTS
modules.doc:
This file defines `Cslib.LTS.reverse`, which reverses every transition of an LTS.
`reverse_canReach`, `reverse_unlabelledTr`, `reverse_image`, `reverse_imageMultistep`,
`reverse_hasOutLabel` and `reverse_boundedUpTo` each state a property about `lts.reverse` in
terms of `lts`.

`reverse_mTr` states that the multistep transitions of `lts.reverse` are the reversed
multistep transitions of `lts`. `reverse_execution` is the same statement for
executions, and is derived from `Execution.reverse`.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse
items.doc: Constructs an LTS by reversing the transitions of an existing LTS.
items.statement: def reverse (lts : LTS State Label) : LTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_tr
items.doc: The transitions of `lts.reverse` are exactly the reversed transitions of `lts`.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_tr {lts : LTS State Label} :
    (lts.reverse).Tr s μ s' ↔ lts.Tr s' μ s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_reverse
items.doc: Reversing an LTS twice gives back the original LTS.
items.statement: theorem reverse_reverse (lts : LTS State Label) : lts.reverse.reverse = lts

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_involutive
items.doc: Reversal of an LTS is an involution.
items.statement: theorem reverse_involutive : Function.Involutive (reverse (Label := Label) (State := State))

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Execution.reverse
items.statement:
theorem Execution.reverse {lts : LTS State Label} (h : lts.Execution s μs s' ss) :
    lts.reverse.Execution s' μs.reverse s ss.reverse

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_execution
items.doc:
An execution of `lts.reverse` is an execution of `lts` with the labels, states
and endpoints reversed.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_execution {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.reverse.Execution s μs s' ss ↔ lts.Execution s' μs.reverse s ss.reverse

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_mTr
items.doc:
The multistep transitions of `lts.reverse` are exactly the reversed multistep transitions of
`lts`.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_mTr {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.reverse.MTr s' μs s ↔ lts.MTr s μs.reverse s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_canReach
items.doc: `lts.reverse` can reach `s'` from `s` iff `lts` can reach `s` from `s'`.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_canReach {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.reverse.CanReach s s' ↔ lts.CanReach s' s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_unlabelledTr
items.doc: The unlabelled transitions of `lts.reverse` are those of `lts` with the endpoints swapped.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_unlabelledTr {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.reverse.UnlabelledTr s s' ↔ lts.UnlabelledTr s' s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_image
items.doc: The `μ`-image of a state in `lts.reverse` is its `μ`-preimage in `lts`.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_image {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.reverse.image s μ = {s' | lts.Tr s' μ s}

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_reverse_image
items.doc: Membership form of `reverse_image`.
items.statement:
theorem mem_reverse_image {lts : LTS State Label} :
    s' ∈ lts.reverse.image s μ ↔ s ∈ lts.image s' μ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_imageMultistep
items.doc: The `μs`-image of a state in `lts.reverse` is its `μs.reverse`-preimage in `lts`.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_imageMultistep {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.reverse.imageMultistep s μs = {s' | lts.MTr s' μs.reverse s}

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_reverse_imageMultistep
items.doc: Membership version of `reverse_imageMultistep`.
items.statement:
theorem mem_reverse_imageMultistep {lts : LTS State Label} :
    s' ∈ lts.reverse.imageMultistep s μs ↔ s ∈ lts.imageMultistep s' μs.reverse

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_hasOutLabel
items.doc:
A state has `μ` as an outgoing label in `lts.reverse` iff it has `μ` as an incoming
label in `lts`.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_hasOutLabel {lts : LTS State Label} :
    lts.reverse.HasOutLabel s μ ↔ ∃ s', lts.Tr s' μ s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.reverse_boundedUpTo
items.doc: `lts.reverse` is bounded up to `n` iff `lts` is.
items.statement:
theorem reverse_boundedUpTo {lts : LTS State Label} {n : ℕ} :
    lts.reverse.BoundedUpTo n ↔ lts.BoundedUpTo n

modules.title: Images of sets of states
modules.doc:
The image of a set of states of an `LTS` along a label and along a list of labels, with lemmas on
membership, singletons, the empty set and the empty list, unions, monotonicity and concatenation.

## Main definitions

- `LTS.setImage`: the `μ`-image of a set of states.
- `LTS.setImageMultistep`: the `μs`-image of a set of states, for a list of labels `μs`.

## Main statements

- `LTS.mem_setImage`, `LTS.mem_setImageMultistep`: membership through `Tr` and `MTr`.
- `LTS.setImageMultistep_foldl_setImage`: the multistep image is a left fold of `setImage`.
- `LTS.setImage_union`, `LTS.setImageMultistep_union`: images distribute over unions.
- `LTS.setImageMultistep_append`: the image along `μs₁ ++ μs₂` is the image along `μs₂` of the
  image along `μs₁`.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImage
items.doc: The `μ`-image of a set of states `S` is the union of all `μ`-images of the states in `S`.
items.statement: def setImage (S : Set State) (μ : Label) : Set State

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep
items.doc:
The `μs`-image of a set of states `S`, where `μs` is a list of labels, is the union of all
`μs`-images of the states in `S`.
items.statement: def setImageMultistep (S : Set State) (μs : List Label) : Set State

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_setImage
items.doc: Characterisation of `setImage` wrt `Tr`.
items.statement:
theorem mem_setImage {lts : LTS State Label} :
  s' ∈ lts.setImage S μ ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, lts.Tr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.tr_setImage
items.statement:
theorem tr_setImage {lts : LTS State Label} (hs : s ∈ S) (htr : lts.Tr s μ s') :
  s' ∈ lts.setImage S μ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_setImageMultistep
items.doc: Characterisation of `setImageMultistep` with `MTr`.
items.statement:
theorem mem_setImageMultistep {lts : LTS State Label} :
  s' ∈ lts.setImageMultistep S μs ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, lts.MTr s μs s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mTr_setImage
items.statement:
theorem mTr_setImage {lts : LTS State Label} (hs : s ∈ S) (htr : lts.MTr s μs s') :
  s' ∈ lts.setImageMultistep S μs

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImage_empty
items.doc: The image of the empty set is always the empty set.
items.statement: theorem setImage_empty (lts : LTS State Label) : lts.setImage ∅ μ = ∅

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_setImage_head
items.statement:
lemma setImageMultistep_setImage_head (lts : LTS State Label) :
  lts.setImageMultistep S (μ :: μs) = lts.setImageMultistep (lts.setImage S μ ) μs

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_foldl_setImage
items.doc: Characterisation of `setImageMultistep` as `List.foldl` on `setImage`.
items.statement:
theorem setImageMultistep_foldl_setImage (lts : LTS State Label) :
  lts.setImageMultistep = List.foldl lts.setImage

items.name: Cslib.LTS.mem_foldl_setImage
items.doc: Characterisation of membership in `List.foldl lts.setImage` with `MTr`.
items.statement:
theorem mem_foldl_setImage (lts : LTS State Label) :
  s' ∈ List.foldl lts.setImage S μs ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, lts.MTr s μs s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImage_singleton
items.doc: The image of a singleton is the image of its element.
items.statement: theorem setImage_singleton (s : State) (μ : Label) : lts.setImage {s} μ = lts.image s μ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImage_union
items.doc: Images of sets distribute over binary unions.
items.statement:
theorem setImage_union (S T : Set State) (μ : Label) :
    lts.setImage (S ∪ T) μ = lts.setImage S μ ∪ lts.setImage T μ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImage_iUnion
items.doc: Images of sets distribute over indexed unions.
items.statement:
theorem setImage_iUnion {ι : Sort*} (S : ι → Set State) (μ : Label) :
    lts.setImage (⋃ i, S i) μ = ⋃ i, lts.setImage (S i) μ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImage_mono
items.doc: Taking the image of a set is monotone.
items.statement:
theorem setImage_mono {S T : Set State} (h : S ⊆ T) (μ : Label) :
    lts.setImage S μ ⊆ lts.setImage T μ

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_nil
items.doc: The multistep image of a set along the empty list is the set itself.
items.statement: theorem setImageMultistep_nil (S : Set State) : lts.setImageMultistep S [] = S

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_empty
items.doc: The multistep image of the empty set is empty.
items.statement: theorem setImageMultistep_empty (μs : List Label) : lts.setImageMultistep ∅ μs = ∅

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_singleton
items.doc: The multistep image of a singleton is the multistep image of its element.
items.statement:
theorem setImageMultistep_singleton (s : State) (μs : List Label) :
    lts.setImageMultistep {s} μs = lts.imageMultistep s μs

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_union
items.doc: Multistep images of sets distribute over binary unions.
items.statement:
theorem setImageMultistep_union (S T : Set State) (μs : List Label) :
    lts.setImageMultistep (S ∪ T) μs =
      lts.setImageMultistep S μs ∪ lts.setImageMultistep T μs

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_iUnion
items.doc: Multistep images of sets distribute over indexed unions.
items.statement:
theorem setImageMultistep_iUnion {ι : Sort*} (S : ι → Set State) (μs : List Label) :
    lts.setImageMultistep (⋃ i, S i) μs = ⋃ i, lts.setImageMultistep (S i) μs

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_mono
items.doc: Taking the multistep image of a set is monotone.
items.statement:
theorem setImageMultistep_mono {S T : Set State} (h : S ⊆ T) (μs : List Label) :
    lts.setImageMultistep S μs ⊆ lts.setImageMultistep T μs

items.name: Cslib.LTS.setImageMultistep_append
items.doc:
The multistep image along `μs₁ ++ μs₂` is the multistep image along `μs₂` of the multistep
image along `μs₁`.
items.statement:
theorem setImageMultistep_append (S : Set State) (μs₁ μs₂ : List Label) :
    lts.setImageMultistep S (μs₁ ++ μs₂) =
      lts.setImageMultistep (lts.setImageMultistep S μs₁) μs₂

modules.title: IsSimulation and Similarity
modules.doc:
A simulation is a binary relation on the states of two `LTS`s: if two states `s₁` and `s2` are
related by a simulation, then `s2` can mimic all transitions of `s₁` in their respective LTSs.
Furthermore, the derivatives reaches through these transitions remain related by the simulation.

Similarity is the largest simulation: given an `LTS`, it relates any two states that are related
by a simulation for that LTS.

The module provides abbreviations for the homogeneous case of comparing states in the same LTS.

For an introduction to theory of simulation, we refer to [Sangiorgi2011].

## Main definitions

- `IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r`: the relation `r` on the states of `lts₁` and `lts₂` is a simulation.
- `IsSimulationMap lts₁ lts₂ f`: the map `f` from the states of `lts₁` to those of `lts₂` sends
transitions to transitions.
- `Similarity lts₁ lts₂` is the binary relation that relates any two states related by some
simulation on `lts₁` and `lts₂`.
- `SimulationEquiv lts₁ lts₂` is the binary relation on the states of `lts₁` and `lts₂` that relates
any two states similar to each other.

## Notations

- `s₁ ≤[lts₁, lts₂] s₂`: the states `s₁` and `s2` are similar under `lts₁` and `lts₂`.
- `s₁ ≤≥[lts₁, lts₂] s2`: the states `s₁` and `s2` are simulation equivalent under `lts₁` and
`lts₂`.

## Main statements

- `HomSimulationEquiv.eqv`: homogeneous simulation equivalence is an equivalence relation.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation
items.doc:
A relation is a simulation if, whenever it relates two states in an lts,
any transition originating from the first state is mimicked by a transition from the second state
and the reached derivatives are themselves related.
items.statement:
def IsSimulation (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) (r : State₁ → State₂ → Prop) :
    Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsHomSimulation
items.doc: A homogeneous simulation is a simulation where the underlying LTSs are the same.
items.statement: abbrev IsHomSimulation (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Similarity
items.doc: Two states are similar if they are related by some simulation.
items.statement: def Similarity (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) : State₁ → State₂ → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomSimilarity
items.doc: Homogeneous similarity is similarity where the underlying LTSs are the same.
items.statement: abbrev HomSimilarity (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomSimilarity.refl
items.doc: Homogeneous similarity is reflexive.
items.statement: theorem HomSimilarity.refl (s : State) : s ≤[lts] s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.comp
items.doc: The composition of two simulations is a simulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.comp
    (r1 : State₁ → State₂ → Prop)
    (r2 : State₂ → State₃ → Prop)
    (h1 : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r1) (h2 : IsSimulation lts₂ lts₃ r2) :
    IsSimulation lts₁ lts₃ (Relation.Comp r1 r2)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Similarity.trans
items.doc: Similarity is transitive.
items.statement:
theorem Similarity.trans (h1 : s₁ ≤[lts₁,lts₂] s2) (h2 : s2 ≤[lts₂,lts₃] s₃) :
    s₁ ≤[lts₁,lts₃] s₃

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.sup
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.sup (hr : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r)
    (hs : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ s) : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ (r ⊔ s)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.sim_trace
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.sim_trace (hr : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hrel : r s₁ s₂) :
    ∀ μs s₁', lts₁.MTr s₁ μs s₁' → ∃ s₂', lts₂.MTr s₂ μs s₂' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulationMap
items.doc:
A map of states is a simulation map if it sends every transition of `lts₁` to a transition of
`lts₂` with the same label.
items.statement:
def IsSimulationMap (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) (f : State₁ → State₂) :
    Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulationMap.isSimulation
items.doc: The graph of a simulation map is a simulation.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulationMap.sim_trace
items.doc: A simulation map sends multistep transitions to multistep transitions.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SimulationEquiv
items.doc:
Simulation equivalence relates all states `s₁` and `s2` such that `s₁ ≤[lts₁ lts₂] s2` and
`s2 ≤[lts₂ lts₁] s₁`.
items.statement:
def SimulationEquiv (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label) :
    State₁ → State₂ → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomSimulationEquiv
items.doc: Homogeneous simulation equivalence.
items.statement: abbrev HomSimulationEquiv (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomSimulationEquiv.refl
items.doc: Homogeneous simulation equivalence is reflexive.
items.statement: theorem HomSimulationEquiv.refl (s : State) : s ≤≥[lts] s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SimulationEquiv.symm
items.doc: Simulation equivalence is symmetric.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SimulationEquiv.trans
items.doc: Simulation equivalence is transitive.
items.statement:
theorem SimulationEquiv.trans (h1 : s₁ ≤≥[lts₁,lts₂] s2) (h2 : s2 ≤≥[lts₂,lts₃] s₃) :
    s₁ ≤≥[lts₁,lts₃] s₃

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomSimulationEquiv.eqv
items.doc: Homogeneous simulation equivalence is an equivalence relation.
items.statement: theorem HomSimulationEquiv.eqv : Equivalence (· ≤≥[lts] ·)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.follow
items.doc: Helper for following a transition by the first state in a pair of a simulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.follow
    (hb : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂) (htr : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁') :
    ∃ s₂', lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.follow_internal
items.doc: Utility theorem for following internal transitions along a saturated lts.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.isSimulation_saturate_left
items.doc: If the right-hand lts is saturated, a simulation lifts along saturating the left-hand lts.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.mono
items.doc:
Simulation is preserved by removing transitions on the left, and adding transitions on the
right.
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.mono (h₁ : lts₁'.Tr ≤ lts₁.Tr) (h₂ : lts₂.Tr ≤ lts₂'.Tr)
    (h : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) : IsSimulation lts₁' lts₂' r

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.match_deterministic
items.doc:
When a deterministic state matches a transition in a simulation, then the derivatives are still
in the simulation.
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.match_deterministic (hb : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂)
    (hdet : lts₂.DeterministicStateLabel s₂ μ) (htr₁ : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁') (htr₂ : lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂') :
    r s₁' s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.follow_deterministic
items.doc:
If a state is deterministic for `μ`, then any transition made by a related state in a
simulation is matched by a unique transition.
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.follow_deterministic (hb : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hr : r s₁ s₂)
    (hdet : lts₂.DeterministicStateLabel s₂ μ) (htr : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁') :
    ∃! s₂', lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂' ∧ r s₁' s₂'

modules.title: Termination of LTS
modules.doc: This module relates global execution bounds, well-founded termination, and acyclicity.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Bounded.toTerminating
items.doc: Bounded LTSs are terminating.
items.statement: theorem Bounded.toTerminating (h : lts.Bounded) : lts.Terminating

items.name: Cslib.LTS.bounded_terminating
items.doc: A bounded LTS is available as a terminating LTS through typeclass inference.
items.statement: instance bounded_terminating [lts.Bounded] : lts.Terminating

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Terminating.toAcyclic
items.doc: Terminating LTSs are acyclic.
items.statement: theorem Terminating.toAcyclic (h : lts.Terminating) : lts.Acyclic

items.name: Cslib.LTS.terminating_acyclic
items.doc: A terminating LTS is available as an acyclic LTS through typeclass inference.
items.statement: instance terminating_acyclic [lts.Terminating] : lts.Acyclic

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Acyclic.toBoundedUpTo
items.doc:
On a finite state space, an acyclic LTS has execution length strictly less than the number of
states.
items.statement:
theorem Acyclic.toBoundedUpTo [Finite State] (h : lts.Acyclic) :
    lts.BoundedUpTo (Nat.card State)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Acyclic.toBounded
items.doc: On a finite state space, acyclic LTSs are bounded.
items.statement: theorem Acyclic.toBounded [Finite State] (h : lts.Acyclic) : lts.Bounded

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Acyclic.toTerminating
items.doc: On a finite state space, acyclic LTSs are terminating.
items.statement: theorem Acyclic.toTerminating [Finite State] (h : lts.Acyclic) : lts.Terminating

items.name: Cslib.LTS.MayTerminate
items.doc:
A state 'may terminate' if it can reach a terminated state. The definition of `Terminated`
is a parameter.
items.statement: def MayTerminate (s : State) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Stuck
items.doc:
A state 'is stuck' if it is not terminated and cannot go forward. The definition of `Terminated`
is a parameter.
items.statement: def Stuck (s : State) : Prop

modules.title: Total LTS
modules.doc:
This file defines, and proves some theorems about, the notion of an LTS being "total"
and a "totalize" construction that converts any LTS into a total LTS.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Total
items.doc: An LTS is total iff every state has a `μ`-derivative for every label `μ`.
items.statement:
class Total (lts : LTS State Label) where
  /-- The condition of being total. -/
  total s μ : ∃ s', lts.Tr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.chooseFLTS
items.doc: Choose an FLTS that is a "sub-LTS" of a total LTS.
items.statement: noncomputable def chooseFLTS (lts : LTS State Label) [h : lts.Total] : FLTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Total.chooseFLTS
items.doc: The FLTS chosen by `chooseFLTS` always provides legal transitions.
items.statement:
theorem Total.chooseFLTS (lts : LTS State Label) [h : lts.Total] (s : State) (μ : Label) :
    lts.Tr s μ (lts.chooseFLTS.tr s μ)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.chooseOmegaExecution
items.doc:
`chooseOmegaExecution` builds an infinite execution of a total LTS from any starting state
and over any infinite sequence of labels.
items.statement:
noncomputable def chooseOmegaExecution (lts : LTS State Label) [lts.Total]
    (s : State) (μs : ωSequence Label) : ℕ → State

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Total.omegaExecution_exists
items.doc:
If a LTS is total, then there exists an infinite execution from any starting state and
over any infinite sequence of labels.
items.statement:
theorem Total.omegaExecution_exists [h : lts.Total] (s : State) (μs : ωSequence Label) :
    ∃ ss, lts.OmegaExecution ss μs ∧ ss 0 = s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Total.extend_omegaExecution
items.doc:
If a LTS is total, then any finite execution can be extended to an infinite execution,
provided that the label type is inbabited.
items.statement:
theorem Total.extend_omegaExecution [Inhabited Label] [ht : lts.Total]
    {μl : List Label} {s t : State} (hm : lts.MTr s μl t) :
    ∃ μs ss, lts.OmegaExecution ss (μl ++ω μs) ∧ ss 0 = s ∧ ss μl.length = t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.totalize
items.doc: `totalize` constructs a total LTS from any given LTS by adding a sink state.
items.statement: def totalize (lts : LTS State Label) : LTS (Option State) Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.totalize.no_sink_to_nonsink
items.doc: In `totalize`, there is no finite execution from the sink state to any non-sink state.
items.statement:
theorem totalize.no_sink_to_nonsink {μs : List Label} {t : State} :
    ¬ lts.totalize.MTr (none) μs (some t)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.totalize.nonsink_tr_iff
items.doc:
In `totalize`, the transitions between non-sink states correspond exactly to
the transitions in the original LTS.
items.statement:
theorem totalize.nonsink_tr_iff {μ : Label} {s t : State} :
    lts.totalize.Tr (some s) μ (some t) ↔ lts.Tr s μ t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.totalize.nonsink_mtr_iff
items.doc:
In `totalize`, the multistep transitions between non-sink states correspond exactly to
the multistep transitions in the original LTS.
items.statement:
theorem totalize.nonsink_mtr_iff {μs : List Label} {s t : State} :
    lts.totalize.MTr (some s) μs (some t) ↔ lts.MTr s μs t

modules.title: Trace Equivalence
modules.doc:
Definitions and results on trace equivalence for `LTS`s.

## Main definitions

- `LTS.traces`: the set of traces of a state.
- `TraceEq s₁ s₂`: `s₁` and `s₂` are trace equivalent, i.e., they have the same sets of traces.

## Notations

- `s₁ ~tr[lts] s₂`: the states `s₁` and `s₂` are trace equivalent in `lts`.

## Main statements

- `TraceEq.eqv`: trace equivalence is an equivalence relation (see `Equivalence`).
- `Deterministic.isSimulation_traceEq`: in any deterministic `LTS`, trace equivalence is a
  simulation.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.IsSimulation.traces_subset
items.doc: If `s₁` is simulated by `s₂` all of `s₁`'s traces are also traces of `s₂`.
items.statement:
theorem IsSimulation.traces_subset (hr : IsSimulation lts₁ lts₂ r) (hrel : r s₁ s₂) :
    lts₁.traces s₁ ⊆ lts₂.traces s₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TraceEq
items.doc: Two states are trace equivalent if they have the same set of traces.
items.statement:
def TraceEq (lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label) (lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label)
    (s₁ : State₁) (s₂ : State₂)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomTraceEq
items.doc: Homogeneous trace equivalence compares states on the same LTS.
items.statement: abbrev HomTraceEq (lts : LTS State Label)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomTraceEq.refl
items.doc: Homogeneous trace equivalence is reflexive.
items.statement: theorem HomTraceEq.refl (s : State) : s ~tr[lts] s

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TraceEq.flip_eq
items.statement: theorem TraceEq.flip_eq : flip (TraceEq lts₁ lts₂) = TraceEq lts₂ lts₁

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TraceEq.symm
items.doc: Trace equivalence is symmetric.
items.statement: theorem TraceEq.symm (h : s₁ ~tr[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) : s₂ ~tr[lts₂,lts₁] s₁

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TraceEq.trans
items.doc: Trace equivalence is transitive.
items.statement:
theorem TraceEq.trans (h1 : s₁ ~tr[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) (h2 : s₂ ~tr[lts₂,lts₃] s₃) :
    s₁ ~tr[lts₁,lts₃] s₃

items.name: Cslib.LTS.HomTraceEq.eqv
items.doc: Homogeneous trace equivalence is an equivalence relation.
items.statement: theorem HomTraceEq.eqv : Equivalence (· ~tr[lts] ·)

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TraceEq.exists_mTr_of_mTr
items.doc: For trace-equivalent states, any multistep transition of one can be mimicked by the other.
items.statement:
theorem TraceEq.exists_mTr_of_mTr {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label}
    (h : s₁ ~tr[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) (htr : lts₁.MTr s₁ μs s₁') : ∃ s₂', lts₂.MTr s₂ μs s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TraceEq.exists_tr_of_tr
items.doc: For trace-equivalent states, any single-step transition of one can be mimicked by the other.
items.statement:
theorem TraceEq.exists_tr_of_tr {lts₁ : LTS State₁ Label} {lts₂ : LTS State₂ Label}
    (h : s₁ ~tr[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) (htr : lts₁.Tr s₁ μ s₁') : ∃ s₂', lts₂.Tr s₂ μ s₂'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.TraceEq.traceEq_of_tr_of_tr
items.doc:
For deterministic lts's, trace equivalence is preserved by respective transitions with the same
label.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic.isSimulation_traceEq
items.doc: In deterministic LTSs, trace equivalence is a simulation.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.SimulationEquiv.traceEq
items.doc: Simulation equivalence implies trace equivalence.
items.statement: theorem SimulationEquiv.traceEq (h : s₁ ≤≥[lts₁,lts₂] s₂) : s₁ ~tr[lts₁,lts₂] s₂

items.name: Cslib.LTS.Deterministic.traceEq_iff_simulationEquiv
items.doc: Simulation equivalence and trace equivalence are equivalence for detemrinistic lts's.

modules.title: Union of LTSs
modules.doc:
Note: there is a nontrivial balance between ergonomics and generality here. These definitions might
change in the future.

items.name: Cslib.LTS.union
items.doc: The union of two LTSs defined on the same types.
items.statement: def union (lts1 lts2 : LTS State Label) : LTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSubtype
items.doc: The union of two LTSs that have common supertypes for states and labels.
items.statement:
def unionSubtype
{S1 : State → Prop} {L1 : Label → Prop} {S2 : State → Prop} {L2 : Label → Prop}
(lts1 : LTS (@Subtype State S1) (@Subtype Label L1))
(lts2 : LTS (@Subtype State S2) (@Subtype Label L2)) :
  LTS State Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.inl
items.doc: Lifting of an `LTS State Label` to `LTS (State ⊕ State') Label`.
items.statement:
def inl (lts : LTS State Label) :
    LTS { x : State ⊕ State' // x.isLeft } { _label : Label // True }

items.name: Cslib.LTS.inr
items.doc: Lifting of an `LTS State Label` to `LTS (State' ⊕ State) Label`.
items.statement:
def inr (lts : LTS State Label) :
    LTS { x : State' ⊕ State // x.isRight } { _label : Label // True }

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum
items.doc:
Union of two LTSs with the same `Label` type. The result combines the original respective
state types `State1` and `State2` into `(State1 ⊕ State2)`.
items.statement:
def unionSum (lts1 : LTS State1 Label) (lts2 : LTS State2 Label) :
    LTS (State1 ⊕ State2) Label

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_tr_inl_inl
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_tr_inl_inl {s s' : State1} {μ : Label} :
    (unionSum lts1 lts2).Tr (.inl s) μ (.inl s') ↔ lts1.Tr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_tr_inr_inr
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_tr_inr_inr {s s' : State2} {μ : Label} :
    (unionSum lts1 lts2).Tr (.inr s) μ (.inr s') ↔ lts2.Tr s μ s'

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_not_tr_inl_inr
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_not_tr_inl_inr {s : State1} {s' : State2} {μ : Label} :
    ¬(unionSum lts1 lts2).Tr (.inl s) μ (.inr s')

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_not_tr_inr_inl
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_not_tr_inr_inl {s : State2} {s' : State1} {μ : Label} :
    ¬(unionSum lts1 lts2).Tr (.inr s) μ (.inl s')

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_mTr_inl
items.doc:
A run of `unionSum lts1 lts2` from a state of `lts1` stays among the states of `lts1`, where it
is a run of `lts1`.
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_mTr_inl {s : State1} {μs : List Label} {y : State1 ⊕ State2}
    (h : (unionSum lts1 lts2).MTr (.inl s) μs y) : ∃ t, y = .inl t ∧ lts1.MTr s μs t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_mTr_inr
items.doc:
A run of `unionSum lts1 lts2` from a state of `lts2` stays among the states of `lts2`, where it
is a run of `lts2`.
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_mTr_inr {s : State2} {μs : List Label} {y : State1 ⊕ State2}
    (h : (unionSum lts1 lts2).MTr (.inr s) μs y) : ∃ t, y = .inr t ∧ lts2.MTr s μs t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_mTr_inl_iff
items.doc: The runs of `unionSum lts1 lts2` between states of `lts1` are the runs of `lts1`.
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_mTr_inl_iff {s t : State1} {μs : List Label} :
    (unionSum lts1 lts2).MTr (.inl s) μs (.inl t) ↔ lts1.MTr s μs t

items.name: Cslib.LTS.unionSum_mTr_inr_iff
items.doc: The runs of `unionSum lts1 lts2` between states of `lts2` are the runs of `lts2`.
items.statement:
theorem unionSum_mTr_inr_iff {s t : State2} {μs : List Label} :
    (unionSum lts1 lts2).MTr (.inr s) μs (.inr t) ↔ lts2.MTr s μs t

modules.doc: Typeclass for congruence over a context.

items.name: Cslib.Congruence
items.doc:
The relation `r` is a congruence on `α`. This class gives access to the `≡[r]` notation.
To instantiate a canonical congruence for `α`, see `HasCongruence`.

Congruence relations should also instantiate `LawfulCongruence` to prove that the relation respects
the expected congruence laws.
items.statement: class Congruence (r : α → α → Prop)

items.name: Cslib.Congruence.r
items.doc: `a ≡[r] b` means that the `a` and `b` are related by the congruence `r`.
items.statement: abbrev Congruence.r (r : α → α → Prop) [Congruence r]

items.name: Cslib.DefaultCongruence
