items.doc: The type `α` has a canonical congruence relation. This gives access to the `≡` notation.
items.statement: class DefaultCongruence (α : Type*) (r : outParam (α → α → Prop))

items.name: Cslib.DefaultCongruence.r
items.doc:
`a ≡ b` means that `a` and `b` are related by the canonical congruence relation for their
type.
items.statement: abbrev DefaultCongruence.r {α : Type*} {r : α → α → Prop} [DefaultCongruence α r] (a b : α)

items.name: Cslib.LawfulCongruence
items.doc: An equivalence relation on `α` preserved by all contexts.
items.statement:
class LawfulCongruence (r : α → α → Prop) [Congruence r] [HasContext α] extends
  IsEquiv α r, covariant : CovariantClass (HasContext.Context α) α (·<[·]) r

modules.doc: Typeclasses for contexts, with heterogeneous and homogeneous variants.

items.name: Cslib.HasHContext
items.doc: Class for types with a canonical notion of heterogeneous single-hole contexts.
items.statement:
class HasHContext (α β : Type*) where
  /-- The type of contexts. -/
  {Context : Type*}
  /-- Replaces the hole in the context with a value, resulting in a new value. -/
  fill (c : Context) (b : β) : α

@[inherit_doc] notation:max c "<[" t "]" => HasHContext.fill c t

items.name: Cslib.HasContext
items.doc:
Class for types (`α`) that have a canonical notion of homogeneous single-hole contexts
(`Context`).
items.statement: abbrev HasContext (α : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.HasContext.Context
items.statement: def HasContext.Context (α : Type*) [HasContext α] : Type*

modules.doc: Notation typeclass for α-equivalence.

items.name: Cslib.HasAlphaEquiv
items.doc: Typeclass for the α-equivalence notation `x =α y`.
items.statement:
class HasAlphaEquiv (β : Type u) where
  /-- α-equivalence relation for type β. -/
  AlphaEquiv : β → β → Prop

modules.doc: Notation typeclass for substitution.

items.name: Cslib.HasSubstitution
items.doc: Typeclass for substitution relations and access to their notation.
items.statement:
class HasSubstitution (α : Type u) (β : Type v) (γ : Type w) where
  /-- Substitution function. Replaces `x` in `t` with `t'`. -/
  subst (t : α) (x : β) (t' : γ) : α

items.name: Cslib.unexpandHasSubstitutionSubst
items.doc: Pretty-printer support for `HasSubstitution.subst`.
items.statement: meta def unexpandHasSubstitutionSubst : Lean.PrettyPrinter.Unexpander

modules.doc: Notation typeclass for well-formedness.

items.name: Cslib.HasWellFormed
items.doc: Typeclass for types equipped with a well-formedness predicate.
items.statement:
class HasWellFormed (α : Type u) where
  /-- Establishes whether `x` is well-formed. -/
  wf (x : α) : Prop

modules.title: CSLib Initialization
modules.doc:
This is the root file in CSLib: it is imported by virtually *all* CSLib files.
For this reason, the imports of this file are carefully curated.

Similar to Mathlib.Init, this file imports linters that should be active by default
throughout the CSLib library.

modules.title: Calculus of Communicating Systems (CCS)
modules.doc:
CCS [Milner80], as presented in [Sangiorgi2011]. In the semantics (see `CCS.lts`), we adopt the
option of constant definitions (K = P).

## Main definitions
- `CCS.Process`: processes.
- `CCS.Context`: contexts.

## Main results
- `CCS.Context.complete`: any process is equal to some context filled an atomic process
(nil or a constant).

## References

* [R. Milner, *A Calculus of Communicating Systems*][Milner80]
* [D. Sangiorgi, *Introduction to Bisimulation and Coinduction*][Sangiorgi2011]

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act
items.doc: Actions.
items.statement:
inductive Act (Name : Type u) : Type u where
  | name (a : Name)
  | coname (a : Name)
  | τ
deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Process
items.doc: Processes.
items.statement:
inductive Process (Name : Type u) (Constant : Type v) : Type (max u v) where
  /-- Terminated process. -/
  | nil
  /-- Do `μ` and proceed as `p`. -/
  | pre (μ : Act Name) (p : Process Name Constant)
  /-- `p` parallel `q`. -/
  | par (p q : Process Name Constant)
  /-- Do `p` or `q` (nondeterministically). -/
  | choice (p q : Process Name Constant)
  /-- Restriction. -/
  | res (a : Name) (p : Process Name Constant)
  /-- Constant. -/
  | const (c : Constant)
deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act.IsVisible
items.doc: An action is visible if it a name or a coname.
items.statement:
inductive IsVisible : Act Name → Prop where
  | name : IsVisible (Act.name a)
  | coname : IsVisible (Act.coname a)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act.isVisible_neq_τ
items.doc: If an action is visible, it is not `τ`.
items.statement: theorem isVisible_neq_τ {μ : Act Name} (h : μ.IsVisible) : μ ≠ Act.τ

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act.Co
items.doc: Checks that an action is the coaction of another.
items.statement:
inductive Co {Name : Type u} : Act Name → Act Name → Prop where
  | nc : Co (name a) (coname a)
  | cn : Co (coname a) (name a)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act.Co.symm
items.doc: `Act.Co` is symmetric.
items.statement: theorem Co.symm (h : Act.Co μ μ') : Act.Co μ' μ

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act.co_isVisible
items.doc: If two actions are one the coaction of the other, then they are both visible.
items.statement: theorem co_isVisible (h : Act.Co μ μ') : μ.IsVisible ∧ μ'.IsVisible

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act.isCo
items.doc: Checks that an action is the coaction of another. This is the Boolean version of `Act.Co`.
items.statement: def isCo [DecidableEq Name] (μ μ' : Act Name) : Bool

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Act.isCo_iff
items.statement: theorem isCo_iff [DecidableEq Name] {μ μ' : Act Name} : isCo μ μ' ↔ Co μ μ'

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Context
items.doc: Contexts.
items.statement:
inductive Context (Name : Type u) (Constant : Type v) : Type (max u v) where
  | hole
  | pre (μ : Act Name) (c : Context Name Constant)
  | parL (c : Context Name Constant) (q : Process Name Constant)
  | parR (p : Process Name Constant) (c : Context Name Constant)
  | choiceL (c : Context Name Constant) (q : Process Name Constant)
  | choiceR (p : Process Name Constant) (c : Context Name Constant)
  | res (a : Name) (c : Context Name Constant)
deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Context.fill
items.doc: Replaces the hole in a `Context` with a `Process`.
items.statement: def Context.fill (c : Context Name Constant) (p : Process Name Constant) : Process Name Constant

items.name: Cslib.CCS.context_fill_def
items.doc: Definition of context filling.
items.statement:
theorem context_fill_def (c : Context Name Constant) (p : Process Name Constant) :
  c<[p] = c.fill p

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Context.complete
items.doc:
Any `Process` can be obtained by filling a `Context` with an atom. This proves that `Context`
is a complete formalisation of syntactic contexts for CCS.
items.statement:
theorem Context.complete (p : Process Name Constant) :
    ∃ c : Context Name Constant, p = c<[(Process.nil : Process Name Constant)] ∨
    ∃ k : Constant, p = c<[(Process.const k : Process Name Constant)]

modules.title: Behavioural theory of CCS
modules.doc:
## Main results

- `CCS.bisimilarityCongruence`: bisimilarity is a congruence in CCS.

Additionally, some standard laws of bisimilarity for CCS, including:
- `CCS.bisimilarity_par_nil`: P | 𝟎 ~ P.
- `CCS.bisimilarity_par_comm`: P | Q ~ Q | P
- `CCS.bisimilarity_choice_comm`: P + Q ~ Q + P

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_par_nil
items.doc: P | 𝟎 ~ P
items.statement: theorem bisimilarity_par_nil : (par p nil) ~[lts (defs := defs)] p

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_par_comm
items.doc: P | Q ~ Q | P
items.statement: theorem bisimilarity_par_comm : (par p q) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (par q p)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_nil_par
items.doc: 𝟎 | P ~ P
items.statement: theorem bisimilarity_nil_par : (par nil p) ~[lts (defs := defs)] p

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_par_assoc
items.doc: P | (Q | R) ~ (P | Q) | R
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_par_assoc :
    (par p (par q r)) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (par (par p q) r)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_choice_nil
items.doc: P + 𝟎 ~ P
items.statement: theorem bisimilarity_choice_nil : (choice p nil) ~[lts (defs := defs)] p

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_choice_idem
items.doc: P + P ~ P
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_choice_idem :
    (choice p p) ~[lts (defs := defs)] p

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_choice_comm
items.doc: P + Q ~ Q + P
items.statement: theorem bisimilarity_choice_comm : (choice p q) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (choice q p)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_choice_assoc
items.doc: P + (Q + R) ~ (P + Q) + R
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_choice_assoc :
    (choice p (choice q r)) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (choice (choice p q) r)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_congr_pre
items.doc: P ~ Q → μ.P ~ μ.Q
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_congr_pre :
    (p ~[lts (defs := defs)] q) → (pre μ p) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (pre μ q)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_congr_res
items.doc: P ~ Q → (ν a) P ~ (ν a) Q
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_congr_res :
    (p ~[lts (defs := defs)] q) → (res a p) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (res a q)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_congr_choice
items.doc: P ~ Q → P + R ~ Q + R
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_congr_choice :
    (p ~[lts (defs := defs)] q) → (choice p r) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (choice q r)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_congr_par
items.doc: P ~ Q → P | R ~ Q | R
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_congr_par :
    (p ~[lts (defs := defs)] q) → (par p r) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (par q r)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarity_is_congruence
items.doc: Bisimilarity is a congruence in CCS.
items.statement:
theorem bisimilarity_is_congruence
    (p q : Process Name Constant) (c : Context Name Constant) (h : p ~[lts (defs := defs)] q) :
    (c.fill p) ~[lts (defs := defs)] (c.fill q)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.bisimilarityCongruence
items.doc: Bisimilarity is a congruence in CCS.
items.statement: instance bisimilarityCongruence : LawfulCongruence (HomBisimilarity (lts (defs := defs)))

modules.title: Semantics of CCS
modules.doc:
## Main definitions
- `CCS.Tr`: transition relation for CCS.
- `CCS.lts`: the `LTS` of CCS.

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Tr
items.doc:
The transition relation for CCS. This is a direct formalisation of the one found in
[Sangiorgi2011].
items.statement:
inductive Tr : Process Name Constant → Act Name → Process Name Constant → Prop where
  | pre : Tr (pre μ p) μ p
  | parL : Tr p μ p' → Tr (par p q) μ (par p' q)
  | parR : Tr q μ q' → Tr (par p q) μ (par p q')
  | com :
    μ.Co μ' → Tr p μ p' → Tr q μ' q' → Tr (par p q) Act.τ (par p' q')
  | choiceL : Tr p μ p' → Tr (choice p q) μ p'
  | choiceR : Tr q μ q' → Tr (choice p q) μ q'
  | res : μ ≠ Act.name a → μ ≠ Act.coname a → Tr p μ p' → Tr (res a p) μ (res a p')
  | const : defs k = some p → Tr p μ p' → Tr («const» k) μ p'

items.name: Cslib.CCS.Terminated
items.doc: A process is (successfully) terminated if it is a composition of `nil`s.
items.statement:
inductive Terminated : Process Name Constant → Prop where
  | nil : Terminated Process.nil
  | par : Terminated p → Terminated q → Terminated (par p q)
  | choice : Terminated p → Terminated q → Terminated (choice p q)
  | res : Terminated p → Terminated (res a p)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.not_tr_of_terminated
items.doc: A terminated process has no outgoing transitions.
items.statement: theorem not_tr_of_terminated (h : Terminated p) : ¬(lts (defs := defs)).Tr p μ p'

items.name: Cslib.CCS.pre_tr
items.doc: Inversion lemma for prefix transitions.
items.statement: theorem pre_tr (h : (lts (defs := defs)).Tr (pre μ p) μ' p') : μ = μ' ∧ p = p'

items.name: Cslib.CCS.const_tr
items.doc: Inversion lemma for constant transitions.
items.statement:
theorem const_tr (h : (lts (defs := defs)).Tr («const» k) μ p') :
    ∃ p, defs k = some p ∧ (lts (defs := defs)).Tr p μ p'

items.name: Cslib.CCS.pre_deterministicState
items.doc: Prefixes are deterministic.
items.statement: theorem pre_deterministicState : DeterministicState (lts (defs := defs)) (pre μ p)

items.name: Cslib.CCS.const_deterministicStateLabel
items.doc: Constants are deterministic if their definition is deterministic.
items.statement:
theorem const_deterministicStateLabel (hdef : defs k = some p)
    (h : DeterministicStateLabel (lts (defs := defs)) p μ) :
    DeterministicStateLabel (lts (defs := defs)) («const» k) μ

items.name: Cslib.CCS.res_deterministicStateLabel
items.doc: Restriction is deterministic if its subterm is deterministic.
items.statement:
theorem res_deterministicStateLabel
    (h : DeterministicStateLabel (lts (defs := defs)) p μ) :
    DeterministicStateLabel (lts (defs := defs)) (res μ' p) μ

modules.title: Basic results for the SKI calculus
modules.doc:
## Main definition

- `Polynomial`: the type of SKI terms with fixed number of "holes" (read: free variables).

## Notation

- `⬝'` : application between polynomials,
- `&i` : the ith free variable of a polynomial.

## Main results

- Bracket abstraction: an algorithm `Polynomial.toSKI` to convert a polynomial
$Γ(x_0, ..., x_\{n-1\})$ into a term such that (`Polynomial.toSKI_correct`)
`Γ.toSKI ⬝ t₁ ⬝ ... ⬝ tₙ` reduces to `Γ(t₁, ..., tₙ)`.

## References

For a presentation of the bracket abstraction algorithm see:
<https://web.archive.org/web/19970727171324/http://www.cs.oberlin.edu/classes/cs280/labs/lab4/lab43.html#@l13>

items.note: ### Polynomials and the bracket astraction algorithm

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Polynomial
items.doc: A polynomial is an SKI terms with free variables.
items.statement:
protected inductive Polynomial (n : Nat) : Type where
  | term : SKI → SKI.Polynomial n
  | var : Fin n → SKI.Polynomial n
  | app : SKI.Polynomial n → SKI.Polynomial n → SKI.Polynomial n

items.name: Cslib.SKI.CoeTermPolynomial
items.statement: instance CoeTermPolynomial (n : Nat) : Coe SKI (SKI.Polynomial n)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Polynomial.eval
items.doc: Substitute terms for the free variables of a polynomial
items.statement:
def Polynomial.eval {n : Nat} (Γ : SKI.Polynomial n) (l : List SKI) (hl : List.length l = n) :
    SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Polynomial.varFreeToSKI
items.doc: A polynomial with no free variables is a term
items.statement: def Polynomial.varFreeToSKI (Γ : SKI.Polynomial 0) : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Polynomial.elimVar
items.doc:
Inductively define a polynomial `Γ'` so that (up to the fact that we haven't
defined reduction on polynomials) `Γ' ⬝ t ↠ Γ[xₙ ← t]`.
items.statement: def Polynomial.elimVar {n : Nat} : SKI.Polynomial (n+1) → SKI.Polynomial n

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Polynomial.elimVar_correct
items.doc:
Correctness for the elimVar algorithm, which provides the inductive step of the bracket abstraction
algorithm. We induct backwards on the list, corresponding to applying the transformation from the
inside out. Since we haven't defined reduction for polynomials, we substitute arbitrary terms
for the inner variables.
items.statement:
theorem Polynomial.elimVar_correct {n : Nat} (Γ : SKI.Polynomial (n + 1)) {ys : List SKI}
    (hys : ys.length = n) (z : SKI) :
    (Γ.elimVar.eval ys hys ⬝ z) ↠ Γ.eval (ys ++ [z])
      (by rw [List.length_append, hys, List.length_singleton])

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Polynomial.toSKI
items.doc: Bracket abstraction, by induction using `SKI.Polynomial.elimVar`
items.statement: def Polynomial.toSKI {n : Nat} (Γ : SKI.Polynomial n) : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Polynomial.toSKI_correct
items.doc: Correctness for the toSKI (bracket abstraction) algorithm.
items.statement:
theorem Polynomial.toSKI_correct {n : Nat} (Γ : SKI.Polynomial n) (xs : List SKI)
    (hxs : xs.length = n) : Γ.toSKI.applyList xs ↠ Γ.eval xs hxs

Each combinator is defined by a polynomial, which is then proved to have the reduction property
we want. Before each definition we provide its lambda calculus equivalent. If there is accepted
notation for a given combinator, we use that (given everywhere a capital letter), otherwise we
choose a descriptive name.

modules.title: SKI-computable functions
modules.doc:
This file defines the notion of SKI-computability for partial functions on natural
numbers, via Church numerals: a term computes `f : ℕ →. ℕ` if it maps Church numeral
inputs to Church numeral outputs wherever `f` is defined.

## Main definitions

- `SKI.Computes`: an SKI term computes a given partial function.
- `SKI.Computable`: a partial function is SKI-computable if some SKI term computes it.

## Implementation notes

Unlike `Cslib.URM.Computes`, which is a two-sided equality of `Part` values, this
predicate is one-sided: it constrains the term's behavior only where the function is
defined, and says nothing about inputs outside the domain.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Computes
items.doc:
An SKI term `t` computes a partial function `f : ℕ →. ℕ` if,
for every Church numeral input, `t` applied to the input is a Church numeral
for the output whenever `f` is defined.
items.statement: def Computes (t : SKI) (f : ℕ →. ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Computable
items.doc:
A partial function `f : ℕ →. ℕ` is SKI-computable if there exists an SKI term that
computes it.
items.statement: def Computable (f : ℕ →. ℕ) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.SKI.computes_of_total
items.doc:
To show that a term computes a total function, it suffices to produce a Church
numeral for the output on every input.
items.statement:
theorem computes_of_total {t : SKI} {f : ℕ →. ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℕ)
    (heval : ∀ n, f n = Part.some (g n))
    (hcorrect : ∀ n cn, IsChurch n cn → IsChurch (g n) (t ⬝ cn)) :
    Computes t f

items.name: Cslib.SKI.comp_computes
items.doc: Composition of computable functions is computable.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.pair_computes
items.doc: Pairing of computable functions is computable.
items.statement:
theorem pair_computes {f g : ℕ →. ℕ} {tf tg : SKI}
    (hf : Computes tf f) (hg : Computes tg g) :
    Computes (S ⬝ (B ⬝ NatPair ⬝ tf) ⬝ tg)
      (fun n => Nat.pair <$> f n <*> g n)

modules.title: SKI reduction is confluent
modules.doc:
This file proves the **Church-Rosser** theorem for the SKI calculus, that is, if `a ↠ b` and
`a ↠ c`, `b ↠ d` and `c ↠ d` for some term `d`. More strongly (though equivalently), we show
that the relation of having a common reduct is transitive — in the above situation, `a` and `b`,
and `a` and `c` have common reducts, so the result implies the same of `b` and `c`. Note that
`Join (ReflTransGen Red)` is symmetric (trivially) and reflexive (since `↠` is), so we in fact show
that `Join (ReflTransGen Red)` is an equivalence.

Our proof
follows the method of Tait and Martin-Löf for the lambda calculus, as presented for instance in
Chapter 4 of Peter Selinger's notes:
<https://www.mscs.dal.ca/~selinger/papers/papers/lambdanotes.pdf>.

## Main definitions

- `ParallelReduction` : a relation `⭢ₚ` on terms such that `⭢ ⊆ ⭢ₚ ⊆ ↠`, allowing simultaneous
reduction on the head and tail of a term.

## Main results

- `parallelReduction_diamond` : parallel reduction satisfies the diamond property, that is, it is
confluent in a single step.
- `join_mRed_equivalence` : by a general result, the diamond property for `⭢ₚ` implies the same
for its reflexive-transitive closure. This closure is exactly `↠`, which implies the
**Church-Rosser** theorem as sketched above.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.ParallelReduction
items.doc: A reduction step allowing simultaneous reduction of disjoint redexes
items.statement:
inductive ParallelReduction : SKI → SKI → Prop
  /-- Parallel reduction is reflexive, -/
  | refl (a : SKI) : ParallelReduction a a
  /-- Contains `Red`, -/
  | red_I (a : SKI) : ParallelReduction (I ⬝ a) a
  | red_K (a b : SKI) : ParallelReduction (K ⬝ a ⬝ b) a
  | red_S (a b c : SKI) : ParallelReduction (S ⬝ a ⬝ b ⬝ c) (a ⬝ c ⬝ (b ⬝ c))
  /-- and allows simultaneous reduction of disjoint redexes. -/
  | par ⦃a a' b b' : SKI⦄ :
      ParallelReduction a a' → ParallelReduction b b' → ParallelReduction (a ⬝ b) (a' ⬝ b')

items.name: Cslib.SKI.ParallelReduction.le_reflTransGen_red
items.doc: The inclusion `(· ⭢ₚ ·) ≤ (· ↠ ·)`.
items.statement:
theorem ParallelReduction.le_reflTransGen_red :
    (· ⭢ₚ ·) ≤ (· ↠ ·)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Red.le_parallelReduction
items.doc: The inclusion `(· ⭢ ·) ≤ (· ⭢ₚ ·)`.
items.statement:
theorem Red.le_parallelReduction :
    (· ⭢ ·) ≤ (· ⭢ₚ ·)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.reflTransGen_parallelReduction_mRed
items.doc: The relations `⭢` and `⭢ₚ` have the same reflexive-transitive closure.
items.statement:
theorem reflTransGen_parallelReduction_mRed :
    ReflTransGen ParallelReduction = ReflTransGen Red

items.name: Cslib.SKI.parallelReduction_diamond
items.doc:
The key result: the Church-Rosser property holds for `⭢ₚ`. The proof is a lengthy case analysis
on the reductions `a ⭢ₚ a₁` and `a ⭢ₚ a₂`, but is entirely mechanical.
items.statement: theorem parallelReduction_diamond : Diamond ParallelReduction

    Equivalence (Join (ReflTransGen ParallelReduction))

modules.title: SKI Combinatory Logic
modules.doc:
This file defines the syntax and operational semantics (reduction rules) of combinatory logic,
using the SKI basis.

## Main definitions

- `SKI`: the type of expressions in the SKI calculus,
- `Red`: single-step reduction of SKI expressions,
- `MRed`: multi-step reduction of SKI expressions.

## Notation

- `⬝` : application between SKI terms,
- `⭢` : single-step reduction,
- `↠` : multi-step reduction,

## References

The setup of SKI combinatory logic is standard, see for example:
- <https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/SKI_combinator_calculus>
- <https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combinatory_logic>

items.name: Cslib.SKI
items.doc: An SKI expression is built from the primitive combinators `S`, `K` and `I`, and application.
items.statement:
inductive SKI where
  /-- `S`-combinator, with semantics $λxyz.xz(yz)$ -/
  | S
  /-- `K`-combinator, with semantics $λxy.x$ -/
  | K
  /-- `I`-combinator, with semantics $λx.x$ -/
  | I
  /-- Application $x y ↦ xy$ -/
  | app : SKI → SKI → SKI
deriving Repr, DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.SKI.applyList
items.doc: Apply a term to a list of terms
items.statement: def applyList (f : SKI) (xs : List SKI) : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.applyList_concat
items.statement:
lemma applyList_concat (f : SKI) (ys : List SKI) (z : SKI) :
    f.applyList (ys ++ [z]) = f.applyList ys ⬝ z

items.name: Cslib.SKI.size
items.doc: The size of an SKI term is its number of combinators.
items.statement: def size : SKI → Nat

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Red
items.doc: Single-step reduction of SKI terms
items.statement:
inductive Red : SKI → SKI → Prop where
  /-- The operational semantics of the `S`, -/
  | red_S (x y z : SKI) : Red (S ⬝ x ⬝ y ⬝ z) (x ⬝ z ⬝ (y ⬝ z))
  /-- `K`, -/
  | red_K (x y : SKI) : Red (K ⬝ x ⬝ y) x
  /-- and `I` combinators. -/
  | red_I (x : SKI) : Red (I ⬝ x) x
  /-- Reduction on the head -/
  | red_head (x x' y : SKI) (_ : Red x x') : Red (x ⬝ y) (x' ⬝ y)
  /-- and tail of an SKI term. -/
  | red_tail (x y y' : SKI) (_ : Red y y') : Red (x ⬝ y) (x ⬝ y')

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Red.ne
items.statement: lemma Red.ne {x y : SKI} : (x ⭢ y) → x ≠ y

items.name: Cslib.SKI.MRed.S
items.statement: theorem MRed.S (x y z : SKI) : (S ⬝ x ⬝ y ⬝ z) ↠ (x ⬝ z ⬝ (y ⬝ z))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.MRed.K
items.statement: theorem MRed.K (x y : SKI) : (K ⬝ x ⬝ y) ↠ x

items.name: Cslib.SKI.MRed.I
items.statement: theorem MRed.I (x : SKI) : (I ⬝ x) ↠ x

items.name: Cslib.SKI.MRed.head
items.statement: theorem MRed.head {a a' : SKI} (b : SKI) (h : a ↠ a') : (a ⬝ b) ↠ (a' ⬝ b)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.MRed.tail
items.statement: theorem MRed.tail (a : SKI) {b b' : SKI} (h : b ↠ b') : (a ⬝ b) ↠ (a ⬝ b')

items.name: Cslib.SKI.parallel_mRed
items.statement:
lemma parallel_mRed {a a' b b' : SKI} (ha : a ↠ a') (hb : b ↠ b') :
    (a ⬝ b) ↠ (a' ⬝ b')

items.name: Cslib.SKI.parallel_red
items.statement: lemma parallel_red {a a' b b' : SKI} (ha : a ⭢ a') (hb : b ⭢ b') : (a ⬝ b) ↠ (a' ⬝ b')

items.name: Cslib.SKI.join_mRed_head
items.statement:
theorem join_mRed_head {x x' : SKI} (y : SKI) :
    Join (ReflTransGen Red) x x' → Join (ReflTransGen Red) (x ⬝ y) (x' ⬝ y)

items.statement: alias mJoin_red_head

    Join (ReflTransGen Red) y y' → Join (ReflTransGen Red) (x ⬝ y) (x ⬝ y')

modules.title: Evaluation results
modules.doc:
This file formalises evaluation and normal forms of SKI terms.

## Main definitions

- `RedexFree` : a predicate expressing that a term has no redexes
- `evalStep` : SKI-reduction as a function

## Main results

- `evalStep_right_correct` : correctness for `evalStep`
- `redexFree_iff` and `redexFree_iff_mred_eq` : a term is redex free if and only if it has
(respectively) no one-step reductions, or if its only many step reduction is itself.
- `unique_normal_form` : if `x` reduces to both `y` and `z`, and both `y` and `z` are in normal
form, then they are equal.
- **Rice's theorem**: no SKI term is a non-trivial predicate.

## References

This file draws heavily from <https://gist.github.com/b-mehta/e412c837818223b8f16ca0b4aa19b166>.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RedexFree
items.doc: The predicate that a term has no reducible sub-terms.
items.statement: def RedexFree : SKI → Prop

items.name: Cslib.SKI.evalStep
items.doc:
One-step evaluation as a function: either it returns a term that has been reduced by one step,
or a proof that the term is redex free. Uses normal-order reduction.
items.statement: def evalStep : (x : SKI) → PLift (x.RedexFree) ⊕ SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.evalStep_right_correct
items.doc: The normal-order reduction implemented by `evalStep` indeed computes a one-step reduction.
items.statement: theorem evalStep_right_correct : (x y : SKI) → (x.evalStep = Sum.inr y) → x ⭢ y

items.name: Cslib.SKI.redexFree_of_normal_red
items.statement: theorem redexFree_of_normal_red {x : SKI} (h : Normal Red x) : x.RedexFree

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RedexFree.normal_red
items.statement: theorem RedexFree.normal_red {x : SKI} (hx : x.RedexFree) : Normal Red x

items.name: Cslib.SKI.redexFree_iff
items.doc: A term is redex free iff it has no one-step reductions.
items.statement: theorem redexFree_iff {x : SKI} : x.RedexFree ↔ Normal Red x

items.name: Cslib.SKI.redexFree_iff_evalStep
items.statement: theorem redexFree_iff_evalStep {x : SKI} : x.RedexFree ↔ (x.evalStep).isLeft = true

items.name: Cslib.SKI.redexFree_iff_mred_eq
items.doc: A term is redex free iff its only many-step reduction is itself.
items.statement: theorem redexFree_iff_mred_eq {x : SKI} : x.RedexFree ↔ ∀ y, (x ↠ y) ↔ x = y

items.name: Cslib.SKI.join_mRed_redexFree
items.doc: If a term has a common reduct with a normal term, it in fact reduces to that term.
items.statement:
theorem join_mRed_redexFree {x y : SKI} (hy : y.RedexFree) (h : Join (ReflTransGen Red) x y) :
    x ↠ y

items.name: Cslib.SKI.mJoin_red_redexFree
items.statement: alias mJoin_red_redexFree

items.name: Cslib.SKI.confluent_redexFree
items.doc: If `x` reduces to both `y` and `z`, and `z` is not reducible, then `y` reduces to `z`.
items.statement: lemma confluent_redexFree {x y z : SKI} (hxy : x ↠ y) (hxz : x ↠ z) (hz : RedexFree z) : y ↠ z

items.name: Cslib.SKI.unique_normal_form
items.doc: If `x` reduces to both `y` and `z`, and both `y` and `z` are in normal form, then they are equal.
items.statement:
lemma unique_normal_form {x y z : SKI}
    (hxy : x ↠ y) (hxz : x ↠ z) (hy : y.RedexFree) (hz : RedexFree z) : y = z

items.name: Cslib.SKI.eq_of_join_mRed_redexFree
items.doc: If `x` and `y` are normal and have a common reduct, then they are equal.
items.statement:
lemma eq_of_join_mRed_redexFree {x y : SKI} (h : Join (ReflTransGen Red) x y)
    (hx : x.RedexFree) (hy : y.RedexFree) : x = y

items.name: Cslib.SKI.eq_of_mJoin_red_redexFree
items.statement: alias eq_of_mJoin_red_redexFree

items.name: Cslib.SKI.sk_nequiv
items.statement: lemma sk_nequiv : ¬ Join (ReflTransGen Red) S K

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isBool_injective
items.doc: Injectivity for booleans.
items.statement:
theorem isBool_injective (x y : SKI) (u v : Bool) (hx : IsBool u x) (hy : IsBool v y)
    (hxy : Join (ReflTransGen Red) x y) : u = v

items.name: Cslib.SKI.TF_nequiv
items.statement: lemma TF_nequiv : ¬ Join (ReflTransGen Red) TT FF

items.name: Cslib.SKI.churchK
items.doc: A specialisation of `Church : Nat → SKI`.
items.statement: def churchK : Nat → SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.churchK_church
items.statement: lemma churchK_church : (n : Nat) → churchK n = Church n K K

items.name: Cslib.SKI.churchK_redexFree
items.statement: lemma churchK_redexFree : (n : Nat) → RedexFree (churchK n)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.churchK_size
items.statement: lemma churchK_size : (n : Nat) → (churchK n).size = n+1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.churchK_injective
items.statement: lemma churchK_injective : Function.Injective churchK

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isChurch_injective
items.doc: Injectivity for Church numerals
items.statement:
theorem isChurch_injective (x y : SKI) (n m : Nat) (hx : IsChurch n x) (hy : IsChurch m y)
    (hxy : Join (ReflTransGen Red) x y) : n = m

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rice
items.doc:
**Rice's theorem**: no SKI term is a non-trivial predicate.

More specifically, say a term `P` is a *predicate* if, for every term `x`, `P · x` reduces to either
`TT` or `FF`. A predicate `P` is *trivial* if either it always reduces to true, or always to false.
This version of Rice's theorem derives a contradiction from the existence of a predicate `P` and the
existence of terms `x` for which `P · x` is true (`P · x ↠ TT`) and for which `P · x` is false
(`P · x ↠ FF`).
items.statement:
theorem rice {P : SKI} (hP : ∀ x : SKI, ((P ⬝ x) ↠ TT) ∨ (P ⬝ x) ↠ FF)
    (hxt : ∃ x : SKI, (P ⬝ x) ↠ TT) (hxf : ∃ x : SKI, (P ⬝ x) ↠ FF) : False

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rice'
items.doc:
**Rice's theorem**: any SKI predicate is trivial.

This version of Rice's theorem proves (classically) that any SKI predicate `P` either is constantly
true (ie `P · x ↠ TT` for every `x`) or is constantly false (`P · x ↠ FF` for every `x`).
items.statement:
theorem rice' {P : SKI} (hP : ∀ x : SKI, ((P ⬝ x) ↠ TT) ∨ (P ⬝ x) ↠ FF) :
    (∀ x : SKI, (P ⬝ x) ↠ TT) ∨ (∀ x : SKI, (P ⬝ x) ↠ FF)

modules.title: Church-Encoded Lists in SKI Combinatory Logic
modules.doc:
Church-encoded lists for proving SKI ≃ TM equivalence. A list is encoded as
`λ c n. c a₀ (c a₁ (... (c aₖ n)...))` where each `aᵢ` is a Church numeral.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.IsChurchList
items.doc: A term correctly Church-encodes a list of natural numbers.
items.statement: def IsChurchList : List ℕ → SKI → Prop

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isChurchList_trans
items.doc: `IsChurchList` is preserved under multi-step reduction of the term.
items.statement:
theorem isChurchList_trans {ns : List ℕ} {cns cns' : SKI} (h : cns ↠ cns')
    (hcns' : IsChurchList ns cns') : IsChurchList ns cns

items.name: Cslib.SKI.IsChurchListPair
items.doc: Both components of a pair are Church lists.
items.statement:
structure IsChurchListPair (prev curr : List ℕ) (p : SKI) : Prop where
  fst : IsChurchList prev (Fst ⬝ p)
  snd : IsChurchList curr (Snd ⬝ p)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isChurchListPair_trans
items.doc: IsChurchListPair is preserved under reduction.
items.statement:
theorem isChurchListPair_trans {prev curr : List ℕ} {p p' : SKI} (hp : p ↠ p')
    (hp' : IsChurchListPair prev curr p') : IsChurchListPair prev curr p

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.NilPoly
items.doc: nil = λ c n. n
items.statement: def NilPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.Nil
items.doc: The SKI term for the empty list.
items.statement: def Nil : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.nil_def
items.doc: Reduction: `Nil ⬝ c ⬝ n ↠ n`.
items.statement: theorem nil_def (c n : SKI) : (Nil ⬝ c ⬝ n) ↠ n

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.nil_correct
items.doc: The empty list term correctly represents `[]`.
items.statement: theorem nil_correct : IsChurchList [] Nil

items.note: ### Cons: Consing an element onto a list

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.ConsPoly
items.doc: cons = λ x xs c n. c x (xs c n)
items.statement: def ConsPoly : SKI.Polynomial 4

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.Cons
items.doc: The SKI term for list cons.
items.statement: def Cons : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.cons_def
items.doc: Reduction: `Cons ⬝ x ⬝ xs ⬝ c ⬝ n ↠ c ⬝ x ⬝ (xs ⬝ c ⬝ n)`.
items.statement:
theorem cons_def (x xs c n : SKI) :
    (Cons ⬝ x ⬝ xs ⬝ c ⬝ n) ↠ c ⬝ x ⬝ (xs ⬝ c ⬝ n)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.cons_correct
items.doc: Cons preserves Church list representation.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.singleton_correct
items.doc: Singleton list correctness.
items.statement:
theorem singleton_correct {x : ℕ} {cx : SKI} (hcx : IsChurch x cx) :
    IsChurchList [x] (Cons ⬝ cx ⬝ Nil)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.toChurch
items.doc: The canonical SKI term for a Church-encoded list.
items.statement: def toChurch : List ℕ → SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.toChurch_nil
items.doc: `toChurch [] = Nil`.
items.statement: lemma toChurch_nil : toChurch [] = Nil

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.toChurch_cons
items.doc: `toChurch (x :: xs) = Cons ⬝ SKI.toChurch x ⬝ toChurch xs`.
items.statement:
lemma toChurch_cons (x : ℕ) (xs : List ℕ) :
    toChurch (x :: xs) = Cons ⬝ (SKI.toChurch x) ⬝ (toChurch xs)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.toChurch_correct
items.doc: `toChurch ns` correctly represents `ns`.
items.statement: theorem toChurch_correct (ns : List ℕ) : IsChurchList ns (toChurch ns)

items.note: ### Head: Extract the head of a list

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.HeadDPoly
items.doc: headD d xs = xs K d (returns d for empty list)
items.statement: def HeadDPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.HeadD
items.doc: The SKI term for list head with default.
items.statement: def HeadD : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.headD_def
items.doc: Reduction: `HeadD ⬝ d ⬝ xs ↠ xs ⬝ K ⬝ d`.
items.statement: theorem headD_def (d xs : SKI) : (HeadD ⬝ d ⬝ xs) ↠ xs ⬝ K ⬝ d

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.headD_correct
items.doc: General head-with-default correctness.
items.statement:
theorem headD_correct {d : ℕ} {cd : SKI} (hcd : IsChurch d cd)
    {ns : List ℕ} {cns : SKI} (hcns : IsChurchList ns cns) :
    IsChurch (ns.headD d) (HeadD ⬝ cd ⬝ cns)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.Head
items.doc: The SKI term for list head (default 0).
items.statement: def Head : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.head_def
items.doc: Reduction: `Head ⬝ xs ↠ xs ⬝ K ⬝ Zero`.
items.statement: theorem head_def (xs : SKI) : (Head ⬝ xs) ↠ xs ⬝ K ⬝ SKI.Zero

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.head_correct
items.doc: Head correctness (default 0).
items.statement:
theorem head_correct (ns : List ℕ) (cns : SKI) (hcns : IsChurchList ns cns) :
    IsChurch (ns.headD 0) (Head ⬝ cns)

items.note: ### Tail: Extract the tail of a list

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.TailStepPoly
items.doc: Step function for tail: (prev, curr) → (curr, cons h curr)
items.statement: def TailStepPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.TailStep
items.doc: The step function for computing list tail.
items.statement: def TailStep : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.tailStep_def
items.doc: Reduction of the tail step function.
items.statement:
theorem tailStep_def (h p : SKI) :
    (TailStep ⬝ h ⬝ p) ↠ MkPair ⬝ (Snd ⬝ p) ⬝ (Cons ⬝ h ⬝ (Snd ⬝ p))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.TailPoly
items.doc: tail xs = Fst (xs TailStep (MkPair Nil Nil))
items.statement: def TailPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.Tail
items.doc: The tail of a Church-encoded list.
items.statement: def Tail : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.tail_def
items.doc: Reduction: `Tail ⬝ xs ↠ Fst ⬝ (xs ⬝ TailStep ⬝ (MkPair ⬝ Nil ⬝ Nil))`.
items.statement:
theorem tail_def (xs : SKI) :
    (Tail ⬝ xs) ↠ Fst ⬝ (xs ⬝ TailStep ⬝ (MkPair ⬝ Nil ⬝ Nil))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.tail_init
items.doc: The initial pair (nil, nil) satisfies the invariant.
items.statement: theorem tail_init : IsChurchListPair [] [] (MkPair ⬝ Nil ⬝ Nil)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.tailStep_correct
items.doc: The step function preserves the tail-computing invariant.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.tailFold_correct
items.statement:
theorem tailFold_correct (ns : List ℕ) (cns : SKI) (hcns : IsChurchList ns cns) :
    ∃ p, (cns ⬝ TailStep ⬝ (MkPair ⬝ Nil ⬝ Nil)) ↠ p ∧
         IsChurchListPair ns.tail ns p

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.tail_correct
items.doc: Tail correctness.
items.statement:
theorem tail_correct (ns : List ℕ) (cns : SKI) (hcns : IsChurchList ns cns) :
    IsChurchList ns.tail (Tail ⬝ cns)

items.note: ### Prepending zero to a list (for Code.zero')

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.PrependZeroPoly
items.doc: PrependZero xs = cons 0 xs = Cons ⬝ Zero ⬝ xs
items.statement: def PrependZeroPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.PrependZero
items.doc: Prepend zero to a Church-encoded list.
items.statement: def PrependZero : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.prependZero_def
items.doc: Reduction: `PrependZero ⬝ xs ↠ Cons ⬝ Zero ⬝ xs`.
items.statement: theorem prependZero_def (xs : SKI) : (PrependZero ⬝ xs) ↠ Cons ⬝ SKI.Zero ⬝ xs

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.prependZero_correct
items.doc: Prepending zero preserves Church list representation.
items.statement:
theorem prependZero_correct {ns : List ℕ} {cns : SKI} (hcns : IsChurchList ns cns) :
    IsChurchList (0 :: ns) (PrependZero ⬝ cns)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.SuccHead
items.doc: SuccHead xs = cons (succ (head xs)) nil
items.statement: def SuccHead : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.List.succHead_correct
items.doc: `SuccHead` correctly computes a singleton containing `succ(head ns)`.
items.statement:
theorem succHead_correct (ns : List ℕ) (cns : SKI) (hcns : IsChurchList ns cns) :
    IsChurchList [ns.headD 0 + 1] (SuccHead ⬝ cns)

modules.title: Partial Recursive → SKI-computable (Nat.Partrec)
modules.doc:
This file translates `Nat.Partrec.Code` to SKI terms and proves the translation
correct, showing that every partial recursive function is SKI-computable in the
sense of `SKI.Computes` (from `Cslib.Languages.CombinatoryLogic.Computable`).

## Main definitions

- `Nat.Partrec.Code.toSKI`: translates `Nat.Partrec.Code` constructors to SKI terms.

## Main results

- `Nat.Partrec.Code.toSKI_correct`: each translated code computes the corresponding `Code.eval`.
- `natPartrec_skiComputable`: every `Nat.Partrec` function is SKI-computable.

items.name: Cslib.SKI.PrecStepPoly
items.doc:
Step function for primitive recursion:
`λ a cn prev. tg ⬝ (NatPair ⬝ a ⬝ (NatPair ⬝ (Pred ⬝ cn) ⬝ prev))`
Variables: &0 = a, &1 = cn, &2 = prev
items.statement: def PrecStepPoly (tg : SKI) : SKI.Polynomial 3

items.name: Cslib.SKI.PrecStep
items.doc: SKI term for the primitive recursion step function.
items.statement: def PrecStep (tg : SKI) : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.precStep_def
items.statement:
theorem precStep_def (tg a cn prev : SKI) :
    (PrecStep tg ⬝ a ⬝ cn ⬝ prev) ↠
      tg ⬝ (NatPair ⬝ a ⬝ (NatPair ⬝ (Pred ⬝ cn) ⬝ prev))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.PrecTransPoly
items.doc:
Full primitive recursion translation:
`λ n. Rec (tf (left n)) (PrecStep tg (left n)) (right n)`
items.statement: def PrecTransPoly (tf tg : SKI) : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.PrecTrans
items.doc: SKI term for primitive recursion via `Rec` with pair/unpair plumbing.
items.statement: def PrecTrans (tf tg : SKI) : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.precTrans_def
items.statement:
theorem precTrans_def (tf tg cn : SKI) :
    (PrecTrans tf tg ⬝ cn) ↠
      Rec ⬝ (tf ⬝ (NatUnpairLeft ⬝ cn))
          ⬝ (PrecStep tg ⬝ (NatUnpairLeft ⬝ cn))
          ⬝ (NatUnpairRight ⬝ cn)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindTransPoly
items.doc:
Unbounded search translation:
`λ n. RFindAbove ⬝ (NatUnpairRight ⬝ n) ⬝ (B ⬝ tf ⬝ (NatPair ⬝ (NatUnpairLeft ⬝ n)))`
items.statement: def RFindTransPoly (tf : SKI) : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindTrans
items.doc: SKI term for unbounded search (μ-recursion).
items.statement: def RFindTrans (tf : SKI) : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rfindTrans_def
items.statement:
theorem rfindTrans_def (tf cn : SKI) :
    (RFindTrans tf ⬝ cn) ↠
      RFindAbove ⬝ (NatUnpairRight ⬝ cn)
                 ⬝ (B ⬝ tf ⬝ (NatPair ⬝ (NatUnpairLeft ⬝ cn)))

items.name: Nat.Partrec.Code.toSKI
items.doc: Translate `Nat.Partrec.Code` to SKI terms operating on Church numerals.
items.statement: def _root_.Nat.Partrec.Code.toSKI : Code → SKI

items.name: Nat.Partrec.Code.toSKI_correct
items.doc: Main correctness theorem: `Code.toSKI` correctly computes `Code.eval`.
items.statement: theorem _root_.Nat.Partrec.Code.toSKI_correct (c : Code) : Computes c.toSKI c.eval

items.name: Cslib.SKI.natPartrec_skiComputable
items.doc: Every partial recursive function on `ℕ` is SKI-computable.
items.statement:
theorem natPartrec_skiComputable (f : ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : Nat.Partrec f) :
    SKI.Computable f

modules.title: General recursion in the SKI calculus
modules.doc:
In this file we implement general recursion functions (on the natural numbers), inspired by the
formalisation of `Mathlib.Computability.Partrec`. Since composition (`B`-combinator) and pairs
(`MkPair`, `Fst`, `Snd`) have been implemented in `Cslib.Computability.CombinatoryLogic.Basic`,
what remains are the following definitions and proofs of their correctness.

- Church numerals : a predicate `IsChurch n a` expressing that the term `a` is βη-equivalent to
the standard church numeral `n` — that is, `a ⬝ f ⬝ x ↠ f ⬝ (f ⬝ ... ⬝ (f ⬝ x)))`.
- SKI numerals : `Zero` and `Succ`, corresponding to `Partrec.zero` and `Partrec.succ`, and
correctness proofs `zero_correct` and `succ_correct`.
- Predecessor : a term `Pred` so that (`pred_correct`)
`IsChurch n a → IsChurch n.pred (Pred ⬝ a)`.
- Primitive recursion : a term `Rec` so that (`rec_correct_succ`) `IsChurch (n+1) a` implies
`Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ a ↠ g ⬝ a ⬝ (Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ (Pred ⬝ a))` and (`rec_correct_zero`) `IsChurch 0 a`
implies `Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ a ↠ x`.
- Unbounded root finding (μ-recursion) : given a term  `f` representing a function `fℕ: Nat → Nat`,
which takes on the value 0 a term `RFind` such that (`rFind_correct`) `RFind ⬝ f ↠ a` such that
`IsChurch n a` for `n` the smallest root of `fℕ`.
- Integer square root : a term `Sqrt` so that (`sqrt_correct`)
`IsChurch n a → IsChurch n.sqrt (Sqrt ⬝ a)`.
- Nat pairing : a term `NatPair` so that (`natPair_correct`)
`IsChurch a x → IsChurch b y → IsChurch (Nat.pair a b) (NatPair ⬝ x ⬝ y)`.
- Nat unpairing : terms `NatUnpairLeft` and `NatUnpairRight` so that (`natUnpairLeft_correct`)
`IsChurch n a → IsChurch n.unpair.1 (NatUnpairLeft ⬝ a)` and (`natUnpairRight_correct`)
`IsChurch n a → IsChurch n.unpair.2 (NatUnpairRight ⬝ a)`.

## References

- For church numerals and recursion via the fixed-point combinator, see sections 3.2 and 3.3 of
Selinger's notes <https://www.mscs.dal.ca/~selinger/papers/papers/lambdanotes.pdf>

…

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Church
items.doc: Function form of the church numerals.
items.statement: def Church (n : Nat) (f x : SKI) : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Church_zero
items.statement: lemma Church_zero (f x : SKI) : Church 0 f x = x

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Church_succ
items.statement: lemma Church_succ (n : Nat) (f x : SKI) : Church (n+1) f x = f ⬝ Church n f x

items.name: Cslib.SKI.church_red
items.doc: `church` commutes with reduction.
items.statement:
lemma church_red (n : Nat) (f f' x x' : SKI) (hf : f ↠ f') (hx : x ↠ x') :
    Church n f x ↠ Church n f' x'

items.name: Cslib.SKI.IsChurch
items.doc: The term `a` is βη-equivalent to a standard church numeral.
items.statement: def IsChurch (n : Nat) (a : SKI) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isChurch_trans
items.doc: To show `IsChurch n a` it suffices to show the same for a reduct of `a`.
items.statement:
theorem isChurch_trans (n : Nat) {a a' : SKI} (h : a ↠ a') :
    IsChurch n a' → IsChurch n a

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Zero
items.doc: Church zero := λ f x. x
items.statement: protected def Zero : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.zero_correct
items.statement: theorem zero_correct : IsChurch 0 SKI.Zero

items.name: Cslib.SKI.One
items.doc: Church one := λ f x. f x
items.statement: protected def One : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.one_correct
items.statement: theorem one_correct : IsChurch 1 SKI.One

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Succ
items.doc: Church succ := λ a f x. f (a f x) ~ λ a f. B f (a f) ~ λ a. S B a ~ S B
items.statement: protected def Succ : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.succ_correct
items.statement:
theorem succ_correct (n : Nat) (a : SKI) (h : IsChurch n a) :
    IsChurch (n+1) (SKI.Succ ⬝ a)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.toChurch
items.doc: Build the canonical SKI Church numeral for `n`.
items.statement: def toChurch : ℕ → SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.toChurch_zero
items.doc: `toChurch 0 = Zero`.
items.statement: lemma toChurch_zero : toChurch 0 = SKI.Zero

items.name: Cslib.SKI.toChurch_succ
items.doc: `toChurch (n + 1) = Succ ⬝ toChurch n`.
items.statement: lemma toChurch_succ (n : ℕ) : toChurch (n + 1) = SKI.Succ ⬝ (toChurch n)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.toChurch_correct
items.doc: `toChurch n` correctly represents `n`.
items.statement: theorem toChurch_correct (n : ℕ) : IsChurch n (toChurch n)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.PredAuxPoly
items.doc:
To define the predecessor, iterate the function `PredAux` ⟨i, j⟩ ↦ ⟨j, j+1⟩ on ⟨0,0⟩, then take
the  first component.
items.statement: def PredAuxPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.PredAux
items.doc: A term representing PredAux
items.statement: def PredAux : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.predAux_def
items.statement: theorem predAux_def (p : SKI) :  (PredAux ⬝ p) ↠ MkPair ⬝ (Snd ⬝ p) ⬝ (SKI.Succ ⬝ (Snd ⬝ p))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.IsChurchPair
items.doc: Useful auxiliary definition expressing that `p` represents ns ∈ Nat × Nat.
items.statement: def IsChurchPair (ns : Nat × Nat) (x : SKI) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isChurchPair_trans
items.statement:
theorem isChurchPair_trans (ns : Nat × Nat) (a a' : SKI) (h : a ↠ a') :
    IsChurchPair ns a' → IsChurchPair ns a

items.name: Cslib.SKI.predAux_correct
items.statement:
theorem predAux_correct (p : SKI) (ns : Nat × Nat) (h : IsChurchPair ns p) :
    IsChurchPair ⟨ns.2, ns.2+1⟩ (PredAux ⬝ p)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.predAux_correct'
items.doc: The stronger induction hypothesis necessary for the proof of `pred_correct`.
items.statement:
theorem predAux_correct' (n : Nat) :
    IsChurchPair (n.pred, n) <| Church n PredAux  (MkPair ⬝ SKI.Zero ⬝ SKI.Zero)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.PredPoly
items.doc: Predecessor := λ n. Fst ⬝ (n ⬝ PredAux ⬝ (MkPair ⬝ Zero ⬝ Zero))
items.statement: def PredPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Pred
items.doc: A term representing Pred
items.statement: def Pred : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.pred_def
items.statement: theorem pred_def (a : SKI) : (Pred ⬝ a) ↠ Fst ⬝ (a ⬝ PredAux ⬝ (MkPair ⬝ SKI.Zero ⬝ SKI.Zero))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.pred_correct
items.statement: theorem pred_correct (n : Nat) (a : SKI) (h : IsChurch n a) : IsChurch n.pred (Pred ⬝ a)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.IsZeroPoly
items.doc: IsZero := λ n. n (K FF) TT
items.statement: def IsZeroPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.IsZero
items.doc: A term representing IsZero
items.statement: def IsZero : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isZero_def
items.statement: theorem isZero_def (a : SKI) : (IsZero ⬝ a) ↠ a ⬝ (K ⬝ FF) ⬝ TT

items.name: Cslib.SKI.isZero_correct
items.statement:
theorem isZero_correct (n : Nat) (a : SKI) (h : IsChurch n a) :
    IsBool (n = 0) (IsZero ⬝ a)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RecAuxPoly
items.doc:
To define `Rec x g n := if n==0 then x else (Rec x g (Pred n))`, we obtain a fixed point of
R ↦ λ x g n. Cond ⬝ (IsZero ⬝ n) ⬝ x ⬝ (g ⬝ a ⬝ (R ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ (Pred ⬝ n)))
items.statement: def RecAuxPoly : SKI.Polynomial 4

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RecAux
items.doc: A term representing RecAux
items.statement: def RecAux : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.recAux_def
items.statement:
theorem recAux_def (R₀ x g a : SKI) :
    (RecAux ⬝ R₀ ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ a) ↠
      SKI.Cond ⬝ x ⬝ (g ⬝ a ⬝ (R₀ ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ (Pred ⬝ a))) ⬝ (IsZero ⬝ a)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Rec
items.doc:
We define Rec so that
`Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ a ↠ SKI.Cond ⬝ x ⬝ (g ⬝ a ⬝ (Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ (Pred ⬝ a))) ⬝ (IsZero ⬝ a)`
items.statement: def Rec : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rec_def
items.statement:
theorem rec_def (x g a : SKI) :
    (Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ a) ↠ SKI.Cond ⬝ x ⬝ (g ⬝ a ⬝ (Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ (Pred ⬝ a))) ⬝ (IsZero ⬝ a)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rec_zero
items.statement: theorem rec_zero (x g a : SKI) (ha : IsChurch 0 a) : (Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ a) ↠ x

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rec_succ
items.statement:
theorem rec_succ (n : Nat) (x g a : SKI) (ha : IsChurch (n + 1) a) :
    (Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ a) ↠ g ⬝ a ⬝ (Rec ⬝ x ⬝ g ⬝ (Pred ⬝ a))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rec_correct'
items.doc:
Generalized primitive recursion. Given a sequence `r : ℕ → ℕ`, if `base` computes the base
value `r 0` and `step` computes the recursion step pointwise — taking the Church numeral of the
current index `k + 1` and the previous result `r k` to `r (k + 1)` — then `Rec ⬝ base ⬝ step`
computes `r` on every input. This is the primitive-recursion counterpart of `RFindAbove_correct'`
for μ-recursion: it isolates the behaviour of `Rec` from any particular client (such as the
translation of `Nat.Partrec.Code.prec`).
items.statement:
theorem rec_correct' (base step : SKI) (r : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hbase : IsChurch (r 0) base)
    (hstep : ∀ k : Nat, ∀ cb cp : SKI, IsChurch (k + 1) cb → IsChurch (r k) cp →
      IsChurch (r (k + 1)) (step ⬝ cb ⬝ cp)) :
    ∀ n : Nat, ∀ cn : SKI, IsChurch n cn → IsChurch (r n) (Rec ⬝ base ⬝ step ⬝ cn)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindAboveAuxPoly
items.doc:
First define an auxiliary function `RFindAbove` that looks for roots above a fixed number n, as a
fixed point of R ↦ λ n f. if f n = 0 then n else R f (n+1)
                 ~ λ n f. Cond ⬝ n (R f (Succ n)) (IsZero (f n))
items.statement: def RFindAboveAuxPoly : SKI.Polynomial 3

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindAboveAux
items.doc: A term representing RFindAboveAux
items.statement: def RFindAboveAux : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rfindAboveAux_def
items.statement:
lemma rfindAboveAux_def (R₀ f a : SKI) :
    (RFindAboveAux ⬝ R₀ ⬝ a ⬝ f) ↠ SKI.Cond ⬝ a ⬝ (R₀ ⬝ (SKI.Succ ⬝ a) ⬝ f) ⬝ (IsZero ⬝ (f ⬝ a))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rfindAboveAux_base
items.statement:
theorem rfindAboveAux_base (R₀ f a : SKI) (hfa : IsChurch 0 (f ⬝ a)) :
    (RFindAboveAux ⬝ R₀ ⬝ a ⬝ f) ↠ a

items.name: Cslib.SKI.rfindAboveAux_step
items.statement:
theorem rfindAboveAux_step (R₀ f a : SKI) {m : Nat} (hfa : IsChurch (m + 1) (f ⬝ a)) :
    (RFindAboveAux ⬝ R₀ ⬝ a ⬝ f) ↠ R₀ ⬝ (SKI.Succ ⬝ a) ⬝ f

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindAbove
items.doc: Find the minimal root of `fNat` above a number n
items.statement: def RFindAbove : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindAbove_unfold
items.doc: One unfolding of `RFindAbove`: apply the fixed-point combinator once.
items.statement:
theorem RFindAbove_unfold (x g : SKI) :
    (RFindAbove ⬝ x ⬝ g) ↠ RFindAboveAux ⬝ RFindAbove ⬝ x ⬝ g

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindAbove_correct'
items.doc:
Generalized root-finding that works with pointwise properties rather than a total
function. At the root `m + n`, `f` yields Church 0; below, a nonzero Church numeral.
items.statement:
theorem RFindAbove_correct' (f x : SKI) (n m : Nat) (hx : IsChurch m x)
    (hf_root : ∀ y, IsChurch (m + n) y → IsChurch 0 (f ⬝ y))
    (hf_below : ∀ i < n, ∀ y, IsChurch (m + i) y → ∃ k, IsChurch (k + 1) (f ⬝ y)) :
    IsChurch (m + n) (RFindAbove ⬝ x ⬝ f)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFindAbove_correct
items.statement:
theorem RFindAbove_correct (fNat : Nat → Nat) (f x : SKI)
    (hf : ∀ i : Nat, ∀ y : SKI, IsChurch i y → IsChurch (fNat i) (f ⬝ y))
    (n m : Nat) (hx : IsChurch m x) (hroot : fNat (m + n) = 0) (hpos : ∀ i < n, fNat (m + i) ≠ 0) :
    IsChurch (m + n) (RFindAbove ⬝ x ⬝ f)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFind
items.doc: Ordinary root finding is root finding above zero
items.statement: def RFind

items.name: Cslib.SKI.RFind_correct
items.statement:
theorem RFind_correct (fNat : Nat → Nat) (f : SKI)
    (hf : ∀ (i : Nat) (y : SKI), IsChurch i y → IsChurch (fNat i) (f ⬝ y))
    (n : Nat) (hroot : fNat n = 0) (hpos : ∀ i < n, fNat i ≠ 0) : IsChurch n (RFind ⬝ f)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.AddPoly
items.doc: Addition: λ n m. n Succ m
items.statement: def AddPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Add
items.doc: A term representing addition on church numerals
items.statement: protected def Add : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.add_def
items.statement: theorem add_def (a b : SKI) : (SKI.Add ⬝ a ⬝ b) ↠ a ⬝ SKI.Succ ⬝ b

items.name: Cslib.SKI.add_correct
items.statement:
theorem add_correct (n m : Nat) (a b : SKI) (ha : IsChurch n a) (hb : IsChurch m b) :
    IsChurch (n + m) (SKI.Add ⬝ a ⬝ b)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.MulPoly
items.doc: Multiplication: λ n m. n (Add m) Zero
items.statement: def MulPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Mul
items.doc: A term representing multiplication on church numerals
items.statement: protected def Mul : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.mul_def
items.statement: theorem mul_def (a b : SKI) : (SKI.Mul ⬝ a ⬝ b) ↠ a ⬝ (SKI.Add ⬝ b) ⬝ SKI.Zero

items.name: Cslib.SKI.mul_correct
items.statement:
theorem mul_correct {n m : Nat} {a b : SKI} (ha : IsChurch n a) (hb : IsChurch m b) :
    IsChurch (n * m) (SKI.Mul ⬝ a ⬝ b)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.SubPoly
items.doc: Subtraction: λ n m. n Pred m
items.statement: def SubPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Sub
items.doc: A term representing subtraction on church numerals
items.statement: protected def Sub : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.sub_def
items.statement: theorem sub_def (a b : SKI) : (SKI.Sub ⬝ a ⬝ b) ↠ b ⬝ Pred ⬝ a

items.name: Cslib.SKI.sub_correct
items.statement:
theorem sub_correct (n m : Nat) (a b : SKI) (ha : IsChurch n a) (hb : IsChurch m b) :
    IsChurch (n - m) (SKI.Sub ⬝ a ⬝ b)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.LEPoly
items.doc: Comparison: (. ≤ .) := λ n m. IsZero ⬝ (Sub ⬝ n ⬝ m)
items.statement: def LEPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.LE
items.doc: A term representing comparison on church numerals
items.statement: protected def LE : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.le_def
items.statement: theorem le_def (a b : SKI) : (SKI.LE ⬝ a ⬝ b) ↠ IsZero ⬝ (SKI.Sub ⬝ a ⬝ b)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.le_correct
items.statement:
theorem le_correct (n m : Nat) (a b : SKI) (ha : IsChurch n a) (hb : IsChurch m b) :
    IsBool (n ≤ m) (SKI.LE ⬝ a ⬝ b)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.SqrtCondPoly
items.doc:
Inner condition for Sqrt: with &0 = n, &1 = k,
computes `if n < (k+1)² then 0 else 1`.
items.statement: def SqrtCondPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.SqrtCond
items.doc: SKI term for the inner condition of Sqrt
items.statement: def SqrtCond : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.sqrtCond_def
items.doc:
`SqrtCond ⬝ n ⬝ k` reduces to: return 0 if `(k+1)² > n`, else 1.
Used by `RFind` to locate the smallest such `k`, which is `√n`.
items.statement:
theorem sqrtCond_def (cn ck : SKI) :
    (SqrtCond ⬝ cn ⬝ ck) ↠
      SKI.Cond ⬝ SKI.Zero ⬝ SKI.One ⬝
        (SKI.Neg ⬝ (SKI.LE ⬝ (SKI.Mul ⬝ (SKI.Succ ⬝ ck) ⬝ (SKI.Succ ⬝ ck)) ⬝ cn))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.SqrtPoly
items.doc:
Sqrt n = smallest k such that (k+1)² > n, i.e., the integer square root.
Defined as `λ n. RFind (SqrtCond n)`.
items.statement: def SqrtPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.Sqrt
items.doc: SKI term for integer square root
items.statement: def Sqrt : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.sqrt_def
items.doc: `Sqrt ⬝ n` reduces to an `RFind` search for the smallest `k` with `(k+1)² > n`.
items.statement: theorem sqrt_def (cn : SKI) : (Sqrt ⬝ cn) ↠ RFind ⬝ (SqrtCond ⬝ cn)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.sqrt_correct
items.doc: `Sqrt` correctly computes `Nat.sqrt`.
items.statement:
theorem sqrt_correct (n : Nat) (cn : SKI) (hcn : IsChurch n cn) :
    IsChurch (Nat.sqrt n) (Sqrt ⬝ cn)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.NatPairPoly
items.doc:
NatPair a b = if a < b then b*b + a else a*a + a + b.
With &0 = a, &1 = b. The condition `a < b` is `¬(b ≤ a)`.
items.statement: def NatPairPoly : SKI.Polynomial 2

items.name: Cslib.SKI.NatPair
items.doc: SKI term for Nat pairing
items.statement: def NatPair : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.natPair_def
items.doc: `NatPair ⬝ a ⬝ b` reduces to: if `a < b` then `b² + a`, else `a² + a + b`.
items.statement:
theorem natPair_def (ca cb : SKI) :
    (NatPair ⬝ ca ⬝ cb) ↠
      SKI.Cond ⬝ (SKI.Add ⬝ (SKI.Mul ⬝ cb ⬝ cb) ⬝ ca)
               ⬝ (SKI.Add ⬝ (SKI.Add ⬝ (SKI.Mul ⬝ ca ⬝ ca) ⬝ ca) ⬝ cb)
               ⬝ (SKI.Neg ⬝ (SKI.LE ⬝ cb ⬝ ca))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.natPair_correct
items.doc: `NatPair` correctly computes `Nat.pair`.
items.statement:
theorem natPair_correct (a b : Nat) (ca cb : SKI)
    (ha : IsChurch a ca) (hb : IsChurch b cb) :
    IsChurch (Nat.pair a b) (NatPair ⬝ ca ⬝ cb)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.NatUnpairLeftPoly
items.doc: `NatUnpairLeft n = if n - s² < s then n - s² else s` where `s = Nat.sqrt n`.
items.statement: def NatUnpairLeftPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.NatUnpairLeft
items.doc: SKI term for left projection of Nat.unpair
items.statement: def NatUnpairLeft : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.natUnpairLeft_def
items.doc:
`NatUnpairLeft ⬝ n` reduces to: let `s = √n` and `d = n - s²`;
return `d` if `d < s`, else `s`.
items.statement:
theorem natUnpairLeft_def (cn : SKI) :
    (NatUnpairLeft ⬝ cn) ↠
      SKI.Cond ⬝ (SKI.Sub ⬝ cn ⬝ (SKI.Mul ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn) ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)))
               ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)
               ⬝ (SKI.Neg ⬝ (SKI.LE ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)
                    ⬝ (SKI.Sub ⬝ cn ⬝ (SKI.Mul ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn) ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)))))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.natUnpairLeft_correct
items.doc: `NatUnpairLeft` correctly computes the first component of `Nat.unpair`.
items.statement:
theorem natUnpairLeft_correct (n : Nat) (cn : SKI) (hcn : IsChurch n cn) :
    IsChurch (Nat.unpair n).1 (NatUnpairLeft ⬝ cn)

items.name: Cslib.SKI.NatUnpairRightPoly
items.doc: NatUnpairRight n = let s = sqrt n in if n - s² < s then s else n - s² - s.
items.statement: def NatUnpairRightPoly : SKI.Polynomial 1

items.name: Cslib.SKI.NatUnpairRight
items.doc: SKI term for right projection of Nat.unpair
items.statement: def NatUnpairRight : SKI

items.name: Cslib.SKI.natUnpairRight_def
items.doc:
`NatUnpairRight ⬝ n` reduces to: let `s = √n` and `d = n - s²`;
return `s` if `d < s`, else `d - s`.
items.statement:
theorem natUnpairRight_def (cn : SKI) :
    (NatUnpairRight ⬝ cn) ↠
      SKI.Cond ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)
               ⬝ (SKI.Sub ⬝ (SKI.Sub ⬝ cn ⬝ (SKI.Mul ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn) ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)))
                            ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn))
               ⬝ (SKI.Neg ⬝ (SKI.LE ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)
                    ⬝ (SKI.Sub ⬝ cn ⬝ (SKI.Mul ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn) ⬝ (Sqrt ⬝ cn)))))

items.name: Cslib.SKI.natUnpairRight_correct
items.doc: `NatUnpairRight` correctly computes the second component of `Nat.unpair`.
items.statement:
theorem natUnpairRight_correct (n : Nat) (cn : SKI) (hcn : IsChurch n cn) :
    IsChurch (Nat.unpair n).2 (NatUnpairRight ⬝ cn)

modules.title: λ-calculus
modules.doc: Contexts as pairs of free variables and types.

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Context
items.doc: A typing context is a list of free variables and corresponding types.
items.statement: abbrev Context (α : Type u) (β : Type v)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Context.dom
items.doc: The domain of a context is the finite set of free variables it uses.
items.statement: def dom (Γ : Context α β) : Finset α

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Context.haswellformed_def
items.statement: theorem haswellformed_def (Γ : Context α β) : Γ✓ = Γ.NodupKeys

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Context.mapVal
items.doc: A mapping of values within a context.

modules.title: λ-calculus
modules.doc:
The λ-calculus with polymorphism and subtyping, with a locally nameless representation of syntax.

## References

* [A. Chargueraud, *The Locally Nameless Representation*][Chargueraud2012]
* See also <https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~plclub/popl08-tutorial/code/>, from which
  this is adapted

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty
items.doc: Types of the polymorphic lambda calculus.
items.statement:
inductive Ty (Var : Type*)
  /-- The type ⊤, with a single inhabitant. -/
  | top : Ty Var
  /-- Bound variables that appear in a type, using a de-Bruijn index. -/
  | bvar : ℕ → Ty Var
  /-- Free type variables. -/
  | fvar : Var → Ty Var
  /-- A function type. -/
  | arrow : Ty Var → Ty Var → Ty Var
  /-- A universal quantification. -/
  | all : Ty Var → Ty Var → Ty Var
  /-- A sum type. -/
  | sum : Ty Var → Ty Var → Ty Var
  deriving Inhabited

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term
items.doc: Syntax of locally nameless lambda terms, with free variables over `Var`.
items.statement:
inductive Term (Var : Type*)
  /-- Bound term variables that appear under a lambda abstraction, using a de-Bruijn index. -/
  | bvar : ℕ → Term Var
  /-- Free term variables. -/
  | fvar : Var → Term Var
  /-- Lambda abstraction, introducing a new bound term variable. -/
  | abs : Ty Var → Term Var → Term Var
  /-- Function application. -/
  | app : Term Var → Term Var → Term Var
  /-- Type abstraction, introducing a new bound type variable. -/
  | tabs : Ty Var → Term Var → Term Var
  /-- Type application. -/
  | tapp : Term Var → Ty Var → Term Var
  /-- Binding of a term. -/
  | let' : Term Var → Term Var → Term Var
  /-- Left constructor of a sum. -/
  | inl : Term Var → Term Var
  /-- Right constructor of a sum. -/
  | inr : Term Var → Term Var
  /-- Case matching on a sum. -/
  | case : Term Var → Term Var → Term Var → Term Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Binding
items.doc: A context binding.
items.statement:
inductive Binding (Var : Type*)
  /-- Subtype binding. -/
  | sub : Ty Var → Binding Var
  /-- Type binding. -/
  | ty : Ty Var → Binding Var
  deriving Inhabited

modules.title: λ-calculus
modules.doc:
The λ-calculus with polymorphism and subtyping, with a locally nameless representation of syntax.
This file defines opening, local closure, and substitution.

## References

* [A. Chargueraud, *The Locally Nameless Representation*][Chargueraud2012]
* See also <https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~plclub/popl08-tutorial/code/>, from which
  this is adapted

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.openRec
items.doc: Variable opening (type opening to type) of the ith bound variable.
items.statement: def openRec (X : ℕ) (δ : Ty Var) : Ty Var → Ty Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.open'
items.doc: Variable opening (type opening to type) of the closest binding.
items.statement: def open' (γ δ : Ty Var)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.LC
items.doc: Locally closed types.
items.statement:
inductive LC : Ty Var → Prop
  | top : LC top
  | var : LC (fvar X)
  | arrow : LC σ → LC τ → LC (arrow σ τ)
  | all (L : Finset Var) : LC σ → (∀ X ∉ L, LC (τ ^ᵞ fvar X)) → LC (all σ τ)
  | sum : LC σ → LC τ → LC (sum σ τ)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.subst
items.doc: Type substitution.
items.statement: def subst (X : Var) (δ : Ty Var) : Ty Var → Ty Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.openRec_neq_eq
items.doc: An opening appearing in both sides of an equality of types can be removed.
items.statement:
lemma openRec_neq_eq {σ τ γ : Ty Var} (neq : X ≠ Y) (h : σ⟦Y ↝ τ⟧ᵞ = σ⟦Y ↝ τ⟧ᵞ⟦X ↝ γ⟧ᵞ) :
    σ = σ⟦X ↝ γ⟧ᵞ

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.openRec_lc
items.doc: A locally closed type is unchanged by opening.
items.statement: lemma openRec_lc {σ τ : Ty Var} (lc : σ.LC) : σ = σ⟦X ↝ τ⟧ᵞ

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.subst_def
items.statement: lemma subst_def : Ty.subst (X : Var) (δ : Ty Var) (γ : Ty Var) = γ[X := δ]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.subst_fresh
items.doc: Substitution of a free variable not present in a type leaves it unchanged.
items.statement: lemma subst_fresh (nmem : X ∉ γ.fv) (δ : Ty Var) : γ = γ[X := δ]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.openRec_subst
items.doc: Substitution of a locally closed type distributes with opening.
items.statement:
lemma openRec_subst (Y : ℕ) (σ τ : Ty Var) (lc : δ.LC) (X : Var) :
    (σ⟦Y ↝ τ⟧ᵞ)[X := δ] = σ[X := δ]⟦Y ↝ τ[X := δ]⟧ᵞ

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.open_subst
items.doc: Specialize `Ty.openRec_subst` to the first opening.
items.statement: lemma open_subst (σ τ : Ty Var) (lc : δ.LC) (X : Var) : (σ ^ᵞ τ)[X := δ] = σ[X := δ] ^ᵞ τ[X := δ]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.open_subst_var
items.doc: Specialize `Ty.subst_open` to free variables.
items.statement:
lemma open_subst_var (σ : Ty Var) (neq : Y ≠ X) (lc : δ.LC) :
    (σ ^ᵞ fvar Y)[X := δ] = (σ[X := δ]) ^ᵞ fvar Y

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.openRec_subst_intro
items.doc: Opening to a type is equivalent to opening to a free variable and substituting.
items.statement:
lemma openRec_subst_intro (Y : ℕ) (δ : Ty Var) (nmem : X ∉ γ.fv) :
    γ⟦Y ↝ δ⟧ᵞ = (γ⟦Y ↝ fvar X⟧ᵞ)[X := δ]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.open_subst_intro
items.doc: Specialize `Ty.openRec_subst_intro` to the first opening.
items.statement: lemma open_subst_intro (δ : Ty Var) (nmem : X ∉ γ.fv) : γ ^ᵞ δ = (γ ^ᵞ fvar X)[X := δ]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Ty.subst_lc
items.statement: lemma subst_lc (σ_lc : σ.LC) (τ_lc : τ.LC) (X : Var) : σ[X := τ].LC

items.statement: lemma nmem_fv_openRec (nmem : X ∉ (σ⟦k ↝ γ⟧ᵞ).fv) : X ∉ σ.fv

items.doc: Variable opening (term opening to term) of the closest binding.

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.LC
items.doc: Locally closed terms.
items.statement:
inductive LC : Term Var → Prop
  | var : LC (fvar x)
  | abs (L : Finset Var) : σ.LC → (∀ x ∉ L, LC (t₁ ^ᵗᵗ fvar x)) → LC (abs σ t₁)
  | app : LC t₁ → LC t₂ → LC (app t₁ t₂)
  | tabs (L : Finset Var) : σ.LC → (∀ X ∉ L, LC (t₁ ^ᵗᵞ .fvar X)) → LC (tabs σ t₁)
  | tapp : LC t₁ → σ.LC → LC (tapp t₁ σ)
  | let' (L : Finset Var) : LC t₁ → (∀ x ∉ L, LC (t₂ ^ᵗᵗ fvar x)) → LC (let' t₁ t₂)
  | inl : LC t₁ → LC (inl t₁)
  | inr : LC t₁ → LC (inr t₁)
  | case (L : Finset Var) :
      LC t₁ →
      (∀ x ∉ L, LC (t₂ ^ᵗᵗ fvar x)) →
      (∀ x ∉ L, LC (t₃ ^ᵗᵗ fvar x)) →
      LC (case t₁ t₂ t₃)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.openRecTy_neq_eq

modules.title: λ-calculus
modules.doc:
The λ-calculus with polymorphism and subtyping, with a locally nameless representation of syntax.
This file defines a call-by-value reduction.

## References

* [A. Chargueraud, *The Locally Nameless Representation*][Chargueraud2012]
* See also <https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~plclub/popl08-tutorial/code/>, from which
  this is adapted

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.body
items.doc: Existential predicate for being a locally closed body of an abstraction.
items.statement: def body (t : Term Var)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.body_let
items.doc: Locally closed let bindings have a locally closed body.
items.statement: lemma body_let : (let' t₁ t₂).LC ↔ t₁.LC ∧ t₂.body

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.body_case
items.doc: Locally closed case bindings have a locally closed bodies.
items.statement: lemma body_case : (case t₁ t₂ t₃).LC ↔ t₁.LC ∧ t₂.body ∧ t₃.body

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.open_tm_body
items.doc: Opening a body preserves local closure.
items.statement: lemma open_tm_body (body : t₁.body) (lc : t₂.LC) : (t₁ ^ᵗᵗ t₂).LC

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.Value
items.doc: Values are irreducible terms.
items.statement:
inductive Value : Term Var → Prop
  | abs : LC (abs σ t₁) → Value (abs σ t₁)
  | tabs : LC (tabs σ t₁) → Value (tabs σ t₁)
  | inl : Value t₁ → Value (inl t₁)
  | inr : Value t₁ → Value (inr t₁)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.Value.lc
items.statement: lemma Value.lc {t : Term Var} (val : t.Value) : t.LC

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.Red
items.doc: The call-by-value reduction relation.
items.statement:
inductive Red : Term Var → Term Var → Prop
  | appₗ : LC t₂ → Red t₁ t₁' → Red (app t₁ t₂) (app t₁' t₂)
  | appᵣ : Value t₁ → Red t₂ t₂' → Red (app t₁ t₂) (app t₁ t₂')
  | tapp : σ.LC → Red t₁ t₁' → Red (tapp t₁ σ) (tapp t₁' σ)
  | abs : LC (abs σ t₁) → Value t₂ → Red (app (abs σ t₁) t₂) (t₁ ^ᵗᵗ t₂)
  | tabs : LC (tabs σ t₁) → τ.LC → Red (tapp (tabs σ t₁) τ) (t₁ ^ᵗᵞ τ)
  | let_bind : Red t₁ t₁' → t₂.body → Red (let' t₁ t₂) (let' t₁' t₂)
  | let_body : Value t₁ → t₂.body → Red (let' t₁ t₂) (t₂ ^ᵗᵗ t₁)
  | inl : Red t₁ t₁' → Red (inl t₁) (inl t₁')
  | inr : Red t₁ t₁' → Red (inr t₁) (inr t₁')
  | case : Red t₁ t₁' → t₂.body → t₃.body → Red (case t₁ t₂ t₃) (case t₁' t₂ t₃)
  | case_inl : Value t₁ → t₂.body → t₃.body → Red (case (inl t₁) t₂ t₃) (t₂ ^ᵗᵗ t₁)
  | case_inr : Value t₁ → t₂.body → t₃.body → Red (case (inr t₁) t₂ t₃) (t₃ ^ᵗᵗ t₁)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Term.Red.lc
items.doc: Terms of a reduction are locally closed.
items.statement: lemma Red.lc {t t' : Term Var} (red : t ⭢βᵛ t') : t.LC ∧ t'.LC
