modules.title: The Leftmost Reduction Theorem
modules.doc:
## Reference

* [M. Copes, *A machine-checked proof of the Standardization Theorem in λ-calculus*][Copes2018]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.BetaNormal
items.doc: A term is in normal form when it contains no β-redexes.
items.statement: def BetaNormal (m : Term Var) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost
items.doc: Leftmost reduction: a β-reduction contracting the redex at position 0.
items.statement: abbrev Leftmost : Term Var → Term Var → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.BetaNormal.app_inv
items.doc:
In a normal-form application, both sides are normal and the operator is not an
abstraction.
items.statement:
lemma BetaNormal.app_inv (h : BetaNormal (app L M)) :
    ¬IsAbs L ∧ BetaNormal L ∧ BetaNormal M

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.BetaNormal.abs_open
items.doc: The body of a normal-form abstraction opens to a normal form.
items.statement: lemma BetaNormal.abs_open {x : Var} (h : BetaNormal (abs M)) : BetaNormal (M ^ fvar x)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.steps_isAbs_r
items.doc: Leftmost reduction preserves being an abstraction.
items.statement: lemma Leftmost.steps_isAbs_r (h : M ↠ℓ N) (ha : IsAbs M) : IsAbs N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.steps_app_l_cong
items.doc: Left congruence for leftmost reduction, provided the target is not an abstraction.
items.statement:
lemma Leftmost.steps_app_l_cong (h : L ↠ℓ L') (hna : ¬IsAbs L') :
    app L M ↠ℓ app L' M

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.BetaAt.app_r_cong
items.doc: Reducing the operand across a non-abstraction normal form keeps the position.
items.statement:
lemma BetaAt.app_r_cong (h : BetaAt i M M') (hL : BetaNormal L) (hna : ¬IsAbs L) :
    BetaAt i (app L M) (app L M')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.steps_app_r_cong
items.doc:
Right congruence for leftmost reduction, provided the operator is a non-abstraction
normal form.
items.statement:
lemma Leftmost.steps_app_r_cong (h : M ↠ℓ M') (hL : BetaNormal L) (hna : ¬IsAbs L) :
    app L M ↠ℓ app L M'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.steps_app_cong
items.doc:
Congruence for leftmost reduction on applications whose reduced operator is a
non-abstraction normal form.
items.statement:
lemma Leftmost.steps_app_cong (hL : L ↠ℓ L') (hM : M ↠ℓ M')
    (hnf : BetaNormal L') (hna : ¬IsAbs L') : app L M ↠ℓ app L' M'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.of_cbn
items.doc: Call-by-Name reduction is contained in leftmost reduction.
items.statement: lemma Leftmost.of_cbn (h : M ↠ₙ N) : M ↠ℓ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.steps_lc_r
items.doc: Leftmost reduction preserves local closure.
items.statement: lemma Leftmost.steps_lc_r (h : M ↠ℓ M') (lc : LC M) : LC M'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.steps_abs_close
items.doc: Leftmost reduction is preserved by closing a variable and abstracting.
items.statement:
lemma Leftmost.steps_abs_close {x : Var} (h : M ↠ℓ M') (lc : LC M) :
    (M⟦0 ↜ x⟧.abs) ↠ℓ (M'⟦0 ↜ x⟧.abs)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.steps_abs_cong
items.doc: Cofinite congruence rule for leftmost reduction under an abstraction.
items.statement:
lemma Leftmost.steps_abs_cong (xs : Finset Var)
    (cofin : ∀ x ∉ xs, (M ^ fvar x) ↠ℓ (M' ^ fvar x)) (lc : LC (abs M)) :
    abs M ↠ℓ abs M'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.of_standard
items.doc: A standard reduction to a normal form is a leftmost reduction.
items.statement: theorem Leftmost.of_standard (h : M ⭢ₛ N) (hn : BetaNormal N) : M ↠ℓ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Leftmost.normalization
items.doc:
The leftmost reduction theorem: if a term β-reduces to a normal form, then leftmost
reduction reaches it.
items.statement: theorem Leftmost.normalization (lc : LC M) (h : M ↠βᶠ N) (hn : BetaNormal N) : M ↠ℓ N

modules.doc: Multiple application for untyped lambda calculus.

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiApp
items.doc:
multiApp f [x₁, x₂, ..., xₙ] applies the arguments x₁, x₂, ..., xₙ
to f in left-associative order, i.e. as (((f x₁) x₂) ... xₙ).
items.statement: def multiApp (f : Term Var) : List (Term Var) → Term Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.ListFullBeta
items.doc:
A list of arguments performs a single reduction step

[x₁, ..., xᵢ ..., xₙ] ⭢βᶠ [x₁, ..., xᵢ', ..., xₙ]

if one of the arguments performs a single step xᵢ ⭢βᶠ xᵢ'
and the rest of the arguments are locally closed.
items.statement: inductive ListFullBeta : List (Term Var) → List (Term Var) → Prop where

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiApp_tail
items.statement: lemma multiApp_tail {N} : (M.multiApp (Ns ++ [N])) = (M.multiApp Ns).app  N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiApp_lc
items.doc:
A term resulting from a multi-application is locally closed if
and only if the leftmost term and all arguments applied to it are locally closed
items.statement: lemma multiApp_lc : LC (M.multiApp Ns) ↔ LC M ∧ (∀ N ∈ Ns, LC N)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.step_multiApp_l
items.doc:
Just like ordinary beta reduction, the left-hand side
of a multi-application step is locally closed
items.statement:
lemma step_multiApp_l (steps : M ⭢βᶠ M') (lc_Ns : ∀ N ∈ Ns, LC N) :
    M.multiApp Ns ⭢βᶠ M'.multiApp Ns

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.steps_multiApp_l
items.doc: Congruence lemma for multi reduction of the left most term of a multi-application
items.statement:
lemma steps_multiApp_l (steps : M ↠βᶠ M') (lc_Ns : ∀ N ∈ Ns, LC N) :
    M.multiApp Ns ↠βᶠ M'.multiApp Ns

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.step_multiApp_r
items.doc: Congruence lemma for single reduction of one of the arguments of a multi-application
items.statement: lemma step_multiApp_r (steps : Ns ⭢lβᶠ Ns') (lc_M : LC M) : M.multiApp Ns ⭢βᶠ M.multiApp Ns'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.steps_multiApp_r
items.doc: Congruence lemma for multiple reduction of one of the arguments of a multi-application
items.statement: lemma steps_multiApp_r (steps : Ns ↠lβᶠ Ns') (lc_M : LC M) : M.multiApp Ns ↠βᶠ M.multiApp Ns'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.listFullBeta_cons_r
items.statement: lemma listFullBeta_cons_r (h : Ns ⭢lβᶠ Ns') (h_lc : ∀ M ∈ l, LC M) : (l ++ Ns) ⭢lβᶠ (l ++ Ns')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.listFullBeta_cons_l
items.statement: lemma listFullBeta_cons_l (h : Ns ⭢lβᶠ Ns') (h_lc : ∀ M ∈ l, LC M) : (Ns ++ l) ⭢lβᶠ (Ns' ++ l)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.invert_abs_multiApp_st
items.doc:
If a term (λ M) N P_1 ... P_n reduces in a single step to Q, then
Q must be one of the following forms:

Q = (λ M') N P₁ ... Pₙ where M ⭢βᶠ M' or
Q = (λ M) N' P₁ ... Pₙ where N ⭢βᶠ N' or
Q = (λ M) N P₁' ... Pₙ' where P_i ⭢βᶠ P_i' for some i or
Q = (M ^ N) P₁ ... Pₙ
items.statement:
lemma invert_abs_multiApp_st {Ps} {M N Q : Term Var}
  (h_red : multiApp (M.abs.app N) Ps ⭢βᶠ Q) :
    (∃ M', M.abs ⭢βᶠ Term.abs M' ∧ Q = multiApp (M'.abs.app N) Ps) ∨
    (∃ N', N ⭢βᶠ N' ∧ Q = multiApp (M.abs.app N') Ps) ∨
    (∃ Ps', Ps ⭢lβᶠ Ps' ∧ Q = multiApp (M.abs.app N) Ps') ∨
    (Q = multiApp (M ^ N) Ps)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.invert_abs_multiApp_mst
items.doc:
If a term (λ M) N P₁ ... Pₙ reduces in multiple steps to Q, then either Q if of the form

   Q = (λ M') N' P'₁ ... P'ₙ

   or

 we first reach an intermediate term of this shape,

   (λ M) N P₁ ... Pₙ ↠βᶠ (λ M') N' P'₁ ... P'ₙ

   then perform a beta reduction and reduce further to Q

   (λ M') N' P'₁ ... P'ₙ ↠βᶠ M' ^ N' P'_₁ ... P'_ₙ ↠βᶠ Q

where M ↠βᶠ M' and N ↠βᶠ N' and P_i ↠βᶠ P_i' for all i
items.statement:
lemma invert_abs_multiApp_mst {Ps} {M N Q : Term Var}
  (h_red : multiApp (M.abs.app N) Ps ↠βᶠ Q) :
    ∃ M' N' Ns', M.abs ↠βᶠ M'.abs ∧ N ↠βᶠ N' ∧ Ps ↠lβᶠ Ns' ∧
                 (Q = multiApp (M'.abs.app N') Ns' ∨
     (multiApp (M.abs.app N) Ps ↠βᶠ multiApp (M' ^ N') Ns' ∧
                                     multiApp (M' ^ N') Ns' ↠βᶠ Q))

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiApp_step_lc_r
items.doc:
Just like ordinary beta reduction, the right-hand side
of a multi-application step is locally closed
items.statement: lemma multiApp_step_lc_r (step : Ns ⭢lβᶠ Ns') : ∀ N ∈ Ns', LC N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiApp_steps_lc
items.doc: Just like ordinary beta reduction, multiple steps of a argument list preserves local closure
items.statement: lemma multiApp_steps_lc (step : Ns ↠lβᶠ Ns') (H : ∀ N ∈ Ns, LC N) : ∀ N ∈ Ns', LC N

modules.doc: Multiple substitution for untyped lambda calculus.

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Env
items.doc:
An environment in context of multi substitution is a list of pairs of
variable targets and terms to be substituted for that target
items.statement: abbrev Env (Var : Type u)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiSubst
items.doc:
Multi-substitution substitutes all target variables
in an environment by their corresponding terms
items.statement: def multiSubst (E : Env Var) (M : Term Var) : Term Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Env.fv
items.doc:
The free variables of an environment are the union of
the free variables of all terms in the environment.
The target variables are not necessarily included
items.statement: def Env.fv (E : Env Var) : Finset Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.envLC
items.doc: An environment is locally closed if all terms in the environment are locally closed
items.statement: abbrev envLC (E : Env Var) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.envLC_cons
items.doc: Adding a locally closed term to an environment preserves local closure
items.statement: lemma envLC_cons (lc_sub : LC sub) (lc_E : envLC E) : envLC (⟨ x, sub ⟩ :: E)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiSubst_fvar_fresh
items.doc: Multi-substitution of a fresh variable does nothing
items.statement: lemma multiSubst_fvar_fresh (E : Env Var) : ∀ x ∉ E.dom, multiSubst E (fvar x) = fvar x

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiSubst_preserves_not_fvar
items.doc:
If x is neither a free variable of an environment Ns or a term M, then
x is also not a free variable of the multi-substitution of Ns into M
items.statement:
lemma multiSubst_preserves_not_fvar (M : Term Var) (E : Env Var) :
    (multiSubst E M).fv ⊆ M.fv ∪ E.fv

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiSubst_app
items.doc: Multi-substitution propagates recursively through an application
items.statement:
lemma multiSubst_app (M N : Term Var) (E : Env Var) :
    multiSubst E (app M N) = app (multiSubst E M) (multiSubst E N)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiSubst_abs
items.doc: Multi-substitution propagates recursively through an abstraction
items.statement:
lemma multiSubst_abs (M : Term Var) (E : Env Var) :
    multiSubst E (abs M) = abs (multiSubst E M)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.multiSubst_open_var
items.doc:
Multi-substitution commutes with opening a term with a fresh variable,
provided that the variable is not in the domain of the environment
and the environment is locally closed
items.statement:
lemma multiSubst_open_var [HasFresh Var] (M : Term Var) (E : Env Var) (x : Var)
  (h_ndom : x ∉ E.dom) (h_lc : envLC E) :
    multiSubst E (M ^ fvar x) = multiSubst E M ^ fvar x

modules.doc: General properties of opening and substitution in untyped lambda calculus terms.

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_fresh
items.doc: Substitution of a free variable not present in a term leaves it unchanged.
items.statement: theorem subst_fresh (x : Var) (t sub : Term Var) (nmem : x ∉ t.fv) : t[x := sub] = t

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.open_close
items.statement: lemma open_close (x : Var) (t : Term Var) (k : ℕ) (nmem : x ∉ t.fv) : t = t⟦k ↝ fvar x⟧⟦k ↜ x⟧

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.open_close_var
items.doc: Specializes `open_close` to the first closing.
items.statement: lemma open_close_var (x : Var) (t : Term Var) (nmem : x ∉ t.fv) : t = (t ^ fvar x) ^* x

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.open_injective
items.doc: Opening is injective.
items.statement:
lemma open_injective (x : Var) (M M') (free_M : x ∉ M.fv) (free_M' : x ∉ M'.fv)
    (eq : M ^ fvar x = M' ^ fvar x) : M = M'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.swap_open_fvar_close
items.doc: Opening and closing are associative for nonclashing free variables.
items.statement:
lemma swap_open_fvar_close (k n : ℕ) (x y : Var) (m : Term Var) (neq₁ : k ≠ n) (neq₂ : x ≠ y) :
    m⟦n ↝ fvar y⟧⟦k ↜ x⟧ = m⟦k ↜ x⟧⟦n ↝ fvar y⟧

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.close_rec_fv
items.doc: Closing preserves free variables.
items.statement: lemma close_rec_fv {k y} (m : Term Var) : (m⟦k ↜ y⟧).fv = m.fv.erase y

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.close_var_not_fvar
items.doc: Specializes `close_var_not_fvar_rec` to first closing.
items.statement: lemma close_var_not_fvar (x) (t : Term Var) : (t ^* x).fv = t.fv.erase x

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.open_preserve_not_fvar
items.doc: Opening preserves free variables.
items.statement:
theorem open_preserve_not_fvar (k) (m n : Term Var) :
    m⟦k ↝ n⟧.fv = m.fv ∪ n.fv ∨ m⟦k ↝ n⟧.fv = m.fv

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_preserve_not_fvar
items.doc: Substitution preserves free variables.
items.statement:
lemma subst_preserve_not_fvar {y : Var} (m n : Term Var) :
    m[y := n].fv = m.fv.erase y ∨ m[y := n].fv = m.fv.erase y ∪ n.fv

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_refl
items.statement: lemma subst_refl (m : Term Var) (x : Var) : m[x := fvar x] = m

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_intro_openRec
items.statement:
lemma subst_intro_openRec {x} {t e : Term Var} (mem : x ∉ e.fv) {k : ℕ} :
    e ⟦k ↝ t⟧ = (e ⟦ k ↝ fvar x⟧)[ x := t ]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_intro
items.doc: Opening to a term `t` is equivalent to opening to a free variable and substituting for `t`.
items.statement:
lemma subst_intro (x : Var) (t e : Term Var) (mem : x ∉ e.fv) :
    e ^ t = (e ^ fvar x)[x := t]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.open_lc
items.doc: A locally closed term is unchanged by opening.
items.statement: lemma open_lc (k t) (e : Term Var) (e_lc : e.LC) : e⟦k ↝ t⟧ = e

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.swap_open
items.doc: Opening is associative for nonclashing locally closed terms.
items.statement:
lemma swap_open (k n : ℕ) (t₁ t₂ m : Term Var) (neq : k ≠ n) (h1 : t₁.LC) (h2 : t₂.LC) :
    m⟦n ↝ t₂⟧⟦k ↝ t₁⟧ = m⟦k ↝ t₁⟧⟦n ↝ t₂⟧

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.open_eq_app
items.statement:
lemma open_eq_app {x : Var} {m n : Term Var} (hw_n : x ∉ n.fv) (hw_m : x ∉ m.fv) (lc_m : LC m)
    (h : n ^ fvar x = app m (fvar x)) : n = app m (bvar 0)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_openRec
items.doc: Substitution of a locally closed term distributes with opening.
items.statement:
lemma subst_openRec (x : Var) (t : Term Var) (k : ℕ) (u e : Term Var) (lc : LC t) :
    (e⟦ k ↝ u ⟧)[x := t] = e[x := t]⟦k ↝ u[x := t]⟧

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_open
items.doc: Specialize `subst_openRec` to the first opening.
items.statement:
lemma subst_open (x : Var) (t : Term Var) (u e : Term Var) (lc : LC t) :
    (e ^ u)[x := t] = e[x := t] ^ u[x := t]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_open_var
items.doc: Specialize `subst_open` to the free variables.
items.statement:
theorem subst_open_var (x y : Var) (u e : Term Var) (neq : y ≠ x) (u_lc : LC u) :
    (e ^ fvar x)[y := u] = e[y := u] ^ fvar x

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.subst_lc
items.doc: Substitution of locally closed terms is locally closed.
items.statement: theorem subst_lc {x : Var} {e u : Term Var} (e_lc : LC e) (u_lc : LC u) : LC (e[x := u])

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.beta_lc
items.doc: Opening of locally closed terms is locally closed.
items.statement: theorem beta_lc {M N : Term Var} (m_lc : M.abs.LC) (n_lc : LC N) : LC (M ^ N)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.close_openRec_to_subst
items.doc: Closing then opening is equivalent to substitution.
items.statement:
lemma close_openRec_to_subst (m n : Term Var) (x : Var) (k : ℕ) (m_lc : LC m) (n_lc : LC n) :
    m ⟦k ↜ x⟧⟦k ↝ n⟧ = m[x := n]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.close_open_to_subst
items.statement:
lemma close_open_to_subst (m n : Term Var) (x : Var) (m_lc : LC m) (n_lc : LC n) :
    (m ^* x) ^ n = m[x := n]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.close_open
items.doc: Closing and opening are inverses.
items.statement: lemma close_open (x : Var) (t : Term Var) (k : ℕ) (t_lc : LC t) : t⟦k ↜ x⟧⟦k ↝ fvar x⟧ = t

modules.title: Standard Reduction and the Standardization Theorem
modules.doc:
## References

* [B. Calisto, *Formalization in Coq of the Standardization Theorem for λ-calculus*][Calisto2022]
* [M. Copes, *A machine-checked proof of the Standardization Theorem in λ-calculus*][Copes2018]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq
items.doc:
A standard β-reduction sequence contracts redexes at non-decreasing positions. The index
`n` is the last position contracted.
items.statement: inductive StandardSeq : Nat → Term Var → Term Var → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard
items.doc: The Standard reduction relation.
items.statement: inductive Standard : Term Var → Term Var → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.lc_l
items.doc: The left side of a standard reduction is locally closed.
items.statement: lemma Standard.lc_l (step : M ⭢ₛ N) : LC M

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.lc_refl
items.doc: Standard reduction is reflexive for locally closed terms.
items.statement: lemma Standard.lc_refl (M : Term Var) (lc : LC M) : M ⭢ₛ M

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.lc_r
items.doc: The right side of a standard reduction is locally closed.
items.statement: lemma Standard.lc_r (step : M ⭢ₛ N) : LC N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.of_cbn_step
items.doc: A single Call-by-Name step is a standard reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.of_cbn_step (step : M ⭢ₙ N) (lc_N : LC N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.cbn_step_trans
items.doc: A Call-by-Name step followed by a standard reduction is a standard reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.cbn_step_trans (step : M ⭢ₙ P) (std : P ⭢ₛ N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.cbn_trans
items.doc: A Call-by-Name reduction followed by a standard reduction is a standard reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.cbn_trans (h1 : M ↠ₙ P) (h2 : P ⭢ₛ N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.of_cbn
items.doc: Call-by-Name reduction is contained in standard reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.of_cbn (step : M ↠ₙ N) (lc_N : LC N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.isAbs_r
items.doc: Standard sequences preserve being an abstraction.
items.statement: lemma StandardSeq.isAbs_r (h : StandardSeq n M N) (ha : IsAbs M) : IsAbs N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.head_leftmost
items.doc: A standard sequence preceded by a step at position `0` remains standard.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.head_leftmost (seq : StandardSeq n P N) :
    ∀ {M}, BetaAt 0 M P → ∃ k, k ≤ n ∧ StandardSeq k M N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.cbn_head
items.doc: A standard sequence stays standard when preceded by a Call-by-Name reduction.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.cbn_head (h : M ↠ₙ P) (hseq : StandardSeq n P N) :
    ∃ k, StandardSeq k M N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_r_abs
items.doc: Right congruence for standard sequences when the operator is an abstraction.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_r_abs (h : StandardSeq n M M') (ha : IsAbs L) :
    StandardSeq (n + countRedexes L + 1) (app L M) (app L M')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_r_noAbs
items.doc: Right congruence for standard sequences when the operator is a non-abstraction.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_r_noAbs (h : StandardSeq n M M') (hna : ¬IsAbs L) :
    StandardSeq (n + countRedexes L) (app L M) (app L M')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_r_cong
items.doc: Right application congruence for standard sequences.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_r_cong (h : StandardSeq n M M') :
    ∃ k, StandardSeq k (app L M) (app L M') ∧
      k ≤ n + countRedexes L + (if IsAbs L then 1 else 0)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.le_countRedexes_of_ne
items.doc: The final position of a nonempty standard sequence is at most its target's redex count.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.le_countRedexes_of_ne (h : StandardSeq n M N) (hne : M ≠ N) :
    n ≤ countRedexes N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_l_cong
items.doc:
Reducing the operator of an application yields a standard sequence, with the final position
bounded.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_l_cong (h : StandardSeq n L L') :
    ∃ k, StandardSeq k (app L M) (app L' M) ∧
      k ≤ n + (if IsAbs L' then 1 else 0)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_l_cong_of_ne
items.doc:
A nonempty operator reduction lifts to the application, bounded by the operator's redex
count.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_l_cong_of_ne (h : StandardSeq n L L') (hne : L ≠ L') :
    ∃ k, StandardSeq k (app L M) (app L' M) ∧
      k ≤ countRedexes L' + (if IsAbs L' then 1 else 0)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_r_tail
items.doc: Append an operand step to a standard sequence of applications.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_r_tail (h : StandardSeq n (app L M) (app L' N))
    (step : BetaAt i N N')
    (hle : n ≤ i + countRedexes L' + (if IsAbs L' then 1 else 0)) :
    StandardSeq (i + countRedexes L' + (if IsAbs L' then 1 else 0))
      (app L M) (app L' N')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_r_trans
items.doc: Compose an application sequence with a standard reduction of its operand.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_r_trans (h : StandardSeq n M M')
    (happ : StandardSeq i (app L M) (app L' M))
    (hc : i ≤ countRedexes L' + (if IsAbs L' then 1 else 0)) :
    ∃ d, StandardSeq d (app L M) (app L' M') ∧
      d ≤ n + countRedexes L' + (if IsAbs L' then 1 else 0)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.app_cong
items.doc: If operator and operand each reduce by a standard sequence, so does the application.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.app_cong (hL : StandardSeq n L L') (hM : StandardSeq b M M') :
    ∃ k, StandardSeq k (app L M) (app L' M')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.subst
items.doc: Standard reduction is preserved by substitution.
items.statement:
lemma Standard.subst (hM : M ⭢ₛ M') (hN : N ⭢ₛ N') (x : Var) (lc_N : LC N) (lc_N' : LC N') :
    (M[x := N]) ⭢ₛ (M'[x := N'])

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.of_beta_step
items.doc: A single full β-step is a standard reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.of_beta_step (step : M ⭢βᶠ N) (lc_M : LC M) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.to_redex
items.doc: Standard reduction is contained in full β-reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.to_redex (step : M ⭢ₛ N) : M ↠βᶠ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.abs_inv
items.doc:
If a standard reduction reaches an abstraction, then its leading Call-by-Name
reduction reaches an abstraction that standardly reduces to the same target.
items.statement:
lemma Standard.abs_inv (h : M ⭢ₛ N) (M' : Term Var) (eq : N = Term.abs M') :
    ∃ M'', M ↠ₙ Term.abs M'' ∧ Term.abs M'' ⭢ₛ Term.abs M'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.abs_subst
items.doc: Standard reduction of abstractions is preserved by opening.
items.statement:
lemma Standard.abs_subst
    (h_abs : Term.abs M ⭢ₛ Term.abs M') (hN : N ⭢ₛ N') (lc_N : LC N) (lc_N' : LC N') :
    (M ^ N) ⭢ₛ (M' ^ N')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.trans_step
items.doc: A standard reduction followed by a full β-step is a standard reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.trans_step (h1 : M ⭢ₛ P) (h2 : P ⭢βᶠ N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.trans_redex
items.doc: A standard reduction followed by a full β-reduction is a standard reduction.
items.statement: lemma Standard.trans_redex (h1 : M ⭢ₛ P) (h2 : P ↠βᶠ N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.trans
items.doc: Standard reduction is transitive.
items.statement: lemma Standard.trans (h1 : M ⭢ₛ P) (h2 : P ⭢ₛ N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.standardization
items.doc: The standardization theorem: every full β-reduction is a standard reduction.
items.statement: theorem Standard.standardization (lc_M : LC M) (step : M ↠βᶠ N) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.iff_redex
items.doc: Standard reduction coincides with full β-reduction on locally closed terms.
items.statement: theorem Standard.iff_redex (lc_M : LC M) : M ⭢ₛ N ↔ M ↠βᶠ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.lc_r
items.doc: Standard sequences preserve local closure.
items.statement: lemma StandardSeq.lc_r (h : StandardSeq n M N) (lc : LC M) : LC N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.abs_close
items.doc: Closing a variable and abstracting preserves a standard sequence.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.abs_close {x : Var} (h : StandardSeq n M M') (lc : LC M) :
    StandardSeq n (M⟦0 ↜ x⟧.abs) (M'⟦0 ↜ x⟧.abs)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.abs_cong
items.doc: Abstraction congruence for standard sequences.
items.statement:
lemma StandardSeq.abs_cong (xs : Finset Var)
    (cofin : ∀ x ∉ xs, ∃ n, StandardSeq n (M ^ fvar x) (M' ^ fvar x))
    (lc : LC (abs M)) : ∃ n, StandardSeq n (abs M) (abs M')

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.to_redex
items.doc: A standard sequence is a full β-reduction.
items.statement: lemma StandardSeq.to_redex (h : StandardSeq n M N) (lc_M : LC M) : M ↠βᶠ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.to_seq
items.doc: A standard reduction gives a standard β-reduction sequence.
items.statement: theorem Standard.to_seq (h : M ⭢ₛ N) : ∃ n, StandardSeq n M N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.StandardSeq.to_standard
items.doc: A standard β-reduction sequence gives a standard reduction.
items.statement: theorem StandardSeq.to_standard (h : StandardSeq n M N) (lc_M : LC M) : M ⭢ₛ N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Standard.iff_seq
items.doc: Standard reduction coincides with the existence of a standard β-reduction sequence.
items.statement: theorem Standard.iff_seq (lc_M : LC M) : M ⭢ₛ N ↔ ∃ n, StandardSeq n M N

modules.doc: Strong normalization (termination) for full beta-reduction of untyped lambda calculus.

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_step
items.doc: A single β-reduction step preserves strong normalization.
items.statement: lemma sn_step (t_st_t' : t ⭢βᶠ t') (sn_t : SN FullBeta t) : SN FullBeta t'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_steps
items.doc: Multiple β-reduction steps also preserve strong normalization.
items.statement: lemma sn_steps (t_st_t' : t ↠βᶠ t') (sn_t : SN FullBeta t) : SN FullBeta t'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_fvar
items.doc: Free variables are strongly normalizing.
items.statement: lemma sn_fvar {x : Var} : SN FullBeta (fvar x)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_app
items.doc:
An application is strongly normalizing if the left and right terms are strongly normalizing,
as well as all possible future top level abstraction application beta reductions
items.statement:
lemma sn_app (t s : Term Var) (sn_t : SN FullBeta t) (sn_s : SN FullBeta s)
    (hβ : ∀ {t' s' : Term Var}, t ↠βᶠ t'.abs → s ↠βᶠ s' → SN FullBeta (t' ^ s')) :
    SN FullBeta (t.app s)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_app_left
items.doc: The left side of a strongly normalizing application is strongly normalizing.
items.statement:
lemma sn_app_left (M N : Term Var) (lc_N : Term.LC N) (sn_MN : SN FullBeta (M.app N)) :
    SN FullBeta M

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_app_right
items.doc: The right side of a strongly normalizing application is strongly normalizing.
items.statement:
lemma sn_app_right (M N : Term Var) (lc_M : Term.LC M) (sn_MN : SN FullBeta (M.app N)) :
    SN FullBeta N

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.Neutral
items.doc:
A neutral term is a term of the form v t₁ … t_n where
v is a variable and t₁ … t_n are strongly normalizing terms.
items.statement: inductive Neutral : Term Var → Prop

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.neutral_step
items.doc: Neutral terms only reduce to other neutral terms in a single step
items.statement: lemma neutral_step (Hneut : Neutral t) (Hstep : t ⭢βᶠ t') : Neutral t'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.neutral_steps
items.doc: Neutral terms only reduce to other neutral terms in multiple steps
items.statement: lemma neutral_steps (Hneut : Neutral t) (Hsteps : t ↠βᶠ t') : Neutral t'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_neutral
items.doc: Neutral terms are strongly normalizing.
items.statement: lemma sn_neutral (Hneut : Neutral t) : SN FullBeta t

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_abs
items.doc: A lambda abstraction is strongly normalizing if its body is strongly normalizing.
items.statement:
lemma sn_abs [DecidableEq Var] [HasFresh Var] {M N : Term Var} (sn_MN : SN FullBeta (M ^ N))
    (lc_N : LC N) : SN FullBeta (abs M)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Untyped.Term.sn_abs_app_multiApp
items.doc:
A term of the form λ M N P_1 … P_n is strongly normalizing if
1. N is strongly normalizing,
1. M ^ N P₁ … Pₙ is strongly normalizing,
1. N is locally closed,
1. M ^ N P₁ … Pₙ is locally closed
items.statement:
lemma sn_abs_app_multiApp [DecidableEq Var] [HasFresh Var] {Ps} {M N : Term Var}
    (sn_N : SN FullBeta N) (sn_MNPs : SN FullBeta (multiApp (M ^ N) Ps))
    (lc_N : LC N) (lc_MNPs : LC (multiApp (M ^ N) Ps)) :
    SN FullBeta (multiApp (M.abs.app N) Ps)

modules.title: λ-calculus
modules.doc:
The untyped λ-calculus, with a named representation of variables. This file contains the definitions
of α-equivalence and capture-avoiding substitution.

## References

* [H. Barendregt, *Introduction to Lambda Calculus*][Barendregt1984]
* Definition of α-equivalence [M. Gabbay and A. Pitts, *A New Approach to Abstract Syntax with
Variable Binding*][Gabbay2002]

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term
items.doc: Syntax of terms.
items.statement:
inductive Term (Var : Type u) : Type u where
  | var (x : Var)
  | abs (x : Var) (m : Term Var)
  | app (m n : Term Var)
deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.fv
items.doc: Free variables.
items.statement: def fv : Term Var → Finset Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.bv
items.doc: Bound variables.
items.statement: def bv : Term Var → Finset Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.vars
items.doc: Variable names (free and bound) in a term.
items.statement: def vars : Term Var → Finset Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename
items.doc:
Variable renaming, applying to both free and bound variables.
`m.rename x y` changes all occurrences of `x` into `y` in `m`.
items.statement: def rename (m : Term Var) (x y : Var) : Term Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_eq_sizeOf
items.doc: Renaming preserves size.
items.statement: theorem rename_eq_sizeOf {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} : sizeOf (m.rename x y) = sizeOf m

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv
items.doc: α-equivalence.
items.statement:
inductive AlphaEquiv : Term Var → Term Var → Prop where
  | var {x} : AlphaEquiv (var x) (var x)
  | abs {y x1 x2 m1 m2} : y ∉ m1.vars ∪ m2.vars ∪ {x1, x2} →
    AlphaEquiv (m1.rename x1 y) (m2.rename x2 y) → AlphaEquiv (abs x1 m1) (abs x2 m2)
  | app {m1 n1 m2 n2} : AlphaEquiv m1 n1 → AlphaEquiv m2 n2 → AlphaEquiv (app m1 m2) (app n1 n2)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.instHasAlphaEquivTerm
items.doc: Instance for the notation `m =α n`.
items.statement: instance instHasAlphaEquivTerm : HasAlphaEquiv (Term Var)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv_def
items.doc: Allow grind to recognise the notation of α-equivalence.
items.statement: theorem AlphaEquiv_def (m n : Term Var) : m =α n ↔ AlphaEquiv m n

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Subst
items.doc: Capture-avoiding substitution, as an inference system.
items.statement:
inductive Subst : Term Var → Var → Term Var → Term Var → Prop where
  | varHit {x r} : (var x).Subst x r r
  | varMiss {x y r} : y ≠ x → (var y).Subst x r (var y)
  | absShadow {x m r} : (abs x m).Subst x r (abs x m)
  | absIn {x y m r m'} : y ∉ r.fv ∪ {x} → m.Subst x r m' → (abs y m).Subst x r (abs y m')
  | app {m n x r m' n'} : m.Subst x r m' → n.Subst x r n' → (app m n).Subst x r (app m' n')
  | alpha {m m' r r' n n' x} : m =α m' → r =α r' → n =α n' → Subst m x r n → m'.Subst x r' n'

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.subst
items.doc:
Capture-avoiding substitution. `m.subst x r` replaces the free occurrences of variable `x`
in `m` with `r`.
items.statement:
def subst (m : Term Var) (x : Var) (r : Term Var) :
    Term Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.instHasSubstitutionTerm
items.doc: `Term.subst` is a substitution for λ-terms. Gives access to the notation `m[x := n]`.
items.statement:
instance instHasSubstitutionTerm :
    HasSubstitution (Term Var) Var (Term Var)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.subst_def
items.doc: Allow grind to recognise the notation of substitution.
items.statement: theorem subst_def (m r : Term Var) (x : Var) : m[x := r] = m.subst x r

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Context
items.doc: Contexts.
items.statement:
inductive Context (Var : Type u) : Type u where
  | hole
  | abs (x : Var) (c : Context Var)
  | appL (c : Context Var) (m : Term Var)
  | appR (m : Term Var) (c : Context Var)
deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Context.fill
items.doc: Replaces the hole in a `Context` with a `Term`.
items.statement: def Context.fill (c : Context Var) (m : Term Var) : Term Var

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Context.vars
items.doc: Variables (both free and bound) in a context.
items.statement: def Context.vars : Context Var → Finset Var

modules.title: λ-calculus
modules.doc:
The untyped λ-calculus, with a named representation of variables. This file contains properties of
α-equivalence and capture-avoiding substitution.

## Main results

- `AlphaEquiv.refl`: reflexivity of α-equivalence
- `AlphaEquiv.symm`: symmetry of α-equivalence
- `AlphaEquiv.trans`: transitivity of α-equivalence
- `Subst.relation_iff_function`: the relational and functional definition of capture-avoiding
  substitution are equivalent, modulo alpha-equivalence
- `subst.commutativity`: commutativity of substitution, more commonly known as the
  "substitution lemma" (e.g. in [Barendregt1984])

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.vars_either_fv_or_bv
items.doc: A variable in a term is either free or bound.
items.statement: theorem vars_either_fv_or_bv {m : Term Var} : m.vars = m.fv ∪ m.bv

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_unused
items.doc: Renaming an unused variable has no effect.
items.statement: theorem rename_unused {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} : x ∉ m.vars → m.rename x y = m

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_same
items.doc: Renaming a variable to itself has no effect.
items.statement: theorem rename_same {m : Term Var} {x : Var} : m.rename x x = m

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_vars_used
items.doc: Renaming a used variable changes the set of variables.
items.statement:
theorem rename_vars_used {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} : x ∈ m.vars →
    (m.rename x y).vars = m.vars.erase x ∪ {y}

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_remove
items.doc: Renaming removes the variable.
items.statement: theorem rename_remove {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} : x ≠ y → x ∉ (m.rename x y).vars

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_vars
items.doc: The set of variables after renaming.
items.statement:
theorem rename_vars {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} :
    (m.rename x y).vars = m.vars \ {x} ∪ (if x ∈ m.vars then {y} else ∅)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_fv
items.doc: The set of free variables after renaming.
items.statement:
theorem rename_fv {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} :
    y ∉ m.vars → (m.rename x y).fv = m.fv \ {x} ∪ (if x ∈ m.fv then {y} else ∅)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_concat
items.doc: Concatenation of renaming.
items.statement:
theorem rename_concat {m : Term Var} {x y z : Var} : y ∉ m.vars →
    (m.rename x y).rename y z = m.rename x z

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_comm_fresh
items.doc: Commutativity of renaming distinct variables.
items.statement:
theorem rename_comm_fresh {m : Term Var} {x y z w : Var} :
    x ≠ z → y ∉ m.vars ∪ {x, z} → w ∉ m.vars ∪ {x, z} →
    (m.rename x y).rename z w = (m.rename z w).rename x y

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.rename_comm
items.doc: Commutativity of renaming.
items.statement:
theorem rename_comm {m : Term Var} {x y z w : Var} :
    y ∉ m.vars ∪ {x, z} → w ∉ m.vars ∪ {x, y, z} →
    (m.rename x y).rename (if z = x then y else z) w = (m.rename z w).rename x y

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.induction_by_sizeOf
Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.eq_sizeOf
items.doc: α-equivalent terms have the same size.
items.statement: theorem AlphaEquiv.eq_sizeOf {m n : Term Var} : m =α n → sizeOf m = sizeOf n

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.same_fv
items.doc: α-equivalent terms have the same free variables.
items.statement: theorem AlphaEquiv.same_fv {m n : Term Var} : m =α n → m.fv = n.fv

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.refl
items.doc: Reflexivity of α-equivalence.
items.statement: theorem AlphaEquiv.refl (m : Term Var) : m =α m

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.symm
items.doc: Symmetry of α-equivalence.
items.statement: theorem AlphaEquiv.symm {m n : Term Var} : m =α n → n =α m

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.rename_preserve
items.doc: Renaming α-equivalent terms produces α-equivalent terms.
items.statement:
theorem AlphaEquiv.rename_preserve (m n : Term Var) (x y : Var) :
    y ∉ m.vars ∪ n.vars → m =α n → (m.rename x y) =α (n.rename x y)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.abs_elim
items.doc:
Elimination rule for α-equivalence of abstractions.
It states that if two abstractions are α-equivalent,
then their bodies can be renamed to ``any'' fresh variable y and remain α-equivalent.
This is sometimes easier to use than using by_cases on the equivalence,
which can only produce the claim for ``some'' fresh y.
items.statement:
theorem AlphaEquiv.abs_elim {m1 m2 : Term Var} {x1 x2 y : Var} :
    y ∉ m1.vars ∪ m2.vars ∪ {x1, x2} → (Term.abs x1 m1) =α (Term.abs x2 m2) →
    (m1.rename x1 y) =α (m2.rename x2 y)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.trans
items.doc: Transitivity of α-equivalence.
items.statement: theorem AlphaEquiv.trans {m n p : Term Var} : m =α n → n =α p → m =α p

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.rename_non_fv
items.doc: Renaming a non-free variable results in an α-equivalent term
items.statement:
theorem AlphaEquiv.rename_non_fv {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} : x ∉ m.fv → y ∉ m.vars →
    m =α (m.rename x y)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.abs_non_fv
items.doc:
Abstracting over an arbitrary non-free variable results in the same term,
modulo α-equivalence.
items.statement:
theorem AlphaEquiv.abs_non_fv {m1 m2 : Term Var} {x1 x2 : Var} :
    m1 =α m2 → x1 ∉ m1.fv → x2 ∉ m2.fv → (Term.abs x1 m1) =α (Term.abs x2 m2)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.abs_rename
items.doc: Renaming an abstraction leads to an α-equivalent term.
items.statement:
theorem AlphaEquiv.abs_rename {m : Term Var} {x y : Var} :
    y ∉ m.vars ∪ {x} → (Term.abs x m) =α (Term.abs y (m.rename x y))

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Context.complete
items.doc:
Any `Term` can be obtained by filling a `Context` with a variable. This proves that `Context`
completely captures the syntax of terms.
items.statement: theorem Context.complete (m : Term Var) : ∃ (c : Context Var) (x : Var), m = (c.fill (var x))

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Context.fill_vars
items.doc: The set of variables after filling a context.
items.statement: theorem Context.fill_vars {c : Context Var} {m : Term Var} : (c.fill m).vars = c.vars ∪ m.vars

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.AlphaEquiv.context
items.doc: α-equivalence is preserved under context filling.
items.statement:
theorem AlphaEquiv.context {m n : Term Var} {c : Context Var} :
    m =α n → (c.fill m) =α (c.fill n)

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Subst.function_to_relation
items.doc: The functional definition of substitution satisfies the relational definition of substitution.
items.statement: theorem Subst.function_to_relation {m r : Term Var} {x : Var} : m.Subst x r (m[x := r])

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.subst.non_free
items.doc: Substituting a non-free variable has no effect.
items.statement: theorem subst.non_free {m r : Term Var} {x : Var} : x ∉ m.fv → (m[x := r]) =α m

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.subst.abs_fresh
items.doc:
Modulo α-equivalence, substituting an abstraction falls back to the fresh variable case only.
With this lemma, the three cases in the definition of subst can be reduced to one.
items.statement:
theorem subst.abs_fresh {m r : Term Var} {x y z : Var} : z ∉ m.vars ∪ r.vars ∪ {x, y} →
    ((Term.abs y m)[x := r]) =α (Term.abs z ((m.rename y z)[x := r]))

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.subst.preserve_AlphaEquiv
items.doc: Substituting α-equivalent terms produces α-equivalent terms.
items.statement:
theorem subst.preserve_AlphaEquiv {m m' r r' : Term Var} {x : Var} :
    m =α m' → r =α r' → (m[x := r]) =α (m'[x := r'])

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.Subst.relation_iff_function
items.doc:
The relational definition of substitution coincides with the functional definition of
substitution, modulo α-equivalence.
items.statement:
theorem Subst.relation_iff_function {m n r : Term Var} {x : Var} :
    m.Subst x r n ↔ n =α (m[x := r])

items.name: Cslib.LambdaCalculus.Named.Untyped.Term.subst.commutativity
items.doc: Commutativity of substitution (a.k.a. the substitution lemma)
items.statement:
theorem subst.commutativity {m r1 r2 : Term Var} {x y : Var} :
    x ∉ r2.fv ∪ {y} → ((m[x := r1])[y := r2]) =α ((m[y := r2])[x := (r1[y := r2])])

modules.title: Choreography
modules.doc:
A choreography defines the collective behaviour of a system of communicating participants
(processes) [Montesi2023].

## Limitations

Some notable features not yet included:
- Recursion (only the syntax is implemented, but no semantics).
- General recursion (the current syntax supports only tail recursion).
- Choreographic choice (for barriers, first-come/first-served patterns, etc.).
- Asynchronous communication.

## References

* [F. Montesi, *Introduction to Choreographies*][Montesi2023]

items.name: Cslib.Languages.Mech.Expr
items.doc: Expressions for local computation.
items.statement:
inductive Expr (Var Val FunId : Type*) where
  /-- Read variable `x`. -/
  | var (x : Var)
  /-- Value `v`. -/
  | val (v : Val)
  /-- Call function `f` with arguments `args`. -/
  | call (f : FunId) (args : List (Expr Var Val FunId))

items.name: Cslib.Languages.Mech.Prefix
items.doc: Choreographic prefix.
items.statement:
inductive Prefix (Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel : Type*) where
  /-- `p` assigns `x` the value computed from `e`. -/
  | assign (p : Pid) (x : Var) (e : Expr Var Val FunId)
  /-- `p` communicates the evaluation of `e` to `q`, which stores it in its variable `x`. -/
  | com (p : Pid) (e : Expr Var Val FunId) (q : Pid) (x : Var)
  /-- `p` communicates the selection label (a static tag used to denote a choice) to `q`. -/
  | sel (p : Pid) (q : Pid) (l : SelLabel)

items.name: Cslib.Languages.Mech.Choreography
items.doc: Choreographies.
items.statement:
inductive Choreography (Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName : Type*) where
  /-- The terminated choreography. -/
  | nil
  /-- Do `prf` and continue as `c`. -/
  | pre (prf : Prefix Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel)
    (c : Choreography Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName)
  /-- Conditional: `p` evaluates `e` to choose between `c₁` and `c₂`. -/
  | cond (p : Pid) (e : Expr Var Val FunId)
    (c₁ c₂ : Choreography Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName)
  /-- Call the procedure `proc`. -/
  | call (proc : ProcName) (ps : List Pid)

items.name: Cslib.Languages.Mech.Prefix.pn
items.doc: Process names in a prefix.
items.statement: def Prefix.pn : Prefix Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel → Finset Pid

items.name: Cslib.Languages.Mech.Choreography.pn
items.doc: Process names in a choreography.

modules.title: Local expressions, stores, and evaluation
modules.doc:
Choreographic programming and associated languages (like process calculi for modelling distributed
protocol implementations) are typically defined abstracting from how processes locally compute and
store values [Montesi2023]. This module defines this interface, as well as the derived concept of
global store.

## Implementation notes

The module is currently developed with minimality in mind. In the future, we plan on adding
facilities for typing expressions and easy integration with Lean and other IRs/FFIs.

## References

* [F. Montesi, *Introduction to Choreographies*][Montesi2023]

items.name: Cslib.Mech.Expr
items.doc: Expressions for local computation.
items.statement:
inductive Expr (Var Val FunId : Type*) where
  /-- Read variable `x`. -/
  | var (x : Var)
  /-- Value `v`. -/
  | val (v : Val)
  /-- Call function `f` with arguments `args`. -/
  | call (f : FunId) (args : List (Expr Var Val FunId))

items.name: Cslib.Mech.LocalStore
items.doc: A local store represents the memory state of a process, mapping variables to values.
items.statement: abbrev LocalStore Var Val

items.name: Cslib.Mech.FunCallEval
items.doc:
Type of (potentially nondeterministic) evaluation relations for local function calls at
processes.
items.statement: abbrev FunCallEval FunId Val

items.name: Cslib.Mech.FunCallEval.EvalExpr
items.doc: Evaluation relation for expressions.
items.statement:
inductive FunCallEval.EvalExpr (eval : FunCallEval FunId Val) :
    (σ : LocalStore Var Val) → (e : Expr Var Val FunId) → (v : Val) → Prop where
  /-- A value evaluates to itself. -/
  | val : eval.EvalExpr σ (.val v) v
  /-- A variable evaluates to its mapped value in the store. -/
  | var : eval.EvalExpr σ (.var x) (σ x)
  /-- A function call first recursively evaluates its expression arguments, and then
  invokes the parameter for function evaluation. -/
  | call
    (hArgs : List.Forall₂ (eval.EvalExpr σ) args vals)
    (hFun : eval f vals v) :
    eval.EvalExpr σ (.call f args) v

items.name: Cslib.Mech.GlobalStore
items.doc:
A global store represents the memory state of an entire system, mapping each process to its
local store.
items.statement: abbrev GlobalStore Pid Var Val

items.name: Cslib.Mech.AtPid
items.doc: Type of an element of type `α` located at a process.
items.statement: abbrev AtPid Pid α

items.name: Cslib.Mech.AtPid.pid
items.doc: The process name of a located element.
items.statement: abbrev AtPid.pid (a : AtPid Pid α)

items.name: Cslib.Mech.AtPid.elem
items.doc: The element of a located element.
items.statement: abbrev AtPid.elem (a : AtPid Pid α)

modules.title: Stateful Processes
modules.doc:
The language of Stateful Processes (SP for short), a process calculus
where processes communicate via message passing [Montesi2023]. Stateful processes or similar
languages are typically used to model implementations of choreographic programs (concurrent and/or
distributed protocols), but they are also designed to be used as abstract representations that can
be later compiled to executable mainstream languages.

## Limitations

The current formalisation does not cover process polymorphism (procedures do not take process
parameters) nor general recursion (this is the tail-recursive fragment of Stateful Processes).
For recursion, only the syntax is currently implemented. Its semantics will follow a similar
approach to that for `CCS`.

## Implementation notes

This development follows the presentation in [Montesi2023], with one difference: we adopt a modular
approach to the definition of operational semantics, by first defining a symbolic semantics from
which a concrete semantics is then derived by adding stores (process memory). This approach is
described in [Acclavio2026].

## References

* [M. Acclavio, G. Manara, F. Montesi, X. Qin, *Choreographic Programming: a Semantic Approach*][Acclavio2026]
* [F. Montesi, *Introduction to Choreographies*][Montesi2023]

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Prefix
items.doc: Prefixes.
items.statement:
inductive Prefix (Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel : Type*) where
  /-- Assign to `x` the result of evaluating `e`. -/
  | assign (x : Var) (e : Expr Var Val FunId)
  /-- Send to `p` the result of evaluating `e`. -/
  | sendValue (p : Pid) (e : Expr Var Val FunId)
  /-- Receive a value from `p` and store it in `x`. -/
  | recvValue (p : Pid) (x : Var)
  /-- Send to `p` the label `l`. -/
  | sendLabel (p : Pid) (l : SelLabel)

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Process
items.doc: Processes.
items.statement:
inductive Process (Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName : Type*) where
  /-- The terminated process. -/
  | nil
  /-- Execute the prefix `prf` and proceed as the continuation `pr`. -/
  | pre (prf : Prefix Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel) (pr : Process Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName)
  /-- Branching process: receives a selection label and continues accordingly. -/
  | recvLabel (p : Pid) (branches : List (SelLabel × Process Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName))
  /-- Conditional: evaluate `e` to choose between `pr₁` and `pr₂`. -/
  | cond (e : Expr Var Val FunId) (pr₁ pr₂ : Process Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName)
  /-- Call the procedure `proc`. -/
  | call (proc : ProcName) (ps : List Pid)

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Act
items.doc: Actions.
items.statement:
inductive Act (Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel : Type*) where
  /-- Assign to `x` the result of evaluating `e`. -/
  | assign (x : Var) (e : Expr Var Val FunId)
  /-- Send to `p` the result of evaluating `e`. -/
  | sendValue (p : Pid) (e : Expr Var Val FunId)
  /-- Receive a value from `p` and store it in variable `x`. -/
  | recvValue (p : Pid) (x : Var)
  /-- Send to `p` the selection label `l`. -/
  | sendLabel (p : Pid) (l : SelLabel)
  /-- Receive from `p` the selection label `l`. -/
  | recvLabel (p : Pid) (l : SelLabel)
  /-- Choose the then-branch of a conditional guarded by `e`. -/
  | condThen (e : Expr Var Val FunId)
  /-- Choose the else-branch of a conditional guarded by `e`. -/
  | condElse (e : Expr Var Val FunId)

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Act.isInternal
items.doc: An action is internal if it is not meant to interact with another process.
items.statement: def Act.isInternal : Act Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel → Bool

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Prefix.toAct
items.doc: Transforms a `Prefix` into an `Act`.
items.statement: abbrev Prefix.toAct : Prefix Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel → Act Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Process.Tr
items.doc:
Symbolic transition relation for processes.
Do not use this directly, use `Process.lts` instead.
items.statement:
inductive Process.Tr :
    Process Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName → Act Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel →
    Process Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName → Prop
  | pre : Tr (pre prf pr) prf.toAct (pr)
  | condThen : Tr (cond e pr₁ pr₂) (.condThen e) pr₁
  | condElse : Tr (cond e pr₁ pr₂) (.condElse e) pr₂
  | recvLabel (h : (l, pr) ∈ branches): Tr (recvLabel p branches) (.recvLabel p l) pr

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Process.lts
items.doc: Symbolic LTS of processes.
items.statement:
def Process.lts :
    LTS (Process Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName) (Act Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel)

modules.title: Networks of stateful processes and their semantics
modules.doc:
This module defines networks (maps from process names to process terms), as well as their symbolic
and concrete operational semantics.

## Implementation notes

We leverage the fact that networks are functions to formulate the semantics without requiring a
definition of parallel composition.

## References

* [F. Montesi, *Introduction to Choreographies*][Montesi2023]

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Network
items.doc: A network maps process names to process terms.
items.statement: abbrev Network (Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Network.TrLabel
items.doc: Symbolic transition labels for networks.
items.statement:
inductive Network.TrLabel Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel
  | local (p : Pid) (μ : Act Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel)
  | com (p : Pid) (e : Expr Var Val FunId) (q : Pid) (x : Var)
  | sel (p : Pid) (q : Pid) (l : SelLabel)

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Network.Tr
items.doc: Symbolic transition relation for networks.
items.statement:
inductive Network.Tr :
    Network Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName → TrLabel Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel →
    Network Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName → Prop
  | local
    (hμ : μ.isInternal) (htr : Process.lts.Tr (n p) μ prP)
    (hn' : n' = n[p := prP]) :
    Tr n (TrLabel.local p μ) n'
  | com
    (hsend : Process.lts.Tr (n p) (.sendValue q e) prP)
    (hrecv : Process.lts.Tr (n q) (.recvValue p x) prQ)
    (hn' : n' = n[p := prP][q := prQ]) :
    Tr n (TrLabel.com p e q x) n'
  | sel
    (hsend : Process.lts.Tr (n p) (.sendLabel q l) prP)
    (hrecv : Process.lts.Tr (n q) (.recvLabel p l) prQ)
    (hn' : n' = n[p := prP][q := prQ]) :
    Tr n (TrLabel.sel p q l) n'

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Network.lts
items.doc: Symbolic LTS of networks.
items.statement:
def Network.lts :
    LTS (Network Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName) (TrLabel Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel)

items.note: ## Stores, evaluation, and concrete semantics of networks

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Cfg
items.doc: Configurations, consisting of a network and a global store.
items.statement:
structure Cfg (Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName : Type*) where
  /-- The network of the configuration. -/
  net : Network Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName
  /-- The global store of the configuration. -/
  store : GlobalStore Pid Var Val

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Cfg.TrLabel
items.doc:
Transition labels for network configurations.

These labels model what can be observed from execution, and thus hide internal computational
details.
items.statement:
inductive Cfg.TrLabel Pid Val SelLabel
  | local (p : Pid)
  | com (p : Pid) (q : Pid) (v : Val)
  | sel (p : Pid) (q : Pid) (l : SelLabel)

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Cfg.Tr
items.doc: Transition relation for network configurations.
items.statement:
inductive Cfg.Tr [DecidableEq Var] (isTrue : Val → Bool) (Eval : FunCallEval FunId Val) :
    Cfg Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName → Cfg.TrLabel Pid Val SelLabel →
    Cfg Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName → Prop where
  -- Internal actions
  | assign
    (htr : Network.lts.Tr cfg.net (.local p (.assign x e)) cfg'.net)
    (heval : Eval.EvalExpr (cfg.store p) e v)
    (hstore : cfg'.store = cfg.store[(p, x) := v]) :
    Tr isTrue Eval cfg (Cfg.TrLabel.local p) cfg'
  | condThen
    (htr : Network.lts.Tr cfg.net (.local p (.condThen e)) cfg'.net)
    (heval : Eval.EvalExpr (cfg.store p) e v)
    (hguard : isTrue v)
    (hstore : cfg'.store = cfg.store) :
    Tr isTrue Eval cfg (Cfg.TrLabel.local p) cfg'
  | condElse
    (htr : Network.lts.Tr cfg.net (.local p (.condElse e)) cfg'.net)
    (heval : Eval.EvalExpr (cfg.store p) e v)
    (hguard : ¬isTrue v)
    (hstore : cfg'.store = cfg.store) :
    Tr isTrue Eval cfg (Cfg.TrLabel.local p) cfg'
  -- Interactions
  | com
    (htr : Network.lts.Tr cfg.net (.com p e q x) cfg'.net)
    (heval : Eval.EvalExpr (cfg.store p) e v)
    (hstore : cfg'.store = cfg.store[(q, x) := v]) :
    Tr isTrue Eval cfg (Cfg.TrLabel.com p q v) cfg'
  | sel
    (htr : Network.lts.Tr cfg.net (.sel p q l) cfg'.net)
    (hstore : cfg'.store = cfg.store) :
    Tr isTrue Eval cfg (Cfg.TrLabel.sel p q l) cfg'

items.name: Cslib.StatefulProcesses.Cfg.lts
items.doc: LTS of network configurations.
items.statement:
def Cfg.lts [DecidableEq Var] (isTrue : Val → Bool) (Eval : FunCallEval FunId Val) :
    LTS (Cfg Pid Var Val FunId SelLabel ProcName) (Cfg.TrLabel Pid Val SelLabel)

modules.title: Basic Temporal Logic (BTL)
modules.doc:
The basic temporal language has two unary modalities: `F` (sometime in the future) and
`P` (sometime in the past).

## Notation

Open `Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL` for the directions `F` and `P` and the judgement `BTL[m,w ⊨ φ]`.
With `Cslib.Logic` open, use the standard dynamic modalities `d⟨F⟩φ` and `d⟨P⟩φ` for
sometime in the future and past, and `d[F]φ` and `d[P]φ` for always in the future and past.
Satisfaction is expressed by `⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ φ]`, using the modal inference system.

## References

* [P. Blackburn, M. de Rijke, Y. Venema, *Modal Logic*][Blackburn2001]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Direction
items.doc: The two directions of the basic temporal language.
items.statement:
inductive Direction where
  /-- Into the future. -/
  | F
  /-- Into the past. -/
  | P
  deriving DecidableEq

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.τBTL
items.doc: The modal signature of the basic temporal language.
items.statement: abbrev τBTL : PFunctor

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Proposition
items.doc: Temporal propositions, with a unary modality for each direction.
items.statement: abbrev Proposition Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Proposition.always_eq_not_future_not
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.always_eq_not_future_not (φ : Proposition Atom) :
    (d[F]φ) = ¬d⟨F⟩¬φ

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Proposition.hasAlwaysBeen_eq_not_past_not
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.hasAlwaysBeen_eq_not_past_not (φ : Proposition Atom) :
    (d[P]φ) = ¬d⟨P⟩¬φ

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Model
items.doc:
A temporal model consists of an accessibility relation and a valuation at each world.

No order properties are imposed on the relation. In particular, the modalities include
the present only when the relation is reflexive at the current world, and the flow of time is
modelled only when the relation is transitive.
items.statement:
structure Model World Atom where
  /-- The accessibility relation. -/
  r : World → World → Prop
  /-- Valuation of atoms at each world. -/
  v : World → Atom → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Model.toFrame
items.doc:
The bidirectional frame of a temporal model.

This definition guarantees by construction that the future and past accessibility relations are
inverse of each other. Modally, this is witnessed by `btl_future_past_prop` and
`btl_past_future_prop`.
items.statement: def Model.toFrame (m : Model World Atom) : Frame World τBTL

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Model.toModal
items.doc: Interprets a temporal model as a unary modal model.
items.statement: def Model.toModal (m : Model World Atom) : Modal.Model World τBTL Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Model.toModal_toFrame
items.statement: theorem Model.toModal_toFrame (m : Model World Atom) : m.toModal.toFrame = m.toFrame

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Model.toFrame_future_iff
items.statement:
theorem Model.toFrame_future_iff (m : Model World Atom) (w w' : World) :
    m.toFrame.diagonal F w w' ↔ m.r w w'

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.BTL.Model.toFrame_past_iff
items.statement:
theorem Model.toFrame_past_iff (m : Model World Atom) (w w' : World) :
    m.toFrame.diagonal P w w' ↔ m.r w' w

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_atom_iff
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_atom_iff {a : Atom} : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ a] ↔ m.v w a

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_future_sometime_iff
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_future_sometime_iff : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d⟨F⟩φ] ↔ ∃ w', m.r w w' ∧ ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_past_sometime_iff
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_past_sometime_iff : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d⟨P⟩φ] ↔ ∃ w', m.r w' w ∧ ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_future_always_iff
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_future_always_iff : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d[F]φ] ↔ ∀ w', m.r w w' → ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_past_always_iff
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.btl_past_always_iff :
    ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d[P]φ] ↔ ∀ w', m.r w' w → ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_future_sometime_intro
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.btl_future_sometime_intro (hr : m.r w w') (h : ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]) :
    ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d⟨F⟩φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_past_sometime_intro
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.btl_past_sometime_intro (hr : m.r w' w) (h : ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]) :
    ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d⟨P⟩φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_future_always_elim
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_future_always_elim (h : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d[F]φ]) (hr : m.r w w') : ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_past_always_elim
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_past_always_elim (h : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ d[P]φ]) (hr : m.r w' w) : ⇓BTL[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_future_past
items.doc: If a proposition holds now, then it is always going to be the case that it was true.
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_future_past : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ φ → d[F](d⟨P⟩φ)]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.btl_past_future
items.doc: If a proposition holds now, then it has always been the case that it will be true.
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.btl_past_future : ⇓BTL[m,w ⊨ φ → d[P](d⟨F⟩φ)]

modules.authors: Fabrizio Montesi, Marco Peressotti, Alexandre Rademaker
modules.title: Hennessy-Milner Logic (HML)
modules.doc:
Hennessy-Milner Logic (HML) is a logic for reasoning about the behaviour of nondeterministic and
concurrent systems.

## Implementation notes
There are two main versions of HML. The original [Hennessy1985], which includes a negation
connective, and a variation without negation, for example as in [Aceto1999].
We follow the former and focus on a minimal set of connectives, recovering the others as derived
constructs.

## Main definitions

- `Proposition`: the language of propositions.
- `Satisfies lts s a`: in the LTS `lts`, the state `s` satisfies the proposition `a`.
- `denotation a`: the denotation of a proposition `a`, defined as the set of states that
satisfy `a`.
- `theory lts s`: the set of all propositions satisfied by state `s` in the LTS `lts`.

## Main statements

- `satisfies_mem_denotation`: the denotational semantics of HML is correct, in the sense that it
coincides with the notion of satisfiability.
- `not_theoryEq_satisfies`: if two states have different theories, then there exists a
distinguishing proposition that one state satisfies and the other does not.
- `theoryEq_eq_bisimilarity`: two states have the same theory iff they are bisimilar
(see `Bisimilarity`).

## References

* [M. Hennessy, R. Milner, *Algebraic Laws for Nondeterminism and Concurrency*][Hennessy1985]
* [L. Aceto, A. Ingólfsdóttir, *Testing Hennessy-Milner Logic with Recursion*][Aceto1999]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.HML.Proposition
items.doc: Propositions.
items.statement: abbrev Proposition (Label Atom : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.HML.Model
items.doc: An HML model consists of an LTS and a valuation for its states.
items.statement:
structure Model State Label Atom where
  /-- The labelled transition system. -/
  lts : LTS State Label
  /-- Valuation of atoms at states. -/
  v : State → Atom → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.HML.Model.toModal
items.doc: Converts an HML into a unary modal model.
items.statement: def Model.toModal (m : Model State Label Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.HML.Model.toModal_toFrame
items.statement:
theorem Model.toModal_toFrame (m : Model State Label Atom) :
    m.toModal.toFrame = m.lts.toFrame

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.hml_atom_iff
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.hml_atom_iff {p : Atom} : ⇓HML[m,s ⊨ p] ↔ m.v s p

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.hml_dynDiamond_iff_exists
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.hml_dynDiamond_iff_exists :
    ⇓HML[m,s ⊨ d⟨μ⟩φ] ↔ ∃ s', m.lts.Tr s μ s' ∧ ⇓HML[m,s' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.hml_dynBox_iff_forall
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.hml_dynBox_iff_forall :
    ⇓HML[m,s ⊨ d[μ]φ] ↔ ∀ s', m.lts.Tr s μ s' → ⇓HML[m,s' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.hml_dynDiamond_intro
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.hml_dynDiamond_intro (htr : m.lts.Tr s μ s')
    (h : ⇓HML[m,s' ⊨ φ]) : ⇓HML[m,s ⊨ d⟨μ⟩φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.hml_dynBox_elim
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.hml_dynBox_elim (hbox : ⇓HML[m,s ⊨ d[μ]φ])
    (htr : m.lts.Tr s μ s') : ⇓HML[m,s' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.propositions
items.doc: The list of propositions over finite μ-derivatives.
items.statement: noncomputable def propositions : List (HML.Proposition Label Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.propositions_complete
items.statement: theorem propositions_complete (s' : m.lts.image s μ) : stateMap s' ∈ propositions stateMap

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.propositions_satisfies_conjunction
items.statement:
theorem propositions_satisfies_conjunction (htr : m.lts.Tr s1 μ s1')
    (hdist_spec : ∀ s2', ⇓HML[m,s1' ⊨ (stateMap s2')]) :
    ⇓HML[m,s1 ⊨ d⟨μ⟩(⋀(propositions stateMap))]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.theoryEq_isBisimulation
items.doc: Theory equivalence is a bisimulation.
items.statement:
theorem theoryEq_isBisimulation
    [image_finite : ∀ s μ, Finite (m.lts.image s μ)] :
    m.lts.IsHomBisimulation (TheoryEq m.toModal)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.bisimulation_satisfies
items.doc: If two states are in a bisimulation, one satisfies a proposition iff the other does.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.bisimulation_theoryEq
Cslib.Logic.Modal.theoryEq_eq_bisimilarity
items.doc: Theory equivalence and bisimilarity coincide for image-finite LTSs.
items.statement:
theorem theoryEq_eq_bisimilarity
    [image_finite : ∀ s μ, Finite (m.lts.image s μ)]
    (hv : ∀ {s1 s2}, s1 ~[m.lts] s2 → ∀ p, m.v s1 p ↔ m.v s2 p := by grind) :
    TheoryEq m.toModal = HomBisimilarity m.lts

* [J.-Y. Girard, *Linear Logic: its syntax and semantics*][Girard1995]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition
items.doc: Propositions.
items.statement:
inductive Proposition (Atom : Type u) : Type u where
  | atom (x : Atom)
  | atomDual (x : Atom)
  | one
  | zero
  | top
  | bot
  /-- The multiplicative conjunction connective. -/
  | tensor (a b : Proposition Atom)
  /-- The multiplicative disjunction connective. -/
  | parr (a b : Proposition Atom)
  /-- The additive disjunction connective. -/
  | oplus (a b : Proposition Atom)
  /-- The additive conjunction connective. -/
  | with (a b : Proposition Atom)
  /-- The "of course" exponential. -/
  | bang (a : Proposition Atom)
  /-- The "why not" exponential.
  This is written as ʔ, or \_?, to distinguish itself from the lean syntatical hole ? syntax -/
  | quest (a : Proposition Atom)
deriving DecidableEq, BEq

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.Context
items.doc: Propositional contexts (single-hole contexts for propositions).
items.statement:
inductive Proposition.Context (Atom : Type u) : Type u where
  | hole
  | tensorL (c : Context Atom) (b : Proposition Atom)
  | tensorR (a : Proposition Atom) (c : Context Atom)
  | parrL (c : Context Atom) (b : Proposition Atom)
  | parrR (a : Proposition Atom) (c : Context Atom)
  | oplusL (c : Context Atom) (b : Proposition Atom)
  | oplusR (a : Proposition Atom) (c : Context Atom)
  | withL (c : Context Atom) (b : Proposition Atom)
  | withR (a : Proposition Atom) (c : Context Atom)
  | bang (c : Context Atom)
  | quest (c : Context Atom)
deriving DecidableEq, BEq

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.Context.fill
items.doc: Replaces the hole in a propositional context with a propositions.
items.statement: def Proposition.Context.fill (c : Context Atom) (a : Proposition Atom) : Proposition Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.context_fill_def
items.doc: Definition of context filling.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.context_fill_def (c : Context Atom) (a : Proposition Atom) :
  c<[a] = c.fill a

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.positive

items.statement: def Proposition.positive : Proposition Atom → Bool

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.negative

items.statement: def Proposition.dual : Proposition Atom → Proposition Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.top_eq_zero_dual
items.statement: theorem Proposition.top_eq_zero_dual : ⊤ = (0⫠ : Proposition Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.dual_sizeOf

items.statement: theorem Proposition.dual_inj (a b : Proposition Atom) : a⫠ = b⫠ ↔ a = b

items.doc: Linear implication.
items.statement: def Proposition.linImpl (a b : Proposition Atom) : Proposition Atom

items.doc: A sequent in CLL is a multiset of propositions.

items.statement: def Sequent.allQuest (Γ : Sequent Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proof
items.doc: A proof in the sequent calculus for classical linear logic.
items.statement:
inductive Proof : Sequent Atom → Type u where
  | ax : Proof {a, a⫠}
  | cut : Proof (a ::ₘ Γ) → Proof (a⫠ ::ₘ Δ) → Proof (Γ + Δ)
  | one : Proof {1}
  | bot : Proof Γ → Proof (⊥ ::ₘ Γ)
  | parr : Proof (a ::ₘ b ::ₘ Γ) → Proof ((a ⅋ b) ::ₘ Γ)
  | tensor : Proof (a ::ₘ Γ) → Proof (b ::ₘ Δ) → Proof ((a ⊗ b) ::ₘ (Γ + Δ))
  | oplus₁ : Proof (a ::ₘ Γ) → Proof ((a ⊕ b) ::ₘ Γ)
  | oplus₂ : Proof (b ::ₘ Γ) → Proof ((a ⊕ b) ::ₘ Γ)
  | with : Proof (a ::ₘ Γ) → Proof (b ::ₘ Γ) → Proof ((a & b) ::ₘ Γ)
  | top : Proof (⊤ ::ₘ Γ)
  | quest : Proof (a ::ₘ Γ) → Proof (ʔa ::ₘ Γ)
  | weaken : Proof Γ → Proof (ʔa ::ₘ Γ)
  | contract : Proof (ʔa ::ₘ ʔa ::ₘ Γ) → Proof (ʔa ::ₘ Γ)
  | bang {Γ : Sequent Atom} {a} : Γ.allQuest → Proof (a ::ₘ Γ) → Proof ((!a) ::ₘ Γ)

Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other and vice versa.

items.statement: theorem Proposition.equiv.toProp (h : a ≡⇓ b) : a ≡ b

items.statement: noncomputable def chooseEquiv (h : a ≡ b) : a ≡⇓ b

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.equiv.symm

modules.title: Multiplicative Classical Linear Logic (MLL)
modules.doc:
Multiplicative classical linear logic, defined as a fragment of classical linear logic by means of
a predicate (unbundled style) and `Subtype` (bundled style).

This file serves as the reference example of how to define a fragment of an inference system
through tagging of `InferenceSystem` and `Subtype`, following the next recipe. It is a work in
progress: the recipe will evolve together with how the Lean and CSLib ecosystems can
deal with this general problem.

1. Define predicates for restricting relevant types to the fragment, here `IsMLL` for propositions
(`CLL.Proposition`) and proofs (`CLL.Proof`). This part lives under the namespace of the original
system (here `Cslib.Logic.CLL`). Custom recursors can be defined for convenient case analysis that
automatically discharges irrelevant cases (those not in the fragment).
2. Define the inference system in the fragment -- here `MLL.Proof` -- as an abbreviation of
a subtype. This part lives under the namespace of the fragment (here `Cslib.Logic.CLL.MLL`).

We also call the first part the 'unbundled part' and the second the 'bundled part'.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.IsMLL
items.doc: A proposition is in the multiplicative fragment of CLL.
items.statement: def Proposition.IsMLL : Proposition Atom → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.IsMLL.rec
items.doc: Recursor for MLL propositions.
items.statement:
def Proposition.IsMLL.rec
    {motive : {a : Proposition Atom} → (h : a.IsMLL) → Sort u}
    (atom : ∀ x : Atom, motive (a := .atom x) (by simp))
    (atomDual : ∀ x : Atom, motive (a := .atomDual x) (by simp))
    (one : motive (a := .one) (by simp))
    (bot : motive (a := .bot) (by simp))
    (tensor : ∀ (a b : Proposition Atom) {ha : a.IsMLL} {hb : b.IsMLL},
      motive ha → motive hb → motive (a :=.tensor a b) (by simp [ha,hb]))
    (parr : ∀ (a b : Proposition Atom) {ha : a.IsMLL} {hb : b.IsMLL},
      motive ha → motive hb → motive (a := .parr a b) (by simp [ha,hb]))
    {a : Proposition Atom} (h : a.IsMLL) : motive (a := a) h

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.isMLL_dual
items.doc: Duality in MLL stays in MLL.
items.statement: theorem Proposition.isMLL_dual {a : Proposition Atom} (ha : a.IsMLL) : a⫠.IsMLL

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.Context.IsMLL
items.doc: A multiplicative propositional context.
items.statement: def Proposition.Context.IsMLL : Context Atom → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proposition.Context.isMLL_fill
items.doc: Filling a multiplicative propositional context with a multiplicative proposition stays in MLL.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.Context.isMLL_fill {c : CLL.Proposition.Context Atom} {a : CLL.Proposition Atom}
    (hc : c.IsMLL) : (c.fill a).IsMLL ↔ a.IsMLL

items.doc: A multiplicative sequent.
items.statement: def Sequent.IsMLL (Γ : Sequent Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proof.IsMLL
items.doc: A proof is in MLL.
items.statement: def Proof.IsMLL {Γ : Sequent Atom} : ⇓Γ → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proof.IsMLL.rec
items.doc: Recursor for MLL derivations.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proof.isMLL_sequent
items.doc: A proof in the MLL fragment can only prove MLL sequents.
items.statement: theorem Proof.isMLL_sequent {Γ : Sequent Atom} {p : ⇓Γ} (h : p.IsMLL) : Γ.IsMLL

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.Proof.isMLL_cutFree
items.doc: If a CLL derivation is cut-free and concludes an MLL sequent, then it is an MLL derivation.
items.statement:
theorem Proof.isMLL_cutFree {Γ : Sequent Atom} (p : ⇓Γ) (hΓ : Γ.IsMLL)
    (hp : p.cutFree) : p.IsMLL

items.doc: MLL derivations.
items.statement: abbrev MLL.Proof (Γ : CLL.Sequent Atom)

items.doc: Tag for the MLL inference system.
items.statement: opaque MLL : Type
