modules.title: Phase semantics for Classical Linear Logic
modules.doc:
This file develops the phase semantics for Classical Linear Logic (CLL), providing an
algebraic interpretation of linear logic propositions in terms of phase spaces.

Phase semantics is a denotational semantics for linear logic where
propositions are interpreted as subsets of a commutative monoid, and logical operations
correspond to specific set-theoretic operations.

## Main definitions

* `PhaseSpace`: A commutative monoid equipped with a distinguished subset ⊥
* `PhaseSpace.imp`: Linear implication `X ⊸ Y` between sets in a phase space
* `PhaseSpace.orthogonal`: The orthogonal `X⫠` of a set X
* `PhaseSpace.isFact`: A fact is a set that equals its biorthogonal closure
* `Fact`: The type of facts in a phase space
* `PhaseSpace.FactExpr`: Inductive type for representing operations on facts
* `PhaseSpace.interpret`: Interpretation of the connectives on facts
* `PhaseSpace.interpProp`: Interpretation of CLL propositions as facts in a phase space

## Main results

* `PhaseSpace.biorthogonalClosure`: The biorthogonal operation forms a closure operator
* `PhaseSpace.orth_iUnion`: Orthogonal of union equals intersection of orthogonals
* `PhaseSpace.sInf_isFact` and `PhaseSpace.inter_isFact_of_isFact`: Facts are closed under
  intersections
* `PhaseSpace.biorth_least_fact`: The biorthogonal closure gives the smallest fact containing a set

Several lemmas about facts and orthogonality useful in the proof of soundness are proven here.

…
## References

* [J.-Y. Girard, *Linear logic*][Girard1987]
* [J.-Y. Girard, *Linear Logic: its syntax and semantics*][Girard1995]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace
items.doc:
A phase space is a commutative monoid M equipped with a distinguished subset ⊥.
This forms the algebraic foundation for interpreting linear logic propositions.
items.statement:
class PhaseSpace (M : Type u) extends CommMonoid M where
  /-- The distinguished subset ⊥ used to define orthogonality -/
  bot : Set M

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.imp
items.doc:
Implication between two sets in a phase space: the set of elements `m` such that
for all `x ∈ X`, we have `m * x ∈ Y`.
items.statement: def imp [PhaseSpace M] (X Y : Set M) : Set M

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.orthogonal
items.doc: The orthogonal `X⫠` of a set X: the set of elements that map X into ⊥ under multiplication.
items.statement: def orthogonal (G : Set P) : Set P

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.orthogonal_def
items.statement: lemma orthogonal_def (X : Set P) : X⫠ = {m | ∀ x ∈ X, m * x ∈ bot}

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.orth_antitone
items.doc: The orthogonal operation is antitone: if X ⊆ Y then Y⫠ ⊆ X⫠.
items.statement: lemma orth_antitone {X Y : Set P} (hXY : X ⊆ Y) : Y⫠ ⊆ X⫠

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.orth_extensive
items.doc: The biorthogonal operation is extensive: X ⊆ X⫠⫠ for any set X.
items.statement: lemma orth_extensive (X : Set P) : X ⊆ X⫠⫠

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.triple_orth
items.doc: The triple orthogonal equals the orthogonal: X⫠⫠⫠ = X⫠.
items.statement: lemma triple_orth (X : Set P) : X⫠⫠⫠ = X⫠

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.triple_dual
items.statement: lemma triple_dual {G : Set P} : G⫠⫠⫠⫠⫠ = G⫠⫠⫠

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.biorthogonalClosure
items.doc: The biorthogonal closure operator on sets in a phase space.
items.statement: def biorthogonalClosure : ClosureOperator (Set P)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.orth_iUnion
items.doc:
Given a phase space (P, ⊥) and a family of subsets (Gᵢ) of P indexed by i ∈ I, we have that
(⋃ᵢ Gᵢ)⫠ = ⋂ᵢ Gᵢ⫠.
items.statement:
lemma orth_iUnion {ι : Sort*} (G : ι → Set P) :
    (⋃ i, G i)⫠ = ⋂ i, (G i)⫠

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.iInter_biorth_eq_orth_iUnion_orth
items.doc:
Given a phase space (P, ⊥) and a family of subsets (Gᵢ) of P indexed by i ∈ I, we have that
∩ᵢ Gᵢ⫠⫠ = (∪ᵢ Gᵢ⫠)⫠.
items.statement:
lemma iInter_biorth_eq_orth_iUnion_orth {ι : Sort*} (G : ι → Set P) :
    (⋂ i, (G i)⫠⫠ : Set P) = (⋃ i, (G i)⫠)⫠

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.isFact
items.doc: A fact is a subset of a phase space that equals its biorthogonal closure.
items.statement: def isFact (X : Set P) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.CLL.PhaseSpace.Fact
items.doc: The type of facts in a phase space.
items.statement:
structure Fact (P : Type*) [PhaseSpace P] where
  /-- The underlying set that is a fact -/
  (carrier : Set P)
  (property : isFact carrier)

modules.title: Modal Logic
modules.doc:
Modal logic is a logic for reasoning about (possibly polyadic) relational structures, studying
**qualified** statements through the use of **modalities** (like necessity, possibility, knowledge,
belief, permission, etc.).

This module formalises general modal logic, parameterised over a signature of modal operators. A
signature is formalised as a polynomial functor (`PFunctor`), generalising the concept of modal
similarity types from the literature [Blackburn2001].

## Implementation notes

- Compared to [Blackburn2001], a triangle takes a map of arguments (from the argument type given
  by the polynomial functor to propositions), instead of a sequence of arguments.
- The use of `τ` to range over signatures of modal operators comes from the literature
  [Blackburn2001].

## References

* [P. Blackburn, M. de Rijke, Y. Venema, *Modal Logic*][Blackburn2001]
* The definitions of theory equivalence and the denotational semantics of worlds are inspired by
  the development of `Cslib.Logic.HML`.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition
items.doc: A modal proposition.
items.statement:
inductive Proposition (τ : PFunctor) (Atom : Type u) where
  /-- Atomic proposition. -/
  | atom (p : Atom)
  /-- Falsehood. -/
  | false
  /-- Negation. -/
  | not (φ : Proposition τ Atom)
  /-- Disjunction. -/
  | or (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom)
  /-- Generalised possibility, or triangle. -/
  | triangle (op : τ.A) (φs : τ.B op → Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap
items.doc: A map of propositions for the operator `op` in the polynomial functor `τ`.
items.statement: abbrev PropositionMap τ op Atom

items.statement: lemma Proposition.false_def : (.false : Proposition (τ := τ) (Atom := Atom)) = ⊥

items.statement: lemma Proposition.not_def (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : φ.not = ¬φ

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.triangle_def
items.statement:
lemma Proposition.triangle_def {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A)
    (φs : τ.B op → Proposition τ Atom) : Proposition.triangle op φs = (Δ[op]φs)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.true
items.doc: Truth.
items.statement: def Proposition.true : Proposition τ Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.true_def
items.statement: lemma Proposition.true_def : Proposition.true (τ := τ) (Atom := Atom) = ⊤

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.and
items.doc: Conjunction.
items.statement: def Proposition.and (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.and_def
items.statement: lemma Proposition.and_def (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) : φ₁.and φ₂ = (φ₁ ∧ φ₂)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.imp
items.doc: Implication.
items.statement: def Proposition.imp (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.imp_def
items.statement: lemma Proposition.imp_def (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) : φ₁.imp φ₂ = (φ₁ → φ₂)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.iff
items.doc: Bi-implication.
items.statement: def Proposition.iff (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.iff_def
items.statement: lemma Proposition.iff_def (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) : φ₁.iff φ₂ = (φ₁ ↔ φ₂)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.not
items.doc: Point-wise negation of a proposition map.
items.statement: def PropositionMap.not (φs : PropositionMap τ op Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.not_apply
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.not_apply {φs : PropositionMap τ op Atom} (i : τ.B op) :
    (¬φs) i = ¬(φs i)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.and
items.doc: Point-wise conjunction of proposition maps.
items.statement: def PropositionMap.and (φs₁ φs₂ : PropositionMap τ op Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.and_apply
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.and_apply (φs₁ φs₂ : PropositionMap τ op Atom) (i : τ.B op) :
    (φs₁ ∧ φs₂) i = (φs₁ i ∧ φs₂ i)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.or
items.doc: Point-wise disjunction of proposition maps.
items.statement: def PropositionMap.or (φs₁ φs₂ : PropositionMap τ op Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.imp
items.doc: Point-wise implication of proposition maps.
items.statement: def PropositionMap.imp (φs₁ φs₂ : PropositionMap τ op Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.iff
items.doc: Point-wise bi-implication of proposition maps.
items.statement: def PropositionMap.iff (φs₁ φs₂ : PropositionMap τ op Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.or_apply
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.or_apply (φs ψs : PropositionMap τ op Atom) (i : τ.B op) :
    (φs ∨ ψs) i = (φs i ∨ ψs i)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.imp_apply
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.imp_apply (φs ψs : PropositionMap τ op Atom) (i : τ.B op) :
    (φs → ψs) i = (φs i → ψs i)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.iff_apply
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.iff_apply (φs ψs : PropositionMap τ op Atom) (i : τ.B op) :
    (φs ↔ ψs) i = (φs i ↔ ψs i)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.nabla
items.doc: Generalised necessity, or nabla (∇), dual of triangle.
items.statement: def Proposition.nabla {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A) (φs : τ.B op → Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.nabla_def
items.statement:
lemma Proposition.nabla_def {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A)
    (φs : τ.B op → Proposition τ Atom) : Proposition.nabla op φs = (∇[op]φs)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.const
items.doc:
The constant proposition map for the operator `op`, used for applying a modality uniformly. This
supplies the same proposition `φ` to every argument position of `op`.
items.statement:
abbrev PropositionMap.const {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A) (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    PropositionMap τ op Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.const_not
items.doc: Negation commutes with constant proposition maps.
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.const_not {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A) (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    PropositionMap.const op (¬φ) = ¬PropositionMap.const op φ

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.const_and
items.doc: Conjunction commutes with constant proposition maps.
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.const_and {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A) (φ ψ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    PropositionMap.const op (φ ∧ ψ) = (PropositionMap.const op φ ∧ PropositionMap.const op ψ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.const_or
items.doc: Disjunction commutes with constant proposition maps.
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.const_or {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A) (φ ψ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    PropositionMap.const op (φ ∨ ψ) = (PropositionMap.const op φ ∨ PropositionMap.const op ψ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.const_imp
items.doc: Implication commutes with constant proposition maps.
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.const_imp {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A) (φ ψ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    PropositionMap.const op (φ → ψ) = (PropositionMap.const op φ → PropositionMap.const op ψ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.const_iff
items.doc: Bi-implication commutes with constant proposition maps.
items.statement:
theorem PropositionMap.const_iff {τ : PFunctor} (op : τ.A) (φ ψ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    PropositionMap.const op (φ ↔ ψ) = (PropositionMap.const op φ ↔ PropositionMap.const op ψ)

modules.title: Denotational semantics for Modal Logic
modules.doc:
A denotational semantics for modal logic, inspired by the one for Hennessy-Milner Logic
(`Cslib.Logic.HML`).

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.denotation
items.doc: Denotation of a proposition.
items.statement:
def Proposition.denotation (m : Model World τ Atom) :
    Proposition τ Atom → Set World

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.satisfies_mem_denotation
items.doc: Characterisation theorem for the denotational semantics.
items.statement:
theorem satisfies_mem_denotation {m : Model World τ Atom} {φ : Proposition τ Atom} :
    w ∈ φ.denotation m ↔ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.not_denotation
items.doc:
A world is in the denotation of a proposition iff it is not in the denotation of the negation
of the proposition.
items.statement:
theorem not_denotation {m : Model World τ Atom} (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    w ∉ (¬φ).denotation m ↔ w ∈ φ.denotation m

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.theoryEq_denotation_eq
items.doc: Two worlds are theory-equivalent iff they are denotationally equivalent.
items.statement:
theorem theoryEq_denotation_eq {m : Model World τ Atom} {w₁ w₂ : World} :
    (TheoryEq m w₁ w₂) ↔
    (∀ (φ : Proposition τ Atom), w₁ ∈ (φ.denotation m) ↔ w₂ ∈ (φ.denotation m))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equiv_iff_denotation_eq
items.doc: Logically equivalent propositions under a model have the same denotation.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equiv_iff_denotation_eq :
    (φ₁ ≡[Equiv m] φ₂) ↔ φ₁.denotation m = φ₂.denotation m

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.denotation_eq_of_equiv
items.doc: `grind`-friendly first part of `Proposition.equiv_iff_denotation_eq`.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.denotation_eq_of_equiv (h : φ₁ ≡[Equiv m] φ₂) :
    φ₁.denotation m = φ₂.denotation m

modules.title: Modal Logic for Lean
modules.doc:
This module develops the interplay between modal logic and Lean's propositional language, in order
to enable the use of modal logic to reason about standard Lean relations using `Prop`.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Model.ofPredicates
items.doc:
Given a frame `f` on `α`, constructs the modal model whose worlds are elements of `α`
and whose atoms are Lean predicates on `α` (`α → Prop`).

Valuation checks that a world satisfies a predicate. For example, under `Model.ofPredicates r`, `□P`
at `a : α` means that `P a'` holds at every `a'` such that `r a a'`.
items.statement: abbrev ofPredicates (f : Frame α τ) : Model α τ (α → Prop)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Model.ofContainers
items.doc:
Given a frame `f` on `α` and a container type `β` for `α` (`Membership α β`), constructs the
modal model whose worlds are elements of `α` and whose atoms are of type `β`.

Valuation is membership. For example, under `Model.ofContainers r`, `□b` at `a : α` means that
`a' ∈ b` holds for every `a'` such that `r a a'`.
items.statement: abbrev ofContainers [Membership α β] (f : Frame α τ) : Model α τ β

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Model.ofSets
items.doc: Abbreviation for `Model.ofContainers` where the container type is a `Set`.
items.statement: abbrev ofSets (f : Frame α τ) : Model α τ (Set α)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Model.ofSets_v_eq_ofPredicates_v
items.doc:
The valuations of the set model and the predicate model of a frame agree under
`Set.ofPred`.
items.statement:
theorem ofSets_v_eq_ofPredicates_v (f : Frame α τ) (w : α) (P : α → Prop) :
    (ofSets f).v w (.ofPred P) = (ofPredicates f).v w P

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.ofPredicates_atom_iff
items.doc: Under `Model.ofPredicates r`, an atomic proposition `P` holds at `a` iff `P a`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.ofPredicates_atom_iff {P : α → Prop} (f : Frame α τ) :
    ⇓Modal[ofPredicates f,a ⊨ P] ↔ P a

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.ofPredicates_preservesMap_iff
items.doc:
In the predicate model generated by `f`, `P → ∇[op]Ps` holds everywhere iff `op`
preserves the predicate map `Ps` from `P`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.ofPredicates_preservesMap_iff {P : α → Prop} {Ps : τ.B op → α → Prop}
    (f : Frame α τ) :
    (∀ w, ⇓Modal[ofPredicates f,w ⊨ P → ∇[op](fun i => (Ps i : Proposition τ (α → Prop)))]) ↔
      f.PreservesMap op P Ps

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.ofContainers_atom_iff
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.ofContainers_atom_iff [Membership α β] {f : Frame α τ} {b : β} :
    ⇓Modal[Model.ofContainers f,w ⊨ (b : Proposition τ β)] ↔ w ∈ b

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Equiv.OfPredicates
items.doc: Logical equivalence under `Model.ofPredicates`.
items.statement: abbrev Proposition.Equiv.OfPredicates (f : Frame α τ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Equiv.OfContainers
items.doc: Logical equivalence under `Model.ofContainers`.
items.statement: abbrev Proposition.Equiv.OfContainers [Membership α β] (f : Frame α τ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equivOfPredicates_denotation_eq
items.doc:
Logically equivalent propositions under `Equiv.OfPredicates f` have the same denotation in the
Lean modal model induced by `ofPredicates f`.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equivOfPredicates_denotation_eq {f : Frame α τ}
    {φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ (α → Prop)} :
    (φ₁ ≡[Equiv.OfPredicates f] φ₂) ↔
      φ₁.denotation (ofPredicates f) = φ₂.denotation (ofPredicates f)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equivOfContainers_denotation_eq
items.doc:
Logically equivalent propositions under `Equiv.OfContainers f` have the same denotation in the
modal model induced by `Model.ofContainers f`.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equivOfContainers_denotation_eq
    [Membership α β] {f : Frame α τ} {φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ β} :
    (φ₁ ≡[Equiv.OfContainers (β := β) f] φ₂) ↔
      φ₁.denotation (ofContainers f) = φ₂.denotation (ofContainers f)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equivOfPredicates_and
items.doc:
Pointwise conjunction of Lean predicates is logically equivalent to their modal conjunction in
the predicate model induced by `f`.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equivOfPredicates_and
    {f : Frame α τ} {P Q : α → Prop} :
    (fun a => P a ∧ Q a) ≡[Equiv.OfPredicates f] (P ∧ Q)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.ofContainers_inf_equiv
items.doc:
Under `Equiv.OfContainers f`, if membership in the infimum of two containers is equivalent to
membership in both containers, then atomic infimum is logically equivalent to modal conjunction.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.ofContainers_inf_equiv
    [Membership α β] [Min β] (f : Frame α τ) (p q : β)
    (h : ∀ x, x ∈ p ⊓ q ↔ x ∈ p ∧ x ∈ q) :
    (↑(p ⊓ q) : Proposition τ β) ≡[Equiv.OfContainers f] (p ∧ q)

modules.title: Logical Equivalence in Modal Logic
modules.doc:
This module defines logical equivalence for modal propositions.
The definitions are parametric on the class of models under consideration.

We also instantiate `LogicalEquivalence` for Modal Logic K, i.e., equivalence
for the class of all models.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Equiv
items.doc: The modal propositions `φ₁` and `φ₂` are equivalent in the model `m`.
items.statement: def Proposition.Equiv (m : Model World τ Atom) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equiv_def
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equiv_def (m : Model World τ Atom) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    (φ₁.Equiv m φ₂) ↔ φ₁ ≡[Equiv m] φ₂

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equiv_iff_forall_der
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equiv_iff_forall_der (m : Model World τ Atom) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom)
    : (φ₁ ≡[Equiv m] φ₂) ↔ ∀ (w : World), ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁ ↔ φ₂]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equiv_iff_forall_iff
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equiv_iff_forall_iff {m : Model World τ Atom} {φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom} :
    (φ₁ ≡[Equiv m] φ₂) ↔ ∀ (w : World), ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁] ↔ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₂]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.ModelClass
items.doc: A class of models, defined as a set.
items.statement: abbrev ModelClass (World : Type*) (τ : PFunctor) (Atom : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.EquivWithin
items.doc: The modal propositions `φ₁` and `φ₂` are equivalent in the model class `S`.
items.statement: def Proposition.EquivWithin (S : ModelClass World τ Atom) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.UEquiv
items.doc: Universal logical equivalence: `φ₁` and `φ₂` are equivalent in the class of all models.
items.statement: abbrev Proposition.UEquiv {World : Type*} (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equivWithin_def
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equivWithin_def (S : ModelClass World τ Atom) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    φ₁.EquivWithin S φ₂ ↔ (φ₁ ≡[EquivWithin S] φ₂)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equivWithin_iff_forall_iff
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equivWithin_iff_forall_iff :
    (φ₁ ≡[EquivWithin S] φ₂) ↔ ∀ m ∈ S, φ₁ ≡[Equiv m] φ₂

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equiv_of_EquivWithin
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equiv_of_EquivWithin {S : ModelClass World τ Atom} (h : φ₁ ≡[EquivWithin S] φ₂)
    (m : Model World τ Atom) (hm : m ∈ S) : φ₁ ≡[Equiv m] φ₂

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equivWithin_valid
items.doc: Logical equivalence preserves validity.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equivWithin_valid (S : ModelClass World τ Atom)
    (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) (h : φ₁ ≡[EquivWithin S] φ₂) :
    (φ₁.valid S ↔ φ₂.valid S)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.PropositionMap.Without
items.doc: A proposition map missing a particular case (index).
items.statement: abbrev PropositionMap.Without (τ : PFunctor) (Atom : Type*) (op : τ.A) (i : τ.B op)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Context
items.doc: Propositional contexts.
items.statement:
inductive Proposition.Context (τ : PFunctor) (Atom : Type u) where
  | hole
  | not (c : Context τ Atom)
  | andL (c : Context τ Atom) (φ : Proposition τ Atom)
  | andR (φ : Proposition τ Atom) (c : Context τ Atom)
  | triangle (op : τ.A) (i : τ.B op) (c : Context τ Atom)
    (φs : PropositionMap.Without τ Atom op i)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Context.fill
items.doc: Replaces a hole in a propositional context with a proposition.
items.statement:
def Proposition.Context.fill {τ : PFunctor} [τ.DecidableEqChildren] {Atom : Type*}
    (c : Context τ Atom) (φ : Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Context.fill_def
Cslib.Logic.Modal.Judgement.Context
items.doc: Judgemental contexts.
items.statement:
structure Judgement.Context (World : Type*) (τ : PFunctor) (Atom : Type*) where
  /-- The model to consider. -/
  m : Model World τ Atom
  /-- The world to check propositions against. -/
  w : World

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Judgement.Context.fill
items.doc: Fills a judgemental context with a proposition.
items.statement:
def Judgement.Context.fill (c : Judgement.Context World τ Atom) (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Judgement World τ Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Judgement.Context.fill_def
items.statement:
lemma Judgement.Context.fill_def {c : Judgement.Context World τ Atom} {φ : Proposition τ Atom} :
    Modal[c.m,c.w ⊨ φ] = c<[φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.axiom_iff_forall_equiv
items.doc: Correspondence of equivalence and axiom validity.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.axiom_iff_forall_equiv (f : Frame World τ) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    (Axiom f⇓(φ₁ ↔ φ₂)) ↔ ∀ v, φ₁ ≡[Equiv ⟨f, v⟩] φ₂

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.equiv_of_axiom
items.doc: A frame-valid bi-implication induces logical equivalence in every model over that frame.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.equiv_of_axiom {f : Frame World τ} {φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom}
    (h : Axiom f⇓(φ₁ ↔ φ₂)) (v : World → Atom → Prop) : φ₁ ≡[Equiv ⟨f, v⟩] φ₂

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.axiom_iff_equivWithin_modelsOfFrame
items.doc: A bi-implication is an axiom of `f` iff its sides are equivalent in every model over `f`.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.axiom_iff_equivWithin_modelsOfFrame
    (f : Frame World τ) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(φ₁ ↔ φ₂) ↔ φ₁ ≡[EquivWithin (modelsOfFrame f)] φ₂

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.dual_equiv
items.doc: Triangle and the negation of the dual nabla are universally logically equivalent.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.dual_equiv (φs : PropositionMap τ op Atom) :
    Δ[op]φs ≡[UEquiv (World := World)] ¬∇[op]¬φs

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Model
items.doc: A model is a frame equipped with a valuation of atoms at worlds.
items.statement:
structure Model (World : Type u) (τ : PFunctor) (Atom : Type v) extends Frame World τ where
  /-- Valuation of atoms at a world. -/
  v : World → Atom → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies
items.doc:
Satisfaction relation. `Satisfies m w φ` means that, in the model `m`, the world `w` satisfies
the proposition `φ`.
items.statement: def Satisfies (m : Model World τ Atom) (w : World) : Proposition τ Atom → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Judgement
items.doc: Judgement, representing the conclusions one reaches in modal logic.
items.statement:
structure Judgement World τ Atom where
  /-- Constructs a judgement. -/
  mk ::
  /-- Model. -/
  m : Model World τ Atom
  /-- The world satisfying the proposition `φ`. -/
  w : World
  /-- The proposition satisfied by the world `w`. -/
  φ : Proposition τ Atom

@[inherit_doc] scoped notation "Modal[" m "," w " ⊨ " φ "]" => Judgement.mk m w φ

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.Bundled
items.doc: Satisfaction for judgements. This just refers to the unbundled `Satisfies`.
items.statement: def Satisfies.Bundled (j : Judgement World τ Atom) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.derivation_def
items.statement:
theorem derivation_def {m : Model World τ Atom} {w : World} {φ : Proposition τ Atom} :
  Satisfies m w φ = ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.atom_iff
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.atom_iff {a : Atom} : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ a] ↔ m.v w a

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.false
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.false : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ ⊥] ↔ False

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.not_iff_not
items.doc: A world satisfies a proposition iff it does not satisfy the negation of the proposition.
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.not_iff_not : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ ¬φ] ↔ ¬⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.true
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.true : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ ⊤]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.or_iff_or
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.or_iff_or {m : Model World τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁ ∨ φ₂] ↔ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁] ∨ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₂]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.triangle_iff_exists
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.triangle_iff_exists {m : Model World τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ Δ[op]φs] ↔ ∃ ws, m.r op w ws ∧ ∀ i, ⇓Modal[m,(ws i) ⊨ (φs i)]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.triangle_not_iff_exists_not
Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.and_iff_and
items.doc:
Characterisation of the `∧` connective.

Conjunction is defined in terms of the more primitive connectives given in `Proposition`.
This result proves that the definition is correct.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.and_iff_and {m : Model World τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁ ∧ φ₂] ↔ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁] ∧ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₂]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.imp_iff_imp
items.doc:
Characterisation of the `→` connective.

Implication is defined in terms of the more primitive connectives given in `Proposition`.
This result proves that the definition is correct.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.imp_iff_imp {m : Model World τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁ → φ₂] ↔ (⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁] → ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₂])

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.iff_iff_iff
items.doc:
Characterisation of the `↔` connective.

Bi-implication is defined in terms of the more primitive connectives given in `Proposition`.
This result proves that the definition is correct.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.iff_iff_iff {m : Model World τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁ ↔ φ₂] ↔ (⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₁] ↔ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ₂])

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.nabla_iff_forall
items.doc:
Characterisation of `∇`.

Necessity is defined in terms of the more primitive connectives given in `Proposition`.
This result proves that the definition is correct.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.nabla_iff_forall {m : Model World τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ ∇[op]φs] ↔ ∀ ws, m.r op w ws → ∃ i, ⇓Modal[m,(ws i) ⊨ (φs i)]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.finiteAnd_iff_forall
items.doc: A state satisfies a finite conjunction iff it satisfies all conjuncts.
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.finiteAnd_iff_forall : ⇓Modal[m,s ⊨ ⋀φs] ↔ ∀ φ ∈ φs, ⇓Modal[m,s ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.finiteOr_iff_exists
items.doc: A state satisfies a finite disjunction iff it satisfies some disjunct.
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.finiteOr_iff_exists : ⇓Modal[m,s ⊨ ⋁φs] ↔ ∃ φ ∈ φs, ⇓Modal[m,s ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.theory
items.doc: The theory of a world in a model is the set of all propositions that it satisfies.
items.statement:
abbrev theory {World : Type*} {τ : PFunctor} {Atom : Type*} (m : Model World τ Atom)
    (w : World) : Set (Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.TheoryEq
items.doc: Two worlds are theory-equivalent under a model if they have the same theory.
items.statement: abbrev TheoryEq (m : Model World τ Atom) (w₁ w₂ : World)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.TheoryEq.ext_iff
items.statement: theorem TheoryEq.ext_iff : TheoryEq m w₁ w₂ ↔ (∀ φ, φ ∈ theory m w₁ ↔ φ ∈ theory m w₂)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.satisfies_theory
items.doc: Any proposition satisfied by a world is in the theory of that world.
items.statement: theorem satisfies_theory (h : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ]) : φ ∈ theory m w

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.not_theoryEq_satisfies
items.doc: If two worlds are not theory equivalent, there exists a distinguishing proposition.
items.statement:
lemma not_theoryEq_satisfies (h : ¬TheoryEq m w₁ w₂) :
    ∃ φ, (⇓Modal[m,w₁ ⊨ φ] ∧ ¬⇓Modal[m,w₂ ⊨ φ])

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.theoryEq_satisfies
items.doc:
If two worlds are theory equivalent and the former satisfies a proposition, the latter does as
well.
items.statement:
theorem theoryEq_satisfies {m : Model World τ Atom} (h : TheoryEq m w₁ w₂)
    (hs : Satisfies m w₁ φ) : ⇓Modal[m,w₂ ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Axiom
items.doc: Every frame induces an inference system tag for proving valid axioms under the frame.
items.statement: inductive Axiom (f : Frame World τ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.axiom_def
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.axiom_def (f : Frame World τ) :
    (∀ v w, ⇓Modal[⟨f,v⟩,w ⊨ φ]) ↔ Axiom f⇓φ

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.der_of_axiom
items.statement: theorem Satisfies.der_of_axiom (h : Axiom m.toFrame⇓φ) : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.of_axiom
items.doc: If a proposition is an axiom under the frame of a model, it is satisfied by every world.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.of_axiom (m : Model World τ Atom) (φ : Proposition τ Atom) (h : Axiom m.toFrame⇓φ)
    (w : World) : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.subst_apply_iff
Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.k
items.doc:
Axiom K, valid for all frames.

This is from Definition 4.13 in [Blackburn2001].
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.k (f : Frame World τ) {φs : PropositionMap τ op Atom} [DecidableEq (τ.B op)]
    {i : τ.B op} {φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom} (hi : φs i = (φ₁ → φ₂)) :
    Axiom f⇓(∇[op]φs → (∇[op]φs[i := φ₁] → ∇[op]φs[i := φ₂]))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.dual
items.doc:
The dual axiom, valid for all frames.

This is from Definition 4.13 in [Blackburn2001].
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.dual (f : Frame World τ) {φs : PropositionMap τ op Atom} :
    Axiom f⇓(Δ[op]φs ↔ ¬∇[op]¬φs)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.triangle_and
items.doc: Possibility preserves conjunction.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.triangle_and (f : Frame World τ) (φs₁ φs₂ : PropositionMap τ op Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(Δ[op](φs₁ ∧ φs₂) → (Δ[op]φs₁ ∧ Δ[op]φs₂))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.triangle_and_nabla
items.doc:
Possibility can be combined with necessity.

This generalises the unimodal law `◇φ₁ ∧ □φ₂ → ◇(φ₁ ∧ φ₂)`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.triangle_and_nabla {m : Model World τ Atom} [DecidableEq (τ.B op)]
    (h : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ Δ[op]φs₁ ∧ ∇[op]φs₂]) : ∃ i, ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ Δ[op]φs₁[i := φs₁ i ∧ φs₂ i]]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.triangle_of_nabla
items.doc:
If `φ₁` is necessary and some successor exists, then some successor satisfies `φ₁`.

This generalises the unimodal law `□φ₁ ∧ ◇φ₂ → ◇φ₁`.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.triangle_of_diagonal
items.doc:
If the diagonal relation for `op` is reflexive, a world satisfying `φ` also satisfies `Δ[op]`
with `φ` at every argument position.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.t
items.doc:
Axiom T, valid for all frames with reflexive diagonals.

This generalises the unimodal law `φ → ◇φ`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.t (f : Frame World τ) [instRefl : Std.Refl (f.diagonal op)]
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Axiom f⇓(φ → Δ[op](PropositionMap.const op φ))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.t_refl
items.doc: Any frame admitting T for `op` has a reflexive diagonal relation.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.t_refl (f : Frame World τ) {op : τ.A} [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ φ : Proposition τ Atom, Axiom f⇓(φ → Δ[op](PropositionMap.const op φ))) :
    Std.Refl (f.diagonal op)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.t_nabla_triangle
items.doc:
In any model whose diagonal relation for `op` is reflexive, `∇[op]φ → φ` is equivalent to
`φ → Δ[op]φ`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.t_nabla_triangle (f : Frame World τ) [Std.Refl (f.diagonal op)] :
    Axiom f⇓((∇[op](PropositionMap.const op φ) → φ) ↔ (φ → Δ[op](PropositionMap.const op φ)))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.b
items.doc: Axiom B, valid for diagonally symmetric frames.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.b (f : Frame World τ) [f.DiagonalSymm op] (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(φ → ∇[op](PropositionMap.const op (Δ[op](PropositionMap.const op φ))))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.b_symm
items.doc: Any frame that admits B at `op` is diagonally symmetric at `op`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.b_symm (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ φ : Proposition τ Atom,
      Axiom f⇓(φ → ∇[op](PropositionMap.const op (Δ[op](PropositionMap.const op φ))))) :
    f.DiagonalSymm op

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.four
items.doc: The 4 axiom, valid for transitive frames.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.four (f : Frame World τ) [f.Trans op]
    (φs ψs : PropositionMap τ op Atom) (i : τ.B op)
    (hi : φs i = (Δ[op]ψs)) :
    Axiom f⇓(Δ[op]φs → Δ[op]ψs)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.four_trans
items.doc: Any frame that admits 4 at `op` is transitive at `op`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.four_trans (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (e : τ.B op ↪ Atom) (h : ∀ (φs ψs : PropositionMap τ op Atom) (i : τ.B op),
      φs i = (Δ[op]ψs) → Axiom f⇓(Δ[op]φs → Δ[op]ψs)) : f.Trans op

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.five
items.doc: Axiom 5, valid for right-Euclidean frames.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.five (f : Frame World τ) [f.RightEuclidean op]
    (φs : PropositionMap τ op Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(Δ[op]φs → ∇[op](PropositionMap.const op (Δ[op]φs)))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.five_rightEuclidean
items.doc: Any frame that admits 5 at `op` is right-Euclidean at `op`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.five_rightEuclidean (f : Frame World τ) (e : τ.B op ↪ Atom)
    (h : ∀ φs : PropositionMap τ op Atom,
      Axiom f⇓(Δ[op]φs → ∇[op](PropositionMap.const op (Δ[op]φs)))) : f.RightEuclidean op

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.valid
items.doc:
A proposition is valid in a class of models `S` (modelled as a set) if it is satisfied under
all models in `S` for all worlds.

Corresponds to Definition 1.28 (for classes of models) in [Blackburn2001].
items.statement:
def Proposition.valid {World : Type*} {τ : PFunctor} {Atom : Type*} (S : Set (Model World τ Atom))
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.logic
items.doc:
The modal logic of a class of models `S` is the set of all propositions valid in `S`.

Corresponds to Definition 1.28 (for classes of models) in [Blackburn2001].
items.statement:
def logic {World : Type*} {τ : PFunctor} {Atom : Type*} (S : Set (Model World τ Atom)) :
    Set (Proposition τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.logic_antitone
items.doc: Modal logic is antitone (wrt the class of models).
items.statement:
theorem logic_antitone {World : Type*} {τ : PFunctor} {Atom : Type*} :
    Antitone (logic (World := World) (τ := τ) (Atom := Atom))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.modelsOfFrame
items.doc: The class of all models generated by a frame (relation).
items.statement:
abbrev modelsOfFrame {World : Type*} {τ : PFunctor} {Atom : Type*} (f : Frame World τ) :
    Set (Model World τ Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.axiom_iff_mem_logic_modelsOfFrame
items.doc:
A proposition is an axiom of a frame exactly when it belongs to the logic of all models over
that frame.
items.statement:
theorem axiom_iff_mem_logic_modelsOfFrame (f : Frame World τ) (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓φ ↔ φ ∈ logic (modelsOfFrame f)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Context.dynDiamond
items.doc: Context constructor for the dynamic diamond modality.
items.statement: def Proposition.Context.dynDiamond (c : Context τ Atom) (a : τ.A) : Context τ Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.unary_triangle_eq_dynDiamond
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.unary_triangle_eq_dynDiamond {a : τ.A}
    (φs : PropositionMap τ a Atom) : (Δ[a]φs) = d⟨a⟩(φs default)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.dynDiamond_iff_exists
Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.dynBox_iff_forall
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.dynBox_iff_forall {m : Model World τ Atom} {φ : Proposition τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ d[a]φ] ↔ ∀ w', m.toFrame.diagonal a w w' → ⇓Modal[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.dynBox_dynDiamond_diagonalInverse₁
items.doc: If two operators `op₁` and `op₂` have inverse diagonal relations, then `φ → d[op₁](d⟨op₂⟩φ)`.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.dynBox_dynDiamond_diagonalInverse₂
items.doc: If two operators `op₁` and `op₂` have inverse diagonal relations, then `φ → d[op₂](d⟨op₁⟩φ)`.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unary_dual
items.doc: The dual axiom (reformulated for unary modal logic).
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unary_dual (f : Frame World τ) {a : τ.A} {φ : Proposition τ Atom} :
    Axiom f⇓(d⟨a⟩φ ↔ ¬d[a]¬φ)

modules.title: Basic Modal Logic
modules.doc:
Basic modal logic is the modal logic with a single unary modality.

## References

* [P. Blackburn, M. de Rijke, Y. Venema, *Modal Logic*][Blackburn2001]

items.name: Cslib.Frame.rel
items.doc: The accessibility relation of a unimodal frame.
items.statement: def rel (f : Frame World τ) : World → World → Prop

items.name: Cslib.Frame.rel_iff_diagonal
items.statement:
theorem rel_iff_diagonal (f : Frame World τ) (w w' : World) :
    f.rel w w' ↔ f.diagonal default w w'

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelation
items.doc: Builds a unimodal frame out of a binary relation.
items.statement: def ofRelation (r : World → World → Prop) : Frame World τ

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelation_rel
items.statement: theorem ofRelation_rel (r : World → World → Prop) : Frame.rel (Frame.ofRelation (τ := τ) r) = r

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelation_rel_iff
items.statement:
theorem ofRelation_rel_iff (r : World → World → Prop) (w w' : World) :
    (ofRelation (τ := τ) r).rel w w' ↔ r w w'

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelation_rel_of
items.statement:
theorem ofRelation_rel_of {r : World → World → Prop} {w w' : World}
    (h : r w w') : (ofRelation (τ := τ) r).rel w w'

items.name: Cslib.Frame.preservesMap_const_iff_preserves
items.statement:
theorem preservesMap_const_iff_preserves {r : α → α → Prop} {P : α → Prop} :
    (ofRelation (τ := τ) r).PreservesMap default P (fun _ => P) ↔ Preserves r P

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.diamond_iff_exists
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.diamond_iff_exists {m : Model World τ Atom} {φ : Proposition τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ ◇φ] ↔ ∃ w', m.rel w w' ∧ ⇓Modal[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.diamond_of
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.diamond_of {m : Model World τ Atom} {φ : Proposition τ Atom}
    (hr : m.toFrame.rel w w') (hφ : ⇓Modal[m,w' ⊨ φ]) : ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ ◇φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.box_iff_forall
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.box_iff_forall {m : Model World τ Atom} {φ : Proposition τ Atom} :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ □φ] ↔ ∀ w', m.rel w w' → ⇓Modal[m,w' ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_k
items.doc: Axiom K for unimodal logic.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_k (f : Frame World τ) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(□(φ₁ → φ₂) → (□φ₁ → □φ₂))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_dual
items.doc: The dual axiom for unimodal logic.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_dual (f : Frame World τ) (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(◇φ ↔ ¬□¬φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.diamond_and
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.diamond_and (f : Frame World τ) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(◇(φ₁ ∧ φ₂) → (◇φ₁ ∧ ◇φ₂))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.diamond_and_box
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.diamond_and_box (f : Frame World τ) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓((◇φ₁ ∧ □φ₂) → ◇(φ₁ ∧ φ₂))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.diamond_of_box
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.diamond_of_box (f : Frame World τ) (φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(□φ₁ ∧ ◇φ₂ → ◇φ₁)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_t
items.doc: Axiom T.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_t (f : Frame World τ) [instRefl : Std.Refl f.rel]
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Axiom f⇓(φ → ◇φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_t_refl
items.doc: Any frame that admits T is reflexive.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_t_refl (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ φ : Proposition τ Atom, Axiom f⇓(φ → ◇φ)) : Std.Refl f.rel

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.t_box_diamond
items.doc: In any reflexive model, `□φ → φ` is equivalent to `φ → ◇φ`.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.t_box_diamond {m : Model World τ Atom} [Std.Refl m.rel] :
    ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ □φ → φ] ↔ ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ φ → ◇φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_b
items.doc: Axiom B.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_b (f : Frame World τ) [Std.Symm f.rel]
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Axiom f⇓(φ → □◇φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_b_symm
items.doc: Any frame that admits B is symmetric.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_b_symm (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ φ : Proposition τ Atom, Axiom f⇓(φ → □◇φ)) : Std.Symm f.rel

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_four
items.doc: Axiom 4, valid for all transitive frames.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_four (f : Frame World τ) [IsTrans World f.rel]
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Axiom f⇓(◇◇φ → ◇φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_four_trans
items.doc: Any frame that admits 4 is transitive.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_four_trans (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ (φ : Proposition τ Atom), Axiom f⇓(◇◇φ → ◇φ)) : IsTrans World f.rel

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_five
items.doc: Axiom 5.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_five (f : Frame World τ) [Relation.RightEuclidean f.rel]
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Axiom f⇓(◇φ → □◇φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.unimodal_five_rightEuclidean
items.doc: Any frame that admits 5 is right Euclidean.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.unimodal_five_rightEuclidean (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ φ : Proposition τ Atom, Axiom f⇓(◇φ → □◇φ)) :
    Relation.RightEuclidean f.rel

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.d
items.doc: Axiom D, valid for all serial frames.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.d (f : Frame World τ) [Relation.Serial f.rel]
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Axiom f⇓(□φ → ◇φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.d_serial
items.doc: Any model that admits D is serial.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.d_serial (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ φ : Proposition τ Atom, Axiom f⇓(□φ → ◇φ)) : Relation.Serial f.rel

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.l
items.doc: The L axiom, or Löb's theorem, valid for all transitive and converse well-founded models.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.l (f : Frame World τ) [IsTrans World f.rel]
    (hwf : Relation.Terminating f.rel) (φ : Proposition τ Atom) :
    Axiom f⇓(□(□φ → φ) → □φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.l_induction
items.doc: Löb induction, via the L axiom.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.l_induction (m : Model World τ Atom) [IsTrans World m.rel]
    (hwf : Relation.Terminating m.rel) (hstep : ∀ w, ⇓Modal[m,w ⊨ □φ → φ]) (w : World) :
    ⇓Modal[m, w ⊨ φ]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.pointTwo
items.doc: Axiom .2, valid for all frames with the diamond property.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.pointTwo (f : Frame World τ) (h : Diamond f.rel)
    (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : Axiom f⇓(◇□φ → □◇φ)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Satisfies.pointTwo_diamond
items.doc: Any model that admits axiom .2 has the diamond property.
items.statement:
theorem Satisfies.pointTwo_diamond (f : Frame World τ) [Nonempty Atom]
    (h : ∀ φ : Proposition τ Atom, Axiom f⇓(◇□φ → □◇φ)) : Diamond f.rel

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.diamond_and_equiv_of_preserves
items.doc:
In a transitive diamond model, possibility distributes over conjunction for propositions
whose satisfaction is preserved along accessibility.
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.diamond_and_equiv_of_preserves {m : Model World τ Atom}
    [IsTrans World m.rel] {φ₁ φ₂ : Proposition τ Atom} (hd : Diamond m.rel)
    (h₁ : Preserves m.rel (⇓Modal[m,· ⊨ φ₁])) (h₂ : Preserves m.rel (⇓Modal[m,· ⊨ φ₂])) :
    ◇(φ₁ ∧ φ₂) ≡[Equiv m] (◇φ₁ ∧ ◇φ₂)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.diamond_diamond_equiv
items.doc: In a reflexive and transitive model, diamond absorbs itself (idempotency).
items.statement:
theorem Proposition.diamond_diamond_equiv {m : Model World τ Atom} [Std.Refl m.rel]
    [IsTrans World m.rel] (φ : Proposition τ Atom) : ◇◇φ ≡[Equiv m] ◇φ

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.Context.diamond
items.doc: Context constructor for the diamond modality.
items.statement: def Proposition.Context.diamond (c : Context τ Atom) : Context τ Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.τUnimodal
items.doc: Constructs a signature for basic modal logic at the same universe level of the input type.
items.statement: def τUnimodal (_ : Type u) : PFunctor.{u,u}

items.name: Cslib.Frame.ofRelation_unimodal_rel_iff
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Cslib.Frame.ofRelation_unimodal_rel_iff
    (r : World → World → Prop) (w w' : World) :
    (Frame.ofRelation (τ := τUnimodal World) r).rel w w' ↔ r w w'

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Unimodal.Model
items.doc: A basic model, constructed on `τUnimodal`.
items.statement: abbrev Model World Atom

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Unimodal.Proposition
items.doc: The language of modal propositions instantiated for `τUnimodal Atom`.
items.statement: abbrev Proposition Atom

modules.title: Modal Logic Cube
modules.doc:
This module formalises the Modal Cube for basic modal logic, including all the 15 foundational modal
logics and their relationships.

## References

* [P. Blackburn, M. de Rijke, Y. Venema, *Modal Logic*][Blackburn2001]

modules.title: Modal Logic for scalar multiplication (SMul)
modules.doc:
Any scalar multiplication operation `•` induces an accessibility relation where two elements are
related if the latter is the result of applying a scalar multiplication to the former.

Properties of the operator translate to properties of the relation, for example a semigroup action
on a commutative semigroup yields a relation with the `Diamond` property. This bridge allows for
studying properties of the operation using modal logic.

items.name: Relation.ofSMul
items.doc:
The accessibility relation induced by a scalar multiplication operation: `x` is related to `y`
when there exists `m` such that `m • x = y`.
items.statement: def ofSMul (M α : Type*) [SMul M α] (x y : α) : Prop

items.name: Relation.ofSMul_diamond
items.doc: The relation induced by an action commuting with itself has the diamond property.
items.statement: theorem ofSMul_diamond [SMul M α] [SMulCommClass M M α] : Diamond (ofSMul M α)

items.name: Relation.ofSMul_preserves_iff
items.doc: Preservation by an action-induced relation is exactly closure under the action.
items.statement:
theorem ofSMul_preserves_iff [SMul M α] {P : α → Prop} :
    Preserves (ofSMul M α) P ↔ ∀ m : M, ∀ x, P x → P (m • x)

items.name: Relation.ofSMul_preserves_mem
items.doc:
Membership in a type closed under a scalar action is preserved by the relation induced by the
action.
items.statement:
theorem ofSMul_preserves_mem [SMul M α] [SetLike S α] [SMulMemClass S M α]
    (s : S) : Preserves (ofSMul M α) (· ∈ s)

items.name: Relation.ofSMul_mem_of_mem
items.statement:
theorem ofSMul_mem_of_mem [SMul M α] [SetLike S α] [SMulMemClass S M α]
    {p : S} {a b : α} (hab : Relation.ofSMul M α a b) (ha : a ∈ p) : b ∈ p

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.ofSMul_diamond_denotation
items.doc: Characterisation of the denotation of a `◇p` under `ofSMul`.
items.statement:
theorem ofSMul_diamond_denotation [SMul M α] [Membership α β] (p : β) :
    (◇p : Proposition τ β).denotation
      (Model.ofContainers (Frame.ofRelation (Relation.ofSMul M α))) =
      {x | ∃ m : M, m • x ∈ p}

items.name: Cslib.Logic.Modal.Proposition.ofSMul_diamond_and_equiv
items.doc:
For `SetLike` objects closed under a commutative semigroup action, simultaneous reachability is
equivalent to separate reachability.
items.statement:
theorem ofSMul_diamond_and_equiv [CommSemigroup M] [SemigroupAction M α] [SetLike S α]
    [SMulMemClass S M α] (p q : S) :
    ◇(p ∧ q : Proposition τ S) ≡[Equiv.OfContainers
      (Frame.ofRelation (τ := τ) (Relation.ofSMul M α))
    ] (◇p ∧ ◇q)

modules.title: Propositions and theories
modules.doc:
## Main definitions

- `Proposition` : the type of propositions over a given type of atom.
- `IsIntuitionistic` : an inference system on `Proposition Atom` is intuitionistic if it
derives the principle of explosion.
- `IsClassical` : an inference is classical if it derives double negation elimination.
- `Proposition.subst` : replace `atom x` in a `A : Proposition Atom` with `f x`, for a function
  `f : Atom → Proposition Atom'`. This induces a monad structure on `Proposition`, with
  `pure := Proposition.atom`.

## Notation

We instantiate the notation classes `HasAnd`, `HasOr`, `HasImpl`, `HasNot`, `Bot` and `Top` for
`Proposition Atom` to give access to, respectively, the notations `∧, ∨, →`, `¬`, `⊥` and `⊤` for
propositional connectives.

## References

* [J. Avigad, *Mathematical Logic and Computation*][Avigad2022]

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.Proposition
items.doc: Propositions.
items.statement:
inductive Proposition (Atom : Type u) : Type u where
  /-- Propositional atoms -/
  | atom (x : Atom)
  /-- Falsum. -/
  | falsum
  /-- Conjunction -/
  | and (a b : Proposition Atom)
  /-- Disjunction -/
  | or (a b : Proposition Atom)
  /-- Implication -/
  | imp (a b : Proposition Atom)
deriving DecidableEq

modules.title: Natural deduction for propositional logic
modules.doc:
We define, for intuitionistic logic, deduction trees (a `Type`) and derivability (a `Prop`)
relative to a set of axioms.

## Main definitions

- `Sequent` : a pair of a context and conclusion.
- `Derivation` : natural deduction derivation, done in "sequent style", ie with explicit
hypotheses at each step. Contexts are `Finset`'s of propositions, which avoids explicit contraction
and exchange, and the axiom rule derives `Γ ⊢ A` for any context `Γ` with `A ∈ Γ`, allowing
weakening to be a derived rule. The derivation may appeal to hypotheses from the
`T : Set (Proposition Atom)`.
- `ND T`, `ND₁ T` : two inference systems, on `Sequent Atom` and `Proposition Atom` respectively,
corresponding to `Derivation T` and `Derivation T ∅`.
- `equiv` : `Type`-valued equivalence of propositions.
- `Equiv` : `Prop`-valued equivalence of propositions.

## Main results

- `Derivation.weak` : weakening as a derived rule.
- `Derivation.cut`, `Derivation.subs` : replace a hypothesis in a derivation — the two versions
differ in the construction of the relevant derivation.
- `equiv_equivalence` : equivalence of propositions is an equivalence relation.

## Notation

The sequent `⟨Γ, A⟩` is notated `Γ ⊢ A`, so that a derivation using axioms from a set `T` is
noted `(ND T)⇓(Γ ⊢ A)`. We define also an `InferenceSystem (ND₁ T) (Proposition Atom)`, so that
`(ND₁ T)⇓A` abbreviates a derivation of `A` in the empty context: `(ND T)⇓(∅ ⊢ A)`.

## Implementation notes

We formalise here a single type of derivations, meaning there is a single collection of inference
rules (those for intuitionistic logic). The extension to classical logic (indeed any extension of
intuitionistic logic) is modelled by adding *axioms* --- in this case, classical derivations can
appeal to axioms of the form `¬¬A → A`, for any proposition `A`. This differs from many on-paper
presentations, which might, for instance, add instead an inference rule corresponding to proof by
contraduction. Discussion on the proper way to capture such developments in cslib is ongoing, see
the following
[zulip discussion](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/513188-CSLib/topic/Logic/with/585843520).

## References

- [J. Avigad, *Mathematical Logic and Computation*][Avigad2022]
- [D. Prawitz, *Natural Deduction: A Proof-Theoretical Study*][Prawitz1965]
- The sequent-style natural deduction presented here doesn't seem to be common, but it is tersely
presented in §10.4 of
[A. S. Troelstra, D. van Dalen, *Constructivism in Mathematics*][TroelstraVanDalen1988], and
in §2.2 of
[M. H. Sorensen, P. Urzyczyn's *Lectures on the Curry-Howard Isomorphism*][SorensenUrzyczyn2006].

items.doc: Contexts are finsets of propositions.
items.statement: abbrev Ctx (Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Ctx.subst
items.doc: Map a context along a substitution.
items.statement:
def Ctx.subst {Atom Atom' : Type*} [DecidableEq Atom'] (f : Atom → Proposition Atom') :
