items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Sequent
items.doc: Sequents \{A₁, ..., Aₙ\} ⊢ B.
items.statement: abbrev Sequent {Atom}

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation
items.doc:
A `T`-derivation of \{A₁, ..., Aₙ\} ⊢ B demonstrates B using (undischarged) assumptions
among Aᵢ, possibly appealing to axioms from `T`.
items.statement:
inductive Derivation (T : Set (Proposition Atom)) : Ctx Atom → Proposition Atom → Type u where
  /-- Axiom -/
  | ax {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A : Proposition Atom} (_ : A ∈ T := by membership) : Derivation T Γ A
  /-- Assumption -/
  | ass {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A : Proposition Atom} (_ : A ∈ Γ := by membership) : Derivation T Γ A
  /-- Ex falso quodlibet. -/
  | efq {Γ : Ctx Atom} (A : Proposition Atom) : Derivation T Γ ⊥ → Derivation T Γ A
  /-- Conjunction introduction -/
  | andI {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A B : Proposition Atom} :
      Derivation T Γ A → Derivation T Γ B → Derivation T Γ (A ∧ B)
  /-- Conjunction elimination left -/
  | andE₁ {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A B : Proposition Atom} : Derivation T Γ (A ∧ B) → Derivation T Γ A
  /-- Conjunction elimination right -/
  | andE₂ {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A B : Proposition Atom} : Derivation T Γ (A ∧ B) → Derivation T Γ B
  /-- Disjunction introduction left -/
  | orI₁ {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A B : Proposition Atom} : Derivation T Γ A → Derivation T Γ (A ∨ B)
  /-- Disjunction introduction right -/
  | orI₂ {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A B : Proposition Atom} : Derivation T Γ B → Derivation T Γ (A ∨ B)
  /-- Disjunction elimination -/
  | orE {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A B C : Proposition Atom} : Derivation T Γ (A ∨ B) →
      Derivation T (insert A Γ) C → Derivation T (insert B Γ) C → Derivation T Γ C
  /-- Implication introduction -/
  | impI {A B : Proposition Atom} (Γ : Ctx Atom) :
      Derivation T (insert A Γ) B → Derivation T Γ (A → B)
  /-- Implication elimination -/
  | impE {Γ : Ctx Atom} {A B : Proposition Atom} :
      Derivation T Γ (A → B) → Derivation T Γ A → Derivation T Γ B

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.ND
items.doc: Type tag for natural deduction derivations from axioms `T`.
items.statement: opaque ND (T : Set (Proposition Atom)) : Type

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.ND₁
items.doc: Type tag for natural deduction derivations of single propositions from axioms `T`.
items.statement: opaque ND₁ (T : Set (Proposition Atom)) : Type

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation.emptySequent_eq
items.statement: theorem Derivation.emptySequent_eq {A : Proposition Atom} : (ND₁ T)⇓A = (ND T)⇓(∅ ⊢ A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.nd₁_iff_derivableIn_nd_empty
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.nd₁_iff_derivableIn_nd_empty
  {A : Proposition Atom} : DerivableIn (ND₁ T) A ↔ DerivableIn (ND T) (∅ ⊢ A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv
items.doc: An equivalence between A and B is a derivation of B from A and vice-versa.
items.statement:
structure equiv (T : Set (Proposition Atom)) (A B : Proposition Atom) where
  /-- The forward direction of the equivalence. -/
  mp : (ND T)⇓({A} ⊢ B)
  /-- The reverse direction of the equivalence. -/
  mpr : (ND T)⇓({B} ⊢ A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Equiv
items.doc: `A` and `B` are T-equivalent if `T.equiv A B` is nonempty.
items.statement: def Equiv (T : Set (Proposition Atom)) (A B : Proposition Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Equiv.mp
items.statement: lemma Equiv.mp {A B : Proposition Atom} (h : A ≡[T] B) : DerivableIn (ND T) ({A} ⊢ B)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Equiv.mpr
items.statement: lemma Equiv.mpr {A B : Proposition Atom} (h : A ≡[T] B) : DerivableIn (ND T) ({B} ⊢ A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv_iff
items.statement:
theorem equiv_iff {A B : Proposition Atom} :
  A ≡[T] B ↔ DerivableIn (ND T) ({A} ⊢ B) ∧ DerivableIn (ND T) ({B} ⊢ A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation.weak
items.doc: Weakening is a derived rule.
items.statement:
def Derivation.weak {T T' : Set (Proposition Atom)} {Γ Δ : Ctx Atom} {A : Proposition Atom}
    (hTheory : T ⊆ T' := by grind only [membership, = Set.subset_def])
    (hCtx : Γ ⊆ Δ := by grind only [membership, = Finset.subset_iff]) :
    Derivation T Γ A → Derivation T' Δ A

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation.weakTheory
items.doc: Weakening the axioms only.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation.weakCtx
items.doc: Weakening the context only.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.weak
items.doc: Proof irrelevant weakening.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.weakTheory
items.doc: Proof irrelevant weakening of the axiom set.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.weakCtx
items.doc: Proof irrelevant weakening of the context.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation.cut
items.doc:
Implement the cut rule, removing a hypothesis `A` from `E` using a derivation `D`. This is *not*
substitution, which would replace appeals to `A` in `E` by the whole derivation `D`.
items.statement:
def Derivation.cut {Γ Δ : Ctx Atom} {A B : Proposition Atom}
    (D : (ND T)⇓(Γ ⊢ A)) (E : (ND T)⇓(insert A Δ ⊢ B)) : (ND T)⇓((Γ ∪ Δ) ⊢ B)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.cut
items.doc: Proof irrelevant cut rule.
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.cut {Γ Δ : Ctx Atom}
    {A B : Proposition Atom} :
    DerivableIn (ND T) (Γ ⊢ A) → DerivableIn (ND T) ((insert A Δ) ⊢ B) →
      DerivableIn (ND T) ((Γ ∪ Δ) ⊢ B)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.cut_away
items.doc:
Remove unnecessary hypotheses. This can't be computable because it requires picking an order
on the finset `Δ`.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation.subs
items.doc:
Substitution of a family of derivations `D` for hypotheses in the context `Γ` of `E`. TODO:
this implementation is not capture avoiding.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Derivation.substAtom
items.doc: Transport a derivation along a substitution of atoms.
items.statement:
def Derivation.substAtom {Atom Atom' : Type*} [DecidableEq Atom] [DecidableEq Atom']
    {T : Set (Proposition Atom)} (f : Atom → Proposition Atom') {Γ : Ctx Atom}
    {B : Proposition Atom} :
    Derivation T Γ B → Derivation ((·.subst f) '' T) (Γ.subst f) (B.subst f)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.InferenceSystem.DerivableIn.substAtom
Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.derivationTop
items.doc: A derivation of the canonical tautology.
items.statement: def derivationTop : (ND₁ T)⇓(⊤ : Proposition Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.derivableIn_top
items.statement: theorem derivableIn_top : DerivableIn (ND₁ T) (⊤ : Proposition Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.derivable_iff_equiv_top
items.statement:
theorem derivable_iff_equiv_top (A : Proposition Atom) :
    DerivableIn (ND₁ T) A ↔ A ≡[T] ⊤

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.mapEquivConclusion
items.doc: Change the conclusion along an equivalence.
items.statement:
def mapEquivConclusion (Γ : Ctx Atom) {A B : Proposition Atom} (e : equiv T A B)
    (D : (ND T)⇓(Γ ⊢ A)) : (ND T)⇓(Γ ⊢ B)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.mapEquivHypothesis
items.doc: Replace a hypothesis along an equivalence.
items.statement:
def mapEquivHypothesis (Γ : Ctx Atom) {A B : Proposition Atom} (e : equiv T A B)
    (C : Proposition Atom) (D : (ND T)⇓(insert A Γ ⊢ C)) : (ND T)⇓(insert B Γ ⊢ C)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv.refl
items.doc: An equivalence of a proposition with itself.
items.statement: def equiv.refl (A : Proposition Atom) : equiv T A A

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv.symm
items.doc: Reverse an equivalence.
items.statement: def equiv.symm {A B : Proposition Atom} (e : equiv T A B) : equiv T B A

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv.trans
items.doc: Compose two equivalences.
items.statement:
def equiv.trans {A B C : Proposition Atom} (eAB : equiv T A B)
    (eBC : equiv T B C) : equiv T A C

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv_iff_equiv_derivableIn
items.doc: `A` and `B` are equivalent (in `T`) iff they are provable from the same contexts.
items.statement:
theorem equiv_iff_equiv_derivableIn {A B : Proposition Atom} :
    A ≡[T] B ↔ ∀ Γ : Ctx Atom, DerivableIn (ND T) (Γ ⊢ A) ↔ DerivableIn (ND T) (Γ ⊢ B)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv_iff_equiv_derivableIn_hypothesis
items.doc: `A` and `B` are equivalent (in `T`) iff they have the same strength as hypotheses.
items.statement:
theorem equiv_iff_equiv_derivableIn_hypothesis {A B : Proposition Atom} :
    A ≡[T] B ↔
      ∀ (Γ : Ctx Atom) (C : Proposition Atom),
      DerivableIn (ND T) ((insert A Γ) ⊢ C) ↔ DerivableIn (ND T) ((insert B Γ) ⊢ C)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Equiv.refl
items.statement: theorem Equiv.refl {T : Set (Proposition Atom)} (A : Proposition Atom) : A ≡[T] A

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Equiv.symm
items.statement:
theorem Equiv.symm {T : Set (Proposition Atom)} {A B : Proposition Atom} :
    (A ≡[T] B) → B ≡[T] A

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.Equiv.trans
items.statement:
theorem Equiv.trans {T : Set (Proposition Atom)} {A B C : Proposition Atom} :
    (A ≡[T] B) → (B ≡[T] C) → A ≡[T] C

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.equiv_equivalence
items.doc: Equivalence is indeed an equivalence relation.
items.statement: theorem equiv_equivalence (T : Set (Proposition Atom)) : Equivalence (Equiv T (Atom := Atom))

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.propositionSetoid
items.doc: The setoid of propositions under equivalence.
items.statement: protected def propositionSetoid (T : Set (Proposition Atom)) : Setoid (Proposition Atom)

modules.title: Auxilliary results on natural deduction
modules.doc:
In this file we prove the expected results that `ND₁ T` is always intuitionistic, and that various
axiomatisations of classical logic (`CPL Atom` using double-negation elimination, `LEM Atom` using
the law of excluded middle, and `Peirce Atom` using Peirce's law) are classical inference systems.
We provide derived rules for common intuitionistic and classical proof patterns.

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.instIsIntuitionisticND₁
items.statement: instance instIsIntuitionisticND₁ : IsIntuitionistic (ND₁ T) (Proposition Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.derivBotImpCtx
items.doc: Derivation of efq in an arbitrary context.
items.statement: def derivBotImpCtx (Γ : Ctx Atom) (A : Proposition Atom) : (ND T)⇓(Γ ⊢ ⊥ → A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.contra
items.doc: Prove any proposition from contradictory hypotheses.
items.statement:
def contra {Γ : Ctx Atom} (A B : Proposition Atom)
    (hΓ : A ∈ Γ := by membership) (hΓ' : (¬A) ∈ Γ := by membership) : (ND T)⇓(Γ ⊢ B)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.instIsClassicalCPL
items.statement: instance instIsClassicalCPL : IsClassical (ND₁ <| CPL Atom) (Proposition Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.byContra
items.doc: Proof by contradiction as a derived rule.
items.statement:
def byContra [IsClassical (ND₁ T) (Proposition Atom)] {Γ : Ctx Atom}
    {A : Proposition Atom} (D : (ND T)⇓(insert (¬ A) Γ ⊢ ⊥)) : (ND T)⇓(Γ ⊢ A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.lem
items.doc: Law of excluded middle in a classical theory.
items.statement: def lem [IsClassical (ND₁ T) (Proposition Atom)] (A : Proposition Atom) : (ND₁ T)⇓(A ∨ ¬ A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.peirce
items.doc: Peirce's law in a classical theory.
items.statement:
def peirce [IsClassical (ND₁ T) (Proposition Atom)] (A B : Proposition Atom) :
    (ND₁ T)⇓(((A → B) → A) → A)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.instIsClassicalLEM
items.statement: instance instIsClassicalLEM : IsClassical (ND₁ <| LEM Atom) (Proposition Atom)

items.name: Cslib.Logic.PL.NaturalDeduction.instIsClassicalPeirce
items.statement: instance instIsClassicalPeirce : IsClassical (ND₁ <| Peirce Atom) (Proposition Atom)

modules.title: PAC Learning
modules.doc:
This file defines the Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning model
introduced by Valiant [Valiant1984], generalized to an arbitrary label type `β`
and parameterized by a family of distributions `𝒟` on `α × β`.

A concept class `C` over domain `α` with labels in `β` is a collection of
functions `α → β`. A learning algorithm receives a labeled sample drawn i.i.d.
from an unknown joint distribution `D` on `α × β` and must produce a hypothesis
whose 0-1 error is within `ε` of the best concept in `C`, with probability at
least `1 - δ`.

The single definition `IsPACLearnerFor` captures the realizable, agnostic, and
noise-tolerant settings by varying the distribution family `𝒟`:

- **Agnostic** [Haussler1992]: `𝒟 = Set.univ` — the learner must work for all distributions.
- **Realizable**: `𝒟` consists of pushforwards of arbitrary probability measures
  `P` on `α` along the graph `x ↦ (x, c x)` of some concept `c ∈ C`, so that
  `optimalError D C = 0`.
- **Noise-tolerant** [AngluinLaird1988]: `𝒟` consists of noisy versions of realizable
  distributions, where each label is corrupted independently with some probability `η`.

The accuracy and confidence parameters `ε` and `δ` are elements of the subtype
`Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1`, which bundles the value together with the proof that it
lies in the open interval `(0, 1)`, ensuring the learning condition is non-vacuous.

All declarations live under the `Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning` namespace so that
generic names like `error` and `optimalError` do not pollute the parent namespace.

## Main definitions

- `ConceptClass`: a set of functions `α → β` (classifiers).
- `LabeledSample`: a finite sequence of `(point, label)` pairs.
- `Learner`: a function from labeled samples to hypotheses.
- `error`: the 0-1 error of a hypothesis under a joint distribution.
- `optimalError`: the infimum of `error` over a concept class.
- `IsPACLearnerFor`: deterministic `(ε, δ)`-PAC learner over a distribution family.
- `IsRPACLearnerFor`: randomized variant of `IsPACLearnerFor`. Universe-polymorphic in the
  randomness space `Ω : Type*`.
- `IsPACLearnable`: a concept class is PAC learnable if `IsPACLearnerFor` holds for
  all `ε, δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1` with some sample size `m`.
- `IsRPACLearnable`: randomized variant of `IsPACLearnable`. Pins the randomness space to
  `Type 0`; `IsRPACLearnerFor` itself remains universe-polymorphic for users who need it.
- `LearnerModel`: the common predicate shape `ℕ → ε → δ → C → 𝒟 → Prop` abstracting both
  the deterministic and randomized learners so sample-complexity lemmas can be shared.
- `sampleComplexity`: sample complexity of a generic learner model.
- `rsampleComplexity`: randomized sample complexity, i.e. `sampleComplexity IsRPACLearnerFor`.

## Binary classification

When `β = Bool`, concepts correspond to subsets of `α`. The section
*Binary Classification* provides:

- `hypothesisError`: the symmetric-difference error `P(h ∆ c)`.
- `falsePositiveError`, `falseNegativeError`: its decomposition.
- `hypothesisError_eq_add`: the decomposition theorem.
- `error_map_eq_hypothesisError`: bridge between the general `error` and
  the binary `hypothesisError` under a realizable distribution.

## Main statements

- `IsPACLearnerFor.toIsRPACLearnerFor`: every deterministic PAC learner is a
  randomized one (via the trivial randomness space `PUnit`).
- `IsPACLearnerFor.antitone_family`, `.antitone_C`: the deterministic PAC learner
  predicate is antitone in the distribution family and concept class.
- `IsPACLearnerFor.mono_δ`, `.mono_ε`: the predicate is monotone in the confidence and
  accuracy parameters (a weaker bound still holds).
- `IsRPACLearnerFor.antitone_family`, `.mono_δ`: analogues for the randomized predicate.
  (`mono_ε` and `antitone_C` are not provided because they change the integrand and
  would require an extra measurability assumption.)
- `IsPACLearnable.toIsRPACLearnable`: deterministic learnability implies randomized.
- `IsPACLearnable.antitone_family`, `.antitone_C`, `IsRPACLearnable.antitone_family`:
  PAC learnability is antitone in the distribution family and concept class.
- `sampleComplexity_antitone_δ`, `_antitone_ε`, `_mono_family`, `_mono_C`: variation of
  deterministic sample complexity in confidence, accuracy, distribution family, and concept
  class (antitone in the numeric parameters, monotone under `⊆` in the set parameters). The
  randomized analogues `rsampleComplexity_antitone_δ` and `_mono_family` are provided.
- `IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_*`, `IsRPACLearnable.rsampleComplexity_*`: the same
  monotonicity facts phrased with a learnability hypothesis in place of the ad-hoc
  `∃ m, IsPACLearnerFor m …` existence witness, so callers who already know the class is
  learnable need not thread it through.
- `hypothesisError_eq_add`: total error = false positive + false negative.

## References

* [L. G. Valiant, *A Theory of the Learnable*][Valiant1984]
* [A. Ehrenfeucht, D. Haussler, M. Kearns, L. Valiant,
  *A General Lower Bound on the Number of Examples Needed for Learning*][EHKV1989]
* [M. J. Kearns, U. V. Vazirani,
  *An Introduction to Computational Learning Theory*][KearnsVazirani1994]
* [D. Haussler, *Decision Theoretic Generalizations of the PAC Model for Neural Net
  and Other Learning Applications*][Haussler1992]
* [D. Angluin, P. Laird, *Learning from Noisy Examples*][AngluinLaird1988]

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.ConceptClass
items.doc:
A *concept class* over domain `α` with label type `β` is a set of functions `α → β`.
For binary classification (`β = Bool`), this is equivalent to a collection of subsets of `α`
via the characteristic function.
items.statement: abbrev ConceptClass (α β : Type*)

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.LabeledSample
items.doc:
A *labeled sample* of size `m` over domain `α` with label type `β` is a finite sequence
of `(point, label)` pairs.
items.statement: abbrev LabeledSample (α β : Type*) (m : ℕ)

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.Learner
items.doc:
A *learner* using `m` samples is a function that takes a labeled sample and produces
a hypothesis (a function from the domain to the label type).
items.statement: abbrev Learner (α β : Type*) (m : ℕ)

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.error
items.doc:
The *prediction error* (0-1 loss) of a hypothesis `h` under a joint distribution `D`
on `α × β`, defined as the probability that the prediction disagrees with the label:
`D({(x, y) | h(x) ≠ y})`.
items.statement: noncomputable def error (D : Measure (α × β)) (h : α → β) : ℝ≥0∞

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.optimalError
items.doc:
The *optimal error* of a concept class `C` under a joint distribution `D`, defined as the
infimum of `error D c` over all concepts `c ∈ C`. When `C` is empty this is `⊤`, making the
PAC learning condition vacuously true.
items.statement: noncomputable def optimalError (D : Measure (α × β)) (C : ConceptClass α β) : ℝ≥0∞

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnerFor
items.doc:
`IsPACLearnerFor m ε δ C 𝒟` asserts that there exists a learner using `m` samples
that is `(ε, δ)`-correct for the concept class `C` over the distribution family `𝒟`: for every
probability measure `D ∈ 𝒟` on `α × β`, the probability (over i.i.d. samples from `D`) that
the learner's hypothesis has error exceeding `opt_C(D) + ε` is at most `δ`.

The parameters `ε` and `δ` are elements of `Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1`, bundling the value with
the proof that it lies in `(0, 1)`. This ensures the condition is non-vacuous:
`ε < 1` prevents the error threshold from exceeding the maximum possible error under a
probability measure, and `δ < 1` prevents the confidence bound from being trivially
satisfied.
items.statement:
def IsPACLearnerFor (m : ℕ) (ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1)
    (C : ConceptClass α β) (𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsRPACLearnerFor
items.doc:
`IsRPACLearnerFor m ε δ C 𝒟` asserts that there exists a *randomized* learner using
`m` samples that is `(ε, δ)`-correct for the concept class `C` over the distribution family
`𝒟`. A randomized learner draws internal randomness `ω` from a probability space `(Ω, Q)` and
acts as the deterministic learner `A(ω)`.

For every probability measure `D ∈ 𝒟`, the failure probability function
`ω ↦ D^m{S | error(A(ω)(S)) > opt_C(D) + ε}` must be `Q`-a.e. measurable, and its
expectation over `ω` must be at most `δ`.

The randomness space `Ω : Type*` is universe-polymorphic; the universe is an implicit
parameter of `IsRPACLearnerFor`, and downstream statements reference it via the pattern
`IsRPACLearnerFor.{_, _, u}`. Fix `u := 0` for the usual case of a standard randomness space.

A deterministic learner (`IsPACLearnerFor`) is the special case `Ω = PUnit`;
see `IsPACLearnerFor.toIsRPACLearnerFor`.
items.statement:
def IsRPACLearnerFor (m : ℕ) (ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1)
    (C : ConceptClass α β) (𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnerFor.toIsRPACLearnerFor
items.doc:
Every deterministic PAC learner is in particular a randomized PAC learner
(with the trivial one-point randomness space `PUnit`).

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnerFor.antitone_family
items.doc:
The deterministic PAC learner predicate is antitone in the distribution family: a
learner for a larger family `𝒟'` is also a learner for any subfamily `𝒟 ⊆ 𝒟'`.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnerFor.mono_δ
items.doc:
A PAC learner with confidence `δ₁` is also a PAC learner with any weaker confidence
`δ₂ ≥ δ₁`: the failure-probability bound only gets looser.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnerFor.mono_ε
items.doc:
A PAC learner with accuracy `ε₁` is also a PAC learner with any weaker accuracy
`ε₂ ≥ ε₁`: the bad event `{error > opt + ε}` only shrinks.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnerFor.antitone_C
items.doc:
The deterministic PAC learner predicate is antitone in the concept class: a learner
for a larger class `C'` is also a learner for any subclass `C ⊆ C'`, since the agnostic
benchmark `optimalError _ C ≥ optimalError _ C'` makes the error requirement easier.
items.statement:
theorem IsPACLearnerFor.antitone_C {m : ℕ} {ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1}
    {C C' : ConceptClass α β} (hC : C ⊆ C')
    {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))} (h : IsPACLearnerFor m ε δ C' 𝒟) :
    IsPACLearnerFor m ε δ C 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsRPACLearnerFor.antitone_family
items.doc:
The randomized PAC learner predicate is antitone in the distribution family. The
universe of the randomness space `Ω` is pinned so the hypothesis and conclusion share it.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsRPACLearnerFor.mono_δ
items.doc:
A randomized PAC learner with confidence `δ₁` is also a randomized PAC learner with
any weaker confidence `δ₂ ≥ δ₁`. Unlike `mono_ε` or `antitone_C`, this does not touch the
integrand, so it carries the `AEMeasurable` part through unchanged.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable
items.doc:
A concept class `C` is *PAC learnable* over the distribution family `𝒟` if for every
accuracy `ε ∈ (0, 1)` and confidence `δ ∈ (0, 1)`, there exists a sample size `m` admitting
a deterministic `(ε, δ)`-PAC learner for `C`. Here `ε` and `δ` are elements of the subtype
`Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1`.
items.statement: def IsPACLearnable (C : ConceptClass α β) (𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsRPACLearnable
items.doc:
A concept class `C` is *randomized PAC learnable* over the distribution family `𝒟` if for
every accuracy `ε ∈ (0, 1)` and confidence `δ ∈ (0, 1)`, there exists a sample size `m`
admitting a randomized `(ε, δ)`-PAC learner for `C`. The randomness space is pinned to
`Type 0` at the learnability level; `IsRPACLearnerFor` itself remains universe-polymorphic.
items.statement: def IsRPACLearnable (C : ConceptClass α β) (𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable.toIsRPACLearnable
items.doc: Deterministic PAC learnability implies randomized PAC learnability.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable.antitone_family
items.doc:
PAC learnability is antitone in the distribution family: a subfamily of a learnable
family is learnable.
items.statement:
theorem IsPACLearnable.antitone_family {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 𝒟' : Set (Measure (α × β))}
    (h𝒟 : 𝒟 ⊆ 𝒟') (h : IsPACLearnable C 𝒟') : IsPACLearnable C 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable.antitone_C
items.doc:
PAC learnability is antitone in the concept class: a subclass of a learnable class is
learnable.
items.statement:
theorem IsPACLearnable.antitone_C {C C' : ConceptClass α β} (hC : C ⊆ C')
    {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))} (h : IsPACLearnable C' 𝒟) : IsPACLearnable C 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsRPACLearnable.antitone_family
items.doc: Randomized PAC learnability is antitone in the distribution family.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.LearnerModel
items.doc:
A *learner model* is a predicate on (sample size, accuracy, confidence, concept class,
distribution family) that classifies which sample sizes admit a learner of the given kind.
Instantiating with `IsPACLearnerFor` gives the deterministic model; with `IsRPACLearnerFor`
gives the randomized one.
items.statement: abbrev LearnerModel (α β : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β]

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.sampleComplexity
items.doc:
The *sample complexity* of a concept class `C` under a learner model `L`, at accuracy
`ε ∈ (0, 1)` and confidence `δ ∈ (0, 1)` over distribution family `𝒟`, is the smallest sample
size `m` with `L m ε δ C 𝒟`. Specialize with `L := IsPACLearnerFor` for the deterministic model
and `L := IsRPACLearnerFor` for the randomized one.

**Caveat**: because `sInf` on `ℕ` returns `0` for the empty set, this definition returns `0`
when no learner exists (e.g., a concept class of infinite VC dimension). It is only meaningful
when the defining set `{m | L m ε δ C 𝒟}` is nonempty. The `IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_*`
variants below discharge this nonemptiness from a learnability hypothesis.
items.statement:
noncomputable def sampleComplexity (L : LearnerModel α β) (C : ConceptClass α β)
    (ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1) (𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.rsampleComplexity
items.doc:
The *randomized sample complexity* of `C`, i.e. `sampleComplexity` instantiated at the
randomized learner model `IsRPACLearnerFor`. The randomness space is pinned to `Type 0`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def rsampleComplexity (C : ConceptClass α β) (ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1)
    (𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))) : ℕ

items.note:
### Monotonicity of Sample Complexity

These lemmas are all special cases of the following observation: if `{m | L₁ m ε₁ δ₁ C₁ 𝒟₁} ⊆
{m | L₂ m ε₂ δ₂ C₂ 𝒟₂}` and the first set is nonempty, then the sample complexity under
`(L₂, ε₂, δ₂, C₂, 𝒟₂)` is at most the sample complexity under `(L₁, ε₁, δ₁, C₁, 𝒟₁)`. The
nonemptiness hypothesis is essential: `sInf` on `ℕ` returns `0` for an empty set, so without
it the inequality can fail at the degenerate boundary. The `IsPACLearnable`-flavoured variants
at the end of this section discharge that witness from a learnability hypothesis.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.sampleComplexity_le_of_forall
items.doc:
General pointwise monotonicity of `sampleComplexity`: if every witness sample size for
`(L₁, ε₁, δ₁, C₁, 𝒟₁)` is also a witness for `(L₂, ε₂, δ₂, C₂, 𝒟₂)`, then the latter's
sample complexity is at most the former's (provided the former is attained).

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.sampleComplexity_antitone_δ
items.doc:
Deterministic sample complexity is antitone in the confidence parameter `δ`: weaker
confidence requires no more samples.
items.statement:
theorem sampleComplexity_antitone_δ {ε δ₁ δ₂ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} (hδ : δ₁.val ≤ δ₂.val)
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))}
    (h : ∃ m, IsPACLearnerFor m ε δ₁ C 𝒟) :
    sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ₂ 𝒟 ≤ sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ₁ 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.sampleComplexity_antitone_ε
items.doc:
Deterministic sample complexity is antitone in the accuracy parameter `ε`: weaker
accuracy requires no more samples.
items.statement:
theorem sampleComplexity_antitone_ε {ε₁ ε₂ δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} (hε : ε₁.val ≤ ε₂.val)
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))}
    (h : ∃ m, IsPACLearnerFor m ε₁ δ C 𝒟) :
    sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε₂ δ 𝒟 ≤ sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε₁ δ 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.sampleComplexity_mono_family
items.doc:
Deterministic sample complexity is monotone in the distribution family under `⊆`: a
smaller family (fewer distributions to cover) requires no more samples.
items.statement:
theorem sampleComplexity_mono_family {ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1}
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 𝒟' : Set (Measure (α × β))} (h𝒟 : 𝒟 ⊆ 𝒟')
    (h : ∃ m, IsPACLearnerFor m ε δ C 𝒟') :
    sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ 𝒟 ≤ sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ 𝒟'

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.sampleComplexity_mono_C
items.doc:
Deterministic sample complexity is monotone in the concept class under `⊆`: a smaller
class (weaker agnostic benchmark) requires no more samples.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.rsampleComplexity_antitone_δ
items.doc: Randomized sample complexity is antitone in the confidence parameter `δ`.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.rsampleComplexity_mono_family
items.doc: Randomized sample complexity is monotone in the distribution family under `⊆`.
items.statement:
theorem rsampleComplexity_mono_family {ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1}
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 𝒟' : Set (Measure (α × β))} (h𝒟 : 𝒟 ⊆ 𝒟')
    (h : ∃ m, IsRPACLearnerFor.{_, _, 0} m ε δ C 𝒟') :
    rsampleComplexity C ε δ 𝒟 ≤ rsampleComplexity C ε δ 𝒟'

items.note:
Convenience variants conditional on learnability, which discharge the nonemptiness
hypothesis `(∃ m, IsPACLearnerFor m …)` from an `IsPACLearnable` / `IsRPACLearnable` witness.
Bodies go through `sampleComplexity_le_of_forall` directly rather than the top-level
`sampleComplexity_*` lemmas, whose unqualified names would resolve as self-recursion inside
these theorems' `IsPACLearnable.*` / `IsRPACLearnable.*` namespaces.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_antitone_δ
items.doc:
`sampleComplexity_antitone_δ` for a learnable class: the nonemptiness hypothesis comes
for free from `IsPACLearnable`.
items.statement:
theorem IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_antitone_δ
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))} (hL : IsPACLearnable C 𝒟)
    {ε δ₁ δ₂ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} (hδ : δ₁.val ≤ δ₂.val) :
    sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ₂ 𝒟 ≤ sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ₁ 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_antitone_ε
items.doc: `sampleComplexity_antitone_ε` for a learnable class.
items.statement:
theorem IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_antitone_ε
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))} (hL : IsPACLearnable C 𝒟)
    {ε₁ ε₂ δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} (hε : ε₁.val ≤ ε₂.val) :
    sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε₂ δ 𝒟 ≤ sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε₁ δ 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_mono_family
items.doc:
`sampleComplexity_mono_family` for a learnable class (learnability at the *larger*
family `𝒟'` is the hypothesis).
items.statement:
theorem IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_mono_family
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 𝒟' : Set (Measure (α × β))}
    (hL : IsPACLearnable C 𝒟') (h𝒟 : 𝒟 ⊆ 𝒟') {ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} :
    sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ 𝒟 ≤ sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ 𝒟'

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_mono_C
items.doc:
`sampleComplexity_mono_C` for a learnable class (learnability at the *larger* class
`C'` is the hypothesis).
items.statement:
theorem IsPACLearnable.sampleComplexity_mono_C
    {C C' : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))}
    (hL : IsPACLearnable C' 𝒟) (hC : C ⊆ C') {ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} :
    sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C ε δ 𝒟 ≤ sampleComplexity IsPACLearnerFor C' ε δ 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsRPACLearnable.rsampleComplexity_antitone_δ
items.doc: `rsampleComplexity_antitone_δ` for a randomized-learnable class.
items.statement:
theorem IsRPACLearnable.rsampleComplexity_antitone_δ
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 : Set (Measure (α × β))} (hL : IsRPACLearnable C 𝒟)
    {ε δ₁ δ₂ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} (hδ : δ₁.val ≤ δ₂.val) :
    rsampleComplexity C ε δ₂ 𝒟 ≤ rsampleComplexity C ε δ₁ 𝒟

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsRPACLearnable.rsampleComplexity_mono_family
items.doc: `rsampleComplexity_mono_family` for a randomized-learnable class.
items.statement:
theorem IsRPACLearnable.rsampleComplexity_mono_family
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {𝒟 𝒟' : Set (Measure (α × β))}
    (hL : IsRPACLearnable C 𝒟') (h𝒟 : 𝒟 ⊆ 𝒟') {ε δ : Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ≥0) 1} :
    rsampleComplexity C ε δ 𝒟 ≤ rsampleComplexity C ε δ 𝒟'

items.note:
### Binary Classification

When `β = Bool`, concepts correspond to subsets of `α` via the characteristic function.
The symmetric-difference error `P(h ∆ c)` is the natural error metric, and it decomposes
into false positive and false negative components.

The bridge lemma `error_map_eq_hypothesisError` connects the general `error` on `α × Bool`
to the binary `hypothesisError` on `α`, showing they coincide for realizable distributions.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.hypothesisError
items.doc:
The *symmetric-difference error* of a hypothesis `h` with respect to a target concept `c`
(both viewed as subsets of `α`) under distribution `P`, defined as `P(h ∆ c)`.
items.statement: noncomputable def hypothesisError (P : Measure α) (h c : Set α) : ℝ≥0∞

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.falsePositiveError
items.doc:
The *false positive error* `P(h \ c)` — points classified positive but not in the
concept.
items.statement: noncomputable def falsePositiveError (P : Measure α) (h c : Set α) : ℝ≥0∞

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.falseNegativeError
items.doc: The *false negative error* `P(c \ h)` — points in the concept but classified negative.
items.statement: noncomputable def falseNegativeError (P : Measure α) (h c : Set α) : ℝ≥0∞

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.hypothesisError_eq_add
items.doc:
The total hypothesis error decomposes as the sum of false positive and false negative
errors, since `h ∆ c = (h \ c) ∪ (c \ h)` is a disjoint union.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.error_map_eq_hypothesisError
items.doc:
Under a realizable distribution `P.map (x ↦ (x, c(x)))`, the general 0-1 `error`
coincides with the binary `hypothesisError P h c`, where `h` and `c` are viewed as subsets
of `α` via the characteristic function `decide (· ∈ ·)`.
items.statement:
theorem error_map_eq_hypothesisError (P : Measure α) (h c : Set α)
    (hh : MeasurableSet h) (hc : MeasurableSet c) :
    error (P.map (fun x => (x, decide (x ∈ c)))) (fun x => decide (x ∈ h)) =
    hypothesisError P h c

modules.title: VC Dimension for Concept Classes
modules.doc:
This file defines *shattering* and the *Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension* for
binary concept classes `C : ConceptClass α Bool`, i.e. sets of `α → Bool`
classifiers. Each Boolean classifier `c` is identified with the subset
`c ⁻¹' {true} ⊆ α` (the "positive set"), and `C` shatters a set `W` if every
subset of `W` can be obtained as the positive set of some `c ∈ C` intersected
with `W`. See also the `Finset`-based definitions in
`Mathlib.Combinatorics.SetFamily.Shatter`.

## Main definitions

- `SetShatters C W`: the concept class `C` shatters the set `W`.
- `vcDim C`: the VC dimension of `C`, i.e. the supremum of the cardinalities of
  finite sets shattered by `C`.

## Main statements

- `SetShatters.subset`: shattering is anti-monotone in the shattered set.
- `SetShatters.superset`: shattering is monotone in the concept class.
- `Finset.Shatters.toSetShatters`: bridge from Mathlib's `Finset.Shatters`
  to `SetShatters`.

## References

* [A. Ehrenfeucht, D. Haussler, M. Kearns, L. Valiant,
  *A General Lower Bound on the Number of Examples Needed
  for Learning*][EHKV1989]

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.SetShatters
items.doc:
A binary concept class `C` *shatters* a set `W` if for every subset `W' ⊆ W`,
there exists a concept `c ∈ C` whose positive set `c ⁻¹' {true}` intersects `W`
in exactly `W'`.
items.statement: def SetShatters (C : ConceptClass α Bool) (W : Set α) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.SetShatters.subset
items.doc:
Shattering is anti-monotone in the shattered set: if `C` shatters `W` and
`V ⊆ W`, then `C` shatters `V`.
items.statement:
theorem SetShatters.subset {C : ConceptClass α Bool} {W V : Set α}
    (hW : SetShatters C W) (hVW : V ⊆ W) : SetShatters C V

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.SetShatters.superset
items.doc:
Shattering is monotone in the concept class: if `C` shatters `W` and `C ⊆ C'`,
then `C'` shatters `W`.
items.statement:
theorem SetShatters.superset {C C' : ConceptClass α Bool} {W : Set α}
    (hW : SetShatters C W) (hCC' : C ⊆ C') : SetShatters C' W

items.name: Finset.Shatters.toSetShatters
items.doc:
If a finite set family `𝒜` shatters a finite set `s` in the sense of Mathlib's
`Finset.Shatters`, then the concept class of characteristic functions of sets in `𝒜`
shatters `↑s` in the sense of `SetShatters`. This bridges Mathlib's finset-based
shattering to the predicate used by the PAC learning lower bounds.
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Finset.Shatters.toSetShatters {𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)} {s : Finset α}
    (h : 𝒜.Shatters s) :
    SetShatters
      {c : α → Bool | ∃ t ∈ 𝒜, ∀ x, c x = decide (x ∈ t)} ↑s

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.vcDim
items.doc:
The *Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension* of a binary concept class `C` is the
supremum of the cardinalities of finite sets shattered by `C`. Returns `0` when
no finite set is shattered (i.e. the defining set is empty).

**Caveat**: because `sSup` on `ℕ` returns `0` for unbounded sets, this definition
is only meaningful when the VC dimension is finite — see `HasFiniteVCDim`.
items.statement: noncomputable def vcDim (C : ConceptClass α Bool) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.HasFiniteVCDim
items.doc:
A binary concept class `C` has *finite VC dimension* if there is a uniform
upper bound on the cardinalities of finite sets it shatters. This is the
hypothesis under which `vcDim C` is mathematically meaningful (otherwise
`vcDim` returns `0` for unbounded shattered families via `sSup` on `ℕ`).
items.statement: def HasFiniteVCDim (C : ConceptClass α Bool) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.hasFiniteVCDim_iff
items.doc:
A class has finite VC dimension iff there is a uniform bound on the
cardinality of every shattered finite set.
items.statement:
theorem hasFiniteVCDim_iff {C : ConceptClass α Bool} :
    HasFiniteVCDim C ↔ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ W : Finset α, SetShatters C ↑W → W.card ≤ N

modules.title: Version Space
modules.doc:
The *version space* of a concept class `C` given a labeled sample `S` is the
subset of `C` whose concepts agree with `S` on every observed point — the
classical "concepts still consistent with the data" of Mitchell (1977) and
Angluin (1980).

## Main definitions

- `VersionSpace C S`: the subset of `C` whose concepts agree with `S` on every
  sample point.
- `IsConsistent A C`: a learner is consistent with `C` if its output lies in
  the version space at every realizable sample.
- `empiricalMiscount h S`: number of sample points where `h` errs (`[DecidableEq β]`).
- `empiricalMeasure S`: the uniform Dirac mixture over the sample.
- `empiricalError h S`: the empirical distribution's mass on the disagreement set.
- `Realizable C S`: some concept in `C` labels every sample point correctly.

## Main results

- `versionSpace_subset`, `versionSpace_empty_sample`, `versionSpace_reindex`,
  `versionSpace_antitone`, `versionSpace_mono_C`: structural properties.
- `mem_versionSpace_iff_empiricalMiscount_zero`: combinatorial bridge.
- `mem_versionSpace_iff_empiricalError_zero`: measure-theoretic bridge.
- `IsConsistent.empiricalMiscount_eq_zero`, `IsConsistent.empiricalError_eq_zero`:
  consistent learners achieve zero error / miscount on every realizable sample.
- `mem_versionSpace_of_realizable`, `Realizable.versionSpace_nonempty`: realizable
  samples give non-empty version spaces.
- `ae_mem_versionSpace_of_realizable`: under iid sampling from a realizable
  joint distribution, the target concept lies in the version space almost surely.

## References

* [Mitchell1977]
* [Mitchell1982]
* [Angluin1980]
* [Mitchell1997]

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.VersionSpace
items.doc:
The *version space* of a concept class `C` given a labeled sample `S`:
the set of concepts in `C` whose labels agree with `S` on every observed point.
items.statement:
def VersionSpace {m : ℕ} (C : ConceptClass α β) (S : LabeledSample α β m) :
    ConceptClass α β

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.mem_versionSpace_iff
items.doc:
Membership in the version space unfolds to concept membership plus
per-sample consistency.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpace_subset
items.doc: The version space is a subset of the original concept class.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpace_subset {m : ℕ} (C : ConceptClass α β)
    (S : LabeledSample α β m) :
    VersionSpace C S ⊆ C

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpace_empty_sample
items.doc: Version space on the empty sample equals the whole concept class.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpace_empty_sample (C : ConceptClass α β)
    (S : LabeledSample α β 0) :
    VersionSpace C S = C

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpace_reindex
items.doc:
*Version space reindexing.* For any reindexing `f : Fin m → Fin n`, the
version space on `S` is contained in the version space on the reindexed sample
`S ∘ f`.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpace_reindex {m n : ℕ} (f : Fin m → Fin n) (C : ConceptClass α β)
    (S : LabeledSample α β n) :
    VersionSpace C S ⊆ VersionSpace C (S ∘ f)

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpace_antitone
items.doc:
*Version space antitonicity.* Given a sample of size `n` and `m ≤ n`, the
version space on all `n` observations is a subset of the version space on the
first `m` observations. Special case of `versionSpace_reindex` with
`f := Fin.castLE hmn`.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpace_antitone {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (C : ConceptClass α β)
    (S : LabeledSample α β n) :
    VersionSpace C S ⊆ VersionSpace C (S ∘ Fin.castLE hmn)

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpace_mono_C
items.doc: *Version space is monotone in the concept class.*
items.statement:
theorem versionSpace_mono_C {m : ℕ} {C C' : ConceptClass α β} (hCC' : C ⊆ C')
    (S : LabeledSample α β m) :
    VersionSpace C S ⊆ VersionSpace C' S

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.empiricalMiscount
items.doc:
The *empirical miscount* of a hypothesis `h` on a labeled sample `S`: the
number of sample points where `h` predicts incorrectly.
items.statement:
def empiricalMiscount [DecidableEq β] {m : ℕ} (h : α → β)
    (S : LabeledSample α β m) : ℕ

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.empiricalMeasure
items.doc:
The *empirical distribution* of a labeled sample: the uniform mixture of
Dirac measures at each sample point. Equals the zero measure when `m = 0`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def empiricalMeasure {m : ℕ} (S : LabeledSample α β m) :
    Measure (α × β)

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.empiricalError
items.doc:
The *empirical 0-1 error* of `h` on `S`: the empirical distribution's
mass on the disagreement set.
items.statement:
noncomputable def empiricalError {m : ℕ} (h : α → β) (S : LabeledSample α β m) :
    ℝ≥0∞

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.mem_versionSpace_iff_empiricalMiscount_zero
items.doc:
Version-space membership equals concept-class membership plus zero empirical
miscount (combinatorial bridge).
items.statement:
theorem mem_versionSpace_iff_empiricalMiscount_zero [DecidableEq β]
    {m : ℕ} {C : ConceptClass α β} {S : LabeledSample α β m} {h : α → β} :
    h ∈ VersionSpace C S ↔ h ∈ C ∧ empiricalMiscount h S = 0

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.mem_versionSpace_iff_empiricalError_zero
items.doc:
Version-space membership equals concept-class membership plus zero empirical
error (measure-theoretic bridge).
items.statement:
theorem mem_versionSpace_iff_empiricalError_zero
    [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass α] [MeasurableSingletonClass β]
    {m : ℕ} {C : ConceptClass α β} {S : LabeledSample α β m} {h : α → β} :
    h ∈ VersionSpace C S ↔ h ∈ C ∧ empiricalError h S = 0

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.empiricalError_eq_div
items.doc:
The empirical 0-1 error equals the empirical miscount divided by the
sample size.
items.statement:
theorem empiricalError_eq_div [DecidableEq β]
    [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass α] [MeasurableSingletonClass β]
    {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (h : α → β) (S : LabeledSample α β m) :
    empiricalError h S = (empiricalMiscount h S : ℝ≥0∞) / m

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.Realizable
items.doc:
A labeled sample `S` is *realizable* by concept class `C` if some concept
in `C` labels every sample point correctly.
items.statement: def Realizable {m : ℕ} (C : ConceptClass α β) (S : LabeledSample α β m) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsConsistent
items.doc:
A learner is *consistent* with the concept class `C` if, on every sample
realizable by `C`, its output hypothesis lies in the version space of `C` at
that sample — i.e. the output is in `C` and agrees with every observed labeled
pair. No condition is imposed on samples that no concept in `C` can realize.
items.statement: def IsConsistent {m : ℕ} (A : Learner α β m) (C : ConceptClass α β) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsConsistent.output_mem_conceptClass
items.doc: A consistent learner's output is in the concept class on every realizable sample.
items.statement:
theorem IsConsistent.output_mem_conceptClass {m : ℕ} {A : Learner α β m}
    {C : ConceptClass α β} (hA : IsConsistent A C) (S : LabeledSample α β m)
    (hS : Realizable C S) :
    A S ∈ C

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsConsistent.output_agrees
items.doc:
On every realizable sample, a consistent learner's output agrees with
every observed point.
items.statement:
theorem IsConsistent.output_agrees {m : ℕ} {A : Learner α β m}
    {C : ConceptClass α β} (hA : IsConsistent A C) (S : LabeledSample α β m)
    (hS : Realizable C S) (i : Fin m) :
    A S (S i).1 = (S i).2

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsConsistent.empiricalMiscount_eq_zero
items.doc: A consistent learner has zero empirical miscount on every realizable sample.
items.statement:
theorem IsConsistent.empiricalMiscount_eq_zero [DecidableEq β]
    {m : ℕ} {A : Learner α β m} {C : ConceptClass α β} (hA : IsConsistent A C)
    (S : LabeledSample α β m) (hS : Realizable C S) :
    empiricalMiscount (A S) S = 0

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.IsConsistent.empiricalError_eq_zero
items.doc: A consistent learner has zero empirical error on every realizable sample.
items.statement:
theorem IsConsistent.empiricalError_eq_zero
    [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass α] [MeasurableSingletonClass β]
    {m : ℕ} {A : Learner α β m} {C : ConceptClass α β}
    (hA : IsConsistent A C) (S : LabeledSample α β m) (hS : Realizable C S) :
    empiricalError (A S) S = 0

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.mem_versionSpace_of_realizable
items.doc:
*Realizable version-space nonemptiness.* If a target concept `c` lies in
`C` and the sample `S` is labeled by `c` (i.e. every `(S i).2 = c (S i).1`),
then `c` itself lies in the version space `VersionSpace C S`.
items.statement:
theorem mem_versionSpace_of_realizable {m : ℕ} {C : ConceptClass α β}
    {c : α → β} (hc : c ∈ C) (S : LabeledSample α β m)
    (hS : ∀ i : Fin m, (S i).2 = c (S i).1) :
    c ∈ VersionSpace C S

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.Realizable.versionSpace_nonempty
items.doc: A realizable sample has nonempty version space.

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.ae_mem_versionSpace_of_realizable
items.doc:
Under iid sampling from the realizable joint distribution induced by
`c ∈ C` and a probability measure `P` on `α`, the target concept `c` lies in
the version space almost surely.
items.statement:
theorem ae_mem_versionSpace_of_realizable
    [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β]
    {C : ConceptClass α β} {c : α → β} (hc : c ∈ C) (hcm : Measurable c)
    (hG : MeasurableSet {p : α × β | p.2 = c p.1})
    (P : Measure α) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (m : ℕ) :
    ∀ᵐ S : LabeledSample α β m
      ∂(Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin m => P.map (fun x => (x, c x)))),
      c ∈ VersionSpace C S

modules.title: Version Space Lattice
modules.doc:
The collection of all version spaces of a concept
class is a ∩-closed family with top `C`, the *version space lattice* of Mitchell (1982).

## Main definitions

- `VersionSpaces C`: the family of all version spaces of `C`, over samples of every size.

## Main results

- `versionSpace_append`: the version space of an appended sample is the intersection of
  the version spaces.
- `self_mem_versionSpaces`, `inter_mem_versionSpaces`: the family contains `C` (top) and
  is closed under intersection.
- `versionSpaces_subset_powerset`, `versionSpaces_finite`, `versionSpaces_ncard_le`: every
  member is a subset of `C` and for a finite class the family is finite of size at most
  `2 ^ C.ncard`.

## References

* [Mitchell1977]
* [Mitchell1982]
* [Mitchell1997]

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpace_append
items.doc:
*The version-space meet law.* The version space of an appended sample is the
intersection of the version spaces of the two parts: constraints accumulate by
intersection.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpace_append {m n : ℕ} (C : ConceptClass α β)
    (S : LabeledSample α β m) (T : LabeledSample α β n) :
    VersionSpace C (Fin.append S T) = VersionSpace C S ∩ VersionSpace C T

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.VersionSpaces
items.doc:
The family of all version spaces of a concept class, over labeled samples of every
size.
items.statement: def VersionSpaces (C : ConceptClass α β) : Set (ConceptClass α β)

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.mem_versionSpaces_iff
items.doc: Membership in the version-space family unfolds to a witnessing sample.
items.statement:
theorem mem_versionSpaces_iff {C V : ConceptClass α β} :
    V ∈ VersionSpaces C ↔ ∃ (m : ℕ) (S : LabeledSample α β m), V = VersionSpace C S

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.self_mem_versionSpaces
items.doc: The whole class is a version space (of the empty sample) which means the family has top `C`.
items.statement: theorem self_mem_versionSpaces (C : ConceptClass α β) : C ∈ VersionSpaces C

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.inter_mem_versionSpaces
items.doc:
The version-space family is closed under intersection (append the witnessing
samples).

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpaces_subset_powerset
items.doc:
Every version space is a subset of the class: the family lives in the powerset
of `C`.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpaces_subset_powerset (C : ConceptClass α β) :
    VersionSpaces C ⊆ 𝒫 C

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpaces_finite
items.doc: A finite concept class has finitely many version spaces.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpaces_finite {C : ConceptClass α β} (hC : C.Finite) :
    (VersionSpaces C).Finite

items.name: Cslib.MachineLearning.PACLearning.versionSpaces_ncard_le
items.doc:
A finite concept class has at most `2 ^ C.ncard` version spaces: the lattice embeds
in the powerset.
items.statement:
theorem versionSpaces_ncard_le {C : ConceptClass α β} (hC : C.Finite) :
    (VersionSpaces C).ncard ≤ 2 ^ C.ncard

modules.authors: Josha Dekker, Devon Tuma, Kexing Ying, Samuel Schlesinger
modules.title: PMF Utilities
modules.doc:
## NB: This module is temporary

The bind/pure and posterior lemmas here have no dependence on any domain-specific
structure. They should be upstreamed to Mathlib
(likely `Mathlib.Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Monad` or a new
`Mathlib.Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Prod`). Once accepted upstream,
these lemmas should be removed and their consumers should import the Mathlib module instead.

The uniform samplers retain the PMF interface removed in
[mathlib#42909](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/42909),
pending a decision on CSLib's probability API. Their definitions and proofs are adapted from
`Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Uniform` before that PR, by Josha Dekker, Devon Tuma,
and Kexing Ying, under the Apache 2.0 license.
Original sampler copyright (c) 2024 Josha Dekker. All rights reserved.

## Main results

- `Cslib.Probability.PMF.bind_pair_apply`: the "pairing" bind at `(a, b)` equals `p a * f a b`
- `Cslib.Probability.PMF.bind_pair_tsum_fst`: marginalizing over the first component
- `Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv`:
  a uniform distribution is invariant under equivalence
- `Cslib.Probability.PMF.posteriorDist`: the posterior as a `PMF`
- `Cslib.Probability.PMF.posteriorDist_eq_prior_of_outputIndist`:
  if the output distribution does not depend on the input, conditioning does
  not change the prior

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFinset
items.doc: Uniform probability mass function on a nonempty finite set.
items.statement: noncomputable def uniformOfFinset (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) : PMF α

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFinset_apply
items.statement:
theorem uniformOfFinset_apply (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) (a : α) :
    uniformOfFinset s hs a = if a ∈ s then (s.card : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ else 0

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.mem_support_uniformOfFinset_iff
items.statement:
theorem mem_support_uniformOfFinset_iff {s : Finset α} (hs : s.Nonempty) (a : α) :
    a ∈ (uniformOfFinset s hs).support ↔ a ∈ s

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFintype
items.doc: Uniform probability mass function on a nonempty finite type.
items.statement: noncomputable def uniformOfFintype (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [Nonempty α] : PMF α

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFintype_apply
items.statement:
theorem uniformOfFintype_apply [Fintype α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
    uniformOfFintype α a = (Fintype.card α : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.bind_pair_apply
items.doc:
Evaluating the "pairing" bind `(do let a ← p; return (a, ← f a))` at `(a, b)`
gives the product `p a * f a b`.
items.statement:
theorem bind_pair_apply (p : PMF α) (f : α → PMF β) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (p.bind fun a' => (f a').bind fun b' => PMF.pure (a', b')) (a, b) = p a * f a b

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.bind_pair_tsum_fst
items.doc: Summing the pairing bind over the first component gives the marginal.
items.statement:
theorem bind_pair_tsum_fst (p : PMF α) (f : α → PMF β) (b : β) :
    ∑' a, (p.bind fun a' => (f a').bind fun b' => PMF.pure (a', b')) (a, b) =
      (p.bind f) b

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv
items.doc: A uniform distribution on a finite type is invariant under any equivalence.
items.statement:
theorem uniformOfFintype_map_equiv {γ : Type v} [Fintype α] [Fintype γ] [Nonempty α] [Nonempty γ]
    (e : α ≃ γ) :
    (uniformOfFintype α).map e = uniformOfFintype γ

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFintype_prod
items.doc: Independent uniform sampling on `α` and `β` equals uniform sampling on `α × β`.
items.statement:
theorem uniformOfFintype_prod (α β : Type*)
    [Fintype α] [Nonempty α] [Fintype β] [Nonempty β] :
    ((PMF.uniformOfFintype α).bind fun a =>
      (PMF.uniformOfFintype β).map fun b => (a, b)) =
    PMF.uniformOfFintype (α × β)

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.posteriorDist
items.doc:
The posterior distribution `Pr[A = a | B = b]` as a `PMF`,
given `a ← p`, `b ← f a`, and that `b` has positive marginal probability:
the joint distribution's slice at `b`, normalized.
items.statement:
noncomputable def posteriorDist (p : PMF α) (f : α → PMF β) (b : β)
    (hb : b ∈ (p.bind f).support) : PMF α

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.posteriorDist_apply
items.statement:
theorem posteriorDist_apply (p : PMF α) (f : α → PMF β) (b : β)
    (hb : b ∈ (p.bind f).support) (a : α) :
    posteriorDist p f b hb a =
      (p.bind fun a' => (f a').bind fun b' => PMF.pure (a', b')) (a, b) /
        (p.bind f) b

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.posteriorDist_eq_prior_of_outputIndist
items.doc:
If the output distribution of a channel does not depend on the input, then
conditioning on any output with positive probability leaves the prior unchanged.
items.statement:
theorem posteriorDist_eq_prior_of_outputIndist (p : PMF α) (f : α → PMF β)
    (h : ∀ a₀ a₁ : α, f a₀ = f a₁)
    (b : β) (hb : b ∈ (p.bind f).support) :
    posteriorDist p f b hb = p

modules.title: Statistical Distance of Finite Probability Mass Functions
modules.doc:
For PMFs `p` and `q` on a finite type, their statistical distance is

`(1 / 2) * ∑ a, |p a - q a|`.

This is [BonehShoup2023], Definition 3.5. The probabilities are converted from
`ℝ≥0∞`, Mathlib's codomain for a `PMF`, to `ℝ` before taking the finite sum.

Statistical distance is packaged as a scoped `MetricSpace` instance on
`PMF α`, so it is spelled `dist p q` and the general metric API applies:
`dist_nonneg`, `dist_self`, `dist_comm`, `dist_triangle`, `dist_eq_zero`, and
so on. Open `Cslib.Probability.PMF` (or `open scoped Cslib.Probability.PMF`)
to activate the instance; it is scoped so that this library does not install a
global metric on Mathlib's `PMF` type.

Besides the metric structure, this file proves that applying the same
transformation — deterministic or randomized — to two PMFs cannot increase
their statistical distance; [BonehShoup2023], Theorem 3.13 is the
deterministic case.

## Main definitions

- `MetricSpace (PMF α)` (scoped instance): statistical distance as a metric
- `StatisticallyClose`: an upper bound on statistical distance

## Main results

- `dist_bind_le`: randomized postprocessing cannot increase statistical
  distance
- `dist_eq_one_of_disjoint_support`: PMFs with disjoint supports are at the
  maximum statistical distance
- `StatisticallyClose.trans`: closeness bounds chain through an intermediate
  distribution, adding the errors
- `statisticallyClose_zero_iff`: zero error is equality

## References

* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023]

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.instMetricSpace
items.doc:
Statistical distance makes the PMFs on a finite type a metric space
([BonehShoup2023], Definition 3.5).
items.statement:
noncomputable scoped instance instMetricSpace [Fintype α] :
    MetricSpace (PMF α)

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_eq
items.doc:
The distance between two PMFs on a finite type is their statistical
distance ([BonehShoup2023], Definition 3.5).
items.statement:
theorem dist_eq [Fintype α] (p q : PMF α) :
    dist p q = (∑ a, |(p a).toReal - (q a).toReal|) / 2

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_le_one
items.doc: Statistical distance is at most one.
items.statement: theorem dist_le_one [Fintype α] (p q : PMF α) : dist p q ≤ 1

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_eq_one_of_disjoint_support
items.doc: PMFs with disjoint supports are at the maximum statistical distance.
items.statement:
theorem dist_eq_one_of_disjoint_support [Fintype α] {p q : PMF α}
    (h : Disjoint p.support q.support) : dist p q = 1

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_bind_le
items.doc:
Applying the same randomized kernel to two PMFs cannot increase their
statistical distance.
items.statement:
theorem dist_bind_le [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (p q : PMF α) (kernel : α → PMF β) :
    dist (p.bind kernel) (q.bind kernel) ≤ dist p q

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_map_le
items.doc:
Deterministic postprocessing cannot increase statistical distance
([BonehShoup2023], Theorem 3.13).
items.statement:
theorem dist_map_le [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (p q : PMF α) (f : α → β) :
    dist (p.map f) (q.map f) ≤ dist p q

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.StatisticallyClose
items.doc:
Two PMFs are `ε`-statistically close when their statistical distance is at
most `ε`. The `ℝ≥0` parameter rules out meaningless negative bounds.
items.statement: def StatisticallyClose [Fintype α] (p q : PMF α) (ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.StatisticallyClose.refl
items.doc: Every PMF is statistically close to itself with zero error.
items.statement: theorem refl [Fintype α] (p : PMF α) : StatisticallyClose p p 0

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.StatisticallyClose.symm
items.doc: Statistical closeness is symmetric.
items.statement:
theorem symm [Fintype α] {p q : PMF α} {ε : ℝ≥0}
    (h : StatisticallyClose p q ε) : StatisticallyClose q p ε

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.StatisticallyClose.mono
items.doc: A statistical-closeness bound remains valid when its error is enlarged.
items.statement: theorem mono [Fintype α] {p q : PMF α} : Monotone (StatisticallyClose p q)

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.StatisticallyClose.trans
items.doc:
Closeness bounds chain through an intermediate distribution, adding the
errors.

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.StatisticallyClose.bind
items.doc:
A shared randomized postprocessing kernel preserves statistical
closeness.

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.StatisticallyClose.map
items.doc: Deterministic postprocessing preserves statistical closeness.

items.name: Cslib.Probability.PMF.statisticallyClose_zero_iff
items.doc: Statistical closeness with zero error is equality.
items.statement:
theorem statisticallyClose_zero_iff [Fintype α] (p q : PMF α) :
    StatisticallyClose p q 0 ↔ p = q
